516sub check_keys {
517 my ( $rtest, $rvalid, $msg, $exact_match ) = @_;
518
519 # Check the keys of a hash:
520 # $rtest = ref to hash to test
521 # $rvalid = ref to hash with valid keys
522
523 # $msg = a message to write in case of error
524 # $exact_match defines the type of check:
525 # = false: test hash must not have unknown key
526 # = true: test hash must have exactly same keys as known hash
527 my @unknown_keys =
528 grep { !exists $rvalid->{$_} } keys %{$rtest};
529 my @missing_keys =
530 grep { !exists $rtest->{$_} } keys %{$rvalid};
531 my $error = @unknown_keys;
532 if ($exact_match) { $error ||= @missing_keys }
533 if ($error) {
534 local $" = ')(';
535 my @expected_keys = sort keys %{$rvalid};
536 @unknown_keys = sort @unknown_keys;
537 Die(<<EOM);
538------------------------------------------------------------------------
539Program error detected checking hash keys
540Message is: '$msg'
541Expected keys: (@expected_keys)
542Unknown key(s): (@unknown_keys)
543Missing key(s): (@missing_keys)
544------------------------------------------------------------------------
545EOM
546 }
547 return;
548}

863sub check_token_array {
864 my $self = shift;

866 # Check for errors in the array of tokens
867 # Uses package variable $NVARS
868 $self->check_self_hash();
869 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
870 for ( my $KK = 0 ; $KK < @{$rLL} ; $KK++ ) {
871 my $nvars = @{ $rLL->[$KK] };
872 if ( $nvars != $NVARS ) {
873 my $type = $rLL->[$KK]->[_TYPE_];
874 $type = '*' unless defined($type);
875 Fault(
876"number of vars for node $KK, type '$type', is $nvars but should be $NVARS"
877 );
878 }
879 foreach my $var ( _TOKEN_, _TYPE_ ) {
880 if ( !defined( $rLL->[$KK]->[$var] ) ) {
881 my $iline = $rLL->[$KK]->[_LINE_INDEX_];
882 Fault("Undefined variable $var for K=$KK, line=$iline\n");
883 }
884 }
885 }
886 return;
887}

967sub keyword_group_scan {
968 my $self = shift;
969
970 # Manipulate blank lines around keyword groups (kgb* flags)
971 # Scan all lines looking for runs of consecutive lines beginning with
972 # selected keywords. Example keywords are 'my', 'our', 'local', ... but
973 # they may be anything. We will set flags requesting that blanks be
974 # inserted around and within them according to input parameters. Note
975 # that we are scanning the lines as they came in in the input stream, so
976 # they are not necessarily well formatted.
977
978 # The output of this sub is a return hash ref whose keys are the indexes of
979 # lines after which we desire a blank line. For line index i:
980 # $rhash_of_desires->{$i} = 1 means we want a blank line AFTER line $i
981 # $rhash_of_desires->{$i} = 2 means we want blank line $i removed
982 my $rhash_of_desires = {};
983
984 my $Opt_blanks_before = $rOpts->{'keyword-group-blanks-before'}; # '-kgbb'
985 my $Opt_blanks_after = $rOpts->{'keyword-group-blanks-after'}; # '-kgba'
986 my $Opt_blanks_inside = $rOpts->{'keyword-group-blanks-inside'}; # '-kgbi'
987 my $Opt_blanks_delete = $rOpts->{'keyword-group-blanks-delete'}; # '-kgbd'
988 my $Opt_size = $rOpts->{'keyword-group-blanks-size'}; # '-kgbs'
989
990 # A range of sizes can be input with decimal notation like 'min.max' with
991 # any number of dots between the two numbers. Examples:
992 # string => min max matches
993 # 1.1 1 1 exactly 1
994 # 1.3 1 3 1,2, or 3
995 # 1..3 1 3 1,2, or 3
996 # 5 5 - 5 or more
997 # 6. 6 - 6 or more
998 # .2 - 2 up to 2
999 # 1.0 1 0 nothing
1000 my ( $Opt_size_min, $Opt_size_max ) = split /\.+/, $Opt_size;
1001 if ( $Opt_size_min && $Opt_size_min !~ /^\d+$/
1002 || $Opt_size_max && $Opt_size_max !~ /^\d+$/ )
1003 {
1004 Warn(<<EOM);
1005Unexpected value for -kgbs: '$Opt_size'; expecting 'min' or 'min.max';
1006ignoring all -kgb flags
1007EOM
1008 return $rhash_of_desires;
1009 }
1010 $Opt_size_min = 1 unless ($Opt_size_min);
1011
1012 if ( $Opt_size_max && $Opt_size_max < $Opt_size_min ) {
1013 return $rhash_of_desires;
1014 }
1015
1016 # codes for $Opt_blanks_before and $Opt_blanks_after:
1017 # 0 = never (delete if exist)
1018 # 1 = stable (keep unchanged)
1019 # 2 = always (insert if missing)
1020
1021 return $rhash_of_desires
1022 unless $Opt_size_min > 0
1023 && ( $Opt_blanks_before != 1
1024 || $Opt_blanks_after != 1
1025 || $Opt_blanks_inside
1026 || $Opt_blanks_delete );
1027
1028 my $Opt_pattern = $keyword_group_list_pattern;
1029 my $Opt_comment_pattern = $keyword_group_list_comment_pattern;
1030 my $Opt_repeat_count =
1031 $rOpts->{'keyword-group-blanks-repeat-count'}; # '-kgbr'
1032
1033 my $rlines = $self->{rlines};
1034 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
1035 my $K_closing_container = $self->{K_closing_container};
1036
1037 # variables for the current group and subgroups:
1038 my ( $ibeg, $iend, $count, $level_beg, $K_closing, @iblanks, @group,
1039 @subgroup );
1040
1041 # Definitions:
1042 # ($ibeg, $iend) = starting and ending line indexes of this entire group
1043 # $count = total number of keywords seen in this entire group
1044 # $level_beg = indententation level of this group
1045 # @group = [ $i, $token, $count ] =list of all keywords & blanks
1046 # @subgroup = $j, index of group where token changes
1047 # @iblanks = line indexes of blank lines in input stream in this group
1048 # where i=starting line index
1049 # token (the keyword)
1050 # count = number of this token in this subgroup
1051 # j = index in group where token changes
1052 #
1053 # These vars will contain values for the most recently seen line:
1054 my ( $line_type, $CODE_type, $K_first, $K_last );
1055
1056 my $number_of_groups_seen = 0;
1057
1058 ####################
1059 # helper subroutines
1060 ####################
1061
1062 my $insert_blank_after = sub {
1063 my ($i) = @_;
1064 $rhash_of_desires->{$i} = 1;
1065 my $ip = $i + 1;
1066 if ( defined( $rhash_of_desires->{$ip} )
1067 && $rhash_of_desires->{$ip} == 2 )
1068 {
1069 $rhash_of_desires->{$ip} = 0;
1070 }
1071 return;
1072 };
1073
1074 my $split_into_sub_groups = sub {
1075
1076 # place blanks around long sub-groups of keywords
1077 # ...if requested
1078 return unless ($Opt_blanks_inside);
1079
1080 # loop over sub-groups, index k
1081 push @subgroup, scalar @group;
1082 my $kbeg = 1;
1083 my $kend = @subgroup - 1;
1084 for ( my $k = $kbeg ; $k <= $kend ; $k++ ) {
1085
1086 # index j runs through all keywords found
1087 my $j_b = $subgroup[ $k - 1 ];
1088 my $j_e = $subgroup[$k] - 1;
1089
1090 # index i is the actual line number of a keyword
1091 my ( $i_b, $tok_b, $count_b ) = @{ $group[$j_b] };
1092 my ( $i_e, $tok_e, $count_e ) = @{ $group[$j_e] };
1093 my $num = $count_e - $count_b + 1;
1094
1095 # This subgroup runs from line $ib to line $ie-1, but may contain
1096 # blank lines
1097 if ( $num >= $Opt_size_min ) {
1098
1099 # if there are blank lines, we require that at least $num lines
1100 # be non-blank up to the boundary with the next subgroup.
1101 my $nog_b = my $nog_e = 1;
1102 if ( @iblanks && !$Opt_blanks_delete ) {
1103 my $j_bb = $j_b + $num - 1;
1104 my ( $i_bb, $tok_bb, $count_bb ) = @{ $group[$j_bb] };
1105 $nog_b = $count_bb - $count_b + 1 == $num;
1106
1107 my $j_ee = $j_e - ( $num - 1 );
1108 my ( $i_ee, $tok_ee, $count_ee ) = @{ $group[$j_ee] };
1109 $nog_e = $count_e - $count_ee + 1 == $num;
1110 }
1111 if ( $nog_b && $k > $kbeg ) {
1112 $insert_blank_after->( $i_b - 1 );
1113 }
1114 if ( $nog_e && $k < $kend ) {
1115 my ( $i_ep, $tok_ep, $count_ep ) = @{ $group[ $j_e + 1 ] };
1116 $insert_blank_after->( $i_ep - 1 );
1117 }
1118 }
1119 }
1120 };
1121
1122 my $delete_if_blank = sub {
1123 my ($i) = @_;
1124
1125 # delete line $i if it is blank
1126 return unless ( $i >= 0 && $i < @{$rlines} );
1127 my $line_type = $rlines->[$i]->{_line_type};
1128 return if ( $line_type ne 'CODE' );
1129 my $code_type = $rlines->[$i]->{_code_type};
1130 if ( $code_type eq 'BL' ) { $rhash_of_desires->{$i} = 2; }
1131 return;
1132 };
1133
1134 my $delete_inner_blank_lines = sub {
1135
1136 # always remove unwanted trailing blank lines from our list
1137 return unless (@iblanks);
1138 while ( my $ibl = pop(@iblanks) ) {
1139 if ( $ibl < $iend ) { push @iblanks, $ibl; last }
1140 $iend = $ibl;
1141 }
1142
1143 # now mark mark interior blank lines for deletion if requested
1144 return unless ($Opt_blanks_delete);
1145
1146 while ( my $ibl = pop(@iblanks) ) { $rhash_of_desires->{$ibl} = 2 }
1147
1148 };
1149
1150 my $end_group = sub {
1151
1152 # end a group of keywords
1153 my ($bad_ending) = @_;
1154 if ( defined($ibeg) && $ibeg >= 0 ) {
1155
1156 # then handle sufficiently large groups
1157 if ( $count >= $Opt_size_min ) {
1158
1159 $number_of_groups_seen++;
1160
1161 # do any blank deletions regardless of the count
1162 $delete_inner_blank_lines->();
1163
1164 if ( $ibeg > 0 ) {
1165 my $code_type = $rlines->[ $ibeg - 1 ]->{_code_type};
1166
1167 # patch for hash bang line which is not currently marked as
1168 # a comment; mark it as a comment
1169 if ( $ibeg == 1 && !$code_type ) {
1170 my $line_text = $rlines->[ $ibeg - 1 ]->{_line_text};
1171 $code_type = 'BC'
1172 if ( $line_text && $line_text =~ /^#/ );
1173 }
1174
1175 # Do not insert a blank after a comment
1176 # (this could be subject to a flag in the future)
1177 if ( $code_type !~ /(BC|SBC|SBCX)/ ) {
1178 if ( $Opt_blanks_before == INSERT ) {
1179 $insert_blank_after->( $ibeg - 1 );
1180
1181 }
1182 elsif ( $Opt_blanks_before == DELETE ) {
1183 $delete_if_blank->( $ibeg - 1 );
1184 }
1185 }
1186 }
1187
1188 # We will only put blanks before code lines. We could loosen
1189 # this rule a little, but we have to be very careful because
1190 # for example we certainly don't want to drop a blank line
1191 # after a line like this:
1192 # my $var = <<EOM;
1193 if ( $line_type eq 'CODE' && defined($K_first) ) {
1194
1195 # - Do not put a blank before a line of different level
1196 # - Do not put a blank line if we ended the search badly
1197 # - Do not put a blank at the end of the file
1198 # - Do not put a blank line before a hanging side comment
1199 my $level = $rLL->[$K_first]->[_LEVEL_];
1200 my $ci_level = $rLL->[$K_first]->[_CI_LEVEL_];
1201
1202 if ( $level == $level_beg
1203 && $ci_level == 0
1204 && !$bad_ending
1205 && $iend < @{$rlines}
1206 && $CODE_type ne 'HSC' )
1207 {
1208 if ( $Opt_blanks_after == INSERT ) {
1209 $insert_blank_after->($iend);
1210 }
1211 elsif ( $Opt_blanks_after == DELETE ) {
1212 $delete_if_blank->( $iend + 1 );
1213 }
1214 }
1215 }
1216 }
1217 $split_into_sub_groups->();
1218 }
1219
1220 # reset for another group
1221 $ibeg = -1;
1222 $iend = undef;
1223 $level_beg = -1;
1224 $K_closing = undef;
1225 @group = ();
1226 @subgroup = ();
1227 @iblanks = ();
1228 };
1229
1230 my $find_container_end = sub {
1231
1232 # If the keyword lines ends with an open token, find the closing token
1233 # '$K_closing' so that we can easily skip past the contents of the
1234 # container.
1235 return if ( $K_last <= $K_first );
1236 my $KK = $K_last;
1237 my $type_last = $rLL->[$KK]->[_TYPE_];
1238 my $tok_last = $rLL->[$KK]->[_TOKEN_];
1239 if ( $type_last eq '#' ) {
1240 $KK = $self->K_previous_nonblank($KK);
1241 $tok_last = $rLL->[$KK]->[_TOKEN_];
1242 }
1243 if ( $KK > $K_first && $tok_last =~ /^[\(\{\[]$/ ) {
1244
1245 my $type_sequence = $rLL->[$KK]->[_TYPE_SEQUENCE_];
1246 my $lev = $rLL->[$KK]->[_LEVEL_];
1247 if ( $lev == $level_beg ) {
1248 $K_closing = $K_closing_container->{$type_sequence};
1249 }
1250 }
1251 };
1252
1253 my $add_to_group = sub {
1254 my ( $i, $token, $level ) = @_;
1255
1256 # End the previous group if we have reached the maximum
1257 # group size
1258 if ( $Opt_size_max && @group >= $Opt_size_max ) {
1259 $end_group->();
1260 }
1261
1262 if ( @group == 0 ) {
1263 $ibeg = $i;
1264 $level_beg = $level;
1265 $count = 0;
1266 }
1267
1268 $count++;
1269 $iend = $i;
1270
1271 # New sub-group?
1272 if ( !@group || $token ne $group[-1]->[1] ) {
1273 push @subgroup, scalar(@group);
1274 }
1275 push @group, [ $i, $token, $count ];
1276
1277 # remember if this line ends in an open container
1278 $find_container_end->();
1279
1280 return;
1281 };
1282
1283 ###################################
1284 # loop over all lines of the source
1285 ###################################
1286 $end_group->();
1287 my $i = -1;
1288 foreach my $line_of_tokens ( @{$rlines} ) {
1289
1290 $i++;
1291 last
1292 if ( $Opt_repeat_count > 0
1293 && $number_of_groups_seen >= $Opt_repeat_count );
1294
1295 $CODE_type = "";
1296 $K_first = undef;
1297 $K_last = undef;
1298 $line_type = $line_of_tokens->{_line_type};
1299
1300 # always end a group at non-CODE
1301 if ( $line_type ne 'CODE' ) { $end_group->(); next }
1302
1303 $CODE_type = $line_of_tokens->{_code_type};
1304
1305 # end any group at a format skipping line
1306 if ( $CODE_type && $CODE_type eq 'FS' ) {
1307 $end_group->();
1308 next;
1309 }
1310
1311 # continue in a verbatim (VB) type; it may be quoted text
1312 if ( $CODE_type eq 'VB' ) {
1313 if ( $ibeg >= 0 ) { $iend = $i; }
1314 next;
1315 }
1316
1317 # and continue in blank (BL) types
1318 if ( $CODE_type eq 'BL' ) {
1319 if ( $ibeg >= 0 ) {
1320 $iend = $i;
1321 push @{iblanks}, $i;
1322
1323 # propagate current subgroup token
1324 my $tok = $group[-1]->[1];
1325 push @group, [ $i, $tok, $count ];
1326 }
1327 next;
1328 }
1329
1330 # examine the first token of this line
1331 my $rK_range = $line_of_tokens->{_rK_range};
1332 ( $K_first, $K_last ) = @{$rK_range};
1333 if ( !defined($K_first) ) {
1334
1335 # Unexpected blank line..shouldn't happen
1336 # $rK_range should be defined for line type CODE
1337 Warn(
1338"Programming Error: Unexpected Blank Line in sub 'keyword_group_scan'. Ignoring"
1339 );
1340 return $rhash_of_desires;
1341 }
1342
1343 my $level = $rLL->[$K_first]->[_LEVEL_];
1344 my $type = $rLL->[$K_first]->[_TYPE_];
1345 my $token = $rLL->[$K_first]->[_TOKEN_];
1346 my $ci_level = $rLL->[$K_first]->[_CI_LEVEL_];
1347
1348 # see if this is a code type we seek (i.e. comment)
1349 if ( $CODE_type
1350 && $Opt_comment_pattern
1351 && $CODE_type =~ /$Opt_comment_pattern/o )
1352 {
1353
1354 my $tok = $CODE_type;
1355
1356 # Continuing a group
1357 if ( $ibeg >= 0 && $level == $level_beg ) {
1358 $add_to_group->( $i, $tok, $level );
1359 }
1360
1361 # Start new group
1362 else {
1363
1364 # first end old group if any; we might be starting new
1365 # keywords at different level
1366 if ( $ibeg > 0 ) { $end_group->(); }
1367 $add_to_group->( $i, $tok, $level );
1368 }
1369 next;
1370 }
1371
1372 # See if it is a keyword we seek, but never start a group in a
1373 # continuation line; the code may be badly formatted.
1374 if ( $ci_level == 0
1375 && $type eq 'k'
1376 && $token =~ /$Opt_pattern/o )
1377 {
1378
1379 # Continuing a keyword group
1380 if ( $ibeg >= 0 && $level == $level_beg ) {
1381 $add_to_group->( $i, $token, $level );
1382 }
1383
1384 # Start new keyword group
1385 else {
1386
1387 # first end old group if any; we might be starting new
1388 # keywords at different level
1389 if ( $ibeg > 0 ) { $end_group->(); }
1390 $add_to_group->( $i, $token, $level );
1391 }
1392 next;
1393 }
1394
1395 # This is not one of our keywords, but we are in a keyword group
1396 # so see if we should continue or quit
1397 elsif ( $ibeg >= 0 ) {
1398
1399 # - bail out on a large level change; we may have walked into a
1400 # data structure or anoymous sub code.
1401 if ( $level > $level_beg + 1 || $level < $level_beg ) {
1402 $end_group->();
1403 next;
1404 }
1405
1406 # - keep going on a continuation line of the same level, since
1407 # it is probably a continuation of our previous keyword,
1408 # - and keep going past hanging side comments because we never
1409 # want to interrupt them.
1410 if ( ( ( $level == $level_beg ) && $ci_level > 0 )
1411 || $CODE_type eq 'HSC' )
1412 {
1413 $iend = $i;
1414 next;
1415 }
1416
1417 # - continue if if we are within in a container which started with
1418 # the line of the previous keyword.
1419 if ( defined($K_closing) && $K_first <= $K_closing ) {
1420
1421 # continue if entire line is within container
1422 if ( $K_last <= $K_closing ) { $iend = $i; next }
1423
1424 # continue at ); or }; or ];
1425 my $KK = $K_closing + 1;
1426 if ( $rLL->[$KK]->[_TYPE_] eq ';' ) {
1427 if ( $KK < $K_last ) {
1428 if ( $rLL->[ ++$KK ]->[_TYPE_] eq 'b' ) { ++$KK }
1429 if ( $KK > $K_last || $rLL->[$KK]->[_TYPE_] ne '#' ) {
1430 $end_group->(1);
1431 next;
1432 }
1433 }
1434 $iend = $i;
1435 next;
1436 }
1437
1438 $end_group->(1);
1439 next;
1440 }
1441
1442 # - end the group if none of the above
1443 $end_group->();
1444 next;
1445 }
1446
1447 # not in a keyword group; continue
1448 else { next }
1449 }
1450
1451 # end of loop over all lines
1452 $end_group->();
1453 return $rhash_of_desires;
1454}

1456sub break_lines {
1457
1458 # Loop over old lines to set new line break points
1459
1460 my $self = shift;
1461 my $rlines = $self->{rlines};
1462
1463 # Note for RT#118553, leave only one newline at the end of a file.
1464 # Example code to do this is in comments below:
1465 # my $Opt_trim_ending_blank_lines = 0;
1466 # if ($Opt_trim_ending_blank_lines) {
1467 # while ( my $line_of_tokens = pop @{$rlines} ) {
1468 # my $line_type = $line_of_tokens->{_line_type};
1469 # if ( $line_type eq 'CODE' ) {
1470 # my $CODE_type = $line_of_tokens->{_code_type};
1471 # next if ( $CODE_type eq 'BL' );
1472 # }
1473 # push @{$rlines}, $line_of_tokens;
1474 # last;
1475 # }
1476 # }
1477
1478 # But while this would be a trivial update, it would have very undesirable
1479 # side effects when perltidy is run from within an editor on a small snippet.
1480 # So this is best done with a separate filter, such
1481 # as 'delete_ending_blank_lines.pl' in the examples folder.
1482
1483 # Flag to prevent blank lines when POD occurs in a format skipping sect.
1484 my $in_format_skipping_section;
1485
1486 # set locations for blanks around long runs of keywords
1487 my $rwant_blank_line_after = $self->keyword_group_scan();
1488
1489 my $line_type = "";
1490 my $i = -1;
1491 foreach my $line_of_tokens ( @{$rlines} ) {
1492 $i++;
1493
1494 # insert blank lines requested for keyword sequences
1495 if ( $i > 0
1496 && defined( $rwant_blank_line_after->{ $i - 1 } )
1497 && $rwant_blank_line_after->{ $i - 1 } == 1 )
1498 {
1499 $self->want_blank_line();
1500 }
1501
1502 my $last_line_type = $line_type;
1503 $line_type = $line_of_tokens->{_line_type};
1504 my $input_line = $line_of_tokens->{_line_text};
1505
1506 # _line_type codes are:
1507 # SYSTEM - system-specific code before hash-bang line
1508 # CODE - line of perl code (including comments)
1509 # POD_START - line starting pod, such as '=head'
1510 # POD - pod documentation text
1511 # POD_END - last line of pod section, '=cut'
1512 # HERE - text of here-document
1513 # HERE_END - last line of here-doc (target word)
1514 # FORMAT - format section
1515 # FORMAT_END - last line of format section, '.'
1516 # DATA_START - __DATA__ line
1517 # DATA - unidentified text following __DATA__
1518 # END_START - __END__ line
1519 # END - unidentified text following __END__
1520 # ERROR - we are in big trouble, probably not a perl script
1521
1522 # put a blank line after an =cut which comes before __END__ and __DATA__
1523 # (required by podchecker)
1524 if ( $last_line_type eq 'POD_END' && !$saw_END_or_DATA_ ) {
1525 $file_writer_object->reset_consecutive_blank_lines();
1526 if ( !$in_format_skipping_section && $input_line !~ /^\s*$/ ) {
1527 $self->want_blank_line();
1528 }
1529 }
1530
1531 # handle line of code..
1532 if ( $line_type eq 'CODE' ) {
1533
1534 my $CODE_type = $line_of_tokens->{_code_type};
1535 $in_format_skipping_section = $CODE_type eq 'FS';
1536
1537 # Handle blank lines
1538 if ( $CODE_type eq 'BL' ) {
1539
1540 # If keep-old-blank-lines is zero, we delete all
1541 # old blank lines and let the blank line rules generate any
1542 # needed blanks.
1543
1544 # We also delete lines requested by the keyword-group logic
1545 my $kgb_keep = !( defined( $rwant_blank_line_after->{$i} )
1546 && $rwant_blank_line_after->{$i} == 2 );
1547
1548 # But the keep-old-blank-lines flag has priority over kgb flags
1549 $kgb_keep = 1 if ( $rOpts_keep_old_blank_lines == 2 );
1550
1551 if ( $rOpts_keep_old_blank_lines && $kgb_keep ) {
1552 $self->flush();
1553 $file_writer_object->write_blank_code_line(
1554 $rOpts_keep_old_blank_lines == 2 );
1555 $last_line_leading_type = 'b';
1556 }
1557 next;
1558 }
1559 else {
1560
1561 # let logger see all non-blank lines of code
1562 my $output_line_number = get_output_line_number();
1563 black_box( $line_of_tokens, $output_line_number );
1564 }
1565
1566 # Handle Format Skipping (FS) and Verbatim (VB) Lines
1567 if ( $CODE_type eq 'VB' || $CODE_type eq 'FS' ) {
1568 $self->write_unindented_line("$input_line");
1569 $file_writer_object->reset_consecutive_blank_lines();
1570 next;
1571 }
1572
1573 # Handle all other lines of code
1574 $self->print_line_of_tokens($line_of_tokens);
1575 }
1576
1577 # handle line of non-code..
1578 else {
1579
1580 # set special flags
1581 my $skip_line = 0;
1582 my $tee_line = 0;
1583 if ( $line_type =~ /^POD/ ) {
1584
1585 # Pod docs should have a preceding blank line. But stay
1586 # out of __END__ and __DATA__ sections, because
1587 # the user may be using this section for any purpose whatsoever
1588 if ( $rOpts->{'delete-pod'} ) { $skip_line = 1; }
1589 if ( $rOpts->{'tee-pod'} ) { $tee_line = 1; }
1590 if ( $rOpts->{'trim-pod'} ) { $input_line =~ s/\s+$// }
1591 if ( !$skip_line
1592 && !$in_format_skipping_section
1593 && $line_type eq 'POD_START'
1594 && !$saw_END_or_DATA_ )
1595 {
1596 $self->want_blank_line();
1597 }
1598 }
1599
1600 # leave the blank counters in a predictable state
1601 # after __END__ or __DATA__
1602 elsif ( $line_type =~ /^(END_START|DATA_START)$/ ) {
1603 $file_writer_object->reset_consecutive_blank_lines();
1604 $saw_END_or_DATA_ = 1;
1605 }
1606
1607 # write unindented non-code line
1608 if ( !$skip_line ) {
1609 if ($tee_line) { $file_writer_object->tee_on() }
1610 $self->write_unindented_line($input_line);
1611 if ($tee_line) { $file_writer_object->tee_off() }
1612 }
1613 }
1614 }
1615 return;
1616}

16651200nssub write_line {
1666
1667 # We are caching tokenized lines as they arrive and converting them to the
1668 # format needed for the final formatting.
1669 my ( $self, $line_of_tokens_old ) = @_;
1670 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
1671 my $Klimit = $self->{Klimit};
1672 my $rlines_new = $self->{rlines};
1673
1674 my $Kfirst;
1675 my $line_of_tokens = {};
1676 foreach my $key (
1677 qw(
1678 _curly_brace_depth
1679 _ending_in_quote
1680 _guessed_indentation_level
1681 _line_number
1682 _line_text
1683 _line_type
1684 _paren_depth
1685 _quote_character
1686 _square_bracket_depth
1687 _starting_in_quote
1688 )
1689 )
1690 {
1691 $line_of_tokens->{$key} = $line_of_tokens_old->{$key};
1692 }
1693
1694 # Data needed by Logger
1695 $line_of_tokens->{_level_0} = 0;
1696 $line_of_tokens->{_ci_level_0} = 0;
1697 $line_of_tokens->{_nesting_blocks_0} = "";
1698 $line_of_tokens->{_nesting_tokens_0} = "";
1699
1700 # Needed to avoid trimming quotes
1701 $line_of_tokens->{_ended_in_blank_token} = undef;
1702
1703 my $line_type = $line_of_tokens_old->{_line_type};
1704 my $input_line_no = $line_of_tokens_old->{_line_number} - 1;
1705 if ( $line_type eq 'CODE' ) {
1706
1707 my $rtokens = $line_of_tokens_old->{_rtokens};
1708 my $rtoken_type = $line_of_tokens_old->{_rtoken_type};
1709 my $rblock_type = $line_of_tokens_old->{_rblock_type};
1710 my $rcontainer_type = $line_of_tokens_old->{_rcontainer_type};
1711 my $rcontainer_environment =
1712 $line_of_tokens_old->{_rcontainer_environment};
1713 my $rtype_sequence = $line_of_tokens_old->{_rtype_sequence};
1714 my $rlevels = $line_of_tokens_old->{_rlevels};
1715 my $rslevels = $line_of_tokens_old->{_rslevels};
1716 my $rci_levels = $line_of_tokens_old->{_rci_levels};
1717 my $rnesting_blocks = $line_of_tokens_old->{_rnesting_blocks};
1718 my $rnesting_tokens = $line_of_tokens_old->{_rnesting_tokens};
1719
1720 my $jmax = @{$rtokens} - 1;
1721 if ( $jmax >= 0 ) {
1722 $Kfirst = defined($Klimit) ? $Klimit + 1 : 0;
1723 foreach my $j ( 0 .. $jmax ) {
1724 my @tokary;
1725 @tokary[
1726 _TOKEN_, _TYPE_,
1727 _BLOCK_TYPE_, _CONTAINER_TYPE_,
1728 _CONTAINER_ENVIRONMENT_, _TYPE_SEQUENCE_,
1729 _LEVEL_, _LEVEL_TRUE_,
1730 _SLEVEL_, _CI_LEVEL_,
1731 _LINE_INDEX_,
1732 ]
1733 = (
1734 $rtokens->[$j], $rtoken_type->[$j],
1735 $rblock_type->[$j], $rcontainer_type->[$j],
1736 $rcontainer_environment->[$j], $rtype_sequence->[$j],
1737 $rlevels->[$j], $rlevels->[$j],
1738 $rslevels->[$j], $rci_levels->[$j],
1739 $input_line_no,
1740 );
1741 push @{$rLL}, \@tokary;
1742 }
1743
1744 $Klimit = @{$rLL} - 1;
1745
1746 # Need to remember if we can trim the input line
1747 $line_of_tokens->{_ended_in_blank_token} =
1748 $rtoken_type->[$jmax] eq 'b';
1749
1750 $line_of_tokens->{_level_0} = $rlevels->[0];
1751 $line_of_tokens->{_ci_level_0} = $rci_levels->[0];
1752 $line_of_tokens->{_nesting_blocks_0} = $rnesting_blocks->[0];
1753 $line_of_tokens->{_nesting_tokens_0} = $rnesting_tokens->[0];
1754 }
1755 }
1756
1757 $line_of_tokens->{_rK_range} = [ $Kfirst, $Klimit ];
1758 $line_of_tokens->{_code_type} = "";
1759 $self->{Klimit} = $Klimit;
1760
1761 push @{$rlines_new}, $line_of_tokens;
1762 return;
1763}
1764
1765sub initialize_whitespace_hashes {
1766
1767 # initialize these global hashes, which control the use of
1768 # whitespace around tokens:
1769 #
1770 # %binary_ws_rules
1771 # %want_left_space
1772 # %want_right_space
1773 # %space_after_keyword
1774 #
1775 # Many token types are identical to the tokens themselves.
1776 # See the tokenizer for a complete list. Here are some special types:
1777 # k = perl keyword
1778 # f = semicolon in for statement
1779 # m = unary minus
1780 # p = unary plus
1781 # Note that :: is excluded since it should be contained in an identifier
1782 # Note that '->' is excluded because it never gets space
1783 # parentheses and brackets are excluded since they are handled specially
1784 # curly braces are included but may be overridden by logic, such as
1785 # newline logic.
1786
1787 # NEW_TOKENS: create a whitespace rule here. This can be as
1788 # simple as adding your new letter to @spaces_both_sides, for
1789 # example.
1790
1791 my @opening_type = qw< L { ( [ >;
1792 @is_opening_type{@opening_type} = (1) x scalar(@opening_type);
1793
1794 my @closing_type = qw< R } ) ] >;
1795 @is_closing_type{@closing_type} = (1) x scalar(@closing_type);
1796
1797 my @spaces_both_sides = qw#
1798 + - * / % ? = . : x < > | & ^ .. << >> ** && .. || // => += -=
1799 .= %= x= &= |= ^= *= <> <= >= == =~ !~ /= != ... <<= >>= ~~ !~~
1800 &&= ||= //= <=> A k f w F n C Y U G v
1801 #;
1802
1803 my @spaces_left_side = qw<
1804 t ! ~ m p { \ h pp mm Z j
1805 >;
1806 push( @spaces_left_side, '#' ); # avoids warning message
1807
1808 my @spaces_right_side = qw<
1809 ; } ) ] R J ++ -- **=
1810 >;
1811 push( @spaces_right_side, ',' ); # avoids warning message
1812
1813 # Note that we are in a BEGIN block here. Later in processing
1814 # the values of %want_left_space and %want_right_space
1815 # may be overridden by any user settings specified by the
1816 # -wls and -wrs parameters. However the binary_whitespace_rules
1817 # are hardwired and have priority.
1818 @want_left_space{@spaces_both_sides} =
1819 (1) x scalar(@spaces_both_sides);
1820 @want_right_space{@spaces_both_sides} =
1821 (1) x scalar(@spaces_both_sides);
1822 @want_left_space{@spaces_left_side} =
1823 (1) x scalar(@spaces_left_side);
1824 @want_right_space{@spaces_left_side} =
1825 (-1) x scalar(@spaces_left_side);
1826 @want_left_space{@spaces_right_side} =
1827 (-1) x scalar(@spaces_right_side);
1828 @want_right_space{@spaces_right_side} =
1829 (1) x scalar(@spaces_right_side);
1830 $want_left_space{'->'} = WS_NO;
1831 $want_right_space{'->'} = WS_NO;
1832 $want_left_space{'**'} = WS_NO;
1833 $want_right_space{'**'} = WS_NO;
1834 $want_right_space{'CORE::'} = WS_NO;
1835
1836 # These binary_ws_rules are hardwired and have priority over the above
1837 # settings. It would be nice to allow adjustment by the user,
1838 # but it would be complicated to specify.
1839 #
1840 # hash type information must stay tightly bound
1841 # as in : ${xxxx}
1842 $binary_ws_rules{'i'}{'L'} = WS_NO;
1843 $binary_ws_rules{'i'}{'{'} = WS_YES;
1844 $binary_ws_rules{'k'}{'{'} = WS_YES;
1845 $binary_ws_rules{'U'}{'{'} = WS_YES;
1846 $binary_ws_rules{'i'}{'['} = WS_NO;
1847 $binary_ws_rules{'R'}{'L'} = WS_NO;
1848 $binary_ws_rules{'R'}{'{'} = WS_NO;
1849 $binary_ws_rules{'t'}{'L'} = WS_NO;
1850 $binary_ws_rules{'t'}{'{'} = WS_NO;
1851 $binary_ws_rules{'}'}{'L'} = WS_NO;
1852 $binary_ws_rules{'}'}{'{'} = WS_OPTIONAL; # RT#129850; was WS_NO
1853 $binary_ws_rules{'$'}{'L'} = WS_NO;
1854 $binary_ws_rules{'$'}{'{'} = WS_NO;
1855 $binary_ws_rules{'@'}{'L'} = WS_NO;
1856 $binary_ws_rules{'@'}{'{'} = WS_NO;
1857 $binary_ws_rules{'='}{'L'} = WS_YES;
1858 $binary_ws_rules{'J'}{'J'} = WS_YES;
1859
1860 # the following includes ') {'
1861 # as in : if ( xxx ) { yyy }
1862 $binary_ws_rules{']'}{'L'} = WS_NO;
1863 $binary_ws_rules{']'}{'{'} = WS_NO;
1864 $binary_ws_rules{')'}{'{'} = WS_YES;
1865 $binary_ws_rules{')'}{'['} = WS_NO;
1866 $binary_ws_rules{']'}{'['} = WS_NO;
1867 $binary_ws_rules{']'}{'{'} = WS_NO;
1868 $binary_ws_rules{'}'}{'['} = WS_NO;
1869 $binary_ws_rules{'R'}{'['} = WS_NO;
1870
1871 $binary_ws_rules{']'}{'++'} = WS_NO;
1872 $binary_ws_rules{']'}{'--'} = WS_NO;
1873 $binary_ws_rules{')'}{'++'} = WS_NO;
1874 $binary_ws_rules{')'}{'--'} = WS_NO;
1875
1876 $binary_ws_rules{'R'}{'++'} = WS_NO;
1877 $binary_ws_rules{'R'}{'--'} = WS_NO;
1878
1879 $binary_ws_rules{'i'}{'Q'} = WS_YES;
1880 $binary_ws_rules{'n'}{'('} = WS_YES; # occurs in 'use package n ()'
1881
1882 # FIXME: we could to split 'i' into variables and functions
1883 # and have no space for functions but space for variables. For now,
1884 # I have a special patch in the special rules below
1885 $binary_ws_rules{'i'}{'('} = WS_NO;
1886
1887 $binary_ws_rules{'w'}{'('} = WS_NO;
1888 $binary_ws_rules{'w'}{'{'} = WS_YES;
1889 return;
1890
1891} ## end initialize_whitespace_hashes
1892
1893sub set_whitespace_flags {
1894
1895 # This routine examines each pair of nonblank tokens and
1896 # sets a flag indicating if white space is needed.
1897 #
1898 # $rwhitespace_flags->[$j] is a flag indicating whether a white space
1899 # BEFORE token $j is needed, with the following values:
1900 #
1901 # WS_NO = -1 do not want a space before token $j
1902 # WS_OPTIONAL= 0 optional space or $j is a whitespace
1903 # WS_YES = 1 want a space before token $j
1904 #
1905
1906 my $self = shift;
1907 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
1908
1909 my $rwhitespace_flags = [];
1910
1911 my ( $last_token, $last_type, $last_block_type, $last_input_line_no,
1912 $token, $type, $block_type, $input_line_no );
1913 my $j_tight_closing_paren = -1;
1914
1915 $token = ' ';
1916 $type = 'b';
1917 $block_type = '';
1918 $input_line_no = 0;
1919 $last_token = ' ';
1920 $last_type = 'b';
1921 $last_block_type = '';
1922 $last_input_line_no = 0;
1923
1924 my $jmax = @{$rLL} - 1;
1925
1926 my ($ws);
1927
1928 # This is some logic moved to a sub to avoid deep nesting of if stmts
1929 my $ws_in_container = sub {
1930
1931 my ($j) = @_;
1932 my $ws = WS_YES;
1933 if ( $j + 1 > $jmax ) { return (WS_NO) }
1934
1935 # Patch to count '-foo' as single token so that
1936 # each of $a{-foo} and $a{foo} and $a{'foo'} do
1937 # not get spaces with default formatting.
1938 my $j_here = $j;
1939 ++$j_here
1940 if ( $token eq '-'
1941 && $last_token eq '{'
1942 && $rLL->[ $j + 1 ]->[_TYPE_] eq 'w' );
1943
1944 # $j_next is where a closing token should be if
1945 # the container has a single token
1946 if ( $j_here + 1 > $jmax ) { return (WS_NO) }
1947 my $j_next =
1948 ( $rLL->[ $j_here + 1 ]->[_TYPE_] eq 'b' )
1949 ? $j_here + 2
1950 : $j_here + 1;
1951
1952 if ( $j_next > $jmax ) { return WS_NO }
1953 my $tok_next = $rLL->[$j_next]->[_TOKEN_];
1954 my $type_next = $rLL->[$j_next]->[_TYPE_];
1955
1956 # for tightness = 1, if there is just one token
1957 # within the matching pair, we will keep it tight
1958 if (
1959 $tok_next eq $matching_token{$last_token}
1960
1961 # but watch out for this: [ [ ] (misc.t)
1962 && $last_token ne $token
1963
1964 # double diamond is usually spaced
1965 && $token ne '<<>>'
1966
1967 )
1968 {
1969
1970 # remember where to put the space for the closing paren
1971 $j_tight_closing_paren = $j_next;
1972 return (WS_NO);
1973 }
1974 return (WS_YES);
1975 };
1976
1977 # main loop over all tokens to define the whitespace flags
1978 for ( my $j = 0 ; $j <= $jmax ; $j++ ) {
1979
1980 my $rtokh = $rLL->[$j];
1981
1982 # Set a default
1983 $rwhitespace_flags->[$j] = WS_OPTIONAL;
1984
1985 if ( $rtokh->[_TYPE_] eq 'b' ) {
1986 next;
1987 }
1988
1989 # set a default value, to be changed as needed
1990 $ws = undef;
1991 $last_token = $token;
1992 $last_type = $type;
1993 $last_block_type = $block_type;
1994 $last_input_line_no = $input_line_no;
1995 $token = $rtokh->[_TOKEN_];
1996 $type = $rtokh->[_TYPE_];
1997 $block_type = $rtokh->[_BLOCK_TYPE_];
1998 $input_line_no = $rtokh->[_LINE_INDEX_];
1999
2000 #---------------------------------------------------------------
2001 # Whitespace Rules Section 1:
2002 # Handle space on the inside of opening braces.
2003 #---------------------------------------------------------------
2004
2005 # /^[L\{\(\[]$/
2006 if ( $is_opening_type{$last_type} ) {
2007
2008 $j_tight_closing_paren = -1;
2009
2010 # let us keep empty matched braces together: () {} []
2011 # except for BLOCKS
2012 if ( $token eq $matching_token{$last_token} ) {
2013 if ($block_type) {
2014 $ws = WS_YES;
2015 }
2016 else {
2017 $ws = WS_NO;
2018 }
2019 }
2020 else {
2021
2022 # we're considering the right of an opening brace
2023 # tightness = 0 means always pad inside with space
2024 # tightness = 1 means pad inside if "complex"
2025 # tightness = 2 means never pad inside with space
2026
2027 my $tightness;
2028 if ( $last_type eq '{'
2029 && $last_token eq '{'
2030 && $last_block_type )
2031 {
2032 $tightness = $rOpts_block_brace_tightness;
2033 }
2034 else { $tightness = $tightness{$last_token} }
2035
2036 #=============================================================
2037 # Patch for test problem <<snippets/fabrice_bug.in>>
2038 # We must always avoid spaces around a bare word beginning
2039 # with ^ as in:
2040 # my $before = ${^PREMATCH};
2041 # Because all of the following cause an error in perl:
2042 # my $before = ${ ^PREMATCH };
2043 # my $before = ${ ^PREMATCH};
2044 # my $before = ${^PREMATCH };
2045 # So if brace tightness flag is -bt=0 we must temporarily reset
2046 # to bt=1. Note that here we must set tightness=1 and not 2 so
2047 # that the closing space
2048 # is also avoided (via the $j_tight_closing_paren flag in coding)
2049 if ( $type eq 'w' && $token =~ /^\^/ ) { $tightness = 1 }
2050
2051 #=============================================================
2052
2053 if ( $tightness <= 0 ) {
2054 $ws = WS_YES;
2055 }
2056 elsif ( $tightness > 1 ) {
2057 $ws = WS_NO;
2058 }
2059 else {
2060 $ws = $ws_in_container->($j);
2061 }
2062 }
2063 } # end setting space flag inside opening tokens
2064 my $ws_1;
2065 $ws_1 = $ws
2066 if FORMATTER_DEBUG_FLAG_WHITE;
2067
2068 #---------------------------------------------------------------
2069 # Whitespace Rules Section 2:
2070 # Handle space on inside of closing brace pairs.
2071 #---------------------------------------------------------------
2072
2073 # /[\}\)\]R]/
2074 if ( $is_closing_type{$type} ) {
2075
2076 if ( $j == $j_tight_closing_paren ) {
2077
2078 $j_tight_closing_paren = -1;
2079 $ws = WS_NO;
2080 }
2081 else {
2082
2083 if ( !defined($ws) ) {
2084
2085 my $tightness;
2086 if ( $type eq '}' && $token eq '}' && $block_type ) {
2087 $tightness = $rOpts_block_brace_tightness;
2088 }
2089 else { $tightness = $tightness{$token} }
2090
2091 $ws = ( $tightness > 1 ) ? WS_NO : WS_YES;
2092 }
2093 }
2094 } # end setting space flag inside closing tokens
2095
2096 my $ws_2;
2097 $ws_2 = $ws
2098 if FORMATTER_DEBUG_FLAG_WHITE;
2099
2100 #---------------------------------------------------------------
2101 # Whitespace Rules Section 3:
2102 # Use the binary rule table.
2103 #---------------------------------------------------------------
2104 if ( !defined($ws) ) {
2105 $ws = $binary_ws_rules{$last_type}{$type};
2106 }
2107 my $ws_3;
2108 $ws_3 = $ws
2109 if FORMATTER_DEBUG_FLAG_WHITE;
2110
2111 #---------------------------------------------------------------
2112 # Whitespace Rules Section 4:
2113 # Handle some special cases.
2114 #---------------------------------------------------------------
2115 if ( $token eq '(' ) {
2116
2117 # This will have to be tweaked as tokenization changes.
2118 # We usually want a space at '} (', for example:
2119 # <<snippets/space1.in>>
2120 # map { 1 * $_; } ( $y, $M, $w, $d, $h, $m, $s );
2121 #
2122 # But not others:
2123 # &{ $_->[1] }( delete $_[$#_]{ $_->[0] } );
2124 # At present, the above & block is marked as type L/R so this case
2125 # won't go through here.
2126 if ( $last_type eq '}' ) { $ws = WS_YES }
2127
2128 # NOTE: some older versions of Perl had occasional problems if
2129 # spaces are introduced between keywords or functions and opening
2130 # parens. So the default is not to do this except is certain
2131 # cases. The current Perl seems to tolerate spaces.
2132
2133 # Space between keyword and '('
2134 elsif ( $last_type eq 'k' ) {
2135 $ws = WS_NO
2136 unless ( $rOpts_space_keyword_paren
2137 || $space_after_keyword{$last_token} );
2138 }
2139
2140 # Space between function and '('
2141 # -----------------------------------------------------
2142 # 'w' and 'i' checks for something like:
2143 # myfun( &myfun( ->myfun(
2144 # -----------------------------------------------------
2145 elsif (( $last_type =~ /^[wUG]$/ )
2146 || ( $last_type =~ /^[wi]$/ && $last_token =~ /^(\&|->)/ ) )
2147 {
2148 $ws = WS_NO unless ($rOpts_space_function_paren);
2149 }
2150
2151 # space between something like $i and ( in <<snippets/space2.in>>
2152 # for $i ( 0 .. 20 ) {
2153 # FIXME: eventually, type 'i' needs to be split into multiple
2154 # token types so this can be a hardwired rule.
2155 elsif ( $last_type eq 'i' && $last_token =~ /^[\$\%\@]/ ) {
2156 $ws = WS_YES;
2157 }
2158
2159 # allow constant function followed by '()' to retain no space
2160 elsif ($last_type eq 'C'
2161 && $rLL->[ $j + 1 ]->[_TOKEN_] eq ')' )
2162 {
2163 $ws = WS_NO;
2164 }
2165 }
2166
2167 # patch for SWITCH/CASE: make space at ']{' optional
2168 # since the '{' might begin a case or when block
2169 elsif ( ( $token eq '{' && $type ne 'L' ) && $last_token eq ']' ) {
2170 $ws = WS_OPTIONAL;
2171 }
2172
2173 # keep space between 'sub' and '{' for anonymous sub definition
2174 if ( $type eq '{' ) {
2175 if ( $last_token eq 'sub' ) {
2176 $ws = WS_YES;
2177 }
2178
2179 # this is needed to avoid no space in '){'
2180 if ( $last_token eq ')' && $token eq '{' ) { $ws = WS_YES }
2181
2182 # avoid any space before the brace or bracket in something like
2183 # @opts{'a','b',...}
2184 if ( $last_type eq 'i' && $last_token =~ /^\@/ ) {
2185 $ws = WS_NO;
2186 }
2187 }
2188
2189 elsif ( $type eq 'i' ) {
2190
2191 # never a space before ->
2192 if ( $token =~ /^\-\>/ ) {
2193 $ws = WS_NO;
2194 }
2195 }
2196
2197 # retain any space between '-' and bare word
2198 elsif ( $type eq 'w' || $type eq 'C' ) {
2199 $ws = WS_OPTIONAL if $last_type eq '-';
2200
2201 # never a space before ->
2202 if ( $token =~ /^\-\>/ ) {
2203 $ws = WS_NO;
2204 }
2205 }
2206
2207 # retain any space between '-' and bare word; for example
2208 # avoid space between 'USER' and '-' here: <<snippets/space2.in>>
2209 # $myhash{USER-NAME}='steve';
2210 elsif ( $type eq 'm' || $type eq '-' ) {
2211 $ws = WS_OPTIONAL if ( $last_type eq 'w' );
2212 }
2213
2214 # always space before side comment
2215 elsif ( $type eq '#' ) { $ws = WS_YES if $j > 0 }
2216
2217 # always preserver whatever space was used after a possible
2218 # filehandle (except _) or here doc operator
2219 if (
2220 $type ne '#'
2221 && ( ( $last_type eq 'Z' && $last_token ne '_' )
2222 || $last_type eq 'h' )
2223 )
2224 {
2225 $ws = WS_OPTIONAL;
2226 }
2227
2228 # space_backslash_quote; RT #123774 <<snippets/rt123774.in>>
2229 # allow a space between a backslash and single or double quote
2230 # to avoid fooling html formatters
2231 elsif ( $last_type eq '\\' && $type eq 'Q' && $token =~ /^[\"\']/ ) {
2232 if ($rOpts_space_backslash_quote) {
2233 if ( $rOpts_space_backslash_quote == 1 ) {
2234 $ws = WS_OPTIONAL;
2235 }
2236 elsif ( $rOpts_space_backslash_quote == 2 ) { $ws = WS_YES }
2237 else { } # shouldnt happen
2238 }
2239 else {
2240 $ws = WS_NO;
2241 }
2242 }
2243
2244 my $ws_4;
2245 $ws_4 = $ws
2246 if FORMATTER_DEBUG_FLAG_WHITE;
2247
2248 #---------------------------------------------------------------
2249 # Whitespace Rules Section 5:
2250 # Apply default rules not covered above.
2251 #---------------------------------------------------------------
2252
2253 # If we fall through to here, look at the pre-defined hash tables for
2254 # the two tokens, and:
2255 # if (they are equal) use the common value
2256 # if (either is zero or undef) use the other
2257 # if (either is -1) use it
2258 # That is,
2259 # left vs right
2260 # 1 vs 1 --> 1
2261 # 0 vs 0 --> 0
2262 # -1 vs -1 --> -1
2263 #
2264 # 0 vs -1 --> -1
2265 # 0 vs 1 --> 1
2266 # 1 vs 0 --> 1
2267 # -1 vs 0 --> -1
2268 #
2269 # -1 vs 1 --> -1
2270 # 1 vs -1 --> -1
2271 if ( !defined($ws) ) {
2272 my $wl = $want_left_space{$type};
2273 my $wr = $want_right_space{$last_type};
2274 if ( !defined($wl) ) { $wl = 0 }
2275 if ( !defined($wr) ) { $wr = 0 }
2276 $ws = ( ( $wl == $wr ) || ( $wl == -1 ) || !$wr ) ? $wl : $wr;
2277 }
2278
2279 if ( !defined($ws) ) {
2280 $ws = 0;
2281 write_diagnostics(
2282 "WS flag is undefined for tokens $last_token $token\n");
2283 }
2284
2285 # Treat newline as a whitespace. Otherwise, we might combine
2286 # 'Send' and '-recipients' here according to the above rules:
2287 # <<snippets/space3.in>>
2288 # my $msg = new Fax::Send
2289 # -recipients => $to,
2290 # -data => $data;
2291 if ( $ws == 0 && $input_line_no != $last_input_line_no ) { $ws = 1 }
2292
2293 if ( ( $ws == 0 )
2294 && $j > 0
2295 && $j < $jmax
2296 && ( $last_type !~ /^[Zh]$/ ) )
2297 {
2298
2299 # If this happens, we have a non-fatal but undesirable
2300 # hole in the above rules which should be patched.
2301 write_diagnostics(
2302 "WS flag is zero for tokens $last_token $token\n");
2303 }
2304
2305 $rwhitespace_flags->[$j] = $ws;
2306
2307 FORMATTER_DEBUG_FLAG_WHITE && do {
2308 my $str = substr( $last_token, 0, 15 );
2309 $str .= ' ' x ( 16 - length($str) );
2310 if ( !defined($ws_1) ) { $ws_1 = "*" }
2311 if ( !defined($ws_2) ) { $ws_2 = "*" }
2312 if ( !defined($ws_3) ) { $ws_3 = "*" }
2313 if ( !defined($ws_4) ) { $ws_4 = "*" }
2314 print STDOUT
2315"NEW WHITE: i=$j $str $last_type $type $ws_1 : $ws_2 : $ws_3 : $ws_4 : $ws \n";
2316 };
2317 } ## end main loop
2318
2319 if ( $rOpts->{'tight-secret-operators'} ) {
2320 new_secret_operator_whitespace( $rLL, $rwhitespace_flags );
2321 }
2322 return $rwhitespace_flags;
2323} ## end sub set_whitespace_flags
2324
2325sub respace_tokens {
2326
2327 my $self = shift;
2328 return if $rOpts->{'indent-only'};
2329
2330 # This routine makes all necessary changes to the tokenization after the
2331 # file has been read. This consists mostly of inserting and deleting spaces
2332 # according to the selected parameters. In a few cases non-space characters
2333 # are added, deleted or modified.
2334
2335 # The old tokens are copied one-by-one, with changes, from the old
2336 # linear storage array to a new array.
2337
2338 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
2339 my $Klimit_old = $self->{Klimit};
2340 my $rlines = $self->{rlines};
2341 my $rpaired_to_inner_container = $self->{rpaired_to_inner_container};
2342
2343 my $rLL_new = []; # This is the new array
2344 my $KK = 0;
2345 my $rtoken_vars;
2346 my $Kmax = @{$rLL} - 1;
2347
2348 # Set the whitespace flags, which indicate the token spacing preference.
2349 my $rwhitespace_flags = $self->set_whitespace_flags();
2350
2351 # we will be setting token lengths as we go
2352 my $cumulative_length = 0;
2353
2354 # We also define these hash indexes giving container token array indexes
2355 # as a function of the container sequence numbers. For example,
2356 my $K_opening_container = {}; # opening [ { or (
2357 my $K_closing_container = {}; # closing ] } or )
2358 my $K_opening_ternary = {}; # opening ? of ternary
2359 my $K_closing_ternary = {}; # closing : of ternary
2360
2361 # List of new K indexes of phantom semicolons
2362 # This will be needed if we want to undo them for iterations
2363 my $rK_phantom_semicolons = [];
2364
2365 # Temporary hashes for adding semicolons
2366 ##my $rKfirst_new = {};
2367
2368 # a sub to link preceding nodes forward to a new node type
2369 my $link_back = sub {
2370 my ( $Ktop, $key ) = @_;
2371
2372 my $Kprev = $Ktop - 1;
2373 while ( $Kprev >= 0
2374 && !defined( $rLL_new->[$Kprev]->[$key] ) )
2375 {
2376 $rLL_new->[$Kprev]->[$key] = $Ktop;
2377 $Kprev -= 1;
2378 }
2379 };
2380
2381 # A sub to store one token in the new array
2382 # All new tokens must be stored by this sub so that it can update
2383 # all data structures on the fly.
2384 my $last_nonblank_type = ';';
2385 my $store_token = sub {
2386 my ($item) = @_;
2387
2388 # This will be the index of this item in the new array
2389 my $KK_new = @{$rLL_new};
2390
2391 # check for a sequenced item (i.e., container or ?/:)
2392 my $type_sequence = $item->[_TYPE_SEQUENCE_];
2393 if ($type_sequence) {
2394
2395 $link_back->( $KK_new, _KNEXT_SEQ_ITEM_ );
2396
2397 my $token = $item->[_TOKEN_];
2398 if ( $is_opening_token{$token} ) {
2399
2400 $K_opening_container->{$type_sequence} = $KK_new;
2401 }
2402 elsif ( $is_closing_token{$token} ) {
2403
2404 $K_closing_container->{$type_sequence} = $KK_new;
2405 }
2406
2407 # These are not yet used but could be useful
2408 else {
2409 if ( $token eq '?' ) {
2410 $K_opening_ternary->{$type_sequence} = $KK_new;
2411 }
2412 elsif ( $token eq ':' ) {
2413 $K_closing_ternary->{$type_sequence} = $KK_new;
2414 }
2415 else {
2416 # shouldn't happen
2417 Fault("Ugh: shouldn't happen");
2418 }
2419 }
2420 }
2421
2422 # find the length of this token
2423 my $token_length = length( $item->[_TOKEN_] );
2424
2425 # and update the cumulative length
2426 $cumulative_length += $token_length;
2427
2428 # Save the length sum to just AFTER this token
2429 $item->[_CUMULATIVE_LENGTH_] = $cumulative_length;
2430
2431 my $type = $item->[_TYPE_];
2432 if ( $type ne 'b' ) { $last_nonblank_type = $type }
2433
2434 # and finally, add this item to the new array
2435 push @{$rLL_new}, $item;
2436 };
2437
2438 my $store_token_and_space = sub {
2439 my ( $item, $want_space ) = @_;
2440
2441 # store a token with preceding space if requested and needed
2442
2443 # First store the space
2444 if ( $want_space
2445 && @{$rLL_new}
2446 && $rLL_new->[-1]->[_TYPE_] ne 'b'
2447 && $rOpts_add_whitespace )
2448 {
2449 my $rcopy = copy_token_as_type( $item, 'b', ' ' );
2450 $rcopy->[_LINE_INDEX_] =
2451 $rLL_new->[-1]->[_LINE_INDEX_];
2452 $store_token->($rcopy);
2453 }
2454
2455 # then the token
2456 $store_token->($item);
2457 };
2458
2459 my $K_end_q = sub {
2460 my ($KK) = @_;
2461 my $K_end = $KK;
2462 my $Kn = $self->K_next_nonblank($KK);
2463 while ( defined($Kn) && $rLL->[$Kn]->[_TYPE_] eq 'q' ) {
2464 $K_end = $Kn;
2465 $Kn = $self->K_next_nonblank($Kn);
2466 }
2467 return $K_end;
2468 };
2469
2470 my $add_phantom_semicolon = sub {
2471
2472 my ($KK) = @_;
2473
2474 my $Kp = $self->K_previous_nonblank( undef, $rLL_new );
2475 return unless ( defined($Kp) );
2476
2477 # we are only adding semicolons for certain block types
2478 my $block_type = $rLL->[$KK]->[_BLOCK_TYPE_];
2479 return
2480 unless ( $ok_to_add_semicolon_for_block_type{$block_type}
2481 || $block_type =~ /^(sub|package)/
2482 || $block_type =~ /^\w+\:$/ );
2483
2484 my $type_sequence = $rLL->[$KK]->[_TYPE_SEQUENCE_];
2485
2486 my $previous_nonblank_type = $rLL_new->[$Kp]->[_TYPE_];
2487 my $previous_nonblank_token = $rLL_new->[$Kp]->[_TOKEN_];
2488
2489 # Do not add a semicolon if...
2490 return
2491 if (
2492
2493 # it would follow a comment (and be isolated)
2494 $previous_nonblank_type eq '#'
2495
2496 # it follows a code block ( because they are not always wanted
2497 # there and may add clutter)
2498 || $rLL_new->[$Kp]->[_BLOCK_TYPE_]
2499
2500 # it would follow a label
2501 || $previous_nonblank_type eq 'J'
2502
2503 # it would be inside a 'format' statement (and cause syntax error)
2504 || ( $previous_nonblank_type eq 'k'
2505 && $previous_nonblank_token =~ /format/ )
2506
2507 # if it would prevent welding two containers
2508 || $rpaired_to_inner_container->{$type_sequence}
2509
2510 );
2511
2512 # We will insert an empty semicolon here as a placeholder. Later, if
2513 # it becomes the last token on a line, we will bring it to life. The
2514 # advantage of doing this is that (1) we just have to check line
2515 # endings, and (2) the phantom semicolon has zero width and therefore
2516 # won't cause needless breaks of one-line blocks.
2517 my $Ktop = -1;
2518 if ( $rLL_new->[$Ktop]->[_TYPE_] eq 'b'
2519 && $want_left_space{';'} == WS_NO )
2520 {
2521
2522 # convert the blank into a semicolon..
2523 # be careful: we are working on the new stack top
2524 # on a token which has been stored.
2525 my $rcopy = copy_token_as_type( $rLL_new->[$Ktop], 'b', ' ' );
2526
2527 # Convert the existing blank to:
2528 # a phantom semicolon for one_line_block option = 0 or 1
2529 # a real semicolon for one_line_block option = 2
2530 my $tok = $rOpts_one_line_block_semicolons == 2 ? ';' : '';
2531
2532 $rLL_new->[$Ktop]->[_TOKEN_] = $tok; # zero length if phantom
2533 $rLL_new->[$Ktop]->[_TYPE_] = ';';
2534 $rLL_new->[$Ktop]->[_SLEVEL_] =
2535 $rLL->[$KK]->[_SLEVEL_];
2536
2537 push @{$rK_phantom_semicolons}, @{$rLL_new} - 1;
2538
2539 # Then store a new blank
2540 $store_token->($rcopy);
2541 }
2542 else {
2543
2544 # insert a new token
2545 my $rcopy = copy_token_as_type( $rLL_new->[$Kp], ';', '' );
2546 $rcopy->[_SLEVEL_] = $rLL->[$KK]->[_SLEVEL_];
2547 $store_token->($rcopy);
2548 push @{$rK_phantom_semicolons}, @{$rLL_new} - 1;
2549 }
2550 };
2551
2552 my $check_Q = sub {
2553
2554 # Check that a quote looks okay
2555 # This sub works but needs to by sync'd with the log file output
2556 # before it can be used.
2557 my ( $KK, $Kfirst ) = @_;
2558 my $token = $rLL->[$KK]->[_TOKEN_];
2559 note_embedded_tab() if ( $token =~ "\t" );
2560
2561 my $Kp = $self->K_previous_nonblank( undef, $rLL_new );
2562 return unless ( defined($Kp) );
2563 my $previous_nonblank_type = $rLL_new->[$Kp]->[_TYPE_];
2564 my $previous_nonblank_token = $rLL_new->[$Kp]->[_TOKEN_];
2565
2566 my $previous_nonblank_type_2 = 'b';
2567 my $previous_nonblank_token_2 = "";
2568 my $Kpp = $self->K_previous_nonblank( $Kp, $rLL_new );
2569 if ( defined($Kpp) ) {
2570 $previous_nonblank_type_2 = $rLL_new->[$Kpp]->[_TYPE_];
2571 $previous_nonblank_token_2 = $rLL_new->[$Kpp]->[_TOKEN_];
2572 }
2573
2574 my $Kn = $self->K_next_nonblank($KK);
2575 my $next_nonblank_token = "";
2576 if ( defined($Kn) ) {
2577 $next_nonblank_token = $rLL->[$Kn]->[_TOKEN_];
2578 }
2579
2580 my $token_0 = $rLL->[$Kfirst]->[_TOKEN_];
2581 my $type_0 = $rLL->[$Kfirst]->[_TYPE_];
2582
2583 # make note of something like '$var = s/xxx/yyy/;'
2584 # in case it should have been '$var =~ s/xxx/yyy/;'
2585 if (
2586 $token =~ /^(s|tr|y|m|\/)/
2587 && $previous_nonblank_token =~ /^(=|==|!=)$/
2588
2589 # preceded by simple scalar
2590 && $previous_nonblank_type_2 eq 'i'
2591 && $previous_nonblank_token_2 =~ /^\$/
2592
2593 # followed by some kind of termination
2594 # (but give complaint if we can not see far enough ahead)
2595 && $next_nonblank_token =~ /^[; \)\}]$/
2596
2597 # scalar is not declared
2598 && !( $type_0 eq 'k' && $token_0 =~ /^(my|our|local)$/ )
2599 )
2600 {
2601 my $guess = substr( $last_nonblank_token, 0, 1 ) . '~';
2602 complain(
2603"Note: be sure you want '$previous_nonblank_token' instead of '$guess' here\n"
2604 );
2605 }
2606 };
2607
2608 # Main loop over all lines of the file
2609 my $last_K_out;
2610 my $CODE_type = "";
2611 my $line_type = "";
2612
2613 # Testing option to break qw. Do not use; it can make a mess.
2614 my $ALLOW_BREAK_MULTILINE_QW = 0;
2615 my $in_multiline_qw;
2616 foreach my $line_of_tokens ( @{$rlines} ) {
2617
2618 $input_line_number = $line_of_tokens->{_line_number};
2619 my $last_line_type = $line_type;
2620 $line_type = $line_of_tokens->{_line_type};
2621 next unless ( $line_type eq 'CODE' );
2622 my $last_CODE_type = $CODE_type;
2623 $CODE_type = $line_of_tokens->{_code_type};
2624 my $rK_range = $line_of_tokens->{_rK_range};
2625 my ( $Kfirst, $Klast ) = @{$rK_range};
2626 next unless defined($Kfirst);
2627
2628 # Check for correct sequence of token indexes...
2629 # An error here means that sub write_line() did not correctly
2630 # package the tokenized lines as it received them.
2631 if ( defined($last_K_out) ) {
2632 if ( $Kfirst != $last_K_out + 1 ) {
2633 Fault(
2634 "Program Bug: last K out was $last_K_out but Kfirst=$Kfirst"
2635 );
2636 }
2637 }
2638 else {
2639 if ( $Kfirst != 0 ) {
2640 Fault("Program Bug: first K is $Kfirst but should be 0");
2641 }
2642 }
2643 $last_K_out = $Klast;
2644
2645 # Handle special lines of code
2646 if ( $CODE_type && $CODE_type ne 'NIN' && $CODE_type ne 'VER' ) {
2647
2648 # CODE_types are as follows.
2649 # 'BL' = Blank Line
2650 # 'VB' = Verbatim - line goes out verbatim
2651 # 'FS' = Format Skipping - line goes out verbatim, no blanks
2652 # 'IO' = Indent Only - only indentation may be changed
2653 # 'NIN' = No Internal Newlines - line does not get broken
2654 # 'HSC'=Hanging Side Comment - fix this hanging side comment
2655 # 'BC'=Block Comment - an ordinary full line comment
2656 # 'SBC'=Static Block Comment - a block comment which does not get
2657 # indented
2658 # 'SBCX'=Static Block Comment Without Leading Space
2659 # 'DEL'=Delete this line
2660 # 'VER'=VERSION statement
2661 # '' or (undefined) - no restructions
2662
2663 # For a hanging side comment we insert an empty quote before
2664 # the comment so that it becomes a normal side comment and
2665 # will be aligned by the vertical aligner
2666 if ( $CODE_type eq 'HSC' ) {
2667
2668 # Safety Check: This must be a line with one token (a comment)
2669 my $rtoken_vars = $rLL->[$Kfirst];
2670 if ( $Kfirst == $Klast && $rtoken_vars->[_TYPE_] eq '#' ) {
2671
2672 # Note that even if the flag 'noadd-whitespace' is set, we
2673 # will make an exception here and allow a blank to be
2674 # inserted to push the comment to the right. We can think
2675 # of this as an adjustment of indentation rather than
2676 # whitespace between tokens. This will also prevent the
2677 # hanging side comment from getting converted to a block
2678 # comment if whitespace gets deleted, as for example with
2679 # the -extrude and -mangle options.
2680 my $rcopy = copy_token_as_type( $rtoken_vars, 'q', '' );
2681 $store_token->($rcopy);
2682 $rcopy = copy_token_as_type( $rtoken_vars, 'b', ' ' );
2683 $store_token->($rcopy);
2684 $store_token->($rtoken_vars);
2685 next;
2686 }
2687 else {
2688
2689 # This line was mis-marked by sub scan_comment
2690 Fault(
2691 "Program bug. A hanging side comment has been mismarked"
2692 );
2693 }
2694 }
2695
2696 # Copy tokens unchanged
2697 foreach my $KK ( $Kfirst .. $Klast ) {
2698 $store_token->( $rLL->[$KK] );
2699 }
2700 next;
2701 }
2702
2703 # Handle normal line..
2704
2705 # Insert any essential whitespace between lines
2706 # if last line was normal CODE.
2707 # Patch for rt #125012: use K_previous_code rather than '_nonblank'
2708 # because comments may disappear.
2709 my $type_next = $rLL->[$Kfirst]->[_TYPE_];
2710 my $token_next = $rLL->[$Kfirst]->[_TOKEN_];
2711 my $Kp = $self->K_previous_code( undef, $rLL_new );
2712 if ( $last_line_type eq 'CODE'
2713 && $type_next ne 'b'
2714 && defined($Kp) )
2715 {
2716 my $token_p = $rLL_new->[$Kp]->[_TOKEN_];
2717 my $type_p = $rLL_new->[$Kp]->[_TYPE_];
2718
2719 my ( $token_pp, $type_pp );
2720 my $Kpp = $self->K_previous_code( $Kp, $rLL_new );
2721 if ( defined($Kpp) ) {
2722 $token_pp = $rLL_new->[$Kpp]->[_TOKEN_];
2723 $type_pp = $rLL_new->[$Kpp]->[_TYPE_];
2724 }
2725 else {
2726 $token_pp = ";";
2727 $type_pp = ';';
2728 }
2729
2730 if (
2731 is_essential_whitespace(
2732 $token_pp, $type_pp, $token_p,
2733 $type_p, $token_next, $type_next,
2734 )
2735 )
2736 {
2737
2738 # Copy this first token as blank, but use previous line number
2739 my $rcopy = copy_token_as_type( $rLL->[$Kfirst], 'b', ' ' );
2740 $rcopy->[_LINE_INDEX_] =
2741 $rLL_new->[-1]->[_LINE_INDEX_];
2742 $store_token->($rcopy);
2743 }
2744 }
2745
2746 # loop to copy all tokens on this line, with any changes
2747 my $type_sequence;
2748 for ( my $KK = $Kfirst ; $KK <= $Klast ; $KK++ ) {
2749 $rtoken_vars = $rLL->[$KK];
2750 my $token = $rtoken_vars->[_TOKEN_];
2751 my $type = $rtoken_vars->[_TYPE_];
2752 my $last_type_sequence = $type_sequence;
2753 $type_sequence = $rtoken_vars->[_TYPE_SEQUENCE_];
2754
2755 # Handle a blank space ...
2756 if ( $type eq 'b' ) {
2757
2758 # Delete it if not wanted by whitespace rules
2759 # or we are deleting all whitespace
2760 # Note that whitespace flag is a flag indicating whether a
2761 # white space BEFORE the token is needed
2762 next if ( $KK >= $Kmax ); # skip terminal blank
2763 my $Knext = $KK + 1;
2764 my $ws = $rwhitespace_flags->[$Knext];
2765 if ( $ws == -1
2766 || $rOpts_delete_old_whitespace )
2767 {
2768
2769 # FIXME: maybe switch to using _new
2770 my $Kp = $self->K_previous_nonblank($KK);
2771 next unless defined($Kp);
2772 my $token_p = $rLL->[$Kp]->[_TOKEN_];
2773 my $type_p = $rLL->[$Kp]->[_TYPE_];
2774
2775 my ( $token_pp, $type_pp );
2776
2777 #my $Kpp = $K_previous_nonblank->($Kp);
2778 my $Kpp = $self->K_previous_nonblank($Kp);
2779 if ( defined($Kpp) ) {
2780 $token_pp = $rLL->[$Kpp]->[_TOKEN_];
2781 $type_pp = $rLL->[$Kpp]->[_TYPE_];
2782 }
2783 else {
2784 $token_pp = ";";
2785 $type_pp = ';';
2786 }
2787 my $token_next = $rLL->[$Knext]->[_TOKEN_];
2788 my $type_next = $rLL->[$Knext]->[_TYPE_];
2789
2790 my $do_not_delete = is_essential_whitespace(
2791 $token_pp, $type_pp, $token_p,
2792 $type_p, $token_next, $type_next,
2793 );
2794
2795 next unless ($do_not_delete);
2796 }
2797
2798 # make it just one character if allowed
2799 if ($rOpts_add_whitespace) {
2800 $rtoken_vars->[_TOKEN_] = ' ';
2801 }
2802 $store_token->($rtoken_vars);
2803 next;
2804 }
2805
2806 # Handle a nonblank token...
2807
2808 # check for a qw quote
2809 if ( $type eq 'q' ) {
2810
2811 # trim blanks from right of qw quotes
2812 # (To avoid trimming qw quotes use -ntqw; the tokenizer handles
2813 # this)
2814 $token =~ s/\s*$//;
2815 $rtoken_vars->[_TOKEN_] = $token;
2816 note_embedded_tab() if ( $token =~ "\t" );
2817
2818 if ($in_multiline_qw) {
2819
2820 # If we are at the end of a multiline qw ..
2821 if ( $in_multiline_qw == $KK ) {
2822
2823 # Split off the closing delimiter character
2824 # so that the formatter can put a line break there if necessary
2825 my $part1 = $token;
2826 my $part2 = substr( $part1, -1, 1, "" );
2827
2828 if ($part1) {
2829 my $rcopy =
2830 copy_token_as_type( $rtoken_vars, 'q', $part1 );
2831 $store_token->($rcopy);
2832 $token = $part2;
2833 $rtoken_vars->[_TOKEN_] = $token;
2834
2835 }
2836 $in_multiline_qw = undef;
2837
2838 # store without preceding blank
2839 $store_token->($rtoken_vars);
2840 next;
2841 }
2842 else {
2843 # continuing a multiline qw
2844 $store_token->($rtoken_vars);
2845 next;
2846 }
2847 }
2848
2849 else {
2850
2851 # we are encountered new qw token...see if multiline
2852 my $K_end = $K_end_q->($KK);
2853 if ( $ALLOW_BREAK_MULTILINE_QW && $K_end != $KK ) {
2854
2855 # Starting multiline qw...
2856 # set flag equal to the ending K
2857 $in_multiline_qw = $K_end;
2858
2859 # Split off the leading part
2860 # so that the formatter can put a line break there if necessary
2861 if ( $token =~ /^(qw\s*.)(.*)$/ ) {
2862 my $part1 = $1;
2863 my $part2 = $2;
2864 if ($part2) {
2865 my $rcopy =
2866 copy_token_as_type( $rtoken_vars, 'q',
2867 $part1 );
2868 $store_token_and_space->(
2869 $rcopy, $rwhitespace_flags->[$KK] == WS_YES
2870 );
2871 $token = $part2;
2872 $rtoken_vars->[_TOKEN_] = $token;
2873
2874 # Second part goes without intermediate blank
2875 $store_token->($rtoken_vars);
2876 next;
2877 }
2878 }
2879 }
2880 else {
2881
2882 # this is a new single token qw -
2883 # store with possible preceding blank
2884 $store_token_and_space->(
2885 $rtoken_vars, $rwhitespace_flags->[$KK] == WS_YES
2886 );
2887 next;
2888 }
2889 }
2890 } ## end if ( $type eq 'q' )
2891
2892 # Modify certain tokens here for whitespace
2893 # The following is not yet done, but could be:
2894 # sub (x x x)
2895 elsif ( $type =~ /^[wit]$/ ) {
2896
2897 # Examples: <<snippets/space1.in>>
2898 # change '$ var' to '$var' etc
2899 # '-> new' to '->new'
2900 if ( $token =~ /^([\$\&\%\*\@]|\-\>)\s/ ) {
2901 $token =~ s/\s*//g;
2902 $rtoken_vars->[_TOKEN_] = $token;
2903 }
2904
2905 # Split identifiers with leading arrows, inserting blanks if
2906 # necessary. It is easier and safer here than in the
2907 # tokenizer. For example '->new' becomes two tokens, '->' and
2908 # 'new' with a possible blank between.
2909 #
2910 # Note: there is a related patch in sub set_whitespace_flags
2911 if ( $token =~ /^\-\>(.*)$/ && $1 ) {
2912 my $token_save = $1;
2913 my $type_save = $type;
2914
2915 # store a blank to left of arrow if necessary
2916 my $Kprev = $self->K_previous_nonblank($KK);
2917 if ( defined($Kprev)
2918 && $rLL->[$Kprev]->[_TYPE_] ne 'b'
2919 && $rOpts_add_whitespace
2920 && $want_left_space{'->'} == WS_YES )
2921 {
2922 my $rcopy =
2923 copy_token_as_type( $rtoken_vars, 'b', ' ' );
2924 $store_token->($rcopy);
2925 }
2926
2927 # then store the arrow
2928 my $rcopy = copy_token_as_type( $rtoken_vars, '->', '->' );
2929 $store_token->($rcopy);
2930
2931 # then reset the current token to be the remainder,
2932 # and reset the whitespace flag according to the arrow
2933 $token = $rtoken_vars->[_TOKEN_] = $token_save;
2934 $type = $rtoken_vars->[_TYPE_] = $type_save;
2935 $store_token->($rtoken_vars);
2936 next;
2937 }
2938
2939 if ( $token =~ /$SUB_PATTERN/ ) {
2940 $token =~ s/\s+/ /g;
2941 $rtoken_vars->[_TOKEN_] = $token;
2942 }
2943
2944 # trim identifiers of trailing blanks which can occur
2945 # under some unusual circumstances, such as if the
2946 # identifier 'witch' has trailing blanks on input here:
2947 #
2948 # sub
2949 # witch
2950 # () # prototype may be on new line ...
2951 # ...
2952 if ( $type eq 'i' ) {
2953 $token =~ s/\s+$//g;
2954 $rtoken_vars->[_TOKEN_] = $token;
2955 }
2956 }
2957
2958 # change 'LABEL :' to 'LABEL:'
2959 elsif ( $type eq 'J' ) {
2960 $token =~ s/\s+//g;
2961 $rtoken_vars->[_TOKEN_] = $token;
2962 }
2963
2964 # patch to add space to something like "x10"
2965 # This avoids having to split this token in the pre-tokenizer
2966 elsif ( $type eq 'n' ) {
2967 if ( $token =~ /^x\d+/ ) {
2968 $token =~ s/x/x /;
2969 $rtoken_vars->[_TOKEN_] = $token;
2970 }
2971 }
2972
2973 # check a quote for problems
2974 elsif ( $type eq 'Q' ) {
2975
2976 # This is ready to go but is commented out because there is
2977 # still identical logic in sub break_lines.
2978 # $check_Q->($KK, $Kfirst);
2979 }
2980
2981 elsif ($type_sequence) {
2982
2983 # if ( $is_opening_token{$token} ) {
2984 # }
2985
2986 if ( $is_closing_token{$token} ) {
2987
2988 # Insert a tentative missing semicolon if the next token is
2989 # a closing block brace
2990 if (
2991 $type eq '}'
2992 && $token eq '}'
2993
2994 # not preceded by a ';'
2995 && $last_nonblank_type ne ';'
2996
2997 # and this is not a VERSION stmt (is all one line, we are not
2998 # inserting semicolons on one-line blocks)
2999 && $CODE_type ne 'VER'
3000
3001 # and we are allowed to add semicolons
3002 && $rOpts->{'add-semicolons'}
3003 )
3004 {
3005 $add_phantom_semicolon->($KK);
3006 }
3007 }
3008 }
3009
3010 # Store this token with possible previous blank
3011 $store_token_and_space->(
3012 $rtoken_vars, $rwhitespace_flags->[$KK] == WS_YES
3013 );
3014
3015 } # End token loop
3016 } # End line loop
3017
3018 # Reset memory to be the new array
3019 $self->{rLL} = $rLL_new;
3020 $self->set_rLL_max_index();
3021 $self->{K_opening_container} = $K_opening_container;
3022 $self->{K_closing_container} = $K_closing_container;
3023 $self->{K_opening_ternary} = $K_opening_ternary;
3024 $self->{K_closing_ternary} = $K_closing_ternary;
3025 $self->{rK_phantom_semicolons} = $rK_phantom_semicolons;
3026
3027 # make sure the new array looks okay
3028 $self->check_token_array();
3029
3030 # reset the token limits of each line
3031 $self->resync_lines_and_tokens();
3032
3033 return;
3034}

3036{ # scan_comments
3037
30381200ns my $Last_line_had_side_comment;
3039 my $In_format_skipping_section;
30401200ns my $Saw_VERSION_in_this_file;
3041
3042 sub scan_comments {
3043 my $self = shift;
3044 my $rlines = $self->{rlines};
3045
3046 $Last_line_had_side_comment = undef;
3047 $In_format_skipping_section = undef;
3048 $Saw_VERSION_in_this_file = undef;
3049
3050 # Loop over all lines
3051 foreach my $line_of_tokens ( @{$rlines} ) {
3052 my $line_type = $line_of_tokens->{_line_type};
3053 next unless ( $line_type eq 'CODE' );
3054 my $CODE_type = $self->get_CODE_type($line_of_tokens);
3055 $line_of_tokens->{_code_type} = $CODE_type;
3056 }
3057 return;
3058 }
3059
3060 sub get_CODE_type {
3061 my ( $self, $line_of_tokens ) = @_;
3062
3063 # We are looking at a line of code and setting a flag to
3064 # describe any special processing that it requires
3065
3066 # Possible CODE_types are as follows.
3067 # 'BL' = Blank Line
3068 # 'VB' = Verbatim - line goes out verbatim
3069 # 'IO' = Indent Only - line goes out unchanged except for indentation
3070 # 'NIN' = No Internal Newlines - line does not get broken
3071 # 'HSC'=Hanging Side Comment - fix this hanging side comment
3072 # 'BC'=Block Comment - an ordinary full line comment
3073 # 'SBC'=Static Block Comment - a block comment which does not get
3074 # indented
3075 # 'SBCX'=Static Block Comment Without Leading Space
3076 # 'DEL'=Delete this line
3077 # 'VER'=VERSION statement
3078 # '' or (undefined) - no restructions
3079
3080 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
3081 my $Klimit = $self->{Klimit};
3082
3083 my $CODE_type = $rOpts->{'indent-only'} ? 'IO' : "";
3084 my $no_internal_newlines = 1 - $rOpts_add_newlines;
3085 if ( !$CODE_type && $no_internal_newlines ) { $CODE_type = 'NIN' }
3086
3087 # extract what we need for this line..
3088
3089 # Global value for error messages:
3090 $input_line_number = $line_of_tokens->{_line_number};
3091
3092 my $rK_range = $line_of_tokens->{_rK_range};
3093 my ( $Kfirst, $Klast ) = @{$rK_range};
3094 my $jmax = -1;
3095 if ( defined($Kfirst) ) { $jmax = $Klast - $Kfirst }
3096 my $input_line = $line_of_tokens->{_line_text};
3097 my $in_continued_quote = my $starting_in_quote =
3098 $line_of_tokens->{_starting_in_quote};
3099 my $in_quote = $line_of_tokens->{_ending_in_quote};
3100 my $ending_in_quote = $in_quote;
3101 my $guessed_indentation_level =
3102 $line_of_tokens->{_guessed_indentation_level};
3103
3104 my $is_static_block_comment = 0;
3105
3106 # Handle a continued quote..
3107 if ($in_continued_quote) {
3108
3109 # A line which is entirely a quote or pattern must go out
3110 # verbatim. Note: the \n is contained in $input_line.
3111 if ( $jmax <= 0 ) {
3112 if ( ( $input_line =~ "\t" ) ) {
3113 note_embedded_tab();
3114 }
3115 $Last_line_had_side_comment = 0;
3116 return 'VB';
3117 }
3118 }
3119
3120 my $is_block_comment =
3121 ( $jmax == 0 && $rLL->[$Kfirst]->[_TYPE_] eq '#' );
3122
3123 # Write line verbatim if we are in a formatting skip section
3124 if ($In_format_skipping_section) {
3125 $Last_line_had_side_comment = 0;
3126
3127 # Note: extra space appended to comment simplifies pattern matching
3128 if ( $is_block_comment
3129 && ( $rLL->[$Kfirst]->[_TOKEN_] . " " ) =~
3130 /$format_skipping_pattern_end/o )
3131 {
3132 $In_format_skipping_section = 0;
3133 write_logfile_entry("Exiting formatting skip section\n");
3134 }
3135 return 'FS';
3136 }
3137
3138 # See if we are entering a formatting skip section
3139 if ( $rOpts_format_skipping
3140 && $is_block_comment
3141 && ( $rLL->[$Kfirst]->[_TOKEN_] . " " ) =~
3142 /$format_skipping_pattern_begin/o )
3143 {
3144 $In_format_skipping_section = 1;
3145 write_logfile_entry("Entering formatting skip section\n");
3146 $Last_line_had_side_comment = 0;
3147 return 'FS';
3148 }
3149
3150 # ignore trailing blank tokens (they will get deleted later)
3151 if ( $jmax > 0 && $rLL->[$Klast]->[_TYPE_] eq 'b' ) {
3152 $jmax--;
3153 }
3154
3155 # Handle a blank line..
3156 if ( $jmax < 0 ) {
3157 $Last_line_had_side_comment = 0;
3158 return 'BL';
3159 }
3160
3161 # see if this is a static block comment (starts with ## by default)
3162 my $is_static_block_comment_without_leading_space = 0;
3163 if ( $is_block_comment
3164 && $rOpts->{'static-block-comments'}
3165 && $input_line =~ /$static_block_comment_pattern/o )
3166 {
3167 $is_static_block_comment = 1;
3168 $is_static_block_comment_without_leading_space =
3169 substr( $input_line, 0, 1 ) eq '#';
3170 }
3171
3172 # Check for comments which are line directives
3173 # Treat exactly as static block comments without leading space
3174 # reference: perlsyn, near end, section Plain Old Comments (Not!)
3175 # example: '# line 42 "new_filename.plx"'
3176 if (
3177 $is_block_comment
3178 && $input_line =~ /^\# \s*
3179 line \s+ (\d+) \s*
3180 (?:\s("?)([^"]+)\2)? \s*
3181 $/x
3182 )
3183 {
3184 $is_static_block_comment = 1;
3185 $is_static_block_comment_without_leading_space = 1;
3186 }
3187
3188 # look for hanging side comment
3189 if (
3190 $is_block_comment
3191 && $Last_line_had_side_comment # last line had side comment
3192 && $input_line =~ /^\s/ # there is some leading space
3193 && !$is_static_block_comment # do not make static comment hanging
3194 && $rOpts->{'hanging-side-comments'} # user is allowing
3195 # hanging side comments
3196 # like this
3197 )
3198 {
3199 $Last_line_had_side_comment = 1;
3200 return 'HSC';
3201 }
3202
3203 # remember if this line has a side comment
3204 $Last_line_had_side_comment =
3205 ( $jmax > 0 && $rLL->[$Klast]->[_TYPE_] eq '#' );
3206
3207 # Handle a block (full-line) comment..
3208 if ($is_block_comment) {
3209
3210 if ( $rOpts->{'delete-block-comments'} ) { return 'DEL' }
3211
3212 # TRIM COMMENTS -- This could be turned off as a option
3213 $rLL->[$Kfirst]->[_TOKEN_] =~ s/\s*$//; # trim right end
3214
3215 if ($is_static_block_comment_without_leading_space) {
3216 return 'SBCX';
3217 }
3218 elsif ($is_static_block_comment) {
3219 return 'SBC';
3220 }
3221 else {
3222 return 'BC';
3223 }
3224 }
3225
3226=pod
3227 # NOTE: This does not work yet. Version in print-line-of-tokens
3228 # is Still used until fixed
3229
3230 # compare input/output indentation except for continuation lines
3231 # (because they have an unknown amount of initial blank space)
3232 # and lines which are quotes (because they may have been outdented)
3233 # Note: this test is placed here because we know the continuation flag
3234 # at this point, which allows us to avoid non-meaningful checks.
3235 my $structural_indentation_level = $rLL->[$Kfirst]->[_LEVEL_];
3236 compare_indentation_levels( $guessed_indentation_level,
3237 $structural_indentation_level )
3238 unless ( $rLL->[$Kfirst]->[_CI_LEVEL_] > 0
3239 || $guessed_indentation_level == 0
3240 && $rLL->[$Kfirst]->[_TYPE_] eq 'Q' );
3241=cut
3242
3243 # Patch needed for MakeMaker. Do not break a statement
3244 # in which $VERSION may be calculated. See MakeMaker.pm;
3245 # this is based on the coding in it.
3246 # The first line of a file that matches this will be eval'd:
3247 # /([\$*])(([\w\:\']*)\bVERSION)\b.*\=/
3248 # Examples:
3249 # *VERSION = \'1.01';
3250 # ( $VERSION ) = '$Revision: 1.74 $ ' =~ /\$Revision:\s+([^\s]+)/;
3251 # We will pass such a line straight through without breaking
3252 # it unless -npvl is used.
3253
3254 # Patch for problem reported in RT #81866, where files
3255 # had been flattened into a single line and couldn't be
3256 # tidied without -npvl. There are two parts to this patch:
3257 # First, it is not done for a really long line (80 tokens for now).
3258 # Second, we will only allow up to one semicolon
3259 # before the VERSION. We need to allow at least one semicolon
3260 # for statements like this:
3261 # require Exporter; our $VERSION = $Exporter::VERSION;
3262 # where both statements must be on a single line for MakeMaker
3263
3264 my $is_VERSION_statement = 0;
3265 if ( !$Saw_VERSION_in_this_file
3266 && $jmax < 80
3267 && $input_line =~
3268 /^[^;]*;?[^;]*([\$*])(([\w\:\']*)\bVERSION)\b.*\=/ )
3269 {
3270 $Saw_VERSION_in_this_file = 1;
3271 write_logfile_entry("passing VERSION line; -npvl deactivates\n");
3272 $CODE_type = 'VER';
3273 }
3274 return $CODE_type;
3275 }
3276}

32781100nssub find_nested_pairs {
3279 my $self = shift;
3280
3281 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
3282 return unless ( defined($rLL) && @{$rLL} );
3283
3284 # We define an array of pairs of nested containers
3285 my @nested_pairs;
3286
3287 # We also set the following hash values to identify container pairs for
3288 # which the opening and closing tokens are adjacent in the token stream:
3289 # $rpaired_to_inner_container->{$seqno_out}=$seqno_in where $seqno_out and
3290 # $seqno_in are the seqence numbers of the outer and inner containers of
3291 # the pair We need these later to decide if we can insert a missing
3292 # semicolon
3293 my $rpaired_to_inner_container = {};
3294
3295 # This local hash remembers if an outer container has a close following
3296 # inner container;
3297 # The key is the outer sequence number
3298 # The value is the token_hash of the inner container
3299
3300 my %has_close_following_opening;
3301
3302 # Names of calling routines can either be marked as 'i' or 'w',
3303 # and they may invoke a sub call with an '->'. We will consider
3304 # any consecutive string of such types as a single unit when making
3305 # weld decisions. We also allow a leading !
3306 my $is_name_type = {
3307 'i' => 1,
3308 'w' => 1,
3309 'U' => 1,
3310 '->' => 1,
3311 '!' => 1,
3312 };
3313
3314 my $is_name = sub {
3315 my $type = shift;
3316 return $type && $is_name_type->{$type};
3317 };
3318
3319 my $last_container;
3320 my $last_last_container;
3321 my $last_nonblank_token_vars;
3322 my $last_count;
3323
3324 my $nonblank_token_count = 0;
3325
3326 # loop over all tokens
3327 foreach my $rtoken_vars ( @{$rLL} ) {
3328
3329 my $type = $rtoken_vars->[_TYPE_];
3330
3331 next if ( $type eq 'b' );
3332
3333 # long identifier-like items are counted as a single item
3334 $nonblank_token_count++
3335 unless ( $is_name->($type)
3336 && $is_name->( $last_nonblank_token_vars->[_TYPE_] ) );
3337
3338 my $type_sequence = $rtoken_vars->[_TYPE_SEQUENCE_];
3339 if ($type_sequence) {
3340
3341 my $token = $rtoken_vars->[_TOKEN_];
3342
3343 if ( $is_opening_token{$token} ) {
3344
3345 # following previous opening token ...
3346 if ( $last_container
3347 && $is_opening_token{ $last_container->[_TOKEN_] } )
3348 {
3349
3350 # adjacent to this one
3351 my $tok_diff = $nonblank_token_count - $last_count;
3352
3353 my $last_tok = $last_nonblank_token_vars->[_TOKEN_];
3354
3355 if ( $tok_diff == 1
3356 || $tok_diff == 2 && $last_container->[_TOKEN_] eq '(' )
3357 {
3358
3359 # remember this pair...
3360 my $outer_seqno = $last_container->[_TYPE_SEQUENCE_];
3361 my $inner_seqno = $type_sequence;
3362 $has_close_following_opening{$outer_seqno} =
3363 $rtoken_vars;
3364 }
3365 }
3366 }
3367
3368 elsif ( $is_closing_token{$token} ) {
3369
3370 # if the corresponding opening token had an adjacent opening
3371 if ( $has_close_following_opening{$type_sequence}
3372 && $is_closing_token{ $last_container->[_TOKEN_] }
3373 && $has_close_following_opening{$type_sequence}
3374 ->[_TYPE_SEQUENCE_] == $last_container->[_TYPE_SEQUENCE_] )
3375 {
3376
3377 # The closing weld tokens must be adjacent
3378 # NOTE: so intermediate commas and semicolons
3379 # can currently block a weld. This is something
3380 # that could be fixed in the future by including
3381 # a flag to delete un-necessary commas and semicolons.
3382 my $tok_diff = $nonblank_token_count - $last_count;
3383
3384 if ( $tok_diff == 1 ) {
3385
3386 # This is a closely nested pair ..
3387 my $inner_seqno = $last_container->[_TYPE_SEQUENCE_];
3388 my $outer_seqno = $type_sequence;
3389 $rpaired_to_inner_container->{$outer_seqno} =
3390 $inner_seqno;
3391
3392 push @nested_pairs, [ $inner_seqno, $outer_seqno ];
3393 }
3394 }
3395 }
3396
3397 $last_last_container = $last_container;
3398 $last_container = $rtoken_vars;
3399 $last_count = $nonblank_token_count;
3400 }
3401 $last_nonblank_token_vars = $rtoken_vars;
3402 }
3403 $self->{rnested_pairs} = \@nested_pairs;
3404 $self->{rpaired_to_inner_container} = $rpaired_to_inner_container;
3405 return;
3406}

3441sub K_next_code {
3442 my ( $self, $KK, $rLL ) = @_;
3443
3444 # return the index K of the next nonblank, non-comment token
3445 return unless ( defined($KK) && $KK >= 0 );
3446
3447 # use the standard array unless given otherwise
3448 $rLL = $self->{rLL} unless ( defined($rLL) );
3449 my $Num = @{$rLL};
3450 my $Knnb = $KK + 1;
3451 while ( $Knnb < $Num ) {
3452 if ( !defined( $rLL->[$Knnb] ) ) {
3453 Fault("Undefined entry for k=$Knnb");
3454 }
3455 if ( $rLL->[$Knnb]->[_TYPE_] ne 'b'
3456 && $rLL->[$Knnb]->[_TYPE_] ne '#' )
3457 {
3458 return $Knnb;
3459 }
3460 $Knnb++;
3461 }
3462 return;
3463}
3464
3465sub K_next_nonblank {
3466 my ( $self, $KK, $rLL ) = @_;
3467
3468 # return the index K of the next nonblank token
3469 return unless ( defined($KK) && $KK >= 0 );
3470
3471 # use the standard array unless given otherwise
3472 $rLL = $self->{rLL} unless ( defined($rLL) );
3473 my $Num = @{$rLL};
3474 my $Knnb = $KK + 1;
3475 while ( $Knnb < $Num ) {
3476 if ( !defined( $rLL->[$Knnb] ) ) {
3477 Fault("Undefined entry for k=$Knnb");
3478 }
3479 if ( $rLL->[$Knnb]->[_TYPE_] ne 'b' ) { return $Knnb }
3480 $Knnb++;
3481 }
3482 return;
3483}

3485sub K_previous_code {
3486
3487 # return the index K of the previous nonblank, non-comment token
3488 # Call with $KK=undef to start search at the top of the array
3489 my ( $self, $KK, $rLL ) = @_;
3490
3491 # use the standard array unless given otherwise
3492 $rLL = $self->{rLL} unless ( defined($rLL) );
3493 my $Num = @{$rLL};
3494 if ( !defined($KK) ) { $KK = $Num }
3495 elsif ( $KK > $Num ) {
3496
3497 # The caller should make the first call with KK_new=undef to
3498 # avoid this error
3499 Fault(
3500"Program Bug: K_previous_nonblank_new called with K=$KK which exceeds $Num"
3501 );
3502 }
3503 my $Kpnb = $KK - 1;
3504 while ( $Kpnb >= 0 ) {
3505 if ( $rLL->[$Kpnb]->[_TYPE_] ne 'b'
3506 && $rLL->[$Kpnb]->[_TYPE_] ne '#' )
3507 {
3508 return $Kpnb;
3509 }
3510 $Kpnb--;
3511 }
3512 return;
3513}
