3515sub K_previous_nonblank {
3516
3517 # return index of previous nonblank token before item K;
3518 # Call with $KK=undef to start search at the top of the array
3519 my ( $self, $KK, $rLL ) = @_;
3520
3521 # use the standard array unless given otherwise
3522 $rLL = $self->{rLL} unless ( defined($rLL) );
3523 my $Num = @{$rLL};
3524 if ( !defined($KK) ) { $KK = $Num }
3525 elsif ( $KK > $Num ) {
3526
3527 # The caller should make the first call with KK_new=undef to
3528 # avoid this error
3529 Fault(
3530"Program Bug: K_previous_nonblank_new called with K=$KK which exceeds $Num"
3531 );
3532 }
3533 my $Kpnb = $KK - 1;
3534 while ( $Kpnb >= 0 ) {
3535 if ( $rLL->[$Kpnb]->[_TYPE_] ne 'b' ) { return $Kpnb }
3536 $Kpnb--;
3537 }
3538 return;
3539}

3541sub weld_containers {
3542
3543 # do any welding operations
3544 my $self = shift;
3545
3546 # initialize weld length hashes needed later for checking line lengths
3547 # TODO: These should eventually be stored in $self rather than be package vars
3548 %weld_len_left_closing = ();
3549 %weld_len_right_closing = ();
3550 %weld_len_left_opening = ();
3551 %weld_len_right_opening = ();
3552
3553 return if ( $rOpts->{'indent-only'} );
3554 return unless ($rOpts_add_newlines);
3555
3556 if ( $rOpts->{'weld-nested-containers'} ) {
3557
3558 # if called, weld_nested_containers must be called before other weld
3559 # operations. # This is because weld_nested_containers could overwrite
3560 # hash values written by weld_cuddled_blocks and weld_nested_quotes.
3561 $self->weld_nested_containers();
3562
3563 $self->weld_nested_quotes();
3564 }
3565
3566 # Note that weld_nested_containers() changes the _LEVEL_ values, so
3567 # weld_cuddled_blocks must use the _TRUE_LEVEL_ values instead.
3568
3569 # Here is a good test case to Be sure that both cuddling and welding
3570 # are working and not interfering with each other: <<snippets/ce_wn1.in>>
3571
3572 # perltidy -wn -ce
3573
3574 # if ($BOLD_MATH) { (
3575 # $labels, $comment,
3576 # join( '', '<B>', &make_math( $mode, '', '', $_ ), '</B>' )
3577 # ) } else { (
3578 # &process_math_in_latex( $mode, $math_style, $slevel, "\\mbox{$text}" ),
3579 # $after
3580 # ) }
3581
3582 $self->weld_cuddled_blocks();
3583
3584 return;
3585}
3586
3587sub cumulative_length_before_K {
3588 my ( $self, $KK ) = @_;
3589 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
3590 return ( $KK <= 0 ) ? 0 : $rLL->[ $KK - 1 ]->[_CUMULATIVE_LENGTH_];
3591}
3592
3593sub cumulative_length_after_K {
3594 my ( $self, $KK ) = @_;
3595 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
3596 return $rLL->[$KK]->[_CUMULATIVE_LENGTH_];
3597}
3598
3599sub weld_cuddled_blocks {
3600 my $self = shift;
3601
3602 # This routine implements the -cb flag by finding the appropriate
3603 # closing and opening block braces and welding them together.
3604 return unless ( %{$rcuddled_block_types} );
3605
3606 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
3607 return unless ( defined($rLL) && @{$rLL} );
3608 my $rbreak_container = $self->{rbreak_container};
3609
3610 my $K_opening_container = $self->{K_opening_container};
3611 my $K_closing_container = $self->{K_closing_container};
3612
3613 my $length_to_opening_seqno = sub {
3614 my ($seqno) = @_;
3615 my $KK = $K_opening_container->{$seqno};
3616 my $lentot = $KK <= 0 ? 0 : $rLL->[ $KK - 1 ]->[_CUMULATIVE_LENGTH_];
3617 return $lentot;
3618 };
3619 my $length_to_closing_seqno = sub {
3620 my ($seqno) = @_;
3621 my $KK = $K_closing_container->{$seqno};
3622 my $lentot = $KK <= 0 ? 0 : $rLL->[ $KK - 1 ]->[_CUMULATIVE_LENGTH_];
3623 return $lentot;
3624 };
3625
3626 my $is_broken_block = sub {
3627
3628 # a block is broken if the input line numbers of the braces differ
3629 # we can only cuddle between broken blocks
3630 my ($seqno) = @_;
3631 my $K_opening = $K_opening_container->{$seqno};
3632 return unless ( defined($K_opening) );
3633 my $K_closing = $K_closing_container->{$seqno};
3634 return unless ( defined($K_closing) );
3635 return $rbreak_container->{$seqno}
3636 || $rLL->[$K_closing]->[_LINE_INDEX_] !=
3637 $rLL->[$K_opening]->[_LINE_INDEX_];
3638 };
3639
3640 # A stack to remember open chains at all levels:
3641 # $in_chain[$level] = [$chain_type, $type_sequence];
3642 my @in_chain;
3643 my $CBO = $rOpts->{'cuddled-break-option'};
3644
3645 # loop over structure items to find cuddled pairs
3646 my $level = 0;
3647 my $KK = 0;
3648 while ( defined( $KK = $rLL->[$KK]->[_KNEXT_SEQ_ITEM_] ) ) {
3649 my $rtoken_vars = $rLL->[$KK];
3650 my $type_sequence = $rtoken_vars->[_TYPE_SEQUENCE_];
3651 if ( !$type_sequence ) {
3652 Fault("sequence = $type_sequence not defined");
3653 }
3654
3655 # We use the original levels because they get changed by sub
3656 # 'weld_nested_containers'. So if this were to be called before that
3657 # routine, the levels would be wrong and things would go bad.
3658 my $last_level = $level;
3659 $level = $rtoken_vars->[_LEVEL_TRUE_];
3660
3661 if ( $level < $last_level ) { $in_chain[$last_level] = undef }
3662 elsif ( $level > $last_level ) { $in_chain[$level] = undef }
3663
3664 # We are only looking at code blocks
3665 my $token = $rtoken_vars->[_TOKEN_];
3666 my $type = $rtoken_vars->[_TYPE_];
3667 next unless ( $type eq $token );
3668
3669 if ( $token eq '{' ) {
3670
3671 my $block_type = $rtoken_vars->[_BLOCK_TYPE_];
3672 if ( !$block_type ) {
3673
3674 # patch for unrecognized block types which may not be labeled
3675 my $Kp = $self->K_previous_nonblank($KK);
3676 while ( $Kp && $rLL->[$Kp]->[_TYPE_] eq '#' ) {
3677 $Kp = $self->K_previous_nonblank($Kp);
3678 }
3679 next unless $Kp;
3680 $block_type = $rLL->[$Kp]->[_TOKEN_];
3681 }
3682 if ( $in_chain[$level] ) {
3683
3684 # we are in a chain and are at an opening block brace.
3685 # See if we are welding this opening brace with the previous
3686 # block brace. Get their identification numbers:
3687 my $closing_seqno = $in_chain[$level]->[1];
3688 my $opening_seqno = $type_sequence;
3689
3690 # The preceding block must be on multiple lines so that its
3691 # closing brace will start a new line.
3692 if ( !$is_broken_block->($closing_seqno) ) {
3693 next unless ( $CBO == 2 );
3694 $rbreak_container->{$closing_seqno} = 1;
3695 }
3696
3697 # we will let the trailing block be either broken or intact
3698 ## && $is_broken_block->($opening_seqno);
3699
3700 # We can weld the closing brace to its following word ..
3701 my $Ko = $K_closing_container->{$closing_seqno};
3702 my $Kon = $self->K_next_nonblank($Ko);
3703
3704 # ..unless it is a comment
3705 if ( $rLL->[$Kon]->[_TYPE_] ne '#' ) {
3706 my $dlen =
3707 $rLL->[$Kon]->[_CUMULATIVE_LENGTH_] -
3708 $rLL->[ $Ko - 1 ]->[_CUMULATIVE_LENGTH_];
3709 $weld_len_right_closing{$closing_seqno} = $dlen;
3710
3711 # Set flag that we want to break the next container
3712 # so that the cuddled line is balanced.
3713 $rbreak_container->{$opening_seqno} = 1
3714 if ($CBO);
3715 }
3716
3717 }
3718 else {
3719
3720 # We are not in a chain. Start a new chain if we see the
3721 # starting block type.
3722 if ( $rcuddled_block_types->{$block_type} ) {
3723 $in_chain[$level] = [ $block_type, $type_sequence ];
3724 }
3725 else {
3726 $block_type = '*';
3727 $in_chain[$level] = [ $block_type, $type_sequence ];
3728 }
3729 }
3730 }
3731 elsif ( $token eq '}' ) {
3732 if ( $in_chain[$level] ) {
3733
3734 # We are in a chain at a closing brace. See if this chain
3735 # continues..
3736 my $Knn = $self->K_next_code($KK);
3737 next unless $Knn;
3738
3739 my $chain_type = $in_chain[$level]->[0];
3740 my $next_nonblank_token = $rLL->[$Knn]->[_TOKEN_];
3741 if (
3742 $rcuddled_block_types->{$chain_type}->{$next_nonblank_token}
3743 )
3744 {
3745
3746 # Note that we do not weld yet because we must wait until
3747 # we we are sure that an opening brace for this follows.
3748 $in_chain[$level]->[1] = $type_sequence;
3749 }
3750 else { $in_chain[$level] = undef }
3751 }
3752 }
3753 }
3754
3755 return;
3756}
3757
3758sub weld_nested_containers {
3759 my $self = shift;
3760
3761 # This routine implements the -wn flag by "welding together"
3762 # the nested closing and opening tokens which were previously
3763 # identified by sub 'find_nested_pairs'. "welding" simply
3764 # involves setting certain hash values which will be checked
3765 # later during formatting.
3766
3767 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
3768 my $Klimit = $self->get_rLL_max_index();
3769 my $rnested_pairs = $self->{rnested_pairs};
3770 my $rlines = $self->{rlines};
3771 my $K_opening_container = $self->{K_opening_container};
3772 my $K_closing_container = $self->{K_closing_container};
3773
3774 # Return unless there are nested pairs to weld
3775 return unless defined($rnested_pairs) && @{$rnested_pairs};
3776
3777 # This array will hold the sequence numbers of the tokens to be welded.
3778 my @welds;
3779
3780 # Variables needed for estimating line lengths
3781 my $starting_indent;
3782 my $starting_lentot;
3783
3784 # A tolerance to the length for length estimates. In some rare cases
3785 # this can avoid problems where a final weld slightly exceeds the
3786 # line length and gets broken in a bad spot.
3787 my $length_tol = 1;
3788
3789 my $excess_length_to_K = sub {
3790 my ($K) = @_;
3791
3792 # Estimate the length from the line start to a given token
3793 my $length = $self->cumulative_length_before_K($K) - $starting_lentot;
3794 my $excess_length =
3795 $starting_indent + $length + $length_tol - $rOpts_maximum_line_length;
3796 return ($excess_length);
3797 };
3798
3799 my $length_to_opening_seqno = sub {
3800 my ($seqno) = @_;
3801 my $KK = $K_opening_container->{$seqno};
3802 my $lentot = $KK <= 0 ? 0 : $rLL->[ $KK - 1 ]->[_CUMULATIVE_LENGTH_];
3803 return $lentot;
3804 };
3805
3806 my $length_to_closing_seqno = sub {
3807 my ($seqno) = @_;
3808 my $KK = $K_closing_container->{$seqno};
3809 my $lentot = $KK <= 0 ? 0 : $rLL->[ $KK - 1 ]->[_CUMULATIVE_LENGTH_];
3810 return $lentot;
3811 };
3812
3813 # Abbreviations:
3814 # _oo=outer opening, i.e. first of { {
3815 # _io=inner opening, i.e. second of { {
3816 # _oc=outer closing, i.e. second of } {
3817 # _ic=inner closing, i.e. first of } }
3818
3819 my $previous_pair;
3820
3821 # We are working from outermost to innermost pairs so that
3822 # level changes will be complete when we arrive at the inner pairs.
3823
3824 while ( my $item = pop( @{$rnested_pairs} ) ) {
3825 my ( $inner_seqno, $outer_seqno ) = @{$item};
3826
3827 my $Kouter_opening = $K_opening_container->{$outer_seqno};
3828 my $Kinner_opening = $K_opening_container->{$inner_seqno};
3829 my $Kouter_closing = $K_closing_container->{$outer_seqno};
3830 my $Kinner_closing = $K_closing_container->{$inner_seqno};
3831
3832 my $outer_opening = $rLL->[$Kouter_opening];
3833 my $inner_opening = $rLL->[$Kinner_opening];
3834 my $outer_closing = $rLL->[$Kouter_closing];
3835 my $inner_closing = $rLL->[$Kinner_closing];
3836
3837 my $iline_oo = $outer_opening->[_LINE_INDEX_];
3838 my $iline_io = $inner_opening->[_LINE_INDEX_];
3839
3840 # Set flag saying if this pair starts a new weld
3841 my $starting_new_weld = !( @welds && $outer_seqno == $welds[-1]->[0] );
3842
3843 # Set flag saying if this pair is adjacent to the previous nesting pair
3844 # (even if previous pair was rejected as a weld)
3845 my $touch_previous_pair =
3846 defined($previous_pair) && $outer_seqno == $previous_pair->[0];
3847 $previous_pair = $item;
3848
3849 # Set a flag if we should not weld. It sometimes looks best not to weld
3850 # when the opening and closing tokens are very close. However, there
3851 # is a danger that we will create a "blinker", which oscillates between
3852 # two semi-stable states, if we do not weld. So the rules for
3853 # not welding have to be carefully defined and tested.
3854 my $do_not_weld;
3855 if ( !$touch_previous_pair ) {
3856
3857 # If this pair is not adjacent to the previous pair (skipped or
3858 # not), then measure lengths from the start of line of oo
3859
3860 my $rK_range = $rlines->[$iline_oo]->{_rK_range};
3861 my ( $Kfirst, $Klast ) = @{$rK_range};
3862 $starting_lentot =
3863 $Kfirst <= 0 ? 0 : $rLL->[ $Kfirst - 1 ]->[_CUMULATIVE_LENGTH_];
3864 $starting_indent = 0;
3865 if ( !$rOpts_variable_maximum_line_length ) {
3866 my $level = $rLL->[$Kfirst]->[_LEVEL_];
3867 $starting_indent = $rOpts_indent_columns * $level;
3868 }
3869
3870 # DO-NOT-WELD RULE 1:
3871 # Do not weld something that looks like the start of a two-line
3872 # function call, like this: <<snippets/wn6.in>>
3873 # $trans->add_transformation(
3874 # PDL::Graphics::TriD::Scale->new( $sx, $sy, $sz ) );
3875 # We will look for a semicolon after the closing paren.
3876
3877 # We want to weld something complex, like this though
3878 # my $compass = uc( opposite_direction( line_to_canvas_direction(
3879 # @{ $coords[0] }, @{ $coords[1] } ) ) );
3880 # Otherwise we will get a 'blinker'
3881
3882 my $iline_oc = $outer_closing->[_LINE_INDEX_];
3883 if ( $iline_oc <= $iline_oo + 1 ) {
3884
3885 # Look for following semicolon...
3886 my $Knext_nonblank = $self->K_next_nonblank($Kouter_closing);
3887 my $next_nonblank_type =
3888 defined($Knext_nonblank)
3889 ? $rLL->[$Knext_nonblank]->[_TYPE_]
3890 : 'b';
3891 if ( $next_nonblank_type eq ';' ) {
3892
3893 # Then do not weld if no other containers between inner
3894 # opening and closing.
3895 my $Knext_seq_item = $inner_opening->[_KNEXT_SEQ_ITEM_];
3896 if ( $Knext_seq_item == $Kinner_closing ) {
3897 $do_not_weld ||= 1;
3898 }
3899 }
3900 }
3901 }
3902
3903 my $iline_ic = $inner_closing->[_LINE_INDEX_];
3904
3905 # DO-NOT-WELD RULE 2:
3906 # Do not weld an opening paren to an inner one line brace block
3907 # We will just use old line numbers for this test and require
3908 # iterations if necessary for convergence
3909
3910 # For example, otherwise we could cause the opening paren
3911 # in the following example to separate from the caller name
3912 # as here:
3913
3914 # $_[0]->code_handler
3915 # ( sub { $more .= $_[1] . ":" . $_[0] . "\n" } );
3916
3917 # Here is another example where we do not want to weld:
3918 # $wrapped->add_around_modifier(
3919 # sub { push @tracelog => 'around 1'; $_[0]->(); } );
3920
3921 # If the one line sub block gets broken due to length or by the
3922 # user, then we can weld. The result will then be:
3923 # $wrapped->add_around_modifier( sub {
3924 # push @tracelog => 'around 1';
3925 # $_[0]->();
3926 # } );
3927
3928 if ( $iline_ic == $iline_io ) {
3929
3930 my $token_oo = $outer_opening->[_TOKEN_];
3931 my $block_type_io = $inner_opening->[_BLOCK_TYPE_];
3932 my $token_io = $inner_opening->[_TOKEN_];
3933 $do_not_weld ||= $token_oo eq '(' && $token_io eq '{';
3934 }
3935
3936 # DO-NOT-WELD RULE 3:
3937 # Do not weld if this makes our line too long
3938 $do_not_weld ||= $excess_length_to_K->($Kinner_opening) > 0;
3939
3940 if ($do_not_weld) {
3941
3942 # After neglecting a pair, we start measuring from start of point io
3943 $starting_lentot =
3944 $self->cumulative_length_before_K($Kinner_opening);
3945 $starting_indent = 0;
3946 if ( !$rOpts_variable_maximum_line_length ) {
3947 my $level = $inner_opening->[_LEVEL_];
3948 $starting_indent = $rOpts_indent_columns * $level;
3949 }
3950
3951 # Normally, a broken pair should not decrease indentation of
3952 # intermediate tokens:
3953 ## if ( $last_pair_broken ) { next }
3954 # However, for long strings of welded tokens, such as '{{{{{{...'
3955 # we will allow broken pairs to also remove indentation.
3956 # This will keep very long strings of opening and closing
3957 # braces from marching off to the right. We will do this if the
3958 # number of tokens in a weld before the broken weld is 4 or more.
3959 # This rule will mainly be needed for test scripts, since typical
3960 # welds have fewer than about 4 welded tokens.
3961 if ( !@welds || @{ $welds[-1] } < 4 ) { next }
3962 }
3963
3964 # otherwise start new weld ...
3965 elsif ($starting_new_weld) {
3966 push @welds, $item;
3967 }
3968
3969 # ... or extend current weld
3970 else {
3971 unshift @{ $welds[-1] }, $inner_seqno;
3972 }
3973
3974 # After welding, reduce the indentation level if all intermediate tokens
3975 my $dlevel = $outer_opening->[_LEVEL_] - $inner_opening->[_LEVEL_];
3976 if ( $dlevel != 0 ) {
3977 my $Kstart = $Kinner_opening;
3978 my $Kstop = $Kinner_closing;
3979 for ( my $KK = $Kstart ; $KK <= $Kstop ; $KK++ ) {
3980 $rLL->[$KK]->[_LEVEL_] += $dlevel;
3981 }
3982 }
3983 }
3984
3985 # Define weld lengths needed later to set line breaks
3986 foreach my $item (@welds) {
3987
3988 # sweep from inner to outer
3989
3990 my $inner_seqno;
3991 my $len_close = 0;
3992 my $len_open = 0;
3993 foreach my $outer_seqno ( @{$item} ) {
3994 if ($inner_seqno) {
3995
3996 my $dlen_opening =
3997 $length_to_opening_seqno->($inner_seqno) -
3998 $length_to_opening_seqno->($outer_seqno);
3999
4000 my $dlen_closing =
4001 $length_to_closing_seqno->($outer_seqno) -
4002 $length_to_closing_seqno->($inner_seqno);
4003
4004 $len_open += $dlen_opening;
4005 $len_close += $dlen_closing;
4006
4007 }
4008
4009 $weld_len_left_closing{$outer_seqno} = $len_close;
4010 $weld_len_right_opening{$outer_seqno} = $len_open;
4011
4012 $inner_seqno = $outer_seqno;
4013 }
4014
4015 # sweep from outer to inner
4016 foreach my $seqno ( reverse @{$item} ) {
4017 $weld_len_right_closing{$seqno} =
4018 $len_close - $weld_len_left_closing{$seqno};
4019 $weld_len_left_opening{$seqno} =
4020 $len_open - $weld_len_right_opening{$seqno};
4021 }
4022 }
4023
4024 #####################################
4025 # DEBUG
4026 #####################################
4027 if (0) {
4028 my $count = 0;
4029 local $" = ')(';
4030 foreach my $weld (@welds) {
4031 print "\nWeld number $count has seq: (@{$weld})\n";
4032 foreach my $seq ( @{$weld} ) {
4033 print <<EOM;
4034 seq=$seq
4035 left_opening=$weld_len_left_opening{$seq};
4036 right_opening=$weld_len_right_opening{$seq};
4037 left_closing=$weld_len_left_closing{$seq};
4038 right_closing=$weld_len_right_closing{$seq};
4039EOM
4040 }
4041
4042 $count++;
4043 }
4044 }
4045 return;
4046}
4047
4048sub weld_nested_quotes {
4049 my $self = shift;
4050
4051 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
4052 return unless ( defined($rLL) && @{$rLL} );
4053
4054 my $K_opening_container = $self->{K_opening_container};
4055 my $K_closing_container = $self->{K_closing_container};
4056 my $rlines = $self->{rlines};
4057
4058 my $is_single_quote = sub {
4059 my ( $Kbeg, $Kend, $quote_type ) = @_;
4060 foreach my $K ( $Kbeg .. $Kend ) {
4061 my $test_type = $rLL->[$K]->[_TYPE_];
4062 next if ( $test_type eq 'b' );
4063 return if ( $test_type ne $quote_type );
4064 }
4065 return 1;
4066 };
4067
4068 my $excess_line_length = sub {
4069 my ( $KK, $Ktest ) = @_;
4070
4071 # what is the excess length if we add token $Ktest to the line with $KK?
4072 my $iline = $rLL->[$KK]->[_LINE_INDEX_];
4073 my $rK_range = $rlines->[$iline]->{_rK_range};
4074 my ( $Kfirst, $Klast ) = @{$rK_range};
4075 my $starting_lentot =
4076 $Kfirst <= 0 ? 0 : $rLL->[ $Kfirst - 1 ]->[_CUMULATIVE_LENGTH_];
4077 my $starting_indent = 0;
4078 my $length_tol = 1;
4079 if ( !$rOpts_variable_maximum_line_length ) {
4080 my $level = $rLL->[$Kfirst]->[_LEVEL_];
4081 $starting_indent = $rOpts_indent_columns * $level;
4082 }
4083
4084 my $length = $rLL->[$Ktest]->[_CUMULATIVE_LENGTH_] - $starting_lentot;
4085 my $excess_length =
4086 $starting_indent + $length + $length_tol - $rOpts_maximum_line_length;
4087 return $excess_length;
4088 };
4089
4090 # look for single qw quotes nested in containers
4091 my $KK = 0;
4092 while ( defined( $KK = $rLL->[$KK]->[_KNEXT_SEQ_ITEM_] ) ) {
4093 my $rtoken_vars = $rLL->[$KK];
4094 my $outer_seqno = $rtoken_vars->[_TYPE_SEQUENCE_];
4095 if ( !$outer_seqno ) {
4096 Fault("sequence = $outer_seqno not defined");
4097 }
4098
4099 my $token = $rtoken_vars->[_TOKEN_];
4100 if ( $is_opening_token{$token} ) {
4101
4102 # see if the next token is a quote of some type
4103 my $Kn = $self->K_next_nonblank($KK);
4104 next unless $Kn;
4105 my $next_token = $rLL->[$Kn]->[_TOKEN_];
4106 my $next_type = $rLL->[$Kn]->[_TYPE_];
4107 next
4108 unless ( ( $next_type eq 'q' || $next_type eq 'Q' )
4109 && $next_token =~ /^q/ );
4110
4111 # The token before the closing container must also be a quote
4112 my $K_closing = $K_closing_container->{$outer_seqno};
4113 my $Kt_end = $self->K_previous_nonblank($K_closing);
4114 next unless $rLL->[$Kt_end]->[_TYPE_] eq $next_type;
4115
4116 # Do not weld to single-line quotes. Nothing is gained, and it may
4117 # look bad.
4118 next if ( $Kt_end == $Kn );
4119
4120 # Only weld to quotes delimited with container tokens. This is
4121 # because welding to arbitrary quote delimiters can produce code
4122 # which is less readable than without welding.
4123 my $closing_delimiter = substr( $rLL->[$Kt_end]->[_TOKEN_], -1, 1 );
4124 next
4125 unless ( $is_closing_token{$closing_delimiter}
4126 || $closing_delimiter eq '>' );
4127
4128 # Now make sure that there is just a single quote in the container
4129 next
4130 unless ( $is_single_quote->( $Kn + 1, $Kt_end - 1, $next_type ) );
4131
4132 # If welded, the line must not exceed allowed line length
4133 # Assume old line breaks for this estimate.
4134 next if ( $excess_line_length->( $KK, $Kn ) > 0 );
4135
4136 # OK to weld
4137 # FIXME: Are these always correct?
4138 $weld_len_left_closing{$outer_seqno} = 1;
4139 $weld_len_right_opening{$outer_seqno} = 2;
4140
4141 # QW PATCH 1 (Testing)
4142 # undo CI for welded quotes
4143 foreach my $K ( $Kn .. $Kt_end ) {
4144 $rLL->[$K]->[_CI_LEVEL_] = 0;
4145 }
4146
4147 # Change the level of a closing qw token to be that of the outer
4148 # containing token. This will allow -lp indentation to function
4149 # correctly in the vertical aligner.
4150 $rLL->[$Kt_end]->[_LEVEL_] = $rLL->[$K_closing]->[_LEVEL_];
4151 }
4152 }
4153 return;
4154}
4155
4156sub weld_len_left {
4157
4158 my ( $seqno, $type_or_tok ) = @_;
4159
4160 # Given the sequence number of a token, and the token or its type,
4161 # return the length of any weld to its left
4162
4163 my $weld_len;
4164 if ($seqno) {
4165 if ( $is_closing_type{$type_or_tok} ) {
4166 $weld_len = $weld_len_left_closing{$seqno};
4167 }
4168 elsif ( $is_opening_type{$type_or_tok} ) {
4169 $weld_len = $weld_len_left_opening{$seqno};
4170 }
4171 }
4172 if ( !defined($weld_len) ) { $weld_len = 0 }
4173 return $weld_len;
4174}
4175
4176sub weld_len_right {
4177
4178 my ( $seqno, $type_or_tok ) = @_;
4179
4180 # Given the sequence number of a token, and the token or its type,
4181 # return the length of any weld to its right
4182
4183 my $weld_len;
4184 if ($seqno) {
4185 if ( $is_closing_type{$type_or_tok} ) {
4186 $weld_len = $weld_len_right_closing{$seqno};
4187 }
4188 elsif ( $is_opening_type{$type_or_tok} ) {
4189 $weld_len = $weld_len_right_opening{$seqno};
4190 }
4191 }
4192 if ( !defined($weld_len) ) { $weld_len = 0 }
4193 return $weld_len;
4194}
4195
4196sub weld_len_left_to_go {
4197 my ($i) = @_;
4198
4199 # Given the index of a token in the 'to_go' array
4200 # return the length of any weld to its left
4201 return if ( $i < 0 );
4202 my $weld_len =
4203 weld_len_left( $type_sequence_to_go[$i], $types_to_go[$i] );
4204 return $weld_len;
4205}
4206
4207sub weld_len_right_to_go {
4208 my ($i) = @_;
4209
4210 # Given the index of a token in the 'to_go' array
4211 # return the length of any weld to its right
4212 return if ( $i < 0 );
4213 if ( $i > 0 && $types_to_go[$i] eq 'b' ) { $i-- }
4214 my $weld_len =
4215 weld_len_right( $type_sequence_to_go[$i], $types_to_go[$i] );
4216 return $weld_len;
4217}

4219sub link_sequence_items {
4220
4221 # This has been merged into 'respace_tokens' but retained for reference
4222 my $self = shift;
4223 my $rlines = $self->{rlines};
4224 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
4225
4226 # We walk the token list and make links to the next sequence item.
4227 # We also define these hashes to container tokens using sequence number as
4228 # the key:
4229 my $K_opening_container = {}; # opening [ { or (
4230 my $K_closing_container = {}; # closing ] } or )
4231 my $K_opening_ternary = {}; # opening ? of ternary
4232 my $K_closing_ternary = {}; # closing : of ternary
4233
4234 # sub to link preceding nodes forward to a new node type
4235 my $link_back = sub {
4236 my ( $Ktop, $key ) = @_;
4237
4238 my $Kprev = $Ktop - 1;
4239 while ( $Kprev >= 0
4240 && !defined( $rLL->[$Kprev]->[$key] ) )
4241 {
4242 $rLL->[$Kprev]->[$key] = $Ktop;
4243 $Kprev -= 1;
4244 }
4245 };
4246
4247 for ( my $KK = 0 ; $KK < @{$rLL} ; $KK++ ) {
4248
4249 $rLL->[$KK]->[_KNEXT_SEQ_ITEM_] = undef;
4250
4251 my $type = $rLL->[$KK]->[_TYPE_];
4252
4253 next if ( $type eq 'b' );
4254
4255 my $type_sequence = $rLL->[$KK]->[_TYPE_SEQUENCE_];
4256 if ($type_sequence) {
4257
4258 $link_back->( $KK, _KNEXT_SEQ_ITEM_ );
4259
4260 my $token = $rLL->[$KK]->[_TOKEN_];
4261 if ( $is_opening_token{$token} ) {
4262
4263 $K_opening_container->{$type_sequence} = $KK;
4264 }
4265 elsif ( $is_closing_token{$token} ) {
4266
4267 $K_closing_container->{$type_sequence} = $KK;
4268 }
4269
4270 # These are not yet used but could be useful
4271 else {
4272 if ( $token eq '?' ) {
4273 $K_opening_ternary->{$type_sequence} = $KK;
4274 }
4275 elsif ( $token eq ':' ) {
4276 $K_closing_ternary->{$type_sequence} = $KK;
4277 }
4278 else {
4279 Fault(<<EOM);
4280Unknown sequenced token type '$type'. Expecting one of '{[(?:)]}'
4281EOM
4282 }
4283 }
4284 }
4285 }
4286
4287 $self->{K_opening_container} = $K_opening_container;
4288 $self->{K_closing_container} = $K_closing_container;
4289 $self->{K_opening_ternary} = $K_opening_ternary;
4290 $self->{K_closing_ternary} = $K_closing_ternary;
4291 return;
4292}
4293
4294sub sum_token_lengths {
4295 my $self = shift;
4296
4297 # This has been merged into 'respace_tokens' but retained for reference
4298 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
4299 my $cumulative_length = 0;
4300 for ( my $KK = 0 ; $KK < @{$rLL} ; $KK++ ) {
4301
4302 # now set the length of this token
4303 my $token_length = length( $rLL->[$KK]->[_TOKEN_] );
4304
4305 $cumulative_length += $token_length;
4306
4307 # Save the length sum to just AFTER this token
4308 $rLL->[$KK]->[_CUMULATIVE_LENGTH_] = $cumulative_length;
4309
4310 }
4311 return;
4312}
4313
4314sub resync_lines_and_tokens {
4315
4316 my $self = shift;
4317 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
4318 my $Klimit = $self->{Klimit};
4319 my $rlines = $self->{rlines};
4320
4321 # Re-construct the arrays of tokens associated with the original input lines
4322 # since they have probably changed due to inserting and deleting blanks
4323 # and a few other tokens.
4324
4325 my $Kmax = -1;
4326
4327 # This is the next token and its line index:
4328 my $Knext = 0;
4329 my $inext;
4330 if ( defined($rLL) && @{$rLL} ) {
4331 $Kmax = @{$rLL} - 1;
4332 $inext = $rLL->[$Knext]->[_LINE_INDEX_];
4333 }
4334
4335 my $get_inext = sub {
4336 if ( $Knext < 0 || $Knext > $Kmax ) { $inext = undef }
4337 else {
4338 $inext = $rLL->[$Knext]->[_LINE_INDEX_];
4339 }
4340 return $inext;
4341 };
4342
4343 # Remember the most recently output token index
4344 my $Klast_out;
4345
4346 my $iline = -1;
4347 foreach my $line_of_tokens ( @{$rlines} ) {
4348 $iline++;
4349 my $line_type = $line_of_tokens->{_line_type};
4350 if ( $line_type eq 'CODE' ) {
4351
4352 my @K_array;
4353 my $rK_range;
4354 $inext = $get_inext->();
4355 while ( defined($inext) && $inext <= $iline ) {
4356 push @{K_array}, $Knext;
4357 $Knext += 1;
4358 $inext = $get_inext->();
4359 }
4360
4361 # Delete any terminal blank token
4362 if (@K_array) {
4363 if ( $rLL->[ $K_array[-1] ]->[_TYPE_] eq 'b' ) {
4364 pop @K_array;
4365 }
4366 }
4367
4368 # Define the range of K indexes for the line:
4369 # $Kfirst = index of first token on line
4370 # $Klast_out = index of last token on line
4371 my ( $Kfirst, $Klast );
4372 if (@K_array) {
4373 $Kfirst = $K_array[0];
4374 $Klast = $K_array[-1];
4375 $Klast_out = $Klast;
4376 }
4377
4378 # It is only safe to trim the actual line text if the input
4379 # line had a terminal blank token. Otherwise, we may be
4380 # in a quote.
4381 if ( $line_of_tokens->{_ended_in_blank_token} ) {
4382 $line_of_tokens->{_line_text} =~ s/\s+$//;
4383 }
4384 $line_of_tokens->{_rK_range} = [ $Kfirst, $Klast ];
4385 }
4386 }
4387
4388 # There shouldn't be any nodes beyond the last one unless we start
4389 # allowing 'link_after' calls
4390 if ( defined($inext) ) {
4391
4392 Fault("unexpected tokens at end of file when reconstructing lines");
4393 }
4394
4395 return;
4396}

4398sub dump_verbatim {
4399 my $self = shift;
4400 my $rlines = $self->{rlines};
4401 foreach my $line ( @{$rlines} ) {
4402 my $input_line = $line->{_line_text};
4403 $self->write_unindented_line($input_line);
4404 }
4405 return;
4406}

4408sub finish_formatting {
4409
4410 my ( $self, $severe_error ) = @_;
4411
4412 # The file has been tokenized and is ready to be formatted.
4413 # All of the relevant data is stored in $self, ready to go.
4414
4415 # output file verbatim if severe error or no formatting requested
4416 if ( $severe_error || $rOpts->{notidy} ) {
4417 $self->dump_verbatim();
4418 $self->wrapup();
4419 return;
4420 }
4421
4422 # Make a pass through the lines, looking at lines of CODE and identifying
4423 # special processing needs, such format skipping sections marked by
4424 # special comments
4425 $self->scan_comments();
4426
4427 # Find nested pairs of container tokens for any welding. This information
4428 # is also needed for adding semicolons, so it is split apart from the
4429 # welding step.
4430 $self->find_nested_pairs();
4431
4432 # Make sure everything looks good
4433 $self->check_line_hashes();
4434
4435 # Future: Place to Begin future Iteration Loop
4436 # foreach my $it_count(1..$maxit) {
4437
4438 # Future: We must reset some things after the first iteration.
4439 # This includes:
4440 # - resetting levels if there was any welding
4441 # - resetting any phantom semicolons
4442 # - dealing with any line numbering issues so we can relate final lines
4443 # line numbers with input line numbers.
4444 #
4445 # If ($it_count>1) {
4446 # Copy {level_raw} to [_LEVEL_] if ($it_count>1)
4447 # Renumber lines
4448 # }
4449
4450 # Make a pass through all tokens, adding or deleting any whitespace as
4451 # required. Also make any other changes, such as adding semicolons.
4452 # All token changes must be made here so that the token data structure
4453 # remains fixed for the rest of this iteration.
4454 $self->respace_tokens();
4455
4456 # Implement any welding needed for the -wn or -cb options
4457 $self->weld_containers();
4458
4459 # Finishes formatting and write the result to the line sink.
4460 # Eventually this call should just change the 'rlines' data according to the
4461 # new line breaks and then return so that we can do an internal iteration
4462 # before continuing with the next stages of formatting.
4463 $self->break_lines();
4464
4465 ############################################################
4466 # A possible future decomposition of 'break_lines()' follows.
4467 # Benefits:
4468 # - allow perltidy to do an internal iteration which eliminates
4469 # many unnecessary steps, such as re-parsing and vertical alignment.
4470 # This will allow iterations to be automatic.
4471 # - consolidate all length calculations to allow utf8 alignment
4472 ############################################################
4473
4474 # Future: Check for convergence of beginning tokens on CODE lines
4475
4476 # Future: End of Iteration Loop
4477
4478 # Future: add_padding($rargs);
4479
4480 # Future: add_closing_side_comments($rargs);
4481
4482 # Future: vertical_alignment($rargs);
4483
4484 # Future: output results
4485
4486 # A final routine to tie up any loose ends
4487 $self->wrapup();
4488 return;
4489}

4503sub leading_spaces_to_go {
4504
4505 # return the number of indentation spaces for a token in the output stream;
4506 # these were previously stored by 'set_leading_whitespace'.
4507
4508 my $ii = shift;
4509 if ( $ii < 0 ) { $ii = 0 }
4510 return get_spaces( $leading_spaces_to_go[$ii] );
4511
4512}
4513
4514sub get_spaces {
4515
4516 # return the number of leading spaces associated with an indentation
4517 # variable $indentation is either a constant number of spaces or an object
4518 # with a get_spaces method.
4519 my $indentation = shift;
4520 return ref($indentation) ? $indentation->get_spaces() : $indentation;
4521}
4522
4523sub get_recoverable_spaces {
4524
4525 # return the number of spaces (+ means shift right, - means shift left)
4526 # that we would like to shift a group of lines with the same indentation
4527 # to get them to line up with their opening parens
4528 my $indentation = shift;
4529 return ref($indentation) ? $indentation->get_recoverable_spaces() : 0;
4530}
4531
4532sub get_available_spaces_to_go {
4533
4534 my $ii = shift;
4535 my $item = $leading_spaces_to_go[$ii];
4536
4537 # return the number of available leading spaces associated with an
4538 # indentation variable. $indentation is either a constant number of
4539 # spaces or an object with a get_available_spaces method.
4540 return ref($item) ? $item->get_available_spaces() : 0;
4541}

4543sub new_lp_indentation_item {
4544
4545 # this is an interface to the IndentationItem class
4546 my ( $spaces, $level, $ci_level, $available_spaces, $align_paren ) = @_;
4547
4548 # A negative level implies not to store the item in the item_list
4549 my $index = 0;
4550 if ( $level >= 0 ) { $index = ++$max_gnu_item_index; }
4551
4552 my $item = Perl::Tidy::IndentationItem->new(
4553 $spaces, $level,
4554 $ci_level, $available_spaces,
4555 $index, $gnu_sequence_number,
4556 $align_paren, $max_gnu_stack_index,
4557 $line_start_index_to_go,
4558 );
4559
4560 if ( $level >= 0 ) {
4561 $gnu_item_list[$max_gnu_item_index] = $item;
4562 }
4563
4564 return $item;
4565}
4566
4567sub set_leading_whitespace {
4568
4569 # This routine defines leading whitespace
4570 # given: the level and continuation_level of a token,
4571 # define: space count of leading string which would apply if it
4572 # were the first token of a new line.
4573
4574 my ( $level_abs, $ci_level, $in_continued_quote ) = @_;
4575
4576 # Adjust levels if necessary to recycle whitespace:
4577 # given $level_abs, the absolute level
4578 # define $level, a possibly reduced level for whitespace
4579 my $level = $level_abs;
4580 if ( $rOpts_whitespace_cycle && $rOpts_whitespace_cycle > 0 ) {
4581 if ( $level_abs < $whitespace_last_level ) {
4582 pop(@whitespace_level_stack);
4583 }
4584 if ( !@whitespace_level_stack ) {
4585 push @whitespace_level_stack, $level_abs;
4586 }
4587 elsif ( $level_abs > $whitespace_last_level ) {
4588 $level = $whitespace_level_stack[-1] +
4589 ( $level_abs - $whitespace_last_level );
4590
4591 if (
4592 # 1 Try to break at a block brace
4593 (
4594 $level > $rOpts_whitespace_cycle
4595 && $last_nonblank_type eq '{'
4596 && $last_nonblank_token eq '{'
4597 )
4598
4599 # 2 Then either a brace or bracket
4600 || ( $level > $rOpts_whitespace_cycle + 1
4601 && $last_nonblank_token =~ /^[\{\[]$/ )
4602
4603 # 3 Then a paren too
4604 || $level > $rOpts_whitespace_cycle + 2
4605 )
4606 {
4607 $level = 1;
4608 }
4609 push @whitespace_level_stack, $level;
4610 }
4611 $level = $whitespace_level_stack[-1];
4612 }
4613 $whitespace_last_level = $level_abs;
4614
4615 # modify for -bli, which adds one continuation indentation for
4616 # opening braces
4617 if ( $rOpts_brace_left_and_indent
4618 && $max_index_to_go == 0
4619 && $block_type_to_go[$max_index_to_go] =~ /$bli_pattern/o )
4620 {
4621 $ci_level++;
4622 }
4623
4624 # patch to avoid trouble when input file has negative indentation.
4625 # other logic should catch this error.
4626 if ( $level < 0 ) { $level = 0 }
4627
4628 #-------------------------------------------
4629 # handle the standard indentation scheme
4630 #-------------------------------------------
4631 unless ($rOpts_line_up_parentheses) {
4632 my $space_count =
4633 $ci_level * $rOpts_continuation_indentation +
4634 $level * $rOpts_indent_columns;
4635 my $ci_spaces =
4636 ( $ci_level == 0 ) ? 0 : $rOpts_continuation_indentation;
4637
4638 if ($in_continued_quote) {
4639 $space_count = 0;
4640 $ci_spaces = 0;
4641 }
4642 $leading_spaces_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = $space_count;
4643 $reduced_spaces_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = $space_count - $ci_spaces;
4644 return;
4645 }
4646
4647 #-------------------------------------------------------------
4648 # handle case of -lp indentation..
4649 #-------------------------------------------------------------
4650
4651 # The continued_quote flag means that this is the first token of a
4652 # line, and it is the continuation of some kind of multi-line quote
4653 # or pattern. It requires special treatment because it must have no
4654 # added leading whitespace. So we create a special indentation item
4655 # which is not in the stack.
4656 if ($in_continued_quote) {
4657 my $space_count = 0;
4658 my $available_space = 0;
4659 $level = -1; # flag to prevent storing in item_list
4660 $leading_spaces_to_go[$max_index_to_go] =
4661 $reduced_spaces_to_go[$max_index_to_go] =
4662 new_lp_indentation_item( $space_count, $level, $ci_level,
4663 $available_space, 0 );
4664 return;
4665 }
4666
4667 # get the top state from the stack
4668 my $space_count = $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index]->get_spaces();
4669 my $current_level = $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index]->get_level();
4670 my $current_ci_level = $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index]->get_ci_level();
4671
4672 my $type = $types_to_go[$max_index_to_go];
4673 my $token = $tokens_to_go[$max_index_to_go];
4674 my $total_depth = $nesting_depth_to_go[$max_index_to_go];
4675
4676 if ( $type eq '{' || $type eq '(' ) {
4677
4678 $gnu_comma_count{ $total_depth + 1 } = 0;
4679 $gnu_arrow_count{ $total_depth + 1 } = 0;
4680
4681 # If we come to an opening token after an '=' token of some type,
4682 # see if it would be helpful to 'break' after the '=' to save space
4683 my $last_equals = $last_gnu_equals{$total_depth};
4684 if ( $last_equals && $last_equals > $line_start_index_to_go ) {
4685
4686 # find the position if we break at the '='
4687 my $i_test = $last_equals;
4688 if ( $types_to_go[ $i_test + 1 ] eq 'b' ) { $i_test++ }
4689
4690 # TESTING
4691 ##my $too_close = ($i_test==$max_index_to_go-1);
4692
4693 my $test_position = total_line_length( $i_test, $max_index_to_go );
4694 my $mll = maximum_line_length($i_test);
4695
4696 if (
4697
4698 # the equals is not just before an open paren (testing)
4699 ##!$too_close &&
4700
4701 # if we are beyond the midpoint
4702 $gnu_position_predictor > $mll - $rOpts_maximum_line_length / 2
4703
4704 # or we are beyond the 1/4 point and there was an old
4705 # break at the equals
4706 || (
4707 $gnu_position_predictor >
4708 $mll - $rOpts_maximum_line_length * 3 / 4
4709 && (
4710 $old_breakpoint_to_go[$last_equals]
4711 || ( $last_equals > 0
4712 && $old_breakpoint_to_go[ $last_equals - 1 ] )
4713 || ( $last_equals > 1
4714 && $types_to_go[ $last_equals - 1 ] eq 'b'
4715 && $old_breakpoint_to_go[ $last_equals - 2 ] )
4716 )
4717 )
4718 )
4719 {
4720
4721 # then make the switch -- note that we do not set a real
4722 # breakpoint here because we may not really need one; sub
4723 # scan_list will do that if necessary
4724 $line_start_index_to_go = $i_test + 1;
4725 $gnu_position_predictor = $test_position;
4726 }
4727 }
4728 }
4729
4730 my $halfway =
4731 maximum_line_length_for_level($level) - $rOpts_maximum_line_length / 2;
4732
4733 # Check for decreasing depth ..
4734 # Note that one token may have both decreasing and then increasing
4735 # depth. For example, (level, ci) can go from (1,1) to (2,0). So,
4736 # in this example we would first go back to (1,0) then up to (2,0)
4737 # in a single call.
4738 if ( $level < $current_level || $ci_level < $current_ci_level ) {
4739
4740 # loop to find the first entry at or completely below this level
4741 my ( $lev, $ci_lev );
4742 while (1) {
4743 if ($max_gnu_stack_index) {
4744
4745 # save index of token which closes this level
4746 $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index]->set_closed($max_index_to_go);
4747
4748 # Undo any extra indentation if we saw no commas
4749 my $available_spaces =
4750 $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index]->get_available_spaces();
4751
4752 my $comma_count = 0;
4753 my $arrow_count = 0;
4754 if ( $type eq '}' || $type eq ')' ) {
4755 $comma_count = $gnu_comma_count{$total_depth};
4756 $arrow_count = $gnu_arrow_count{$total_depth};
4757 $comma_count = 0 unless $comma_count;
4758 $arrow_count = 0 unless $arrow_count;
4759 }
4760 $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index]->set_comma_count($comma_count);
4761 $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index]->set_arrow_count($arrow_count);
4762
4763 if ( $available_spaces > 0 ) {
4764
4765 if ( $comma_count <= 0 || $arrow_count > 0 ) {
4766
4767 my $i = $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index]->get_index();
4768 my $seqno =
4769 $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index]
4770 ->get_sequence_number();
4771
4772 # Be sure this item was created in this batch. This
4773 # should be true because we delete any available
4774 # space from open items at the end of each batch.
4775 if ( $gnu_sequence_number != $seqno
4776 || $i > $max_gnu_item_index )
4777 {
4778 warning(
4779"Program bug with -lp. seqno=$seqno should be $gnu_sequence_number and i=$i should be less than max=$max_gnu_item_index\n"
4780 );
4781 report_definite_bug();
4782 }
4783
4784 else {
4785 if ( $arrow_count == 0 ) {
4786 $gnu_item_list[$i]
4787 ->permanently_decrease_available_spaces(
4788 $available_spaces);
4789 }
4790 else {
4791 $gnu_item_list[$i]
4792 ->tentatively_decrease_available_spaces(
4793 $available_spaces);
4794 }
4795 foreach my $j ( $i + 1 .. $max_gnu_item_index ) {
4796 $gnu_item_list[$j]
4797 ->decrease_SPACES($available_spaces);
4798 }
4799 }
4800 }
4801 }
4802
4803 # go down one level
4804 --$max_gnu_stack_index;
4805 $lev = $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index]->get_level();
4806 $ci_lev = $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index]->get_ci_level();
4807
4808 # stop when we reach a level at or below the current level
4809 if ( $lev <= $level && $ci_lev <= $ci_level ) {
4810 $space_count =
4811 $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index]->get_spaces();
4812 $current_level = $lev;
4813 $current_ci_level = $ci_lev;
4814 last;
4815 }
4816 }
4817
4818 # reached bottom of stack .. should never happen because
4819 # only negative levels can get here, and $level was forced
4820 # to be positive above.
4821 else {
4822 warning(
4823"program bug with -lp: stack_error. level=$level; lev=$lev; ci_level=$ci_level; ci_lev=$ci_lev; rerun with -nlp\n"
4824 );
4825 report_definite_bug();
4826 last;
4827 }
4828 }
4829 }
4830
4831 # handle increasing depth
4832 if ( $level > $current_level || $ci_level > $current_ci_level ) {
4833
4834 # Compute the standard incremental whitespace. This will be
4835 # the minimum incremental whitespace that will be used. This
4836 # choice results in a smooth transition between the gnu-style
4837 # and the standard style.
4838 my $standard_increment =
4839 ( $level - $current_level ) * $rOpts_indent_columns +
4840 ( $ci_level - $current_ci_level ) * $rOpts_continuation_indentation;
4841
4842 # Now we have to define how much extra incremental space
4843 # ("$available_space") we want. This extra space will be
4844 # reduced as necessary when long lines are encountered or when
4845 # it becomes clear that we do not have a good list.
4846 my $available_space = 0;
4847 my $align_paren = 0;
4848 my $excess = 0;
4849
4850 # initialization on empty stack..
4851 if ( $max_gnu_stack_index == 0 ) {
4852 $space_count = $level * $rOpts_indent_columns;
4853 }
4854
4855 # if this is a BLOCK, add the standard increment
4856 elsif ($last_nonblank_block_type) {
4857 $space_count += $standard_increment;
4858 }
4859
4860 # if last nonblank token was not structural indentation,
4861 # just use standard increment
4862 elsif ( $last_nonblank_type ne '{' ) {
4863 $space_count += $standard_increment;
4864 }
4865
4866 # otherwise use the space to the first non-blank level change token
4867 else {
4868
4869 $space_count = $gnu_position_predictor;
4870
4871 my $min_gnu_indentation =
4872 $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index]->get_spaces();
4873
4874 $available_space = $space_count - $min_gnu_indentation;
4875 if ( $available_space >= $standard_increment ) {
4876 $min_gnu_indentation += $standard_increment;
4877 }
4878 elsif ( $available_space > 1 ) {
4879 $min_gnu_indentation += $available_space + 1;
4880 }
4881 elsif ( $last_nonblank_token =~ /^[\{\[\(]$/ ) {
4882 if ( ( $tightness{$last_nonblank_token} < 2 ) ) {
4883 $min_gnu_indentation += 2;
4884 }
4885 else {
4886 $min_gnu_indentation += 1;
4887 }
4888 }
4889 else {
4890 $min_gnu_indentation += $standard_increment;
4891 }
4892 $available_space = $space_count - $min_gnu_indentation;
4893
4894 if ( $available_space < 0 ) {
4895 $space_count = $min_gnu_indentation;
4896 $available_space = 0;
4897 }
4898 $align_paren = 1;
4899 }
4900
4901 # update state, but not on a blank token
4902 if ( $types_to_go[$max_index_to_go] ne 'b' ) {
4903
4904 $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index]->set_have_child(1);
4905
4906 ++$max_gnu_stack_index;
4907 $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index] =
4908 new_lp_indentation_item( $space_count, $level, $ci_level,
4909 $available_space, $align_paren );
4910
4911 # If the opening paren is beyond the half-line length, then
4912 # we will use the minimum (standard) indentation. This will
4913 # help avoid problems associated with running out of space
4914 # near the end of a line. As a result, in deeply nested
4915 # lists, there will be some indentations which are limited
4916 # to this minimum standard indentation. But the most deeply
4917 # nested container will still probably be able to shift its
4918 # parameters to the right for proper alignment, so in most
4919 # cases this will not be noticeable.
4920 if ( $available_space > 0 && $space_count > $halfway ) {
4921 $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index]
4922 ->tentatively_decrease_available_spaces($available_space);
4923 }
4924 }
4925 }
4926
4927 # Count commas and look for non-list characters. Once we see a
4928 # non-list character, we give up and don't look for any more commas.
4929 if ( $type eq '=>' ) {
4930 $gnu_arrow_count{$total_depth}++;
4931
4932 # tentatively treating '=>' like '=' for estimating breaks
4933 # TODO: this could use some experimentation
4934 $last_gnu_equals{$total_depth} = $max_index_to_go;
4935 }
4936
4937 elsif ( $type eq ',' ) {
4938 $gnu_comma_count{$total_depth}++;
4939 }
4940
4941 elsif ( $is_assignment{$type} ) {
4942 $last_gnu_equals{$total_depth} = $max_index_to_go;
4943 }
4944
4945 # this token might start a new line
4946 # if this is a non-blank..
4947 if ( $type ne 'b' ) {
4948
4949 # and if ..
4950 if (
4951
4952 # this is the first nonblank token of the line
4953 $max_index_to_go == 1 && $types_to_go[0] eq 'b'
4954
4955 # or previous character was one of these:
4956 || $last_nonblank_type_to_go =~ /^([\:\?\,f])$/
4957
4958 # or previous character was opening and this does not close it
4959 || ( $last_nonblank_type_to_go eq '{' && $type ne '}' )
4960 || ( $last_nonblank_type_to_go eq '(' and $type ne ')' )
4961
4962 # or this token is one of these:
4963 || $type =~ /^([\.]|\|\||\&\&)$/
4964
4965 # or this is a closing structure
4966 || ( $last_nonblank_type_to_go eq '}'
4967 && $last_nonblank_token_to_go eq $last_nonblank_type_to_go )
4968
4969 # or previous token was keyword 'return'
4970 || ( $last_nonblank_type_to_go eq 'k'
4971 && ( $last_nonblank_token_to_go eq 'return' && $type ne '{' ) )
4972
4973 # or starting a new line at certain keywords is fine
4974 || ( $type eq 'k'
4975 && $is_if_unless_and_or_last_next_redo_return{$token} )
4976
4977 # or this is after an assignment after a closing structure
4978 || (
4979 $is_assignment{$last_nonblank_type_to_go}
4980 && (
4981 $last_last_nonblank_type_to_go =~ /^[\}\)\]]$/
4982
4983 # and it is significantly to the right
4984 || $gnu_position_predictor > $halfway
4985 )
4986 )
4987 )
4988 {
4989 check_for_long_gnu_style_lines();
4990 $line_start_index_to_go = $max_index_to_go;
4991
4992 # back up 1 token if we want to break before that type
4993 # otherwise, we may strand tokens like '?' or ':' on a line
4994 if ( $line_start_index_to_go > 0 ) {
4995 if ( $last_nonblank_type_to_go eq 'k' ) {
4996
4997 if ( $want_break_before{$last_nonblank_token_to_go} ) {
4998 $line_start_index_to_go--;
4999 }
5000 }
5001 elsif ( $want_break_before{$last_nonblank_type_to_go} ) {
5002 $line_start_index_to_go--;
5003 }
5004 }
5005 }
5006 }
5007
5008 # remember the predicted position of this token on the output line
5009 if ( $max_index_to_go > $line_start_index_to_go ) {
5010 $gnu_position_predictor =
5011 total_line_length( $line_start_index_to_go, $max_index_to_go );
5012 }
5013 else {
5014 $gnu_position_predictor =
5015 $space_count + $token_lengths_to_go[$max_index_to_go];
5016 }
5017
5018 # store the indentation object for this token
5019 # this allows us to manipulate the leading whitespace
5020 # (in case we have to reduce indentation to fit a line) without
5021 # having to change any token values
5022 $leading_spaces_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index];
5023 $reduced_spaces_to_go[$max_index_to_go] =
5024 ( $max_gnu_stack_index > 0 && $ci_level )
5025 ? $gnu_stack[ $max_gnu_stack_index - 1 ]
5026 : $gnu_stack[$max_gnu_stack_index];
5027 return;
5028}
5029
5030sub check_for_long_gnu_style_lines {
5031
5032 # look at the current estimated maximum line length, and
5033 # remove some whitespace if it exceeds the desired maximum
5034
5035 # this is only for the '-lp' style
5036 return unless ($rOpts_line_up_parentheses);
5037
5038 # nothing can be done if no stack items defined for this line
5039 return if ( $max_gnu_item_index == UNDEFINED_INDEX );
5040
5041 # see if we have exceeded the maximum desired line length
5042 # keep 2 extra free because they are needed in some cases
5043 # (result of trial-and-error testing)
5044 my $spaces_needed =
5045 $gnu_position_predictor - maximum_line_length($max_index_to_go) + 2;
5046
5047 return if ( $spaces_needed <= 0 );
5048
5049 # We are over the limit, so try to remove a requested number of
5050 # spaces from leading whitespace. We are only allowed to remove
5051 # from whitespace items created on this batch, since others have
5052 # already been used and cannot be undone.
5053 my @candidates = ();
5054 my $i;
5055
5056 # loop over all whitespace items created for the current batch
5057 for ( $i = 0 ; $i <= $max_gnu_item_index ; $i++ ) {
5058 my $item = $gnu_item_list[$i];
5059
5060 # item must still be open to be a candidate (otherwise it
5061 # cannot influence the current token)
5062 next if ( $item->get_closed() >= 0 );
5063
5064 my $available_spaces = $item->get_available_spaces();
5065
5066 if ( $available_spaces > 0 ) {
5067 push( @candidates, [ $i, $available_spaces ] );
5068 }
5069 }
5070
5071 return unless (@candidates);
5072
5073 # sort by available whitespace so that we can remove whitespace
5074 # from the maximum available first
5075 @candidates = sort { $b->[1] <=> $a->[1] } @candidates;
5076
5077 # keep removing whitespace until we are done or have no more
5078 foreach my $candidate (@candidates) {
5079 my ( $i, $available_spaces ) = @{$candidate};
5080 my $deleted_spaces =
5081 ( $available_spaces > $spaces_needed )
5082 ? $spaces_needed
5083 : $available_spaces;
5084
5085 # remove the incremental space from this item
5086 $gnu_item_list[$i]->decrease_available_spaces($deleted_spaces);
5087
5088 my $i_debug = $i;
5089
5090 # update the leading whitespace of this item and all items
5091 # that came after it
5092 for ( ; $i <= $max_gnu_item_index ; $i++ ) {
5093
5094 my $old_spaces = $gnu_item_list[$i]->get_spaces();
5095 if ( $old_spaces >= $deleted_spaces ) {
5096 $gnu_item_list[$i]->decrease_SPACES($deleted_spaces);
5097 }
5098
5099 # shouldn't happen except for code bug:
5100 else {
5101 my $level = $gnu_item_list[$i_debug]->get_level();
5102 my $ci_level = $gnu_item_list[$i_debug]->get_ci_level();
5103 my $old_level = $gnu_item_list[$i]->get_level();
5104 my $old_ci_level = $gnu_item_list[$i]->get_ci_level();
5105 warning(
5106"program bug with -lp: want to delete $deleted_spaces from item $i, but old=$old_spaces deleted: lev=$level ci=$ci_level deleted: level=$old_level ci=$ci_level\n"
5107 );
5108 report_definite_bug();
5109 }
5110 }
5111 $gnu_position_predictor -= $deleted_spaces;
5112 $spaces_needed -= $deleted_spaces;
5113 last unless ( $spaces_needed > 0 );
5114 }
5115 return;
5116}
5117
5118sub finish_lp_batch {
5119
5120 # This routine is called once after each output stream batch is
5121 # finished to undo indentation for all incomplete -lp
5122 # indentation levels. It is too risky to leave a level open,
5123 # because then we can't backtrack in case of a long line to follow.
5124 # This means that comments and blank lines will disrupt this
5125 # indentation style. But the vertical aligner may be able to
5126 # get the space back if there are side comments.
5127
5128 # this is only for the 'lp' style
5129 return unless ($rOpts_line_up_parentheses);
5130
5131 # nothing can be done if no stack items defined for this line
5132 return if ( $max_gnu_item_index == UNDEFINED_INDEX );
5133
5134 # loop over all whitespace items created for the current batch
5135 foreach my $i ( 0 .. $max_gnu_item_index ) {
5136 my $item = $gnu_item_list[$i];
5137
5138 # only look for open items
5139 next if ( $item->get_closed() >= 0 );
5140
5141 # Tentatively remove all of the available space
5142 # (The vertical aligner will try to get it back later)
5143 my $available_spaces = $item->get_available_spaces();
5144 if ( $available_spaces > 0 ) {
5145
5146 # delete incremental space for this item
5147 $gnu_item_list[$i]
5148 ->tentatively_decrease_available_spaces($available_spaces);
5149
5150 # Reduce the total indentation space of any nodes that follow
5151 # Note that any such nodes must necessarily be dependents
5152 # of this node.
5153 foreach ( $i + 1 .. $max_gnu_item_index ) {
5154 $gnu_item_list[$_]->decrease_SPACES($available_spaces);
5155 }
5156 }
5157 }
5158 return;
5159}
5160
5161sub reduce_lp_indentation {
5162
5163 # reduce the leading whitespace at token $i if possible by $spaces_needed
5164 # (a large value of $spaces_needed will remove all excess space)
5165 # NOTE: to be called from scan_list only for a sequence of tokens
5166 # contained between opening and closing parens/braces/brackets
5167
5168 my ( $i, $spaces_wanted ) = @_;
5169 my $deleted_spaces = 0;
5170
5171 my $item = $leading_spaces_to_go[$i];
5172 my $available_spaces = $item->get_available_spaces();
5173
5174 if (
5175 $available_spaces > 0
5176 && ( ( $spaces_wanted <= $available_spaces )
5177 || !$item->get_have_child() )
5178 )
5179 {
5180
5181 # we'll remove these spaces, but mark them as recoverable
5182 $deleted_spaces =
5183 $item->tentatively_decrease_available_spaces($spaces_wanted);
5184 }
5185
5186 return $deleted_spaces;
5187}
5188
5189sub token_sequence_length {
5190
5191 # return length of tokens ($ibeg .. $iend) including $ibeg & $iend
5192 # returns 0 if $ibeg > $iend (shouldn't happen)
5193 my ( $ibeg, $iend ) = @_;
5194 return 0 if ( $iend < 0 || $ibeg > $iend );
5195 return $summed_lengths_to_go[ $iend + 1 ] if ( $ibeg < 0 );
5196 return $summed_lengths_to_go[ $iend + 1 ] - $summed_lengths_to_go[$ibeg];
5197}
5198
5199sub total_line_length {
5200
5201 # return length of a line of tokens ($ibeg .. $iend)
5202 my ( $ibeg, $iend ) = @_;
5203 return leading_spaces_to_go($ibeg) + token_sequence_length( $ibeg, $iend );
5204}
5205
5206sub maximum_line_length_for_level {
5207
5208 # return maximum line length for line starting with a given level
5209 my $maximum_line_length = $rOpts_maximum_line_length;
5210
5211 # Modify if -vmll option is selected
5212 if ($rOpts_variable_maximum_line_length) {
5213 my $level = shift;
5214 if ( $level < 0 ) { $level = 0 }
5215 $maximum_line_length += $level * $rOpts_indent_columns;
5216 }
5217 return $maximum_line_length;
5218}
5219
5220sub maximum_line_length {
5221
5222 # return maximum line length for line starting with the token at given index
5223 my $ii = shift;
5224 return maximum_line_length_for_level( $levels_to_go[$ii] );
5225}
5226
5227sub excess_line_length {
5228
5229 # return number of characters by which a line of tokens ($ibeg..$iend)
5230 # exceeds the allowable line length.
5231 my ( $ibeg, $iend, $ignore_left_weld, $ignore_right_weld ) = @_;
5232
5233 # Include left and right weld lengths unless requested not to
5234 my $wl = $ignore_left_weld ? 0 : weld_len_left_to_go($iend);
5235 my $wr = $ignore_right_weld ? 0 : weld_len_right_to_go($iend);
5236
5237 return total_line_length( $ibeg, $iend ) + $wl + $wr -
5238 maximum_line_length($ibeg);
5239}
5240
5241sub wrapup {
5242
5243 # flush buffer and write any informative messages
5244 my $self = shift;
5245
5246 $self->flush();
5247 $file_writer_object->decrement_output_line_number()
5248 ; # fix up line number since it was incremented
5249 we_are_at_the_last_line();
5250 if ( $added_semicolon_count > 0 ) {
5251 my $first = ( $added_semicolon_count > 1 ) ? "First" : "";
5252 my $what =
5253 ( $added_semicolon_count > 1 ) ? "semicolons were" : "semicolon was";
5254 write_logfile_entry("$added_semicolon_count $what added:\n");
5255 write_logfile_entry(
5256 " $first at input line $first_added_semicolon_at\n");
5257
5258 if ( $added_semicolon_count > 1 ) {
5259 write_logfile_entry(
5260 " Last at input line $last_added_semicolon_at\n");
5261 }
5262 write_logfile_entry(" (Use -nasc to prevent semicolon addition)\n");
5263 write_logfile_entry("\n");
5264 }
5265
5266 if ( $deleted_semicolon_count > 0 ) {
5267 my $first = ( $deleted_semicolon_count > 1 ) ? "First" : "";
5268 my $what =
5269 ( $deleted_semicolon_count > 1 )
5270 ? "semicolons were"
5271 : "semicolon was";
5272 write_logfile_entry(
5273 "$deleted_semicolon_count unnecessary $what deleted:\n");
5274 write_logfile_entry(
5275 " $first at input line $first_deleted_semicolon_at\n");
5276
5277 if ( $deleted_semicolon_count > 1 ) {
5278 write_logfile_entry(
5279 " Last at input line $last_deleted_semicolon_at\n");
5280 }
5281 write_logfile_entry(" (Use -ndsc to prevent semicolon deletion)\n");
5282 write_logfile_entry("\n");
5283 }
5284
5285 if ( $embedded_tab_count > 0 ) {
5286 my $first = ( $embedded_tab_count > 1 ) ? "First" : "";
5287 my $what =
5288 ( $embedded_tab_count > 1 )
5289 ? "quotes or patterns"
5290 : "quote or pattern";
5291 write_logfile_entry("$embedded_tab_count $what had embedded tabs:\n");
5292 write_logfile_entry(
5293"This means the display of this script could vary with device or software\n"
5294 );
5295 write_logfile_entry(" $first at input line $first_embedded_tab_at\n");
5296
5297 if ( $embedded_tab_count > 1 ) {
5298 write_logfile_entry(
5299 " Last at input line $last_embedded_tab_at\n");
5300 }
5301 write_logfile_entry("\n");
5302 }
5303
5304 if ($first_tabbing_disagreement) {
5305 write_logfile_entry(
5306"First indentation disagreement seen at input line $first_tabbing_disagreement\n"
5307 );
5308 }
5309
5310 if ($in_tabbing_disagreement) {
5311 write_logfile_entry(
5312"Ending with indentation disagreement which started at input line $in_tabbing_disagreement\n"
5313 );
5314 }
5315 else {
5316
5317 if ($last_tabbing_disagreement) {
5318
5319 write_logfile_entry(
5320"Last indentation disagreement seen at input line $last_tabbing_disagreement\n"
5321 );
5322 }
5323 else {
5324 write_logfile_entry("No indentation disagreement seen\n");
5325 }
5326 }
5327 if ($first_tabbing_disagreement) {
5328 write_logfile_entry(
5329"Note: Indentation disagreement detection is not accurate for outdenting and -lp.\n"
5330 );
5331 }
5332 write_logfile_entry("\n");
5333
5334 $vertical_aligner_object->report_anything_unusual();
5335
5336 $file_writer_object->report_line_length_errors();
5337
5338 return;
5339}
5340
5341sub check_options {
5342
5343 # This routine is called to check the Opts hash after it is defined
5344 $rOpts = shift;
5345
5346 initialize_whitespace_hashes();
5347 initialize_bond_strength_hashes();
5348
5349 make_static_block_comment_pattern();
5350 make_static_side_comment_pattern();
5351 make_closing_side_comment_prefix();
5352 make_closing_side_comment_list_pattern();
5353 $format_skipping_pattern_begin =
5354 make_format_skipping_pattern( 'format-skipping-begin', '#<<<' );
5355 $format_skipping_pattern_end =
5356 make_format_skipping_pattern( 'format-skipping-end', '#>>>' );
5357
5358 # If closing side comments ARE selected, then we can safely
5359 # delete old closing side comments unless closing side comment
5360 # warnings are requested. This is a good idea because it will
5361 # eliminate any old csc's which fall below the line count threshold.
5362 # We cannot do this if warnings are turned on, though, because we
5363 # might delete some text which has been added. So that must
5364 # be handled when comments are created.
5365 if ( $rOpts->{'closing-side-comments'} ) {
5366 if ( !$rOpts->{'closing-side-comment-warnings'} ) {
5367 $rOpts->{'delete-closing-side-comments'} = 1;
5368 }
5369 }
5370
5371 # If closing side comments ARE NOT selected, but warnings ARE
5372 # selected and we ARE DELETING csc's, then we will pretend to be
5373 # adding with a huge interval. This will force the comments to be
5374 # generated for comparison with the old comments, but not added.
5375 elsif ( $rOpts->{'closing-side-comment-warnings'} ) {
5376 if ( $rOpts->{'delete-closing-side-comments'} ) {
5377 $rOpts->{'delete-closing-side-comments'} = 0;
5378 $rOpts->{'closing-side-comments'} = 1;
5379 $rOpts->{'closing-side-comment-interval'} = 100000000;
5380 }
5381 }
5382
5383 make_bli_pattern();
5384 make_block_brace_vertical_tightness_pattern();
5385 make_blank_line_pattern();
5386 make_keyword_group_list_pattern();
5387
5388 # Make initial list of desired one line block types
5389 # They will be modified by 'prepare_cuddled_block_types'
5390 %want_one_line_block = %is_sort_map_grep_eval;
5391
5392 prepare_cuddled_block_types();
5393 if ( $rOpts->{'dump-cuddled-block-list'} ) {
5394 dump_cuddled_block_list(*STDOUT);
5395 Exit(0);
5396 }
5397
5398 if ( $rOpts->{'line-up-parentheses'} ) {
5399
5400 if ( $rOpts->{'indent-only'}
5401 || !$rOpts->{'add-newlines'}
5402 || !$rOpts->{'delete-old-newlines'} )
5403 {
5404 Warn(<<EOM);
5405-----------------------------------------------------------------------
5406Conflict: -lp conflicts with -io, -fnl, -nanl, or -ndnl; ignoring -lp
5407
5408The -lp indentation logic requires that perltidy be able to coordinate
5409arbitrarily large numbers of line breakpoints. This isn't possible
5410with these flags. Sometimes an acceptable workaround is to use -wocb=3
5411-----------------------------------------------------------------------
5412EOM
5413 $rOpts->{'line-up-parentheses'} = 0;
5414 }
5415 }
5416
5417 # At present, tabs are not compatible with the line-up-parentheses style
5418 # (it would be possible to entab the total leading whitespace
5419 # just prior to writing the line, if desired).
5420 if ( $rOpts->{'line-up-parentheses'} && $rOpts->{'tabs'} ) {
5421 Warn(<<EOM);
5422Conflict: -t (tabs) cannot be used with the -lp option; ignoring -t; see -et.
5423EOM
5424 $rOpts->{'tabs'} = 0;
5425 }
5426
5427 # Likewise, tabs are not compatible with outdenting..
5428 if ( $rOpts->{'outdent-keywords'} && $rOpts->{'tabs'} ) {
5429 Warn(<<EOM);
5430Conflict: -t (tabs) cannot be used with the -okw options; ignoring -t; see -et.
5431EOM
5432 $rOpts->{'tabs'} = 0;
5433 }
5434
5435 if ( $rOpts->{'outdent-labels'} && $rOpts->{'tabs'} ) {
5436 Warn(<<EOM);
5437Conflict: -t (tabs) cannot be used with the -ola option; ignoring -t; see -et.
5438EOM
5439 $rOpts->{'tabs'} = 0;
5440 }
5441

5819 sub prepare_cuddled_block_types {
5820
5821 # the cuddled-else style, if used, is controlled by a hash that
5822 # we construct here
5823
5824 # Include keywords here which should not be cuddled
5825
5826 my $cuddled_string = "";
5827 if ( $rOpts->{'cuddled-else'} ) {
5828
5829 # set the default
5830 $cuddled_string = 'elsif else continue catch finally'
5831 unless ( $rOpts->{'cuddled-block-list-exclusive'} );
5832
5833 # This is the old equivalent but more complex version
5834 # $cuddled_string = 'if-elsif-else unless-elsif-else -continue ';
5835
5836 # Add users other blocks to be cuddled
5837 my $cuddled_block_list = $rOpts->{'cuddled-block-list'};
5838 if ($cuddled_block_list) {
5839 $cuddled_string .= " " . $cuddled_block_list;
5840 }
5841
5842 }
5843
5844 # If we have a cuddled string of the form
5845 # 'try-catch-finally'
5846
5847 # we want to prepare a hash of the form
5848
5849 # $rcuddled_block_types = {
5850 # 'try' => {
5851 # 'catch' => 1,
5852 # 'finally' => 1
5853 # },
5854 # };
5855
5856 # use -dcbl to dump this hash
5857
5858 # Multiple such strings are input as a space or comma separated list
5859
5860 # If we get two lists with the same leading type, such as
5861 # -cbl = "-try-catch-finally -try-catch-otherwise"
5862 # then they will get merged as follows:
5863 # $rcuddled_block_types = {
5864 # 'try' => {
5865 # 'catch' => 1,
5866 # 'finally' => 2,
5867 # 'otherwise' => 1,
5868 # },
5869 # };
5870 # This will allow either type of chain to be followed.
5871
5872 $cuddled_string =~ s/,/ /g; # allow space or comma separated lists
5873 my @cuddled_strings = split /\s+/, $cuddled_string;
5874
5875 $rcuddled_block_types = {};
5876
5877 # process each dash-separated string...
5878 my $string_count = 0;
5879 foreach my $string (@cuddled_strings) {
5880 next unless $string;
5881 my @words = split /-+/, $string; # allow multiple dashes
5882
5883 # we could look for and report possible errors here...
5884 next unless ( @words > 0 );
5885
5886 # allow either '-continue' or *-continue' for arbitrary starting type
5887 my $start = '*';
5888
5889 # a single word without dashes is a secondary block type
5890 if ( @words > 1 ) {
5891 $start = shift @words;
5892 }
5893
5894 # always make an entry for the leading word. If none follow, this
5895 # will still prevent a wildcard from matching this word.
5896 if ( !defined( $rcuddled_block_types->{$start} ) ) {
5897 $rcuddled_block_types->{$start} = {};
5898 }
5899
5900 # The count gives the original word order in case we ever want it.
5901 $string_count++;
5902 my $word_count = 0;
5903 foreach my $word (@words) {
5904 next unless $word;
5905 if ( $no_cuddle{$word} ) {
5906 Warn(
5907"## Ignoring keyword '$word' in -cbl; does not seem right\n"
5908 );
5909 next;
5910 }
5911 $word_count++;
5912 $rcuddled_block_types->{$start}->{$word} =
5913 1; #"$string_count.$word_count";
5914
5915 # git#9: Remove this word from the list of desired one-line
5916 # blocks
5917 $want_one_line_block{$word} = 0;
5918 }
5919 }
5920 return;
5921 }
5922}

6115sub make_block_pattern {
6116
6117 # given a string of block-type keywords, return a regex to match them
6118 # The only tricky part is that labels are indicated with a single ':'
6119 # and the 'sub' token text may have additional text after it (name of
6120 # sub).
6121 #
6122 # Example:
6123 #
6124 # input string: "if else elsif unless while for foreach do : sub";
6125 # pattern: '^((if|else|elsif|unless|while|for|foreach|do|\w+:)$|sub)';
6126
6127 # Minor Update:
6128 #
6129 # To distinguish between anonymous subs and named subs, use 'sub' to
6130 # indicate a named sub, and 'asub' to indicate an anonymous sub
6131
6132 my ( $abbrev, $string ) = @_;
6133 my @list = split_words($string);
6134 my @words = ();
6135 my %seen;
6136 for my $i (@list) {
6137 if ( $i eq '*' ) { my $pattern = '^.*'; return $pattern }
6138 next if $seen{$i};
6139 $seen{$i} = 1;
6140 if ( $i eq 'sub' ) {
6141 }
6142 elsif ( $i eq 'asub' ) {
6143 }
6144 elsif ( $i eq ';' ) {
6145 push @words, ';';
6146 }
6147 elsif ( $i eq '{' ) {
6148 push @words, '\{';
6149 }
6150 elsif ( $i eq ':' ) {
6151 push @words, '\w+:';
6152 }
6153 elsif ( $i =~ /^\w/ ) {
6154 push @words, $i;
6155 }
6156 else {
6157 Warn("unrecognized block type $i after $abbrev, ignoring\n");
6158 }
6159 }
6160 my $pattern = '(' . join( '|', @words ) . ')$';
6161 my $sub_patterns = "";
6162 if ( $seen{'sub'} ) {
6163 $sub_patterns .= '|' . $SUB_PATTERN;
6164 }
6165 if ( $seen{'asub'} ) {
6166 $sub_patterns .= '|' . $ASUB_PATTERN;
6167 }
6168 if ($sub_patterns) {
6169 $pattern = '(' . $pattern . $sub_patterns . ')';
6170 }
6171 $pattern = '^' . $pattern;
6172 return $pattern;
6173}

6297 sub is_essential_whitespace {
6298
6299 # Essential whitespace means whitespace which cannot be safely deleted
6300 # without risking the introduction of a syntax error.
6301 # We are given three tokens and their types:
6302 # ($tokenl, $typel) is the token to the left of the space in question
6303 # ($tokenr, $typer) is the token to the right of the space in question
6304 # ($tokenll, $typell) is previous nonblank token to the left of $tokenl
6305 #
6306 # This is a slow routine but is not needed too often except when -mangle
6307 # is used.
6308 #
6309 # Note: This routine should almost never need to be changed. It is
6310 # for avoiding syntax problems rather than for formatting.
6311 my ( $tokenll, $typell, $tokenl, $typel, $tokenr, $typer ) = @_;
6312
6313 my $result =
6314
6315 # never combine two bare words or numbers
6316 # examples: and ::ok(1)
6317 # return ::spw(...)
6318 # for bla::bla:: abc
6319 # example is "%overload:: and" in files Dumpvalue.pm or colonbug.pl
6320 # $input eq"quit" to make $inputeq"quit"
6321 # my $size=-s::SINK if $file; <==OK but we won't do it
6322 # don't join something like: for bla::bla:: abc
6323 # example is "%overload:: and" in files Dumpvalue.pm or colonbug.pl
6324 ( ( $tokenl =~ /([\'\w]|\:\:)$/ && $typel ne 'CORE::' )
6325 && ( $tokenr =~ /^([\'\w]|\:\:)/ ) )
6326
6327 # do not combine a number with a concatenation dot
6328 # example: pom.caputo:
6329 # $vt100_compatible ? "\e[0;0H" : ('-' x 78 . "\n");
6330 || ( ( $typel eq 'n' ) && ( $tokenr eq '.' ) )
6331 || ( ( $typer eq 'n' ) && ( $tokenl eq '.' ) )
6332
6333 # do not join a minus with a bare word, because you might form
6334 # a file test operator. Example from Complex.pm:
6335 # if (CORE::abs($z - i) < $eps); "z-i" would be taken as a file test.
6336 || ( ( $tokenl eq '-' ) && ( $tokenr =~ /^[_A-Za-z]$/ ) )
6337
6338 # do not join a bare word with a minus, like between 'Send' and
6339 # '-recipients' here <<snippets/space3.in>>
6340 # my $msg = new Fax::Send
6341 # -recipients => $to,
6342 # -data => $data;
6343 # This is the safest thing to do. If we had the token to the right of
6344 # the minus we could do a better check.
6345 || ( ( $tokenr eq '-' ) && ( $typel eq 'w' ) )
6346
6347 # and something like this could become ambiguous without space
6348 # after the '-':
6349 # use constant III=>1;
6350 # $a = $b - III;
6351 # and even this:
6352 # $a = - III;
6353 || ( ( $tokenl eq '-' )
6354 && ( $typer =~ /^[wC]$/ && $tokenr =~ /^[_A-Za-z]/ ) )
6355
6356 # '= -' should not become =- or you will get a warning
6357 # about reversed -=
6358 # || ($tokenr eq '-')
6359
6360 # keep a space between a quote and a bareword to prevent the
6361 # bareword from becoming a quote modifier.
6362 || ( ( $typel eq 'Q' ) && ( $tokenr =~ /^[a-zA-Z_]/ ) )
6363
6364 # keep a space between a token ending in '$' and any word;
6365 # this caused trouble: "die @$ if $@"
6366 || ( ( $typel eq 'i' && $tokenl =~ /\$$/ )
6367 && ( $tokenr =~ /^[a-zA-Z_]/ ) )
6368
6369 # perl is very fussy about spaces before <<
6370 || ( $tokenr =~ /^\<\</ )
6371
6372 # avoid combining tokens to create new meanings. Example:
6373 # $a+ +$b must not become $a++$b
6374 || ( $is_digraph{ $tokenl . $tokenr } )
6375 || ( $is_trigraph{ $tokenl . $tokenr } )
6376
6377 # another example: do not combine these two &'s:
6378 # allow_options & &OPT_EXECCGI
6379 || ( $is_digraph{ $tokenl . substr( $tokenr, 0, 1 ) } )
6380
6381 # don't combine $$ or $# with any alphanumeric
6382 # (testfile mangle.t with --mangle)
6383 || ( ( $tokenl =~ /^\$[\$\#]$/ ) && ( $tokenr =~ /^\w/ ) )
6384
6385 # retain any space after possible filehandle
6386 # (testfiles prnterr1.t with --extrude and mangle.t with --mangle)
6387 || ( $typel eq 'Z' )
6388
6389 # Perl is sensitive to whitespace after the + here:
6390 # $b = xvals $a + 0.1 * yvals $a;
6391 || ( $typell eq 'Z' && $typel =~ /^[\/\?\+\-\*]$/ )
6392
6393 # keep paren separate in 'use Foo::Bar ()'
6394 || ( $tokenr eq '('
6395 && $typel eq 'w'
6396 && $typell eq 'k'
6397 && $tokenll eq 'use' )
6398
6399 # keep any space between filehandle and paren:
6400 # file mangle.t with --mangle:
6401 || ( $typel eq 'Y' && $tokenr eq '(' )
6402
6403 # retain any space after here doc operator ( hereerr.t)
6404 || ( $typel eq 'h' )
6405
6406 # be careful with a space around ++ and --, to avoid ambiguity as to
6407 # which token it applies
6408 || ( ( $typer =~ /^(pp|mm)$/ ) && ( $tokenl !~ /^[\;\{\(\[]/ ) )
6409 || ( ( $typel =~ /^(\+\+|\-\-)$/ ) && ( $tokenr !~ /^[\;\}\)\]]/ ) )
6410
6411 # need space after foreach my; for example, this will fail in
6412 # older versions of Perl:
6413 # foreach my$ft(@filetypes)...
6414 || (
6415 $tokenl eq 'my'
6416
6417 # /^(for|foreach)$/
6418 && $is_for_foreach{$tokenll}
6419 && $tokenr =~ /^\$/
6420 )
6421
6422 # must have space between grep and left paren; "grep(" will fail
6423 || ( $tokenr eq '(' && $is_sort_grep_map{$tokenl} )
6424
6425 # don't stick numbers next to left parens, as in:
6426 #use Mail::Internet 1.28 (); (see Entity.pm, Head.pm, Test.pm)
6427 || ( ( $typel eq 'n' ) && ( $tokenr eq '(' ) )
6428
6429 # We must be sure that a space between a ? and a quoted string
6430 # remains if the space before the ? remains. [Loca.pm, lockarea]
6431 # ie,
6432 # $b=join $comma ? ',' : ':', @_; # ok
6433 # $b=join $comma?',' : ':', @_; # ok!
6434 # $b=join $comma ?',' : ':', @_; # error!
6435 # Not really required:
6436 ## || ( ( $typel eq '?' ) && ( $typer eq 'Q' ) )
6437
6438 # do not remove space between an '&' and a bare word because
6439 # it may turn into a function evaluation, like here
6440 # between '&' and 'O_ACCMODE', producing a syntax error [File.pm]
6441 # $opts{rdonly} = (($opts{mode} & O_ACCMODE) == O_RDONLY);
6442 || ( ( $typel eq '&' ) && ( $tokenr =~ /^[a-zA-Z_]/ ) )
6443
6444 # space stacked labels (TODO: check if really necessary)
6445 || ( $typel eq 'J' && $typer eq 'J' )
6446
6447 ; # the value of this long logic sequence is the result we want
6448##if ($typel eq 'j') {print STDERR "typel=$typel typer=$typer result='$result'\n"}
6449 return $result;
6450 }
6451}
