6618 ) = @saved_token;
6619 return;
6620 }
6621 }
6622
66231300ns sub token_length {
6624
6625 # Returns the length of a token, given:
6626 # $token=text of the token
6627 # $type = type
6628 # $not_first_token = should be TRUE if this is not the first token of
6629 # the line. It might the index of this token in an array. It is
6630 # used to test for a side comment vs a block comment.
6631 # Note: Eventually this should be the only routine determining the
6632 # length of a token in this package.
6633 my ( $token, $type, $not_first_token ) = @_;
6634 my $token_length = length($token);
6635
6636 # We mark lengths of side comments as just 1 if we are
6637 # ignoring their lengths when setting line breaks.
6638 $token_length = 1
6639 if ( $rOpts_ignore_side_comment_lengths
6640 && $not_first_token
6641 && $type eq '#' );
6642 return $token_length;
6643 }
6644
6645 sub rtoken_length {
6646
6647 # return length of ith token in @{$rtokens}
6648 my ($i) = @_;
6649 return token_length( $rinput_token_array->[$i]->[_TOKEN_],
6650 $rinput_token_array->[$i]->[_TYPE_], $i );
6651 }
6652
6653 # Routine to place the current token into the output stream.
6654 # Called once per output token.
6655 sub store_token_to_go {
6656
6657 my ( $self, $side_comment_follows ) = @_;
6658
6659 my $flag = $side_comment_follows ? 1 : $no_internal_newlines;
6660
6661 ++$max_index_to_go;
6662 $K_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = $Ktoken_vars;
6663 $tokens_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = $token;
6664 $types_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = $type;
6665 $nobreak_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = $flag;
6666 $old_breakpoint_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = 0;
6667 $forced_breakpoint_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = 0;
6668 $block_type_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = $block_type;
6669 $type_sequence_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = $type_sequence;
6670 $container_environment_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = $container_environment;
6671 $ci_levels_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = $ci_level;
6672 $mate_index_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = -1;
6673 $matching_token_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = '';
6674 $bond_strength_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = 0;
6675
6676 # Note: negative levels are currently retained as a diagnostic so that
6677 # the 'final indentation level' is correctly reported for bad scripts.
6678 # But this means that every use of $level as an index must be checked.
6679 # If this becomes too much of a problem, we might give up and just clip
6680 # them at zero.
6681 ## $levels_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = ( $level > 0 ) ? $level : 0;
6682 $levels_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = $level;
6683 $nesting_depth_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = ( $slevel >= 0 ) ? $slevel : 0;
6684
6685 # link the non-blank tokens
6686 my $iprev = $max_index_to_go - 1;
6687 $iprev-- if ( $iprev >= 0 && $types_to_go[$iprev] eq 'b' );
6688 $iprev_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = $iprev;
6689 $inext_to_go[$iprev] = $max_index_to_go
6690 if ( $iprev >= 0 && $type ne 'b' );
6691 $inext_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = $max_index_to_go + 1;
6692
6693 $token_lengths_to_go[$max_index_to_go] =
6694 token_length( $token, $type, $max_index_to_go );
6695
6696 # We keep a running sum of token lengths from the start of this batch:
6697 # summed_lengths_to_go[$i] = total length to just before token $i
6698 # summed_lengths_to_go[$i+1] = total length to just after token $i
6699 $summed_lengths_to_go[ $max_index_to_go + 1 ] =
6700 $summed_lengths_to_go[$max_index_to_go] +
6701 $token_lengths_to_go[$max_index_to_go];
6702
6703 # Define the indentation that this token would have if it started
6704 # a new line. We have to do this now because we need to know this
6705 # when considering one-line blocks.
6706 set_leading_whitespace( $level, $ci_level, $in_continued_quote );
6707
6708 # remember previous nonblank tokens seen
6709 if ( $type ne 'b' ) {
6710 $last_last_nonblank_index_to_go = $last_nonblank_index_to_go;
6711 $last_last_nonblank_type_to_go = $last_nonblank_type_to_go;
6712 $last_last_nonblank_token_to_go = $last_nonblank_token_to_go;
6713 $last_nonblank_index_to_go = $max_index_to_go;
6714 $last_nonblank_type_to_go = $type;
6715 $last_nonblank_token_to_go = $token;
6716 if ( $type eq ',' ) {
6717 $comma_count_in_batch++;
6718 }
6719 }
6720
6721 FORMATTER_DEBUG_FLAG_STORE && do {
6722 my ( $a, $b, $c ) = caller();
6723 print STDOUT
6724"STORE: from $a $c: storing token $token type $type lev=$level slev=$slevel at $max_index_to_go\n";
6725 };
6726 return;
6727 }
6728
6729 sub insert_new_token_to_go {
6730
6731 # insert a new token into the output stream. use same level as
6732 # previous token; assumes a character at max_index_to_go.
6733 my ( $self, @args ) = @_;
6734 save_current_token();
6735 ( $token, $type, $slevel, $no_internal_newlines ) = @args;
6736
6737 if ( $max_index_to_go == UNDEFINED_INDEX ) {
6738 warning("code bug: bad call to insert_new_token_to_go\n");
6739 }
6740 $level = $levels_to_go[$max_index_to_go];
6741
6742 # FIXME: it seems to be necessary to use the next, rather than
6743 # previous, value of this variable when creating a new blank (align.t)
6744 #my $slevel = $nesting_depth_to_go[$max_index_to_go];
6745 $ci_level = $ci_levels_to_go[$max_index_to_go];
6746 $container_environment = $container_environment_to_go[$max_index_to_go];
6747 $in_continued_quote = 0;
6748 $block_type = "";
6749 $type_sequence = "";
6750
6751 # store an undef for the K value to catch unexpected usage
6752 # This routine is only called by add_closing_side_comments, and
6753 # eventually that call will be eliminated.
6754 $Ktoken_vars = undef;
6755
6756 $self->store_token_to_go();
6757 restore_current_token();
6758 return;
6759 }

6761 sub copy_hash {
6762 my ($rold_token_hash) = @_;
6763 my %new_token_hash =
6764 map { ( $_, $rold_token_hash->{$_} ) } keys %{$rold_token_hash};
6765 return \%new_token_hash;
6766 }
6767
6768 sub copy_array {
6769 my ($rold) = @_;
6770 my @new = map { $_ } @{$rold};
6771 return \@new;
6772 }
6773
6774 sub copy_token_as_type {
6775 my ( $rold_token, $type, $token ) = @_;
6776 if ( $type eq 'b' ) {
6777 $token = " " unless defined($token);
6778 }
6779 elsif ( $type eq 'q' ) {
6780 $token = '' unless defined($token);
6781 }
6782 elsif ( $type eq '->' ) {
6783 $token = '->' unless defined($token);
6784 }
6785 elsif ( $type eq ';' ) {
6786 $token = ';' unless defined($token);
6787 }
6788 else {
6789 Fault(
6790"Programming error: copy_token_as has type $type but should be 'b' or 'q'"
6791 );
6792 }
6793 my $rnew_token = copy_array($rold_token);
6794 $rnew_token->[_TYPE_] = $type;
6795 $rnew_token->[_TOKEN_] = $token;
6796 $rnew_token->[_BLOCK_TYPE_] = '';
6797 $rnew_token->[_CONTAINER_TYPE_] = '';
6798 $rnew_token->[_CONTAINER_ENVIRONMENT_] = '';
6799 $rnew_token->[_TYPE_SEQUENCE_] = '';
6800 return $rnew_token;
6801 }
6802
6803 sub boolean_equals {
6804 my ( $val1, $val2 ) = @_;
6805 return ( $val1 && $val2 || !$val1 && !$val2 );
6806 }
6807
6808 sub print_line_of_tokens {
6809
6810 my ( $self, $line_of_tokens ) = @_;
6811
6812 # This routine is called once per input line to process all of
6813 # the tokens on that line. This is the first stage of
6814 # beautification.
6815 #
6816 # Full-line comments and blank lines may be processed immediately.
6817 #
6818 # For normal lines of code, the tokens are stored one-by-one,
6819 # via calls to 'sub store_token_to_go', until a known line break
6820 # point is reached. Then, the batch of collected tokens is
6821 # passed along to 'sub output_line_to_go' for further
6822 # processing. This routine decides if there should be
6823 # whitespace between each pair of non-white tokens, so later
6824 # routines only need to decide on any additional line breaks.
6825 # Any whitespace is initially a single space character. Later,
6826 # the vertical aligner may expand that to be multiple space
6827 # characters if necessary for alignment.
6828
6829 $input_line_number = $line_of_tokens->{_line_number};
6830 my $input_line = $line_of_tokens->{_line_text};
6831 my $CODE_type = $line_of_tokens->{_code_type};
6832
6833 my $rK_range = $line_of_tokens->{_rK_range};
6834 my ( $K_first, $K_last ) = @{$rK_range};
6835
6836 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
6837 my $rbreak_container = $self->{rbreak_container};
6838
6839 if ( !defined($K_first) ) {
6840
6841 # Unexpected blank line..
6842 # Calling routine was supposed to handle this
6843 Warn(
6844"Programming Error: Unexpected Blank Line in print_line_of_tokens. Ignoring"
6845 );
6846 return;
6847 }
6848
6849 $no_internal_newlines = 1 - $rOpts_add_newlines;
6850 my $is_comment =
6851 ( $K_first == $K_last && $rLL->[$K_first]->[_TYPE_] eq '#' );
6852 my $is_static_block_comment_without_leading_space =
6853 $CODE_type eq 'SBCX';
6854 $is_static_block_comment =
6855 $CODE_type eq 'SBC' || $is_static_block_comment_without_leading_space;
6856 my $is_hanging_side_comment = $CODE_type eq 'HSC';
6857 my $is_VERSION_statement = $CODE_type eq 'VER';
6858 if ($is_VERSION_statement) {
6859 $saw_VERSION_in_this_file = 1;
6860 $no_internal_newlines = 1;
6861 }
6862
6863 # Add interline blank if any
6864 my $last_old_nonblank_type = "b";
6865 my $first_new_nonblank_type = "b";
6866 my $first_new_nonblank_token = " ";
6867 if ( $max_index_to_go >= 0 ) {
6868 $last_old_nonblank_type = $types_to_go[$max_index_to_go];
6869 $first_new_nonblank_type = $rLL->[$K_first]->[_TYPE_];
6870 $first_new_nonblank_token = $rLL->[$K_first]->[_TOKEN_];
6871 if ( !$is_comment
6872 && $types_to_go[$max_index_to_go] ne 'b'
6873 && $K_first > 0
6874 && $rLL->[ $K_first - 1 ]->[_TYPE_] eq 'b' )
6875 {
6876 $K_first -= 1;
6877 }
6878 }
6879
6880 # Copy the tokens into local arrays
6881 $rinput_token_array = [];
6882 $rinput_K_array = [];
6883 $rinput_K_array = [ ( $K_first .. $K_last ) ];
6884 $rinput_token_array = [ map { $rLL->[$_] } @{$rinput_K_array} ];
6885 my $jmax = @{$rinput_K_array} - 1;
6886
6887 $in_continued_quote = $starting_in_quote =
6888 $line_of_tokens->{_starting_in_quote};
6889 $in_quote = $line_of_tokens->{_ending_in_quote};
6890 $ending_in_quote = $in_quote;
6891 $guessed_indentation_level =
6892 $line_of_tokens->{_guessed_indentation_level};
6893
6894 my $j_next;
6895 my $next_nonblank_token;
6896 my $next_nonblank_token_type;
6897
6898 $block_type = "";
6899 $container_type = "";
6900 $container_environment = "";
6901 $type_sequence = "";
6902
6903 ######################################
6904 # Handle a block (full-line) comment..
6905 ######################################
6906 if ($is_comment) {
6907
6908 if ( $rOpts->{'delete-block-comments'} ) { return }
6909
6910 if ( $rOpts->{'tee-block-comments'} ) {
6911 $file_writer_object->tee_on();
6912 }
6913
6914 destroy_one_line_block();
6915 $self->output_line_to_go();
6916
6917 # output a blank line before block comments
6918 if (
6919 # unless we follow a blank or comment line
6920 $last_line_leading_type !~ /^[#b]$/
6921
6922 # only if allowed
6923 && $rOpts->{'blanks-before-comments'}
6924
6925 # if this is NOT an empty comment line
6926 && $rinput_token_array->[0]->[_TOKEN_] ne '#'
6927
6928 # not after a short line ending in an opening token
6929 # because we already have space above this comment.
6930 # Note that the first comment in this if block, after
6931 # the 'if (', does not get a blank line because of this.
6932 && !$last_output_short_opening_token
6933
6934 # never before static block comments
6935 && !$is_static_block_comment
6936 )
6937 {
6938 $self->flush(); # switching to new output stream
6939 $file_writer_object->write_blank_code_line();
6940 $last_line_leading_type = 'b';
6941 }
6942
6943 # TRIM COMMENTS -- This could be turned off as a option
6944 $rinput_token_array->[0]->[_TOKEN_] =~ s/\s*$//; # trim right end
6945
6946 if (
6947 $rOpts->{'indent-block-comments'}
6948 && ( !$rOpts->{'indent-spaced-block-comments'}
6949 || $input_line =~ /^\s+/ )
6950 && !$is_static_block_comment_without_leading_space
6951 )
6952 {
6953 $self->extract_token(0);
6954 $self->store_token_to_go();
6955 $self->output_line_to_go();
6956 }
6957 else {
6958 $self->flush(); # switching to new output stream
6959 $file_writer_object->write_code_line(
6960 $rinput_token_array->[0]->[_TOKEN_] . "\n" );
6961 $last_line_leading_type = '#';
6962 }
6963 if ( $rOpts->{'tee-block-comments'} ) {
6964 $file_writer_object->tee_off();
6965 }
6966 return;
6967 }
6968
6969 # TODO: Move to sub scan_comments
6970 # compare input/output indentation except for continuation lines
6971 # (because they have an unknown amount of initial blank space)
6972 # and lines which are quotes (because they may have been outdented)
6973 # Note: this test is placed here because we know the continuation flag
6974 # at this point, which allows us to avoid non-meaningful checks.
6975 my $structural_indentation_level = $rinput_token_array->[0]->[_LEVEL_];
6976 compare_indentation_levels( $guessed_indentation_level,
6977 $structural_indentation_level )
6978 unless ( $is_hanging_side_comment
6979 || $rinput_token_array->[0]->[_CI_LEVEL_] > 0
6980 || $guessed_indentation_level == 0
6981 && $rinput_token_array->[0]->[_TYPE_] eq 'Q' );
6982
6983 ##########################
6984 # Handle indentation-only
6985 ##########################
6986
6987 # NOTE: In previous versions we sent all qw lines out immediately here.
6988 # No longer doing this: also write a line which is entirely a 'qw' list
6989 # to allow stacking of opening and closing tokens. Note that interior
6990 # qw lines will still go out at the end of this routine.
6991 if ( $CODE_type eq 'IO' ) {
6992 $self->flush();
6993 my $line = $input_line;
6994
6995 # delete side comments if requested with -io, but
6996 # we will not allow deleting of closing side comments with -io
6997 # because the coding would be more complex
6998 if ( $rOpts->{'delete-side-comments'}
6999 && $rinput_token_array->[$jmax]->[_TYPE_] eq '#' )
7000 {
7001
7002 $line = "";
7003 foreach my $jj ( 0 .. $jmax - 1 ) {
7004 $line .= $rinput_token_array->[$jj]->[_TOKEN_];
7005 }
7006 }
7007
7008 # Fix for rt #125506 Unexpected string formating
7009 # in which leading space of a terminal quote was removed
7010 $line =~ s/\s+$//;
7011 $line =~ s/^\s+// unless ($in_continued_quote);
7012
7013 $self->extract_token(0);
7014 $token = $line;
7015 $type = 'q';
7016 $block_type = "";
7017 $container_type = "";
7018 $container_environment = "";
7019 $type_sequence = "";
7020 $self->store_token_to_go();
7021 $self->output_line_to_go();
7022 return;
7023 }
7024
7025 ############################
7026 # Handle all other lines ...
7027 ############################
7028
7029 #######################################################
7030 # FIXME: this should become unnecessary
7031 # making $j+2 valid simplifies coding
7032 my $rnew_blank =
7033 copy_token_as_type( $rinput_token_array->[$jmax], 'b' );
7034 push @{$rinput_token_array}, $rnew_blank;
7035 push @{$rinput_token_array}, $rnew_blank;
7036 #######################################################
7037
7038 # If we just saw the end of an elsif block, write nag message
7039 # if we do not see another elseif or an else.
7040 if ($looking_for_else) {
7041
7042 unless ( $rinput_token_array->[0]->[_TOKEN_] =~ /^(elsif|else)$/ ) {
7043 write_logfile_entry("(No else block)\n");
7044 }
7045 $looking_for_else = 0;
7046 }
7047
7048 # This is a good place to kill incomplete one-line blocks
7049 if (
7050 (
7051 ( $semicolons_before_block_self_destruct == 0 )
7052 && ( $max_index_to_go >= 0 )
7053 && ( $last_old_nonblank_type eq ';' )
7054 && ( $first_new_nonblank_token ne '}' )
7055 )
7056
7057 # Patch for RT #98902. Honor request to break at old commas.
7058 || ( $rOpts_break_at_old_comma_breakpoints
7059 && $max_index_to_go >= 0
7060 && $last_old_nonblank_type eq ',' )
7061 )
7062 {
7063 $forced_breakpoint_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = 1
7064 if ($rOpts_break_at_old_comma_breakpoints);
7065 destroy_one_line_block();
7066 $self->output_line_to_go();
7067 }
7068
7069 # loop to process the tokens one-by-one
7070 $type = 'b';
7071 $token = "";
7072
7073 # We do not want a leading blank if the previous batch just got output
7074 my $jmin = 0;
7075 if ( $max_index_to_go < 0 && $rLL->[$K_first]->[_TYPE_] eq 'b' ) {
7076 $jmin = 1;
7077 }
7078
7079 foreach my $j ( $jmin .. $jmax ) {
7080
7081 # pull out the local values for this token
7082 $self->extract_token($j);
7083
7084 if ( $type eq '#' ) {
7085
7086 # trim trailing whitespace
7087 # (there is no option at present to prevent this)
7088 $token =~ s/\s*$//;
7089
7090 if (
7091 $rOpts->{'delete-side-comments'}
7092
7093 # delete closing side comments if necessary
7094 || ( $rOpts->{'delete-closing-side-comments'}
7095 && $token =~ /$closing_side_comment_prefix_pattern/o
7096 && $last_nonblank_block_type =~
7097 /$closing_side_comment_list_pattern/o )
7098 )
7099 {
7100 if ( $types_to_go[$max_index_to_go] eq 'b' ) {
7101 unstore_token_to_go();
7102 }
7103 last;
7104 }
7105 }
7106
7107 # If we are continuing after seeing a right curly brace, flush
7108 # buffer unless we see what we are looking for, as in
7109 # } else ...
7110 if ( $rbrace_follower && $type ne 'b' ) {
7111
7112 unless ( $rbrace_follower->{$token} ) {
7113 $self->output_line_to_go();
7114 }
7115 $rbrace_follower = undef;
7116 }
7117
7118 $j_next =
7119 ( $rinput_token_array->[ $j + 1 ]->[_TYPE_] eq 'b' )
7120 ? $j + 2
7121 : $j + 1;
7122 $next_nonblank_token = $rinput_token_array->[$j_next]->[_TOKEN_];
7123 $next_nonblank_token_type =
7124 $rinput_token_array->[$j_next]->[_TYPE_];
7125
7126 ######################
7127 # MAYBE MOVE ELSEWHERE?
7128 ######################
7129 if ( $type eq 'Q' ) {
7130 note_embedded_tab() if ( $token =~ "\t" );
7131
7132 # make note of something like '$var = s/xxx/yyy/;'
7133 # in case it should have been '$var =~ s/xxx/yyy/;'
7134 if (
7135 $token =~ /^(s|tr|y|m|\/)/
7136 && $last_nonblank_token =~ /^(=|==|!=)$/
7137
7138 # preceded by simple scalar
7139 && $last_last_nonblank_type eq 'i'
7140 && $last_last_nonblank_token =~ /^\$/
7141
7142 # followed by some kind of termination
7143 # (but give complaint if we can's see far enough ahead)
7144 && $next_nonblank_token =~ /^[; \)\}]$/
7145
7146 # scalar is not declared
7147 && !(
7148 $types_to_go[0] eq 'k'
7149 && $tokens_to_go[0] =~ /^(my|our|local)$/
7150 )
7151 )
7152 {
7153 my $guess = substr( $last_nonblank_token, 0, 1 ) . '~';
7154 complain(
7155"Note: be sure you want '$last_nonblank_token' instead of '$guess' here\n"
7156 );
7157 }
7158 }
7159
7160 # Do not allow breaks which would promote a side comment to a
7161 # block comment. In order to allow a break before an opening
7162 # or closing BLOCK, followed by a side comment, those sections
7163 # of code will handle this flag separately.
7164 my $side_comment_follows = ( $next_nonblank_token_type eq '#' );
7165 my $is_opening_BLOCK =
7166 ( $type eq '{'
7167 && $token eq '{'
7168 && $block_type
7169 && $block_type ne 't' );
7170 my $is_closing_BLOCK =
7171 ( $type eq '}'
7172 && $token eq '}'
7173 && $block_type
7174 && $block_type ne 't' );
7175
7176 if ( $side_comment_follows
7177 && !$is_opening_BLOCK
7178 && !$is_closing_BLOCK )
7179 {
7180 $no_internal_newlines = 1;
7181 }
7182
7183 # We're only going to handle breaking for code BLOCKS at this
7184 # (top) level. Other indentation breaks will be handled by
7185 # sub scan_list, which is better suited to dealing with them.
7186 if ($is_opening_BLOCK) {
7187
7188 # Tentatively output this token. This is required before
7189 # calling starting_one_line_block. We may have to unstore
7190 # it, though, if we have to break before it.
7191 $self->store_token_to_go($side_comment_follows);
7192
7193 # Look ahead to see if we might form a one-line block..
7194 my $too_long =
7195 $self->starting_one_line_block( $j, $jmax, $level, $slevel,
7196 $ci_level, $rinput_token_array );
7197 clear_breakpoint_undo_stack();
7198
7199 # to simplify the logic below, set a flag to indicate if
7200 # this opening brace is far from the keyword which introduces it
7201 my $keyword_on_same_line = 1;
7202 if ( ( $max_index_to_go >= 0 )
7203 && ( $last_nonblank_type eq ')' )
7204 && ( ( $slevel < $nesting_depth_to_go[0] ) || $too_long ) )
7205 {
7206 $keyword_on_same_line = 0;
7207 }
7208
7209 # decide if user requested break before '{'
7210 my $want_break =
7211
7212 # use -bl flag if not a sub block of any type
7213 $block_type !~ /^sub\b/
7214 ? $rOpts->{'opening-brace-on-new-line'}
7215
7216 # use -sbl flag for a named sub block
7217 : $block_type !~ /$ASUB_PATTERN/
7218 ? $rOpts->{'opening-sub-brace-on-new-line'}
7219
7220 # use -asbl flag for an anonymous sub block
7221 : $rOpts->{'opening-anonymous-sub-brace-on-new-line'};
7222
7223 # Do not break if this token is welded to the left
7224 if ( weld_len_left( $type_sequence, $token ) ) {
7225 $want_break = 0;
7226 }
7227
7228 # Break before an opening '{' ...
7229 if (
7230
7231 # if requested
7232 $want_break
7233
7234 # and we were unable to start looking for a block,
7235 && $index_start_one_line_block == UNDEFINED_INDEX
7236
7237 # or if it will not be on same line as its keyword, so that
7238 # it will be outdented (eval.t, overload.t), and the user
7239 # has not insisted on keeping it on the right
7240 || ( !$keyword_on_same_line
7241 && !$rOpts->{'opening-brace-always-on-right'} )
7242
7243 )
7244 {
7245
7246 # but only if allowed
7247 unless ($no_internal_newlines) {
7248
7249 # since we already stored this token, we must unstore it
7250 $self->unstore_token_to_go();
7251
7252 # then output the line
7253 $self->output_line_to_go();
7254
7255 # and now store this token at the start of a new line
7256 $self->store_token_to_go($side_comment_follows);
7257 }
7258 }
7259
7260 # Now update for side comment
7261 if ($side_comment_follows) { $no_internal_newlines = 1 }
7262
7263 # now output this line
7264 unless ($no_internal_newlines) {
7265 $self->output_line_to_go();
7266 }
7267 }
7268
7269 elsif ($is_closing_BLOCK) {
7270
7271 # If there is a pending one-line block ..
7272 if ( $index_start_one_line_block != UNDEFINED_INDEX ) {
7273
7274 # we have to terminate it if..
7275 if (
7276
7277 # it is too long (final length may be different from
7278 # initial estimate). note: must allow 1 space for this
7279 # token
7280 excess_line_length( $index_start_one_line_block,
7281 $max_index_to_go ) >= 0
7282
7283 # or if it has too many semicolons
7284 || ( $semicolons_before_block_self_destruct == 0
7285 && $last_nonblank_type ne ';' )
7286 )
7287 {
7288 destroy_one_line_block();
7289 }
7290 }
7291
7292 # put a break before this closing curly brace if appropriate
7293 unless ( $no_internal_newlines
7294 || $index_start_one_line_block != UNDEFINED_INDEX )
7295 {
7296
7297 # write out everything before this closing curly brace
7298 $self->output_line_to_go();
7299 }
7300
7301 # Now update for side comment
7302 if ($side_comment_follows) { $no_internal_newlines = 1 }
7303
7304 # store the closing curly brace
7305 $self->store_token_to_go();
7306
7307 # ok, we just stored a closing curly brace. Often, but
7308 # not always, we want to end the line immediately.
7309 # So now we have to check for special cases.
7310
7311 # if this '}' successfully ends a one-line block..
7312 my $is_one_line_block = 0;
7313 my $keep_going = 0;
7314 if ( $index_start_one_line_block != UNDEFINED_INDEX ) {
7315
7316 # Remember the type of token just before the
7317 # opening brace. It would be more general to use
7318 # a stack, but this will work for one-line blocks.
7319 $is_one_line_block =
7320 $types_to_go[$index_start_one_line_block];
7321
7322 # we have to actually make it by removing tentative
7323 # breaks that were set within it
7324 undo_forced_breakpoint_stack(0);
7325 set_nobreaks( $index_start_one_line_block,
7326 $max_index_to_go - 1 );
7327
7328 # then re-initialize for the next one-line block
7329 destroy_one_line_block();
7330
7331 # then decide if we want to break after the '}' ..
7332 # We will keep going to allow certain brace followers as in:
7333 # do { $ifclosed = 1; last } unless $losing;
7334 #
7335 # But make a line break if the curly ends a
7336 # significant block:
7337 if (
7338 (
7339 $is_block_without_semicolon{$block_type}
7340
7341 # Follow users break point for
7342 # one line block types U & G, such as a 'try' block
7343 || $is_one_line_block =~ /^[UG]$/ && $j == $jmax
7344 )
7345
7346 # if needless semicolon follows we handle it later
7347 && $next_nonblank_token ne ';'
7348 )
7349 {
7350 $self->output_line_to_go()
7351 unless ($no_internal_newlines);
7352 }
7353 }
7354
7355 # set string indicating what we need to look for brace follower
7356 # tokens
7357 if ( $block_type eq 'do' ) {
7358 $rbrace_follower = \%is_do_follower;
7359 }
7360 elsif ( $block_type =~ /^(if|elsif|unless)$/ ) {
7361 $rbrace_follower = \%is_if_brace_follower;
7362 }
7363 elsif ( $block_type eq 'else' ) {
7364 $rbrace_follower = \%is_else_brace_follower;
7365 }
7366
7367 # added eval for borris.t
7368 elsif ($is_sort_map_grep_eval{$block_type}
7369 || $is_one_line_block eq 'G' )
7370 {
7371 $rbrace_follower = undef;
7372 $keep_going = 1;
7373 }
7374
7375 # anonymous sub
7376 elsif ( $block_type =~ /$ASUB_PATTERN/ ) {
7377
7378 if ($is_one_line_block) {
7379 $rbrace_follower = \%is_anon_sub_1_brace_follower;
7380 }
7381 else {
7382 $rbrace_follower = \%is_anon_sub_brace_follower;
7383 }
7384 }
7385
7386 # None of the above: specify what can follow a closing
7387 # brace of a block which is not an
7388 # if/elsif/else/do/sort/map/grep/eval
7389 # Testfiles:
7390 # 'Toolbar.pm', 'Menubar.pm', bless.t, '3rules.pl', 'break1.t
7391 else {
7392 $rbrace_follower = \%is_other_brace_follower;
7393 }
7394
7395 # See if an elsif block is followed by another elsif or else;
7396 # complain if not.
7397 if ( $block_type eq 'elsif' ) {
7398
7399 if ( $next_nonblank_token_type eq 'b' ) { # end of line?
7400 $looking_for_else = 1; # ok, check on next line
7401 }
7402 else {
7403
7404 unless ( $next_nonblank_token =~ /^(elsif|else)$/ ) {
7405 write_logfile_entry("No else block :(\n");
7406 }
7407 }
7408 }
7409
7410 # keep going after certain block types (map,sort,grep,eval)
7411 # added eval for borris.t
7412 if ($keep_going) {
7413
7414 # keep going
7415 }
7416
7417 # if no more tokens, postpone decision until re-entring
7418 elsif ( ( $next_nonblank_token_type eq 'b' )
7419 && $rOpts_add_newlines )
7420 {
7421 unless ($rbrace_follower) {
7422 $self->output_line_to_go()
7423 unless ($no_internal_newlines);
7424 }
7425 }
7426
7427 elsif ($rbrace_follower) {
7428
7429 unless ( $rbrace_follower->{$next_nonblank_token} ) {
7430 $self->output_line_to_go()
7431 unless ($no_internal_newlines);
7432 }
7433 $rbrace_follower = undef;
7434 }
7435
7436 else {
7437 $self->output_line_to_go() unless ($no_internal_newlines);
7438 }
7439
7440 } # end treatment of closing block token
7441
7442 # handle semicolon
7443 elsif ( $type eq ';' ) {
7444
7445 # kill one-line blocks with too many semicolons
7446 $semicolons_before_block_self_destruct--;
7447 if (
7448 ( $semicolons_before_block_self_destruct < 0 )
7449 || ( $semicolons_before_block_self_destruct == 0
7450 && $next_nonblank_token_type !~ /^[b\}]$/ )
7451 )
7452 {
7453 destroy_one_line_block();
7454 }
7455
7456 # Remove unnecessary semicolons, but not after bare
7457 # blocks, where it could be unsafe if the brace is
7458 # mistokenized.
7459 if (
7460 (
7461 $last_nonblank_token eq '}'
7462 && (
7463 $is_block_without_semicolon{
7464 $last_nonblank_block_type}
7465 || $last_nonblank_block_type =~ /$SUB_PATTERN/
7466 || $last_nonblank_block_type =~ /^\w+:$/ )
7467 )
7468 || $last_nonblank_type eq ';'
7469 )
7470 {
7471
7472 if (
7473 $rOpts->{'delete-semicolons'}
7474
7475 # don't delete ; before a # because it would promote it
7476 # to a block comment
7477 && ( $next_nonblank_token_type ne '#' )
7478 )
7479 {
7480 note_deleted_semicolon();
7481 $self->output_line_to_go()
7482 unless ( $no_internal_newlines
7483 || $index_start_one_line_block != UNDEFINED_INDEX );
7484 next;
7485 }
7486 else {
7487 write_logfile_entry("Extra ';'\n");
7488 }
7489 }
7490 $self->store_token_to_go();
7491
7492 $self->output_line_to_go()
7493 unless ( $no_internal_newlines
7494 || ( $rOpts_keep_interior_semicolons && $j < $jmax )
7495 || ( $next_nonblank_token eq '}' ) );
7496
7497 }
7498
7499 # handle here_doc target string
7500 elsif ( $type eq 'h' ) {
7501
7502 # no newlines after seeing here-target
7503 $no_internal_newlines = 1;
7504 destroy_one_line_block();
7505 $self->store_token_to_go();
7506 }
7507
7508 # handle all other token types
7509 else {
7510
7511 $self->store_token_to_go();
7512 }
7513
7514 # remember two previous nonblank OUTPUT tokens
7515 if ( $type ne '#' && $type ne 'b' ) {
7516 $last_last_nonblank_token = $last_nonblank_token;
7517 $last_last_nonblank_type = $last_nonblank_type;
7518 $last_nonblank_token = $token;
7519 $last_nonblank_type = $type;
7520 $last_nonblank_block_type = $block_type;
7521 }
7522
7523 # unset the continued-quote flag since it only applies to the
7524 # first token, and we want to resume normal formatting if
7525 # there are additional tokens on the line
7526 $in_continued_quote = 0;
7527
7528 } # end of loop over all tokens in this 'line_of_tokens'
7529
7530 # we have to flush ..
7531 if (
7532
7533 # if there is a side comment
7534 ( ( $type eq '#' ) && !$rOpts->{'delete-side-comments'} )
7535
7536 # if this line ends in a quote
7537 # NOTE: This is critically important for insuring that quoted lines
7538 # do not get processed by things like -sot and -sct
7539 || $in_quote
7540
7541 # if this is a VERSION statement
7542 || $is_VERSION_statement
7543
7544 # to keep a label at the end of a line
7545 || $type eq 'J'
7546
7547 # if we are instructed to keep all old line breaks
7548 || !$rOpts->{'delete-old-newlines'}
7549 )
7550 {
7551 destroy_one_line_block();
7552 $self->output_line_to_go();
7553 }
7554
7555 # mark old line breakpoints in current output stream
7556 if ( $max_index_to_go >= 0 && !$rOpts_ignore_old_breakpoints ) {
7557 my $jobp = $max_index_to_go;
7558 if ( $types_to_go[$max_index_to_go] eq 'b' && $max_index_to_go > 0 )
7559 {
7560 $jobp--;
7561 }
7562 $old_breakpoint_to_go[$jobp] = 1;
7563 }
7564 return;
7565 } ## end sub print_line_of_tokens
7566} ## end block print_line_of_tokens
7567
75681200nssub consecutive_nonblank_lines {
7569 return $file_writer_object->get_consecutive_nonblank_lines() +
7570 $vertical_aligner_object->get_cached_line_count();
7571}
7572
7573# sub output_line_to_go sends one logical line of tokens on down the
7574# pipeline to the VerticalAligner package, breaking the line into continuation
7575# lines as necessary. The line of tokens is ready to go in the "to_go"
7576# arrays.
7577sub output_line_to_go {
7578
7579 my $self = shift;
7580 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
7581
7582 # debug stuff; this routine can be called from many points
7583 FORMATTER_DEBUG_FLAG_OUTPUT && do {
7584 my ( $a, $b, $c ) = caller;
7585 write_diagnostics(
7586"OUTPUT: output_line_to_go called: $a $c $last_nonblank_type $last_nonblank_token, one_line=$index_start_one_line_block, tokens to write=$max_index_to_go\n"
7587 );
7588 my $output_str = join "", @tokens_to_go[ 0 .. $max_index_to_go ];
7589 write_diagnostics("$output_str\n");
7590 };
7591
7592 # Do not end line in a weld
7593 # TODO: Move this fix into the routine?
7594 #my $jnb = $max_index_to_go;
7595 #if ( $jnb > 0 && $types_to_go[$jnb] eq 'b' ) { $jnb-- }
7596 return if ( weld_len_right_to_go($max_index_to_go) );
7597
7598 # just set a tentative breakpoint if we might be in a one-line block
7599 if ( $index_start_one_line_block != UNDEFINED_INDEX ) {
7600 set_forced_breakpoint($max_index_to_go);
7601 return;
7602 }
7603
7604## my $cscw_block_comment;
7605## $cscw_block_comment = $self->add_closing_side_comment()
7606## if ( $rOpts->{'closing-side-comments'} && $max_index_to_go >= 0 );
7607
7608 my $comma_arrow_count_contained = match_opening_and_closing_tokens();
7609
7610 # tell the -lp option we are outputting a batch so it can close
7611 # any unfinished items in its stack
7612 finish_lp_batch();
7613
7614 # If this line ends in a code block brace, set breaks at any
7615 # previous closing code block braces to breakup a chain of code
7616 # blocks on one line. This is very rare but can happen for
7617 # user-defined subs. For example we might be looking at this:
7618 # BOOL { $server_data{uptime} > 0; } NUM { $server_data{load}; } STR {
7619 my $saw_good_break = 0; # flag to force breaks even if short line
7620 if (
7621
7622 # looking for opening or closing block brace
7623 $block_type_to_go[$max_index_to_go]
7624
7625 # but not one of these which are never duplicated on a line:
7626 # until|while|for|if|elsif|else
7627 && !$is_block_without_semicolon{ $block_type_to_go[$max_index_to_go] }
7628 )
7629 {
7630 my $lev = $nesting_depth_to_go[$max_index_to_go];
7631
7632 # Walk backwards from the end and
7633 # set break at any closing block braces at the same level.
7634 # But quit if we are not in a chain of blocks.
7635 for ( my $i = $max_index_to_go - 1 ; $i >= 0 ; $i-- ) {
7636 last if ( $levels_to_go[$i] < $lev ); # stop at a lower level
7637 next if ( $levels_to_go[$i] > $lev ); # skip past higher level
7638
7639 if ( $block_type_to_go[$i] ) {
7640 if ( $tokens_to_go[$i] eq '}' ) {
7641 set_forced_breakpoint($i);
7642 $saw_good_break = 1;
7643 }
7644 }
7645
7646 # quit if we see anything besides words, function, blanks
7647 # at this level
7648 elsif ( $types_to_go[$i] !~ /^[\(\)Gwib]$/ ) { last }
7649 }
7650 }
7651
7652 my $imin = 0;
7653 my $imax = $max_index_to_go;
7654
7655 # trim any blank tokens
7656 if ( $max_index_to_go >= 0 ) {
7657 if ( $types_to_go[$imin] eq 'b' ) { $imin++ }
7658 if ( $types_to_go[$imax] eq 'b' ) { $imax-- }
7659 }
7660
7661 # anything left to write?
7662 if ( $imin <= $imax ) {
7663
7664 # add a blank line before certain key types but not after a comment
7665 if ( $last_line_leading_type !~ /^[#]/ ) {
7666 my $want_blank = 0;
7667 my $leading_token = $tokens_to_go[$imin];
7668 my $leading_type = $types_to_go[$imin];
7669
7670 # blank lines before subs except declarations and one-liners
7671 # MCONVERSION LOCATION - for sub tokenization change
7672 if ( $leading_token =~ /^(sub\s)/ && $leading_type eq 'i' ) {
7673 $want_blank = $rOpts->{'blank-lines-before-subs'}
7674 if (
7675 terminal_type( \@types_to_go, \@block_type_to_go, $imin,
7676 $imax ) !~ /^[\;\}]$/
7677 );
7678 }
7679
7680 # break before all package declarations
7681 # MCONVERSION LOCATION - for tokenizaton change
7682 elsif ($leading_token =~ /^(package\s)/
7683 && $leading_type eq 'i' )
7684 {
7685 $want_blank = $rOpts->{'blank-lines-before-packages'};
7686 }
7687
7688 # break before certain key blocks except one-liners
7689 if ( $leading_token =~ /^(BEGIN|END)$/ && $leading_type eq 'k' ) {
7690 $want_blank = $rOpts->{'blank-lines-before-subs'}
7691 if (
7692 terminal_type( \@types_to_go, \@block_type_to_go, $imin,
7693 $imax ) ne '}'
7694 );
7695 }
7696
7697 # Break before certain block types if we haven't had a
7698 # break at this level for a while. This is the
7699 # difficult decision..
7700 elsif ($leading_type eq 'k'
7701 && $last_line_leading_type ne 'b'
7702 && $leading_token =~ /^(unless|if|while|until|for|foreach)$/ )
7703 {
7704 my $lc = $nonblank_lines_at_depth[$last_line_leading_level];
7705 if ( !defined($lc) ) { $lc = 0 }
7706
7707 # patch for RT #128216: no blank line inserted at a level change
7708 if ( $levels_to_go[$imin] != $last_line_leading_level ) {
7709 $lc = 0;
7710 }
7711
7712 $want_blank =
7713 $rOpts->{'blanks-before-blocks'}
7714 && $lc >= $rOpts->{'long-block-line-count'}
7715 && consecutive_nonblank_lines() >=
7716 $rOpts->{'long-block-line-count'}
7717 && (
7718 terminal_type( \@types_to_go, \@block_type_to_go, $imin,
7719 $imax ) ne '}'
7720 );
7721 }
7722
7723 # Check for blank lines wanted before a closing brace
7724 if ( $leading_token eq '}' ) {
7725 if ( $rOpts->{'blank-lines-before-closing-block'}
7726 && $block_type_to_go[$imin]
7727 && $block_type_to_go[$imin] =~
7728 /$blank_lines_before_closing_block_pattern/ )
7729 {
7730 my $nblanks = $rOpts->{'blank-lines-before-closing-block'};
7731 if ( $nblanks > $want_blank ) {
7732 $want_blank = $nblanks;
7733 }
7734 }
7735 }
7736
7737 if ($want_blank) {
7738
7739 # future: send blank line down normal path to VerticalAligner
7740 Perl::Tidy::VerticalAligner::flush();
7741 $file_writer_object->require_blank_code_lines($want_blank);
7742 }
7743 }
7744
7745 # update blank line variables and count number of consecutive
7746 # non-blank, non-comment lines at this level
7747 $last_last_line_leading_level = $last_line_leading_level;
7748 $last_line_leading_level = $levels_to_go[$imin];
7749 if ( $last_line_leading_level < 0 ) { $last_line_leading_level = 0 }
7750 $last_line_leading_type = $types_to_go[$imin];
7751 if ( $last_line_leading_level == $last_last_line_leading_level
7752 && $last_line_leading_type ne 'b'
7753 && $last_line_leading_type ne '#'
7754 && defined( $nonblank_lines_at_depth[$last_line_leading_level] ) )
7755 {
7756 $nonblank_lines_at_depth[$last_line_leading_level]++;
7757 }
7758 else {
7759 $nonblank_lines_at_depth[$last_line_leading_level] = 1;
7760 }
7761
7762 FORMATTER_DEBUG_FLAG_FLUSH && do {
7763 my ( $package, $file, $line ) = caller;
7764 print STDOUT
7765"FLUSH: flushing from $package $file $line, types= $types_to_go[$imin] to $types_to_go[$imax]\n";
7766 };
7767
7768 # add a couple of extra terminal blank tokens
7769 pad_array_to_go();
7770
7771 # set all forced breakpoints for good list formatting
7772 my $is_long_line = excess_line_length( $imin, $max_index_to_go ) > 0;
7773
7774 my $old_line_count_in_batch =
7775 $self->get_old_line_count( $K_to_go[0], $K_to_go[$max_index_to_go] );
7776
7777 if (
7778 $is_long_line
7779 || $old_line_count_in_batch > 1
7780
7781 # must always call scan_list() with unbalanced batches because it
7782 # is maintaining some stacks
7783 || is_unbalanced_batch()
7784
7785 # call scan_list if we might want to break at commas
7786 || (
7787 $comma_count_in_batch
7788 && ( $rOpts_maximum_fields_per_table > 0
7789 || $rOpts_comma_arrow_breakpoints == 0 )
7790 )
7791
7792 # call scan_list if user may want to break open some one-line
7793 # hash references
7794 || ( $comma_arrow_count_contained
7795 && $rOpts_comma_arrow_breakpoints != 3 )
7796 )
7797 {
7798 ## This caused problems in one version of perl for unknown reasons:
7799 ## $saw_good_break ||= scan_list();
7800 my $sgb = scan_list();
7801 $saw_good_break ||= $sgb;
7802 }
7803
7804 # let $ri_first and $ri_last be references to lists of
7805 # first and last tokens of line fragments to output..
7806 my ( $ri_first, $ri_last );
7807
7808 # write a single line if..
7809 if (
7810
7811 # we aren't allowed to add any newlines
7812 !$rOpts_add_newlines
7813
7814 # or, we don't already have an interior breakpoint
7815 # and we didn't see a good breakpoint
7816 || (
7817 !$forced_breakpoint_count
7818 && !$saw_good_break
7819
7820 # and this line is 'short'
7821 && !$is_long_line
7822 )
7823 )
7824 {
7825 @{$ri_first} = ($imin);
7826 @{$ri_last} = ($imax);
7827 }
7828
7829 # otherwise use multiple lines
7830 else {
7831
7832 ( $ri_first, $ri_last, my $colon_count ) =
7833 set_continuation_breaks($saw_good_break);
7834
7835 break_all_chain_tokens( $ri_first, $ri_last );
7836
7837 break_equals( $ri_first, $ri_last );
7838
7839 # now we do a correction step to clean this up a bit
7840 # (The only time we would not do this is for debugging)
7841 if ( $rOpts->{'recombine'} ) {
7842 ( $ri_first, $ri_last ) =
7843 recombine_breakpoints( $ri_first, $ri_last );
7844 }
7845
7846 insert_final_breaks( $ri_first, $ri_last ) if $colon_count;
7847 }
7848
7849 # do corrector step if -lp option is used
7850 my $do_not_pad = 0;
7851 if ($rOpts_line_up_parentheses) {
7852 $do_not_pad = correct_lp_indentation( $ri_first, $ri_last );
7853 }
7854 $self->unmask_phantom_semicolons( $ri_first, $ri_last );
7855 if ( $rOpts_one_line_block_semicolons == 0 ) {
7856 $self->delete_one_line_semicolons( $ri_first, $ri_last );
7857 }
7858 $self->send_lines_to_vertical_aligner( $ri_first, $ri_last,
7859 $do_not_pad );
7860
7861 # Insert any requested blank lines after an opening brace. We have to
7862 # skip back before any side comment to find the terminal token
7863 my $iterm;
7864 for ( $iterm = $imax ; $iterm >= $imin ; $iterm-- ) {
7865 next if $types_to_go[$iterm] eq '#';
7866 next if $types_to_go[$iterm] eq 'b';
7867 last;
7868 }
7869
7870 # write requested number of blank lines after an opening block brace
7871 if ( $iterm >= $imin && $types_to_go[$iterm] eq '{' ) {
7872 if ( $rOpts->{'blank-lines-after-opening-block'}
7873 && $block_type_to_go[$iterm]
7874 && $block_type_to_go[$iterm] =~
7875 /$blank_lines_after_opening_block_pattern/ )
7876 {
7877 my $nblanks = $rOpts->{'blank-lines-after-opening-block'};
7878 Perl::Tidy::VerticalAligner::flush();
7879 $file_writer_object->require_blank_code_lines($nblanks);
7880 }
7881 }
7882 }
7883
7884 prepare_for_new_input_lines();
7885
7886## # output any new -cscw block comment
7887## if ($cscw_block_comment) {
7888## $self->flush();
7889## $file_writer_object->write_code_line( $cscw_block_comment . "\n" );
7890## }
7891 return;
7892}

7928sub starting_one_line_block {
7929
7930 # after seeing an opening curly brace, look for the closing brace
7931 # and see if the entire block will fit on a line. This routine is
7932 # not always right because it uses the old whitespace, so a check
7933 # is made later (at the closing brace) to make sure we really
7934 # have a one-line block. We have to do this preliminary check,
7935 # though, because otherwise we would always break at a semicolon
7936 # within a one-line block if the block contains multiple statements.
7937
7938 my ( $self, $j, $jmax, $level, $slevel, $ci_level, $rtoken_array ) = @_;
7939 my $rbreak_container = $self->{rbreak_container};
7940
7941 my $jmax_check = @{$rtoken_array};
7942 if ( $jmax_check < $jmax ) {
7943 Fault("jmax=$jmax > $jmax_check");
7944 }
7945
7946 # kill any current block - we can only go 1 deep
7947 destroy_one_line_block();
7948
7949 # return value:
7950 # 1=distance from start of block to opening brace exceeds line length
7951 # 0=otherwise
7952
7953 my $i_start = 0;
7954
7955 # shouldn't happen: there must have been a prior call to
7956 # store_token_to_go to put the opening brace in the output stream
7957 if ( $max_index_to_go < 0 ) {
7958 Fault("program bug: store_token_to_go called incorrectly\n");
7959 }
7960
7961 # return if block should be broken
7962 my $type_sequence = $rtoken_array->[$j]->[_TYPE_SEQUENCE_];
7963 if ( $rbreak_container->{$type_sequence} ) {
7964 return 0;
7965 }
7966
7967 my $block_type = $rtoken_array->[$j]->[_BLOCK_TYPE_];
7968
7969 # find the starting keyword for this block (such as 'if', 'else', ...)
7970
7971 if ( $block_type =~ /^[\{\}\;\:]$/ || $block_type =~ /^package/ ) {
7972 $i_start = $max_index_to_go;
7973 }
7974
7975 # the previous nonblank token should start these block types
7976 elsif (( $last_last_nonblank_token_to_go eq $block_type )
7977 || ( $block_type =~ /^sub\b/ )
7978 || $block_type =~ /\(\)/ )
7979 {
7980 $i_start = $last_last_nonblank_index_to_go;
7981
7982 # For signatures and extended syntax ...
7983 # If this brace follows a parenthesized list, we should look back to
7984 # find the keyword before the opening paren because otherwise we might
7985 # form a one line block which stays intack, and cause the parenthesized
7986 # expression to break open. That looks bad. However, actually
7987 # searching for the opening paren is slow and tedius.
7988 # The actual keyword is often at the start of a line, but might not be.
7989 # For example, we might have an anonymous sub with signature list
7990 # following a =>. It is safe to mark the start anywhere before the
7991 # opening paren, so we just go back to the prevoious break (or start of
7992 # the line) if that is before the opening paren. The minor downside is
7993 # that we may very occasionally break open a block unnecessarily.
7994 if ( $tokens_to_go[$i_start] eq ')' ) {
7995 $i_start = $index_max_forced_break + 1;
7996 if ( $types_to_go[$i_start] eq 'b' ) { $i_start++; }
7997 my $lev = $levels_to_go[$i_start];
7998 if ( $lev > $level ) { return 0 }
7999 }
8000 }
8001
8002 elsif ( $last_last_nonblank_token_to_go eq ')' ) {
8003
8004 # For something like "if (xxx) {", the keyword "if" will be
8005 # just after the most recent break. This will be 0 unless
8006 # we have just killed a one-line block and are starting another.
8007 # (doif.t)
8008 # Note: cannot use inext_index_to_go[] here because that array
8009 # is still being constructed.
8010 $i_start = $index_max_forced_break + 1;
8011 if ( $types_to_go[$i_start] eq 'b' ) {
8012 $i_start++;
8013 }
8014
8015 # Patch to avoid breaking short blocks defined with extended_syntax:
8016 # Strip off any trailing () which was added in the parser to mark
8017 # the opening keyword. For example, in the following
8018 # create( TypeFoo $e) {$bubba}
8019 # the blocktype would be marked as create()
8020 my $stripped_block_type = $block_type;
8021 $stripped_block_type =~ s/\(\)$//;
8022
8023 unless ( $tokens_to_go[$i_start] eq $stripped_block_type ) {
8024 return 0;
8025 }
8026 }
8027
8028 # patch for SWITCH/CASE to retain one-line case/when blocks
8029 elsif ( $block_type eq 'case' || $block_type eq 'when' ) {
8030
8031 # Note: cannot use inext_index_to_go[] here because that array
8032 # is still being constructed.
8033 $i_start = $index_max_forced_break + 1;
8034 if ( $types_to_go[$i_start] eq 'b' ) {
8035 $i_start++;
8036 }
8037 unless ( $tokens_to_go[$i_start] eq $block_type ) {
8038 return 0;
8039 }
8040 }
8041
8042 else {
8043 return 1;
8044 }
8045
8046 my $pos = total_line_length( $i_start, $max_index_to_go ) - 1;
8047
8048 # see if length is too long to even start
8049 if ( $pos > maximum_line_length($i_start) ) {
8050 return 1;
8051 }
8052
8053 foreach my $i ( $j + 1 .. $jmax ) {
8054
8055 # old whitespace could be arbitrarily large, so don't use it
8056 if ( $rtoken_array->[$i]->[_TYPE_] eq 'b' ) { $pos += 1 }
8057 else { $pos += rtoken_length($i) }
8058
8059 # Return false result if we exceed the maximum line length,
8060 if ( $pos > maximum_line_length($i_start) ) {
8061 return 0;
8062 }
8063
8064 # or encounter another opening brace before finding the closing brace.
8065 elsif ($rtoken_array->[$i]->[_TOKEN_] eq '{'
8066 && $rtoken_array->[$i]->[_TYPE_] eq '{'
8067 && $rtoken_array->[$i]->[_BLOCK_TYPE_] )
8068 {
8069 return 0;
8070 }
8071
8072 # if we find our closing brace..
8073 elsif ($rtoken_array->[$i]->[_TOKEN_] eq '}'
8074 && $rtoken_array->[$i]->[_TYPE_] eq '}'
8075 && $rtoken_array->[$i]->[_BLOCK_TYPE_] )
8076 {
8077
8078 # be sure any trailing comment also fits on the line
8079 my $i_nonblank =
8080 ( $rtoken_array->[ $i + 1 ]->[_TYPE_] eq 'b' ) ? $i + 2 : $i + 1;
8081
8082 # Patch for one-line sort/map/grep/eval blocks with side comments:
8083 # We will ignore the side comment length for sort/map/grep/eval
8084 # because this can lead to statements which change every time
8085 # perltidy is run. Here is an example from Denis Moskowitz which
8086 # oscillates between these two states without this patch:
8087
8088## --------
8089## grep { $_->foo ne 'bar' } # asdfa asdf asdf asdf asdf asdf asdf asdf asdf asdf asdf
8090## @baz;
8091##
8092## grep {
8093## $_->foo ne 'bar'
8094## } # asdfa asdf asdf asdf asdf asdf asdf asdf asdf asdf asdf
8095## @baz;
8096## --------
8097
8098 # When the first line is input it gets broken apart by the main
8099 # line break logic in sub print_line_of_tokens.
8100 # When the second line is input it gets recombined by
8101 # print_line_of_tokens and passed to the output routines. The
8102 # output routines (set_continuation_breaks) do not break it apart
8103 # because the bond strengths are set to the highest possible value
8104 # for grep/map/eval/sort blocks, so the first version gets output.
8105 # It would be possible to fix this by changing bond strengths,
8106 # but they are high to prevent errors in older versions of perl.
8107
8108 if ( $rtoken_array->[$i_nonblank]->[_TYPE_] eq '#'
8109 && !$is_sort_map_grep{$block_type} )
8110 {
8111
8112 $pos += rtoken_length($i_nonblank);
8113
8114 if ( $i_nonblank > $i + 1 ) {
8115
8116 # source whitespace could be anything, assume
8117 # at least one space before the hash on output
8118 if ( $rtoken_array->[ $i + 1 ]->[_TYPE_] eq 'b' ) {
8119 $pos += 1;
8120 }
8121 else { $pos += rtoken_length( $i + 1 ) }
8122 }
8123
8124 if ( $pos >= maximum_line_length($i_start) ) {
8125 return 0;
8126 }
8127 }
8128
8129 # ok, it's a one-line block
8130 create_one_line_block( $i_start, 20 );
8131 return 0;
8132 }
8133
8134 # just keep going for other characters
8135 else {
8136 }
8137 }
8138
8139 # Allow certain types of new one-line blocks to form by joining
8140 # input lines. These can be safely done, but for other block types,
8141 # we keep old one-line blocks but do not form new ones. It is not
8142 # always a good idea to make as many one-line blocks as possible,
8143 # so other types are not done. The user can always use -mangle.
8144 if ( $want_one_line_block{$block_type} ) {
8145 create_one_line_block( $i_start, 1 );
8146 }
8147 return 0;
8148}

8177sub undo_ci {
8178
8179 # Undo continuation indentation in certain sequences
8180 # For example, we can undo continuation indentation in sort/map/grep chains
8181 # my $dat1 = pack( "n*",
8182 # map { $_, $lookup->{$_} }
8183 # sort { $a <=> $b }
8184 # grep { $lookup->{$_} ne $default } keys %$lookup );
8185 # To align the map/sort/grep keywords like this:
8186 # my $dat1 = pack( "n*",
8187 # map { $_, $lookup->{$_} }
8188 # sort { $a <=> $b }
8189 # grep { $lookup->{$_} ne $default } keys %$lookup );
8190 my ( $ri_first, $ri_last ) = @_;
8191 my ( $line_1, $line_2, $lev_last );
8192 my $this_line_is_semicolon_terminated;
8193 my $max_line = @{$ri_first} - 1;
8194
8195 # looking at each line of this batch..
8196 # We are looking at leading tokens and looking for a sequence
8197 # all at the same level and higher level than enclosing lines.
8198 foreach my $line ( 0 .. $max_line ) {
8199
8200 my $ibeg = $ri_first->[$line];
8201 my $lev = $levels_to_go[$ibeg];
8202 if ( $line > 0 ) {
8203
8204 # if we have started a chain..
8205 if ($line_1) {
8206
8207 # see if it continues..
8208 if ( $lev == $lev_last ) {
8209 if ( $types_to_go[$ibeg] eq 'k'
8210 && $is_sort_map_grep{ $tokens_to_go[$ibeg] } )
8211 {
8212
8213 # chain continues...
8214 # check for chain ending at end of a statement
8215 if ( $line == $max_line ) {
8216
8217 # see of this line ends a statement
8218 my $iend = $ri_last->[$line];
8219 $this_line_is_semicolon_terminated =
8220 $types_to_go[$iend] eq ';'
8221
8222 # with possible side comment
8223 || ( $types_to_go[$iend] eq '#'
8224 && $iend - $ibeg >= 2
8225 && $types_to_go[ $iend - 2 ] eq ';'
8226 && $types_to_go[ $iend - 1 ] eq 'b' );
8227 }
8228 $line_2 = $line if ($this_line_is_semicolon_terminated);
8229 }
8230 else {
8231
8232 # kill chain
8233 $line_1 = undef;
8234 }
8235 }
8236 elsif ( $lev < $lev_last ) {
8237
8238 # chain ends with previous line
8239 $line_2 = $line - 1;
8240 }
8241 elsif ( $lev > $lev_last ) {
8242
8243 # kill chain
8244 $line_1 = undef;
8245 }
8246
8247 # undo the continuation indentation if a chain ends
8248 if ( defined($line_2) && defined($line_1) ) {
8249 my $continuation_line_count = $line_2 - $line_1 + 1;
8250 @ci_levels_to_go[ @{$ri_first}[ $line_1 .. $line_2 ] ] =
8251 (0) x ($continuation_line_count)
8252 if ( $continuation_line_count >= 0 );
8253 @leading_spaces_to_go[ @{$ri_first}[ $line_1 .. $line_2 ] ]
8254 = @reduced_spaces_to_go[ @{$ri_first}
8255 [ $line_1 .. $line_2 ] ];
8256 $line_1 = undef;
8257 }
8258 }
8259
8260 # not in a chain yet..
8261 else {
8262
8263 # look for start of a new sort/map/grep chain
8264 if ( $lev > $lev_last ) {
8265 if ( $types_to_go[$ibeg] eq 'k'
8266 && $is_sort_map_grep{ $tokens_to_go[$ibeg] } )
8267 {
8268 $line_1 = $line;
8269 }
8270 }
8271 }
8272 }
8273 $lev_last = $lev;
8274 }
8275 return;
8276}

8278sub undo_lp_ci {
8279
8280 # If there is a single, long parameter within parens, like this:
8281 #
8282 # $self->command( "/msg "
8283 # . $infoline->chan
8284 # . " You said $1, but did you know that it's square was "
8285 # . $1 * $1 . " ?" );
8286 #
8287 # we can remove the continuation indentation of the 2nd and higher lines
8288 # to achieve this effect, which is more pleasing:
8289 #
8290 # $self->command("/msg "
8291 # . $infoline->chan
8292 # . " You said $1, but did you know that it's square was "
8293 # . $1 * $1 . " ?");
8294
8295 my ( $line_open, $i_start, $closing_index, $ri_first, $ri_last ) = @_;
8296 my $max_line = @{$ri_first} - 1;
8297
8298 # must be multiple lines
8299 return unless $max_line > $line_open;
8300
8301 my $lev_start = $levels_to_go[$i_start];
8302 my $ci_start_plus = 1 + $ci_levels_to_go[$i_start];
8303
8304 # see if all additional lines in this container have continuation
8305 # indentation
8306 my $n;
8307 my $line_1 = 1 + $line_open;
8308 for ( $n = $line_1 ; $n <= $max_line ; ++$n ) {
8309 my $ibeg = $ri_first->[$n];
8310 my $iend = $ri_last->[$n];
8311 if ( $ibeg eq $closing_index ) { $n--; last }
8312 return if ( $lev_start != $levels_to_go[$ibeg] );
8313 return if ( $ci_start_plus != $ci_levels_to_go[$ibeg] );
8314 last if ( $closing_index <= $iend );
8315 }
8316
8317 # we can reduce the indentation of all continuation lines
8318 my $continuation_line_count = $n - $line_open;
8319 @ci_levels_to_go[ @{$ri_first}[ $line_1 .. $n ] ] =
8320 (0) x ($continuation_line_count);
8321 @leading_spaces_to_go[ @{$ri_first}[ $line_1 .. $n ] ] =
8322 @reduced_spaces_to_go[ @{$ri_first}[ $line_1 .. $n ] ];
8323 return;
8324}

8326sub pad_token {
8327
8328 # insert $pad_spaces before token number $ipad
8329 my ( $ipad, $pad_spaces ) = @_;
8330 if ( $pad_spaces > 0 ) {
8331 $tokens_to_go[$ipad] = ' ' x $pad_spaces . $tokens_to_go[$ipad];
8332 }
8333 elsif ( $pad_spaces == -1 && $tokens_to_go[$ipad] eq ' ' ) {
8334 $tokens_to_go[$ipad] = "";
8335 }
8336 else {
8337
8338 # shouldn't happen
8339 return;
8340 }
8341
8342 $token_lengths_to_go[$ipad] += $pad_spaces;
8343 foreach my $i ( $ipad .. $max_index_to_go ) {
8344 $summed_lengths_to_go[ $i + 1 ] += $pad_spaces;
8345 }
8346 return;
8347}

8358 sub set_logical_padding {
8359
8360 # Look at a batch of lines and see if extra padding can improve the
8361 # alignment when there are certain leading operators. Here is an
8362 # example, in which some extra space is introduced before
8363 # '( $year' to make it line up with the subsequent lines:
8364 #
8365 # if ( ( $Year < 1601 )
8366 # || ( $Year > 2899 )
8367 # || ( $EndYear < 1601 )
8368 # || ( $EndYear > 2899 ) )
8369 # {
8370 # &Error_OutOfRange;
8371 # }
8372 #
8373 my ( $ri_first, $ri_last ) = @_;
8374 my $max_line = @{$ri_first} - 1;
8375
8376 # FIXME: move these declarations below
8377 my ( $ibeg, $ibeg_next, $ibegm, $iend, $iendm, $ipad, $pad_spaces,
8378 $tok_next, $type_next, $has_leading_op_next, $has_leading_op );
8379
8380 # looking at each line of this batch..
8381 foreach my $line ( 0 .. $max_line - 1 ) {
8382
8383 # see if the next line begins with a logical operator
8384 $ibeg = $ri_first->[$line];
8385 $iend = $ri_last->[$line];
8386 $ibeg_next = $ri_first->[ $line + 1 ];
8387 $tok_next = $tokens_to_go[$ibeg_next];
8388 $type_next = $types_to_go[$ibeg_next];
8389
8390 $has_leading_op_next = ( $tok_next =~ /^\w/ )
8391 ? $is_chain_operator{$tok_next} # + - * / : ? && ||
8392 : $is_chain_operator{$type_next}; # and, or
8393
8394 next unless ($has_leading_op_next);
8395
8396 # next line must not be at lesser depth
8397 next
8398 if ( $nesting_depth_to_go[$ibeg] >
8399 $nesting_depth_to_go[$ibeg_next] );
8400
8401 # identify the token in this line to be padded on the left
8402 $ipad = undef;
8403
8404 # handle lines at same depth...
8405 if ( $nesting_depth_to_go[$ibeg] ==
8406 $nesting_depth_to_go[$ibeg_next] )
8407 {
8408
8409 # if this is not first line of the batch ...
8410 if ( $line > 0 ) {
8411
8412 # and we have leading operator..
8413 next if $has_leading_op;
8414
8415 # Introduce padding if..
8416 # 1. the previous line is at lesser depth, or
8417 # 2. the previous line ends in an assignment
8418 # 3. the previous line ends in a 'return'
8419 # 4. the previous line ends in a comma
8420 # Example 1: previous line at lesser depth
8421 # if ( ( $Year < 1601 ) # <- we are here but
8422 # || ( $Year > 2899 ) # list has not yet
8423 # || ( $EndYear < 1601 ) # collapsed vertically
8424 # || ( $EndYear > 2899 ) )
8425 # {
8426 #
8427 # Example 2: previous line ending in assignment:
8428 # $leapyear =
8429 # $year % 4 ? 0 # <- We are here
8430 # : $year % 100 ? 1
8431 # : $year % 400 ? 0
8432 # : 1;
8433 #
8434 # Example 3: previous line ending in comma:
8435 # push @expr,
8436 # /test/ ? undef
8437 # : eval($_) ? 1
8438 # : eval($_) ? 1
8439 # : 0;
8440
8441 # be sure levels agree (do not indent after an indented 'if')
8442 next
8443 if ( $levels_to_go[$ibeg] ne $levels_to_go[$ibeg_next] );
8444
8445 # allow padding on first line after a comma but only if:
8446 # (1) this is line 2 and
8447 # (2) there are at more than three lines and
8448 # (3) lines 3 and 4 have the same leading operator
8449 # These rules try to prevent padding within a long
8450 # comma-separated list.
8451 my $ok_comma;
8452 if ( $types_to_go[$iendm] eq ','
8453 && $line == 1
8454 && $max_line > 2 )
8455 {
8456 my $ibeg_next_next = $ri_first->[ $line + 2 ];
8457 my $tok_next_next = $tokens_to_go[$ibeg_next_next];
8458 $ok_comma = $tok_next_next eq $tok_next;
8459 }
8460
8461 next
8462 unless (
8463 $is_assignment{ $types_to_go[$iendm] }
8464 || $ok_comma
8465 || ( $nesting_depth_to_go[$ibegm] <
8466 $nesting_depth_to_go[$ibeg] )
8467 || ( $types_to_go[$iendm] eq 'k'
8468 && $tokens_to_go[$iendm] eq 'return' )
8469 );
8470
8471 # we will add padding before the first token
8472 $ipad = $ibeg;
8473 }
8474
8475 # for first line of the batch..
8476 else {
8477
8478 # WARNING: Never indent if first line is starting in a
8479 # continued quote, which would change the quote.
8480 next if $starting_in_quote;
8481
8482 # if this is text after closing '}'
8483 # then look for an interior token to pad
8484 if ( $types_to_go[$ibeg] eq '}' ) {
8485
8486 }
8487
8488 # otherwise, we might pad if it looks really good
8489 else {
8490
8491 # we might pad token $ibeg, so be sure that it
8492 # is at the same depth as the next line.
8493 next
8494 if ( $nesting_depth_to_go[$ibeg] !=
8495 $nesting_depth_to_go[$ibeg_next] );
8496
8497 # We can pad on line 1 of a statement if at least 3
8498 # lines will be aligned. Otherwise, it
8499 # can look very confusing.
8500
8501 # We have to be careful not to pad if there are too few
8502 # lines. The current rule is:
8503 # (1) in general we require at least 3 consecutive lines
8504 # with the same leading chain operator token,
8505 # (2) but an exception is that we only require two lines
8506 # with leading colons if there are no more lines. For example,
8507 # the first $i in the following snippet would get padding
8508 # by the second rule:
8509 #
8510 # $i == 1 ? ( "First", "Color" )
8511 # : $i == 2 ? ( "Then", "Rarity" )
8512 # : ( "Then", "Name" );
8513
8514 if ( $max_line > 1 ) {
8515 my $leading_token = $tokens_to_go[$ibeg_next];
8516 my $tokens_differ;
8517
8518 # never indent line 1 of a '.' series because
8519 # previous line is most likely at same level.
8520 # TODO: we should also look at the leasing_spaces
8521 # of the last output line and skip if it is same
8522 # as this line.
8523 next if ( $leading_token eq '.' );
8524
8525 my $count = 1;
8526 foreach my $l ( 2 .. 3 ) {
8527 last if ( $line + $l > $max_line );
8528 my $ibeg_next_next = $ri_first->[ $line + $l ];
8529 if ( $tokens_to_go[$ibeg_next_next] ne
8530 $leading_token )
8531 {
8532 $tokens_differ = 1;
8533 last;
8534 }
8535 $count++;
8536 }
8537 next if ($tokens_differ);
8538 next if ( $count < 3 && $leading_token ne ':' );
8539 $ipad = $ibeg;
8540 }
8541 else {
8542 next;
8543 }
8544 }
8545 }
8546 }
8547
8548 # find interior token to pad if necessary
8549 if ( !defined($ipad) ) {
8550
8551 for ( my $i = $ibeg ; ( $i < $iend ) && !$ipad ; $i++ ) {
8552
8553 # find any unclosed container
8554 next
8555 unless ( $type_sequence_to_go[$i]
8556 && $mate_index_to_go[$i] > $iend );
8557
8558 # find next nonblank token to pad
8559 $ipad = $inext_to_go[$i];
8560 last if ( $ipad > $iend );
8561 }
8562 last unless $ipad;
8563 }
8564
8565 # We cannot pad the first leading token of a file because
8566 # it could cause a bug in which the starting indentation
8567 # level is guessed incorrectly each time the code is run
8568 # though perltidy, thus causing the code to march off to
8569 # the right. For example, the following snippet would have
8570 # this problem:
8571
8572## ov_method mycan( $package, '(""' ), $package
8573## or ov_method mycan( $package, '(0+' ), $package
8574## or ov_method mycan( $package, '(bool' ), $package
8575## or ov_method mycan( $package, '(nomethod' ), $package;
8576
8577 # If this snippet is within a block this won't happen
8578 # unless the user just processes the snippet alone within
8579 # an editor. In that case either the user will see and
8580 # fix the problem or it will be corrected next time the
8581 # entire file is processed with perltidy.
8582 next if ( $ipad == 0 && $peak_batch_size <= 1 );
8583
8584## THIS PATCH REMOVES THE FOLLOWING POOR PADDING (math.t) with -pbp, BUT
8585## IT DID MORE HARM THAN GOOD
8586## ceil(
8587## $font->{'loca'}->{'glyphs'}[$x]->read->{'xMin'} * 1000
8588## / $upem
8589## ),
8590##? # do not put leading padding for just 2 lines of math
8591##? if ( $ipad == $ibeg
8592##? && $line > 0
8593##? && $levels_to_go[$ipad] > $levels_to_go[ $ipad - 1 ]
8594##? && $is_math_op{$type_next}
8595##? && $line + 2 <= $max_line )
8596##? {
8597##? my $ibeg_next_next = $ri_first->[ $line + 2 ];
8598##? my $type_next_next = $types_to_go[$ibeg_next_next];
8599##? next if !$is_math_op{$type_next_next};
8600##? }
8601
8602 # next line must not be at greater depth
8603 my $iend_next = $ri_last->[ $line + 1 ];
8604 next
8605 if ( $nesting_depth_to_go[ $iend_next + 1 ] >
8606 $nesting_depth_to_go[$ipad] );
8607
8608 # lines must be somewhat similar to be padded..
8609 my $inext_next = $inext_to_go[$ibeg_next];
8610 my $type = $types_to_go[$ipad];
8611 my $type_next = $types_to_go[ $ipad + 1 ];
8612
8613 # see if there are multiple continuation lines
8614 my $logical_continuation_lines = 1;
8615 if ( $line + 2 <= $max_line ) {
8616 my $leading_token = $tokens_to_go[$ibeg_next];
8617 my $ibeg_next_next = $ri_first->[ $line + 2 ];
8618 if ( $tokens_to_go[$ibeg_next_next] eq $leading_token
8619 && $nesting_depth_to_go[$ibeg_next] eq
8620 $nesting_depth_to_go[$ibeg_next_next] )
8621 {
8622 $logical_continuation_lines++;
8623 }
8624 }
8625
8626 # see if leading types match
8627 my $types_match = $types_to_go[$inext_next] eq $type;
8628 my $matches_without_bang;
8629
8630 # if first line has leading ! then compare the following token
8631 if ( !$types_match && $type eq '!' ) {
8632 $types_match = $matches_without_bang =
8633 $types_to_go[$inext_next] eq $types_to_go[ $ipad + 1 ];
8634 }
8635
8636 if (
8637
8638 # either we have multiple continuation lines to follow
8639 # and we are not padding the first token
8640 ( $logical_continuation_lines > 1 && $ipad > 0 )
8641
8642 # or..
8643 || (
8644
8645 # types must match
8646 $types_match
8647
8648 # and keywords must match if keyword
8649 && !(
8650 $type eq 'k'
8651 && $tokens_to_go[$ipad] ne $tokens_to_go[$inext_next]
8652 )
8653 )
8654 )
8655 {
8656
8657 #----------------------begin special checks--------------
8658 #
8659 # SPECIAL CHECK 1:
8660 # A check is needed before we can make the pad.
8661 # If we are in a list with some long items, we want each
8662 # item to stand out. So in the following example, the
8663 # first line beginning with '$casefold->' would look good
8664 # padded to align with the next line, but then it
8665 # would be indented more than the last line, so we
8666 # won't do it.
8667 #
8668 # ok(
8669 # $casefold->{code} eq '0041'
8670 # && $casefold->{status} eq 'C'
8671 # && $casefold->{mapping} eq '0061',
8672 # 'casefold 0x41'
8673 # );
8674 #
8675 # Note:
8676 # It would be faster, and almost as good, to use a comma
8677 # count, and not pad if comma_count > 1 and the previous
8678 # line did not end with a comma.
8679 #
8680 my $ok_to_pad = 1;
8681
8682 my $ibg = $ri_first->[ $line + 1 ];
8683 my $depth = $nesting_depth_to_go[ $ibg + 1 ];
8684
8685 # just use simplified formula for leading spaces to avoid
8686 # needless sub calls
8687 my $lsp = $levels_to_go[$ibg] + $ci_levels_to_go[$ibg];
8688
8689 # look at each line beyond the next ..
8690 my $l = $line + 1;
8691 foreach my $ltest ( $line + 2 .. $max_line ) {
8692 $l = $ltest;
8693 my $ibg = $ri_first->[$l];
8694
8695 # quit looking at the end of this container
8696 last
8697 if ( $nesting_depth_to_go[ $ibg + 1 ] < $depth )
8698 || ( $nesting_depth_to_go[$ibg] < $depth );
8699
8700 # cannot do the pad if a later line would be
8701 # outdented more
8702 if ( $levels_to_go[$ibg] + $ci_levels_to_go[$ibg] < $lsp ) {
8703 $ok_to_pad = 0;
8704 last;
8705 }
8706 }
8707
8708 # don't pad if we end in a broken list
8709 if ( $l == $max_line ) {
8710 my $i2 = $ri_last->[$l];
8711 if ( $types_to_go[$i2] eq '#' ) {
8712 my $i1 = $ri_first->[$l];
8713 next
8714 if (
8715 terminal_type( \@types_to_go, \@block_type_to_go,
8716 $i1, $i2 ) eq ','
8717 );
8718 }
8719 }
8720
8721 # SPECIAL CHECK 2:
8722 # a minus may introduce a quoted variable, and we will
8723 # add the pad only if this line begins with a bare word,
8724 # such as for the word 'Button' here:
8725 # [
8726 # Button => "Print letter \"~$_\"",
8727 # -command => [ sub { print "$_[0]\n" }, $_ ],
8728 # -accelerator => "Meta+$_"
8729 # ];
8730 #
8731 # On the other hand, if 'Button' is quoted, it looks best
8732 # not to pad:
8733 # [
8734 # 'Button' => "Print letter \"~$_\"",
8735 # -command => [ sub { print "$_[0]\n" }, $_ ],
8736 # -accelerator => "Meta+$_"
8737 # ];
8738 if ( $types_to_go[$ibeg_next] eq 'm' ) {
8739 $ok_to_pad = 0 if $types_to_go[$ibeg] eq 'Q';
8740 }
8741
8742 next unless $ok_to_pad;
8743
8744 #----------------------end special check---------------
8745
8746 my $length_1 = total_line_length( $ibeg, $ipad - 1 );
8747 my $length_2 = total_line_length( $ibeg_next, $inext_next - 1 );
8748 $pad_spaces = $length_2 - $length_1;
8749
8750 # If the first line has a leading ! and the second does
8751 # not, then remove one space to try to align the next
8752 # leading characters, which are often the same. For example:
8753 # if ( !$ts
8754 # || $ts == $self->Holder
8755 # || $self->Holder->Type eq "Arena" )
8756 #
8757 # This usually helps readability, but if there are subsequent
8758 # ! operators things will still get messed up. For example:
8759 #
8760 # if ( !exists $Net::DNS::typesbyname{$qtype}
8761 # && exists $Net::DNS::classesbyname{$qtype}
8762 # && !exists $Net::DNS::classesbyname{$qclass}
8763 # && exists $Net::DNS::typesbyname{$qclass} )
8764 # We can't fix that.
8765 if ($matches_without_bang) { $pad_spaces-- }
8766
8767 # make sure this won't change if -lp is used
8768 my $indentation_1 = $leading_spaces_to_go[$ibeg];
8769 if ( ref($indentation_1) ) {
8770 if ( $indentation_1->get_recoverable_spaces() == 0 ) {
8771 my $indentation_2 = $leading_spaces_to_go[$ibeg_next];
8772 unless ( $indentation_2->get_recoverable_spaces() == 0 )
8773 {
8774 $pad_spaces = 0;
8775 }
8776 }
8777 }
8778
8779 # we might be able to handle a pad of -1 by removing a blank
8780 # token
8781 if ( $pad_spaces < 0 ) {
8782
8783 if ( $pad_spaces == -1 ) {
8784 if ( $ipad > $ibeg && $types_to_go[ $ipad - 1 ] eq 'b' )
8785 {
8786 pad_token( $ipad - 1, $pad_spaces );
8787 }
8788 }
8789 $pad_spaces = 0;
8790 }
8791
8792 # now apply any padding for alignment
8793 if ( $ipad >= 0 && $pad_spaces ) {
8794
8795 my $length_t = total_line_length( $ibeg, $iend );
8796 if ( $pad_spaces + $length_t <= maximum_line_length($ibeg) )
8797 {
8798 pad_token( $ipad, $pad_spaces );
8799 }
8800 }
8801 }
8802 }
8803 continue {
8804 $iendm = $iend;
8805 $ibegm = $ibeg;
8806 $has_leading_op = $has_leading_op_next;
8807 } # end of loop over lines
8808 return;
8809 }
8810}
8811
88121200nssub correct_lp_indentation {
8813
8814 # When the -lp option is used, we need to make a last pass through
8815 # each line to correct the indentation positions in case they differ
8816 # from the predictions. This is necessary because perltidy uses a
8817 # predictor/corrector method for aligning with opening parens. The
8818 # predictor is usually good, but sometimes stumbles. The corrector
8819 # tries to patch things up once the actual opening paren locations
8820 # are known.
8821 my ( $ri_first, $ri_last ) = @_;
8822 my $do_not_pad = 0;
8823
8824 # Note on flag '$do_not_pad':
8825 # We want to avoid a situation like this, where the aligner inserts
8826 # whitespace before the '=' to align it with a previous '=', because
8827 # otherwise the parens might become mis-aligned in a situation like
8828 # this, where the '=' has become aligned with the previous line,
8829 # pushing the opening '(' forward beyond where we want it.
8830 #
8831 # $mkFloor::currentRoom = '';
8832 # $mkFloor::c_entry = $c->Entry(
8833 # -width => '10',
8834 # -relief => 'sunken',
8835 # ...
8836 # );
8837 #
8838 # We leave it to the aligner to decide how to do this.
8839
8840 # first remove continuation indentation if appropriate
8841 my $max_line = @{$ri_first} - 1;
8842
8843 # looking at each line of this batch..
8844 my ( $ibeg, $iend );
8845 foreach my $line ( 0 .. $max_line ) {
8846 $ibeg = $ri_first->[$line];
8847 $iend = $ri_last->[$line];
8848
8849 # looking at each token in this output line..
8850 foreach my $i ( $ibeg .. $iend ) {
8851
8852 # How many space characters to place before this token
8853 # for special alignment. Actual padding is done in the
8854 # continue block.
8855
8856 # looking for next unvisited indentation item
8857 my $indentation = $leading_spaces_to_go[$i];
8858 if ( !$indentation->get_marked() ) {
8859 $indentation->set_marked(1);
8860
8861 # looking for indentation item for which we are aligning
8862 # with parens, braces, and brackets
8863 next unless ( $indentation->get_align_paren() );
8864
8865 # skip closed container on this line
8866 if ( $i > $ibeg ) {
8867 my $im = max( $ibeg, $iprev_to_go[$i] );
8868 if ( $type_sequence_to_go[$im]
8869 && $mate_index_to_go[$im] <= $iend )
8870 {
8871 next;
8872 }
8873 }
8874
8875 if ( $line == 1 && $i == $ibeg ) {
8876 $do_not_pad = 1;
8877 }
8878
8879 # Ok, let's see what the error is and try to fix it
8880 my $actual_pos;
8881 my $predicted_pos = $indentation->get_spaces();
8882 if ( $i > $ibeg ) {
8883
8884 # token is mid-line - use length to previous token
8885 $actual_pos = total_line_length( $ibeg, $i - 1 );
8886
8887 # for mid-line token, we must check to see if all
8888 # additional lines have continuation indentation,
8889 # and remove it if so. Otherwise, we do not get
8890 # good alignment.
8891 my $closing_index = $indentation->get_closed();
8892 if ( $closing_index > $iend ) {
8893 my $ibeg_next = $ri_first->[ $line + 1 ];
8894 if ( $ci_levels_to_go[$ibeg_next] > 0 ) {
8895 undo_lp_ci( $line, $i, $closing_index, $ri_first,
8896 $ri_last );
8897 }
8898 }
8899 }
8900 elsif ( $line > 0 ) {
8901
8902 # handle case where token starts a new line;
8903 # use length of previous line
8904 my $ibegm = $ri_first->[ $line - 1 ];
8905 my $iendm = $ri_last->[ $line - 1 ];
8906 $actual_pos = total_line_length( $ibegm, $iendm );
8907
8908 # follow -pt style
8909 ++$actual_pos
8910 if ( $types_to_go[ $iendm + 1 ] eq 'b' );
8911 }
8912 else {
8913
8914 # token is first character of first line of batch
8915 $actual_pos = $predicted_pos;
8916 }
8917
8918 my $move_right = $actual_pos - $predicted_pos;
8919
8920 # done if no error to correct (gnu2.t)
8921 if ( $move_right == 0 ) {
8922 $indentation->set_recoverable_spaces($move_right);
8923 next;
8924 }
8925
8926 # if we have not seen closure for this indentation in
8927 # this batch, we can only pass on a request to the
8928 # vertical aligner
8929 my $closing_index = $indentation->get_closed();
8930
8931 if ( $closing_index < 0 ) {
8932 $indentation->set_recoverable_spaces($move_right);
8933 next;
8934 }
8935
8936 # If necessary, look ahead to see if there is really any
8937 # leading whitespace dependent on this whitespace, and
8938 # also find the longest line using this whitespace.
8939 # Since it is always safe to move left if there are no
8940 # dependents, we only need to do this if we may have
8941 # dependent nodes or need to move right.
8942
8943 my $right_margin = 0;
8944 my $have_child = $indentation->get_have_child();
8945
8946 my %saw_indentation;
8947 my $line_count = 1;
8948 $saw_indentation{$indentation} = $indentation;
8949
8950 if ( $have_child || $move_right > 0 ) {
8951 $have_child = 0;
8952 my $max_length = 0;
8953 if ( $i == $ibeg ) {
8954 $max_length = total_line_length( $ibeg, $iend );
8955 }
8956
8957 # look ahead at the rest of the lines of this batch..
8958 foreach my $line_t ( $line + 1 .. $max_line ) {
8959 my $ibeg_t = $ri_first->[$line_t];
8960 my $iend_t = $ri_last->[$line_t];
8961 last if ( $closing_index <= $ibeg_t );
8962
8963 # remember all different indentation objects
8964 my $indentation_t = $leading_spaces_to_go[$ibeg_t];
8965 $saw_indentation{$indentation_t} = $indentation_t;
8966 $line_count++;
8967
8968 # remember longest line in the group
8969 my $length_t = total_line_length( $ibeg_t, $iend_t );
8970 if ( $length_t > $max_length ) {
8971 $max_length = $length_t;
8972 }
8973 }
8974 $right_margin = maximum_line_length($ibeg) - $max_length;
8975 if ( $right_margin < 0 ) { $right_margin = 0 }
8976 }
8977
8978 my $first_line_comma_count =
8979 grep { $_ eq ',' } @types_to_go[ $ibeg .. $iend ];
8980 my $comma_count = $indentation->get_comma_count();
8981 my $arrow_count = $indentation->get_arrow_count();
8982
8983 # This is a simple approximate test for vertical alignment:
8984 # if we broke just after an opening paren, brace, bracket,
8985 # and there are 2 or more commas in the first line,
8986 # and there are no '=>'s,
8987 # then we are probably vertically aligned. We could set
8988 # an exact flag in sub scan_list, but this is good
8989 # enough.
8990 my $indentation_count = keys %saw_indentation;
8991 my $is_vertically_aligned =
8992 ( $i == $ibeg
8993 && $first_line_comma_count > 1
8994 && $indentation_count == 1
8995 && ( $arrow_count == 0 || $arrow_count == $line_count ) );
8996
8997 # Make the move if possible ..
8998 if (
8999
9000 # we can always move left
9001 $move_right < 0
9002
9003 # but we should only move right if we are sure it will
9004 # not spoil vertical alignment
9005 || ( $comma_count == 0 )
9006 || ( $comma_count > 0 && !$is_vertically_aligned )
9007 )
9008 {
9009 my $move =
9010 ( $move_right <= $right_margin )
9011 ? $move_right
9012 : $right_margin;
9013
9014 foreach ( keys %saw_indentation ) {
9015 $saw_indentation{$_}
9016 ->permanently_decrease_available_spaces( -$move );
9017 }
9018 }
9019
9020 # Otherwise, record what we want and the vertical aligner
9021 # will try to recover it.
9022 else {
9023 $indentation->set_recoverable_spaces($move_right);
9024 }
9025 }
9026 }
9027 }
9028 return $do_not_pad;
9029}

9031# flush is called to output any tokens in the pipeline, so that
9032# an alternate source of lines can be written in the correct order
9033
9034sub flush {
9035 my $self = shift;
9036 destroy_one_line_block();
9037 $self->output_line_to_go();
9038 Perl::Tidy::VerticalAligner::flush();
9039 return;
9040}
9041
9042sub reset_block_text_accumulator {
9043
9044 # save text after 'if' and 'elsif' to append after 'else'
9045 if ($accumulating_text_for_block) {
9046
9047 if ( $accumulating_text_for_block =~ /^(if|elsif)$/ ) {
9048 push @{$rleading_block_if_elsif_text}, $leading_block_text;
9049 }
9050 }
9051 $accumulating_text_for_block = "";
9052 $leading_block_text = "";
9053 $leading_block_text_level = 0;
9054 $leading_block_text_length_exceeded = 0;
9055 $leading_block_text_line_number = 0;
9056 $leading_block_text_line_length = 0;
9057 return;
9058}
9059
9060sub set_block_text_accumulator {
9061 my $i = shift;
9062 $accumulating_text_for_block = $tokens_to_go[$i];
9063 if ( $accumulating_text_for_block !~ /^els/ ) {
9064 $rleading_block_if_elsif_text = [];
9065 }
9066 $leading_block_text = "";
9067 $leading_block_text_level = $levels_to_go[$i];
9068 $leading_block_text_line_number = get_output_line_number();
9069 $leading_block_text_length_exceeded = 0;
9070
9071 # this will contain the column number of the last character
9072 # of the closing side comment
9073 $leading_block_text_line_length =
9074 length($csc_last_label) +
9075 length($accumulating_text_for_block) +
9076 length( $rOpts->{'closing-side-comment-prefix'} ) +
9077 $leading_block_text_level * $rOpts_indent_columns + 3;
9078 return;
9079}
9080
9081sub accumulate_block_text {
9082 my $i = shift;
9083
9084 # accumulate leading text for -csc, ignoring any side comments
9085 if ( $accumulating_text_for_block
9086 && !$leading_block_text_length_exceeded
9087 && $types_to_go[$i] ne '#' )
9088 {
9089
9090 my $added_length = $token_lengths_to_go[$i];
9091 $added_length += 1 if $i == 0;
9092 my $new_line_length = $leading_block_text_line_length + $added_length;
9093
9094 # we can add this text if we don't exceed some limits..
9095 if (
9096
9097 # we must not have already exceeded the text length limit
9098 length($leading_block_text) <
9099 $rOpts_closing_side_comment_maximum_text
9100
9101 # and either:
9102 # the new total line length must be below the line length limit
9103 # or the new length must be below the text length limit
9104 # (ie, we may allow one token to exceed the text length limit)
9105 && (
9106 $new_line_length <
9107 maximum_line_length_for_level($leading_block_text_level)
9108
9109 || length($leading_block_text) + $added_length <
9110 $rOpts_closing_side_comment_maximum_text
9111 )
9112
9113 # UNLESS: we are adding a closing paren before the brace we seek.
9114 # This is an attempt to avoid situations where the ... to be
9115 # added are longer than the omitted right paren, as in:
9116
9117 # foreach my $item (@a_rather_long_variable_name_here) {
9118 # &whatever;
9119 # } ## end foreach my $item (@a_rather_long_variable_name_here...
9120
9121 || (
9122 $tokens_to_go[$i] eq ')'
9123 && (
9124 (
9125 $i + 1 <= $max_index_to_go
9126 && $block_type_to_go[ $i + 1 ] eq
9127 $accumulating_text_for_block
9128 )
9129 || ( $i + 2 <= $max_index_to_go
