9418 sub balance_csc_text {
9419
9420 # Append characters to balance a closing side comment so that editors
9421 # such as vim can correctly jump through code.
9422 # Simple Example:
9423 # input = ## end foreach my $foo ( sort { $b ...
9424 # output = ## end foreach my $foo ( sort { $b ...})
9425
9426 # NOTE: This routine does not currently filter out structures within
9427 # quoted text because the bounce algorithms in text editors do not
9428 # necessarily do this either (a version of vim was checked and
9429 # did not do this).
9430
9431 # Some complex examples which will cause trouble for some editors:
9432 # while ( $mask_string =~ /\{[^{]*?\}/g ) {
9433 # if ( $mask_str =~ /\}\s*els[^\{\}]+\{$/ ) {
9434 # if ( $1 eq '{' ) {
9435 # test file test1/braces.pl has many such examples.
9436
9437 my ($csc) = @_;
9438
9439 # loop to examine characters one-by-one, RIGHT to LEFT and
9440 # build a balancing ending, LEFT to RIGHT.
9441 for ( my $pos = length($csc) - 1 ; $pos >= 0 ; $pos-- ) {
9442
9443 my $char = substr( $csc, $pos, 1 );
9444
9445 # ignore everything except structural characters
9446 next unless ( $matching_char{$char} );
9447
9448 # pop most recently appended character
9449 my $top = chop($csc);
9450
9451 # push it back plus the mate to the newest character
9452 # unless they balance each other.
9453 $csc = $csc . $top . $matching_char{$char} unless $top eq $char;
9454 }
9455
9456 # return the balanced string
9457 return $csc;
9458 }
9459}

9764 $types_to_go[$ibeg] eq '#'
9765 && $rOpts->{'outdent-long-comments'}
9766
9767 # but not if this is a static block comment
9768 && !$is_static_block_comment
9769 )
9770 );

9772 my $level_jump =
9773 $nesting_depth_to_go[ $iend + 1 ] - $nesting_depth_to_go[$ibeg];
9774
9775 my $rvertical_tightness_flags =

9777 $ri_first, $ri_last );

9779 # flush an outdented line to avoid any unwanted vertical alignment
9780 Perl::Tidy::VerticalAligner::flush() if ($is_outdented_line);

9783 # vertical alignment of the final term. Here is a
9784 # slightly complex example:
9785 #
9786 # $self->{_text} = (
9787 # !$section ? ''
9788 # : $type eq 'item' ? "the $section entry"
9789 # : "the section on $section"
9790 # )
9791 # . (
9792 # $page
9793 # ? ( $section ? ' in ' : '' ) . "the $page$page_ext manpage"
9794 # : ' elsewhere in this document'
9795 # );
9796 #
9797 my $is_terminal_ternary = 0;
9798 if ( $tokens_to_go[$ibeg] eq ':'
9799 || $n > 0 && $tokens_to_go[ $ri_last->[ $n - 1 ] ] eq ':' )
9800 {
9801 my $last_leading_type = ":";
9802 if ( $n > 0 ) {
9803 my $iprev = $ri_first->[ $n - 1 ];
9804 $last_leading_type = $types_to_go[$iprev];
9805 }
9806 if ( $terminal_type ne ';'
9807 && $n_last_line > $n
9808 && $level_end == $lev )
9809 {
9810 my $inext = $ri_first->[ $n + 1 ];
9811 $level_end = $levels_to_go[$inext];
9812 $terminal_type = $types_to_go[$inext];
9813 }
9814
9815 $is_terminal_ternary = $last_leading_type eq ':'
9816 && ( ( $terminal_type eq ';' && $level_end <= $lev )
9817 || ( $terminal_type ne ':' && $level_end < $lev ) )

9819 # the terminal term must not contain any ternary terms, as in
9820 # my $ECHO = (
9821 # $Is_MSWin32 ? ".\\echo$$"
9822 # : $Is_MacOS ? ":echo$$"
9823 # : ( $Is_NetWare ? "echo$$" : "./echo$$" )

9825 && !grep { /^[\?\:]$/ } @types_to_go[ $ibeg + 1 .. $iend ];

9829 my $forced_breakpoint = $forced_breakpoint_to_go[$iend];

9833 $rvalign_hash->{level_end} = $level_end;
9834 $rvalign_hash->{indentation} = $indentation;
9835 $rvalign_hash->{is_forced_break} =
9836 $forced_breakpoint_to_go[$iend] || $in_comma_list;
9837 $rvalign_hash->{outdent_long_lines} = $outdent_long_lines;
9838 $rvalign_hash->{is_terminal_ternary} = $is_terminal_ternary;
9839 $rvalign_hash->{is_terminal_statement} = $is_semicolon_terminated;
9840 $rvalign_hash->{do_not_pad} = $do_not_pad;
9841 $rvalign_hash->{rvertical_tightness_flags} = $rvertical_tightness_flags;
9842 $rvalign_hash->{level_jump} = $level_jump;
9843
9844 $rvalign_hash->{valign_batch_number} = $valign_batch_number;
9845
9846 Perl::Tidy::VerticalAligner::valign_input( $rvalign_hash, $rfields,
9847 $rtokens, $rpatterns );
9848
9849 $in_comma_list =
9850 $tokens_to_go[$iend] eq ',' && $forced_breakpoint_to_go[$iend];
9851
9852 # flush an outdented line to avoid any unwanted vertical alignment
9853 Perl::Tidy::VerticalAligner::flush() if ($is_outdented_line);
9854
9855 $do_not_pad = 0;
9856
9857 # Set flag indicating if this line ends in an opening
9858 # token and is very short, so that a blank line is not
9859 # needed if the subsequent line is a comment.
9860 # Examples of what we are looking for:
9861 # {
9862 # && (
9863 # BEGIN {
9864 # default {
9865 # sub {
9866 $last_output_short_opening_token
9867
9868 # line ends in opening token
9869 = $types_to_go[$iend] =~ /^[\{\(\[L]$/
9870
9871 # and either
9872 && (
9873 # line has either single opening token
9874 $iend == $ibeg

9876 # or is a single token followed by opening token.
9877 # Note that sub identifiers have blanks like 'sub doit'

9884 } # end of loop to output each line
9885
9886 # remember indentation of lines containing opening containers for
9887 # later use by sub set_adjusted_indentation
9888 save_opening_indentation( $ri_first, $ri_last, $rindentation_list );
9889
9890 # output any new -cscw block comment
9891 if ($cscw_block_comment) {
9892 Perl::Tidy::VerticalAligner::flush();
9893 $file_writer_object->write_code_line( $cscw_block_comment . "\n" );
9894 }

9943 sub delete_needless_alignments {
9944 my ( $ibeg, $iend ) = @_;
9945
9946 # Remove unwanted alignments. This routine is a place to remove alignments
9947 # which might cause problems at later stages. There are currently
9948 # two types of fixes:
9949
9950 # 1. Remove excess parens
9951 # 2. Remove alignments within 'elsif' conditions
9952
9953 # Patch #1: Excess alignment of parens can prevent other good
9954 # alignments. For example, note the parens in the first two rows of
9955 # the following snippet. They would normally get marked for alignment
9956 # and aligned as follows:
9957
9958 # my $w = $columns * $cell_w + ( $columns + 1 ) * $border;
9959 # my $h = $rows * $cell_h + ( $rows + 1 ) * $border;
9960 # my $img = new Gimp::Image( $w, $h, RGB );
9961
9962 # This causes unnecessary paren alignment and prevents the third equals
9963 # from aligning. If we remove the unwanted alignments we get:
9964
9965 # my $w = $columns * $cell_w + ( $columns + 1 ) * $border;
9966 # my $h = $rows * $cell_h + ( $rows + 1 ) * $border;
9967 # my $img = new Gimp::Image( $w, $h, RGB );
9968
9969 # A rule for doing this which works well is to remove alignment of
9970 # parens whose containers do not contain other aligning tokens, with
9971 # the exception that we always keep alignment of the first opening
9972 # paren on a line (for things like 'if' and 'elsif' statements).
9973
9974 # Setup needed constants
9975 my $i_good_paren = -1;
9976 my $imin_match = $iend + 1;
9977 my $i_elsif_close = $ibeg - 1;
9978 my $i_elsif_open = $iend + 1;
9979 if ( $iend > $ibeg ) {
9980 if ( $types_to_go[$ibeg] eq 'k' ) {
9981
9982 # Paren patch: mark a location of a paren we should keep, such
9983 # as one following something like a leading 'if', 'elsif',..
9984 $i_good_paren = $ibeg + 1;
9985 if ( $types_to_go[$i_good_paren] eq 'b' ) {
9986 $i_good_paren++;
9987 }
9988
9989 # 'elsif' patch: remember the range of the parens of an elsif,
9990 # and do not make alignments within them because this can cause
9991 # loss of padding and overall brace alignment in the vertical
9992 # aligner.
9993 if ( $tokens_to_go[$ibeg] eq 'elsif'
9994 && $i_good_paren < $iend
9995 && $tokens_to_go[$i_good_paren] eq '(' )
9996 {
9997 $i_elsif_open = $i_good_paren;
9998 $i_elsif_close = $mate_index_to_go[$i_good_paren];
9999 }
10000 }
10001 }
10002
10003 # Loop to make the fixes on this line
10004 my @imatch_list;
10005 for my $i ( $ibeg .. $iend ) {
10006
10007 if ( $matching_token_to_go[$i] ne '' ) {
10008
10009 # Patch #2: undo alignment within elsif parens
10010 if ( $i > $i_elsif_open && $i < $i_elsif_close ) {
10011 $matching_token_to_go[$i] = '';
10012 next;
10013 }
10014 push @imatch_list, $i;
10015
10016 }
10017 if ( $tokens_to_go[$i] eq ')' ) {
10018
10019 # Patch #1: undo the corresponding opening paren if:
10020 # - it is at the top of the stack
10021 # - and not the first overall opening paren
10022 # - does not follow a leading keyword on this line
10023 my $imate = $mate_index_to_go[$i];
10024 if ( @imatch_list
10025 && $imatch_list[-1] eq $imate
10026 && ( $ibeg > 1 || @imatch_list > 1 )
10027 && $imate > $i_good_paren )
10028 {
10029 $matching_token_to_go[$imate] = '';
10030 pop @imatch_list;
10031 }
10032 }
10033 }
10034 return;
10035 }

10037 sub make_alignment_patterns {
10038
10039 # Here we do some important preliminary work for the
10040 # vertical aligner. We create three arrays for one
10041 # output line. These arrays contain strings that can
10042 # be tested by the vertical aligner to see if
10043 # consecutive lines can be aligned vertically.
10044 #
10045 # The three arrays are indexed on the vertical
10046 # alignment fields and are:
10047 # @tokens - a list of any vertical alignment tokens for this line.
10048 # These are tokens, such as '=' '&&' '#' etc which
10049 # we want to might align vertically. These are
10050 # decorated with various information such as
10051 # nesting depth to prevent unwanted vertical
10052 # alignment matches.
10053 # @fields - the actual text of the line between the vertical alignment
10054 # tokens.
10055 # @patterns - a modified list of token types, one for each alignment
10056 # field. These should normally each match before alignment is
10057 # allowed, even when the alignment tokens match.
10058 my ( $ibeg, $iend ) = @_;
10059 my @tokens = ();
10060 my @fields = ();
10061 my @patterns = ();
10062 my $i_start = $ibeg;
10063
10064 my $depth = 0;
10065 my @container_name = ("");
10066 my @multiple_comma_arrows = (undef);
10067
10068 my $j = 0; # field index
10069
10070 $patterns[0] = "";
10071 for my $i ( $ibeg .. $iend ) {
10072
10073 # Keep track of containers balanced on this line only.
10074 # These are used below to prevent unwanted cross-line alignments.
10075 # Unbalanced containers already avoid aligning across
10076 # container boundaries.
10077 my $tok = $tokens_to_go[$i];
10078 if ( $tok =~ /^[\(\{\[]/ ) { #'(' ) {
10079
10080 # if container is balanced on this line...
10081 my $i_mate = $mate_index_to_go[$i];
10082 if ( $i_mate > $i && $i_mate <= $iend ) {
10083 $depth++;
10084 my $seqno = $type_sequence_to_go[$i];
10085 my $count = comma_arrow_count($seqno);
10086 $multiple_comma_arrows[$depth] = $count && $count > 1;
10087
10088 # Append the previous token name to make the container name
10089 # more unique. This name will also be given to any commas
10090 # within this container, and it helps avoid undesirable
10091 # alignments of different types of containers.
10092
10093 # Containers beginning with { and [ are given those names
10094 # for uniqueness. That way commas in different containers
10095 # will not match. Here is an example of what this prevents:
10096 # a => [ 1, 2, 3 ],
10097 # b => { b1 => 4, b2 => 5 },
10098 # Here is another example of what we avoid by labeling the
10099 # commas properly:
10100 # is_d( [ $a, $a ], [ $b, $c ] );
10101 # is_d( { foo => $a, bar => $a }, { foo => $b, bar => $c } );
10102 # is_d( [ \$a, \$a ], [ \$b, \$c ] );
10103
10104 my $name = $tok;
10105 if ( $tok eq '(' ) {
10106 $name = previous_nonblank_token($i);
10107 $name =~ s/^->//;
10108 }
10109 $container_name[$depth] = "+" . $name;
10110
10111 # Make the container name even more unique if necessary.
10112 # If we are not vertically aligning this opening paren,
10113 # append a character count to avoid bad alignment because
10114 # it usually looks bad to align commas within containers
10115 # for which the opening parens do not align. Here
10116 # is an example very BAD alignment of commas (because
10117 # the atan2 functions are not all aligned):
10118 # $XY =
10119 # $X * $RTYSQP1 * atan2( $X, $RTYSQP1 ) +
10120 # $Y * $RTXSQP1 * atan2( $Y, $RTXSQP1 ) -
10121 # $X * atan2( $X, 1 ) -
10122 # $Y * atan2( $Y, 1 );
10123 #
10124 # On the other hand, it is usually okay to align commas if
10125 # opening parens align, such as:
10126 # glVertex3d( $cx + $s * $xs, $cy, $z );
10127 # glVertex3d( $cx, $cy + $s * $ys, $z );
10128 # glVertex3d( $cx - $s * $xs, $cy, $z );
10129 # glVertex3d( $cx, $cy - $s * $ys, $z );
10130 #
10131 # To distinguish between these situations, we will
10132 # append the length of the line from the previous matching
10133 # token, or beginning of line, to the function name. This
10134 # will allow the vertical aligner to reject undesirable
10135 # matches.
10136
10137 # if we are not aligning on this paren...
10138 if ( $matching_token_to_go[$i] eq '' ) {
10139
10140 # Sum length from previous alignment, or start of line.
10141 my $len =
10142 ( $i_start == $ibeg )
10143 ? total_line_length( $i_start, $i - 1 )
10144 : token_sequence_length( $i_start, $i - 1 );
10145
10146 # tack length onto the container name to make unique
10147 $container_name[$depth] .= "-" . $len;
10148 }
10149 }
10150 }
10151 elsif ( $tokens_to_go[$i] =~ /^[\)\}\]]/ ) {
10152 $depth-- if $depth > 0;
10153 }
10154
10155 # if we find a new synchronization token, we are done with
10156 # a field
10157 if ( $i > $i_start && $matching_token_to_go[$i] ne '' ) {
10158
10159 my $tok = my $raw_tok = $matching_token_to_go[$i];
10160
10161 # map similar items
10162 my $tok_map = $operator_map{$tok};
10163 $tok = $tok_map if ($tok_map);
10164
10165 # make separators in different nesting depths unique
10166 # by appending the nesting depth digit.
10167 if ( $raw_tok ne '#' ) {
10168 $tok .= "$nesting_depth_to_go[$i]";
10169 }
10170
10171 # also decorate commas with any container name to avoid
10172 # unwanted cross-line alignments.
10173 if ( $raw_tok eq ',' || $raw_tok eq '=>' ) {
10174 if ( $container_name[$depth] ) {
10175 $tok .= $container_name[$depth];
10176 }
10177 }
10178
10179 # Patch to avoid aligning leading and trailing if, unless.
10180 # Mark trailing if, unless statements with container names.
10181 # This makes them different from leading if, unless which
10182 # are not so marked at present. If we ever need to name
10183 # them too, we could use ci to distinguish them.
10184 # Example problem to avoid:
10185 # return ( 2, "DBERROR" )
10186 # if ( $retval == 2 );
10187 # if ( scalar @_ ) {
10188 # my ( $a, $b, $c, $d, $e, $f ) = @_;
10189 # }
10190 if ( $raw_tok eq '(' ) {
10191 my $ci = $ci_levels_to_go[$ibeg];
10192 if ( $container_name[$depth] =~ /^\+(if|unless)/
10193 && $ci )
10194 {
10195 $tok .= $container_name[$depth];
10196 }
10197 }
10198
10199 # Decorate block braces with block types to avoid
10200 # unwanted alignments such as the following:
10201 # foreach ( @{$routput_array} ) { $fh->print($_) }
10202 # eval { $fh->close() };
10203 if ( $raw_tok eq '{' && $block_type_to_go[$i] ) {
10204 my $block_type = $block_type_to_go[$i];
10205
10206 # map certain related block types to allow
10207 # else blocks to align
10208 $block_type = $block_type_map{$block_type}
10209 if ( defined( $block_type_map{$block_type} ) );
10210
10211 # remove sub names to allow one-line sub braces to align
10212 # regardless of name
10213 #if ( $block_type =~ /^sub / ) { $block_type = 'sub' }
10214 if ( $block_type =~ /$SUB_PATTERN/ ) { $block_type = 'sub' }
10215
10216 # allow all control-type blocks to align
10217 if ( $block_type =~ /^[A-Z]+$/ ) { $block_type = 'BEGIN' }
10218
10219 $tok .= $block_type;
10220 }
10221
10222 # concatenate the text of the consecutive tokens to form
10223 # the field
10224 push( @fields,
10225 join( '', @tokens_to_go[ $i_start .. $i - 1 ] ) );
10226
10227 # store the alignment token for this field
10228 push( @tokens, $tok );
10229
10230 # get ready for the next batch
10231 $i_start = $i;
10232 $j++;
10233 $patterns[$j] = "";
10234 }
10235
10236 # continue accumulating tokens
10237 # handle non-keywords..
10238 if ( $types_to_go[$i] ne 'k' ) {
10239 my $type = $types_to_go[$i];
10240
10241 # Mark most things before arrows as a quote to
10242 # get them to line up. Testfile: mixed.pl.
10243 if ( ( $i < $iend - 1 ) && ( $type =~ /^[wnC]$/ ) ) {
10244 my $next_type = $types_to_go[ $i + 1 ];
10245 my $i_next_nonblank =
10246 ( ( $next_type eq 'b' ) ? $i + 2 : $i + 1 );
10247
10248 if ( $types_to_go[$i_next_nonblank] eq '=>' ) {
10249 $type = 'Q';
10250
10251 # Patch to ignore leading minus before words,
10252 # by changing pattern 'mQ' into just 'Q',
10253 # so that we can align things like this:
10254 # Button => "Print letter \"~$_\"",
10255 # -command => [ sub { print "$_[0]\n" }, $_ ],
10256 if ( $patterns[$j] eq 'm' ) { $patterns[$j] = "" }
10257 }
10258 }
10259
10260 # Convert a bareword within braces into a quote for matching. This will
10261 # allow alignment of expressions like this:
10262 # local ( $SIG{'INT'} ) = IGNORE;
10263 # local ( $SIG{ALRM} ) = 'POSTMAN';
10264 if ( $type eq 'w'
10265 && $i > $ibeg
10266 && $i < $iend
10267 && $types_to_go[ $i - 1 ] eq 'L'
10268 && $types_to_go[ $i + 1 ] eq 'R' )
10269 {
10270 $type = 'Q';
10271 }
10272
10273 # patch to make numbers and quotes align
10274 if ( $type eq 'n' ) { $type = 'Q' }
10275
10276 # patch to ignore any ! in patterns
10277 if ( $type eq '!' ) { $type = '' }
10278
10279 $patterns[$j] .= $type;
10280 }
10281
10282 # for keywords we have to use the actual text
10283 else {
10284
10285 my $tok = $tokens_to_go[$i];
10286
10287 # but map certain keywords to a common string to allow
10288 # alignment.
10289 $tok = $keyword_map{$tok}
10290 if ( defined( $keyword_map{$tok} ) );
10291 $patterns[$j] .= $tok;
10292 }
10293 }
10294
10295 # done with this line .. join text of tokens to make the last field
10296 push( @fields, join( '', @tokens_to_go[ $i_start .. $iend ] ) );
10297 return ( \@tokens, \@fields, \@patterns );
10298 }
10299
10300} # end make_alignment_patterns

10303
10304 # closure to keep track of unbalanced containers.
10305 # arrays shared by the routines in this block:
103062200ns my @unmatched_opening_indexes_in_this_batch;
10307 my @unmatched_closing_indexes_in_this_batch;
103081200ns my %comma_arrow_count;
10309
10310 sub is_unbalanced_batch {
10311 return @unmatched_opening_indexes_in_this_batch +
10312 @unmatched_closing_indexes_in_this_batch;
10313 }
10314
10315 sub comma_arrow_count {
10316 my $seqno = shift;
10317 return $comma_arrow_count{$seqno};

10320 sub match_opening_and_closing_tokens {
10321
10322 # Match up indexes of opening and closing braces, etc, in this batch.
10323 # This has to be done after all tokens are stored because unstoring
10324 # of tokens would otherwise cause trouble.
10325
10326 @unmatched_opening_indexes_in_this_batch = ();
10327 @unmatched_closing_indexes_in_this_batch = ();
10328 %comma_arrow_count = ();
10329 my $comma_arrow_count_contained = 0;
10330
10331 foreach my $i ( 0 .. $max_index_to_go ) {
10332 if ( $type_sequence_to_go[$i] ) {
10333 my $token = $tokens_to_go[$i];
10334 if ( $token =~ /^[\(\[\{\?]$/ ) {
10335 push @unmatched_opening_indexes_in_this_batch, $i;
10336 }
10337 elsif ( $token =~ /^[\)\]\}\:]$/ ) {
10338
10339 my $i_mate = pop @unmatched_opening_indexes_in_this_batch;
10340 if ( defined($i_mate) && $i_mate >= 0 ) {
10341 if ( $type_sequence_to_go[$i_mate] ==
10342 $type_sequence_to_go[$i] )
10343 {
10344 $mate_index_to_go[$i] = $i_mate;
10345 $mate_index_to_go[$i_mate] = $i;
10346 my $seqno = $type_sequence_to_go[$i];
10347 if ( $comma_arrow_count{$seqno} ) {
10348 $comma_arrow_count_contained +=
10349 $comma_arrow_count{$seqno};
10350 }
10351 }
10352 else {
10353 push @unmatched_opening_indexes_in_this_batch,
10354 $i_mate;
10355 push @unmatched_closing_indexes_in_this_batch, $i;
10356 }
10357 }
10358 else {

10374 sub save_opening_indentation {

10396 lookup_opening_indentation(
10397 $_, $ri_first, $ri_last, $rindentation_list

104051100nssub get_opening_indentation {
10406
10407 # get the indentation of the line which output the opening token
10408 # corresponding to a given closing token in the current output batch.
10409 #
10410 # given:
10411 # $i_closing - index in this line of a closing token ')' '}' or ']'
10412 #
10413 # $ri_first - reference to list of the first index $i for each output
10414 # line in this batch
10415 # $ri_last - reference to list of the last index $i for each output line
10416 # in this batch
10417 # $rindentation_list - reference to a list containing the indentation
10418 # used for each line.
10419 #
10420 # return:
10421 # -the indentation of the line which contained the opening token
10422 # which matches the token at index $i_opening
10423 # -and its offset (number of columns) from the start of the line
10424 #
10425 my ( $i_closing, $ri_first, $ri_last, $rindentation_list ) = @_;
10426
10427 # first, see if the opening token is in the current batch
10428 my $i_opening = $mate_index_to_go[$i_closing];
10429 my ( $indent, $offset, $is_leading, $exists );
10430 $exists = 1;
10431 if ( $i_opening >= 0 ) {
10432
10433 # it is..look up the indentation
10434 ( $indent, $offset, $is_leading ) =
10435 lookup_opening_indentation( $i_opening, $ri_first, $ri_last,
10436 $rindentation_list );
10437 }
10438
10439 # if not, it should have been stored in the hash by a previous batch
10440 else {
10441 my $seqno = $type_sequence_to_go[$i_closing];
10442 if ($seqno) {
10443 if ( $saved_opening_indentation{$seqno} ) {
10444 ( $indent, $offset, $is_leading ) =
10445 @{ $saved_opening_indentation{$seqno} };
10446 }
10447
10448 # some kind of serious error
10449 # (example is badfile.t)
10450 else {
10451 $indent = 0;
10452 $offset = 0;
10453 $is_leading = 0;
10454 $exists = 0;
10455 }
10456 }
10457
10458 # if no sequence number it must be an unbalanced container
10459 else {
10460 $indent = 0;
10461 $offset = 0;
10462 $is_leading = 0;
10463 $exists = 0;
10464 }
10465 }
10466 return ( $indent, $offset, $is_leading, $exists );

10469sub lookup_opening_indentation {
10470
10471 # get the indentation of the line in the current output batch
10472 # which output a selected opening token
10473 #
10474 # given:
10475 # $i_opening - index of an opening token in the current output batch
10476 # whose line indentation we need
10477 # $ri_first - reference to list of the first index $i for each output
10478 # line in this batch
10479 # $ri_last - reference to list of the last index $i for each output line
10480 # in this batch
10481 # $rindentation_list - reference to a list containing the indentation
10482 # used for each line. (NOTE: the first slot in
10483 # this list is the last returned line number, and this is
10484 # followed by the list of indentations).
10485 #
10486 # return
10487 # -the indentation of the line which contained token $i_opening
10488 # -and its offset (number of columns) from the start of the line
10489
10490 my ( $i_opening, $ri_start, $ri_last, $rindentation_list ) = @_;
10491
10492 my $nline = $rindentation_list->[0]; # line number of previous lookup
10493
10494 # reset line location if necessary
10495 $nline = 0 if ( $i_opening < $ri_start->[$nline] );
10496
10497 # find the correct line
10498 unless ( $i_opening > $ri_last->[-1] ) {
10499 while ( $i_opening > $ri_last->[$nline] ) { $nline++; }
10500 }
10501
10502 # error - token index is out of bounds - shouldn't happen
10503 else {
10504 warning(
10505"non-fatal program bug in lookup_opening_indentation - index out of range\n"
10506 );
10507 report_definite_bug();
10508 $nline = $#{$ri_last};
10509 }
10510
10511 $rindentation_list->[0] =
10512 $nline; # save line number to start looking next call
10513 my $ibeg = $ri_start->[$nline];
10514 my $offset = token_sequence_length( $ibeg, $i_opening ) - 1;
10515 my $is_leading = ( $ibeg == $i_opening );
10516 return ( $rindentation_list->[ $nline + 1 ], $offset, $is_leading );
10517}

10986 # inconsistent indentation.

10988 get_spaces($indentation) )
10989 {
10990 $indentation = $last_indentation_written;
10991 }
10992 }
10993
10994 # use previous indentation but use own level
10995 # to cause list to be flushed properly
10996 $lev = $levels_to_go[$ibeg];
10997 }
10998
10999 # remember indentation except for multi-line quotes, which get
11000 # no indentation
11001 unless ( $ibeg == 0 && $starting_in_quote ) {
11002 $last_indentation_written = $indentation;
11003 $last_unadjusted_indentation = $leading_spaces_to_go[$ibeg];
11004 $last_leading_token = $tokens_to_go[$ibeg];
11005 }
11006
11007 # be sure lines with leading closing tokens are not outdented more
11008 # than the line which contained the corresponding opening token.
11009
11010 #############################################################
11011 # updated per bug report in alex_bug.pl: we must not
11012 # mess with the indentation of closing logical braces so
11013 # we must treat something like '} else {' as if it were
11014 # an isolated brace my $is_isolated_block_brace = (
11015 # $iend == $ibeg ) && $block_type_to_go[$ibeg];
11016 #############################################################
11017 my $is_isolated_block_brace = $block_type_to_go[$ibeg]
11018 && ( $iend == $ibeg
11019 || $is_if_elsif_else_unless_while_until_for_foreach{
11020 $block_type_to_go[$ibeg]
11021 } );
11022
11023 # only do this for a ':; which is aligned with its leading '?'
11024 my $is_unaligned_colon = $types_to_go[$ibeg] eq ':' && !$is_leading;
11025
11026 if (
11027 defined($opening_indentation)
11028 && !$leading_paren_arrow # MOJO
11029 && !$is_isolated_block_brace
11030 && !$is_unaligned_colon
11031 )
11032 {
11033 if ( get_spaces($opening_indentation) > get_spaces($indentation) ) {
11034 $indentation = $opening_indentation;
11035 }
11036 }
11037
11038 # remember the indentation of each line of this batch
11039 push @{$rindentation_list}, $indentation;
11040
11041 # outdent lines with certain leading tokens...
11042 if (
11043
11044 # must be first word of this batch
11045 $ibeg == 0
11046
11047 # and ...
11048 && (
11049
11050 # certain leading keywords if requested
11051 (
11052 $rOpts->{'outdent-keywords'}
11053 && $types_to_go[$ibeg] eq 'k'
11054 && $outdent_keyword{ $tokens_to_go[$ibeg] }
11055 )
11056
11057 # or labels if requested
11058 || ( $rOpts->{'outdent-labels'} && $types_to_go[$ibeg] eq 'J' )
11059
11060 # or static block comments if requested
11061 || ( $types_to_go[$ibeg] eq '#'
11062 && $rOpts->{'outdent-static-block-comments'}
11063 && $is_static_block_comment )
11064 )
11065 )
11066
11067 {
11068 my $space_count = leading_spaces_to_go($ibeg);
11069 if ( $space_count > 0 ) {
11070 $space_count -= $rOpts_continuation_indentation;
11071 $is_outdented_line = 1;
11072 if ( $space_count < 0 ) { $space_count = 0 }
11073
11074 # do not promote a spaced static block comment to non-spaced;
11075 # this is not normally necessary but could be for some
11076 # unusual user inputs (such as -ci = -i)
11077 if ( $types_to_go[$ibeg] eq '#' && $space_count == 0 ) {
11078 $space_count = 1;
11079 }
11080
11081 if ($rOpts_line_up_parentheses) {
11082 $indentation =
11083 new_lp_indentation_item( $space_count, $lev, 0, 0, 0 );
11084 }
11085 else {
11086 $indentation = $space_count;
11087 }
11088 }
11089 }
11090
11091 return ( $indentation, $lev, $level_end, $terminal_type,
11092 $is_semicolon_terminated, $is_outdented_line );
11093 }

110961100nssub set_vertical_tightness_flags {

11099
11100 # Define vertical tightness controls for the nth line of a batch.
11101 # We create an array of parameters which tell the vertical aligner
11102 # if we should combine this line with the next line to achieve the
11103 # desired vertical tightness. The array of parameters contains:
11104 #
11105 # [0] type: 1=opening non-block 2=closing non-block
11106 # 3=opening block brace 4=closing block brace
11107 #
11108 # [1] flag: if opening: 1=no multiple steps, 2=multiple steps ok
11109 # if closing: spaces of padding to use
11110 # [2] sequence number of container
11111 # [3] valid flag: do not append if this flag is false. Will be
11112 # true if appropriate -vt flag is set. Otherwise, Will be

11121 # Vertical Tightness Flags Section 1:

11127

11133 my $token_end = $tokens_to_go[$iend];
11134 my $iend_next = $ri_last->[ $n + 1 ];

11136 $type_sequence_to_go[$iend]
11137 && !$block_type_to_go[$iend]
11138 && $is_opening_token{$token_end}
11139 && (
11140 $opening_vertical_tightness{$token_end} > 0
11141
11142 # allow 2-line method call to be closed up

11144 && $token_end eq '('
11145 && $iend > $ibeg
11146 && $types_to_go[ $iend - 1 ] ne 'b' )
11147 )
11148 )

11150
11151 # avoid multiple jumps in nesting depth in one line if
11152 # requested

11154 my $iend_next = $ri_last->[ $n + 1 ];
11155 unless (
11156 $ovt < 2
11157 && ( $nesting_depth_to_go[ $iend_next + 1 ] !=

11178 && !$block_type_to_go[$ibeg_next]
11179 && $is_closing_token{$token_next}
11180 && $types_to_go[$iend] !~ '#' ) # for safety, shouldn't happen!

11183 my $cvt = $closing_vertical_tightness{$token_next};

11185

11188 (
11189 $nesting_depth_to_go[$ibeg_next] ==
11190 $nesting_depth_to_go[ $iend_next + 1 ] + 1
11191 )
11192 && (
11193 $cvt == 2
11194 || (
11195 $container_environment_to_go[$ibeg_next] ne 'LIST'
11196 && (
11197 $cvt == 1
11198
11199 # allow closing up 2-line method calls

11201 && $token_next eq ')' )

11203 )
11204 )

11271 #--------------------------------------------------------------
11272 my $stackable;

11275 # patch to make something like 'qw(' behave like an opening paren
11276 # (aran.t)

11279 $token_beg_next = $1;
11280 }
11281 }

11284 && $is_closing_token{$token_beg_next} )
11285 {
11286 $stackable = $stack_closing_token{$token_beg_next}
11287 unless ( $block_type_to_go[$ibeg_next] )
11288 ; # shouldn't happen; just checking
11289 }
11290 elsif ($is_opening_token{$token_end}
11291 && $is_opening_token{$token_beg_next} )
11292 {
11293 $stackable = $stack_opening_token{$token_beg_next}
11294 unless ( $block_type_to_go[$ibeg_next] )
11295 ; # shouldn't happen; just checking
11296 }
11297
11298 if ($stackable) {
11299
11300 my $is_semicolon_terminated;
11301 if ( $n + 1 == $n_last_line ) {
11302 my ( $terminal_type, $i_terminal ) = terminal_type(
11303 \@types_to_go, \@block_type_to_go,
11304 $ibeg_next, $iend_next
11305 );

11307 && $nesting_depth_to_go[$iend_next] <

11310

11314 $is_semicolon_terminated
11315 || ( $iend_next == $ibeg_next
11316 || $iend_next == $ibeg_next + 2

11318 )
11319 {
11320 my $valid_flag = 1;
11321 my $spaces = ( $types_to_go[ $ibeg_next - 1 ] eq 'b' ) ? 1 : 0;
11322 @{$rvertical_tightness_flags} =
11323 ( 2, $spaces, $type_sequence_to_go[$ibeg_next], $valid_flag,
11324 );
11325 }
11326 }
11327 }
11328
11329 #--------------------------------------------------------------

11331 # Handle type 3, opening block braces on last line of the batch
11332 # Check for a last line with isolated opening BLOCK curly
11333 #--------------------------------------------------------------
11334 elsif ($rOpts_block_brace_vertical_tightness
11335 && $ibeg eq $iend
11336 && $types_to_go[$iend] eq '{'
11337 && $block_type_to_go[$iend] =~
11338 /$block_brace_vertical_tightness_pattern/o )
11339 {

11345 # Vertical Tightness Flags Section 3:

11347 # for a last line with isolated closing BLOCK curly

11350 && $ibeg eq $iend
11351 && $block_type_to_go[$iend]
11352 && $types_to_go[$iend] eq '}' )

11362 return $rvertical_tightness_flags;

11365sub get_seqno {
11366
11367 # get opening and closing sequence numbers of a token for the vertical
11368 # aligner. Assign qw quotes a value to allow qw opening and closing tokens
11369 # to be treated somewhat like opening and closing tokens for stacking
11370 # tokens by the vertical aligner.
11371 my ($ii) = @_;
11372 my $seqno = $type_sequence_to_go[$ii];
11373 if ( $types_to_go[$ii] eq 'q' ) {
11374 my $SEQ_QW = -1;
11375 if ( $ii > 0 ) {
11376 $seqno = $SEQ_QW if ( $tokens_to_go[$ii] =~ /^qw\s*[\(\{\[]/ );
11377 }
11378 else {
11379 if ( !$ending_in_quote ) {
11380 $seqno = $SEQ_QW if ( $tokens_to_go[$ii] =~ /[\)\}\]]$/ );
11381 }
11382 }
11383 }
11384 return ($seqno);
11385}

11412 sub set_vertical_alignment_markers {
11413
11414 # This routine takes the first step toward vertical alignment of the
11415 # lines of output text. It looks for certain tokens which can serve as
11416 # vertical alignment markers (such as an '=').
11417 #
11418 # Method: We look at each token $i in this output batch and set
11419 # $matching_token_to_go[$i] equal to those tokens at which we would
11420 # accept vertical alignment.
11421
11422 my ( $ri_first, $ri_last ) = @_;
11423
11424 # nothing to do if we aren't allowed to change whitespace
11425 if ( !$rOpts_add_whitespace ) {
11426 for my $i ( 0 .. $max_index_to_go ) {
11427 $matching_token_to_go[$i] = '';
11428 }
11429 return;
11430 }
11431
11432 # remember the index of last nonblank token before any sidecomment
11433 my $i_terminal = $max_index_to_go;
11434 if ( $types_to_go[$i_terminal] eq '#' ) {
11435 if ( $i_terminal > 0 && $types_to_go[ --$i_terminal ] eq 'b' ) {
11436 if ( $i_terminal > 0 ) { --$i_terminal }
11437 }
11438 }
11439
11440 # look at each line of this batch..
11441 my $last_vertical_alignment_before_index;
11442 my $vert_last_nonblank_type;
11443 my $vert_last_nonblank_token;
11444 my $vert_last_nonblank_block_type;
11445 my $max_line = @{$ri_first} - 1;
11446
11447 foreach my $line ( 0 .. $max_line ) {
11448 my $ibeg = $ri_first->[$line];
11449 my $iend = $ri_last->[$line];
11450 $last_vertical_alignment_before_index = -1;
11451 $vert_last_nonblank_type = '';
11452 $vert_last_nonblank_token = '';
11453 $vert_last_nonblank_block_type = '';
11454
11455 # look at each token in this output line..
11456 my $count = 0;
11457 foreach my $i ( $ibeg .. $iend ) {
11458 my $alignment_type = '';
11459 my $type = $types_to_go[$i];
11460 my $block_type = $block_type_to_go[$i];
11461 my $token = $tokens_to_go[$i];
11462
11463 # check for flag indicating that we should not align
11464 # this token
11465 if ( $matching_token_to_go[$i] ) {
11466 $matching_token_to_go[$i] = '';
11467 next;
11468 }
11469
11470 #--------------------------------------------------------
11471 # First see if we want to align BEFORE this token
11472 #--------------------------------------------------------
11473
11474 # The first possible token that we can align before
11475 # is index 2 because: 1) it doesn't normally make sense to
11476 # align before the first token and 2) the second
11477 # token must be a blank if we are to align before
11478 # the third
11479 if ( $i < $ibeg + 2 ) { }
11480
11481 # must follow a blank token
11482 elsif ( $types_to_go[ $i - 1 ] ne 'b' ) { }
11483
11484 # align a side comment --
11485 elsif ( $type eq '#' ) {
11486
11487 unless (
11488
11489 # it is a static side comment
11490 (
11491 $rOpts->{'static-side-comments'}
11492 && $token =~ /$static_side_comment_pattern/o
11493 )
11494
11495 # or a closing side comment
11496 || ( $vert_last_nonblank_block_type
11497 && $token =~
11498 /$closing_side_comment_prefix_pattern/o )
11499 )
11500 {
11501 $alignment_type = $type;
11502 } ## Example of a static side comment
11503 }
11504
11505 # otherwise, do not align two in a row to create a
11506 # blank field
11507 elsif ( $last_vertical_alignment_before_index == $i - 2 ) { }
11508
11509 # align before one of these keywords
11510 # (within a line, since $i>1)
11511 elsif ( $type eq 'k' ) {
11512
11513 # /^(if|unless|and|or|eq|ne)$/
11514 if ( $is_vertical_alignment_keyword{$token} ) {
11515 $alignment_type = $token;
11516 }
11517 }
11518
11519 # align before one of these types..
11520 # Note: add '.' after new vertical aligner is operational
11521 elsif ( $is_vertical_alignment_type{$type} ) {
11522 $alignment_type = $token;
11523
11524 # Do not align a terminal token. Although it might
11525 # occasionally look ok to do this, this has been found to be
11526 # a good general rule. The main problems are:
11527 # (1) that the terminal token (such as an = or :) might get
11528 # moved far to the right where it is hard to see because
11529 # nothing follows it, and
11530 # (2) doing so may prevent other good alignments.
11531 # Current exceptions are && and ||
11532 if ( $i == $iend || $i >= $i_terminal ) {
11533 $alignment_type = ""
11534 unless ( $is_terminal_alignment_type{$type} );
11535 }
11536
11537 # Do not align leading ': (' or '. ('. This would prevent
11538 # alignment in something like the following:
11539 # $extra_space .=
11540 # ( $input_line_number < 10 ) ? " "
11541 # : ( $input_line_number < 100 ) ? " "
11542 # : "";
11543 # or
11544 # $code =
11545 # ( $case_matters ? $accessor : " lc($accessor) " )
11546 # . ( $yesno ? " eq " : " ne " )
11547 if ( $i == $ibeg + 2
11548 && $types_to_go[$ibeg] =~ /^[\.\:]$/
11549 && $types_to_go[ $i - 1 ] eq 'b' )
11550 {
11551 $alignment_type = "";
11552 }
11553
11554 # For a paren after keyword, only align something like this:
11555 # if ( $a ) { &a }
11556 # elsif ( $b ) { &b }
11557 if ( $token eq '(' && $vert_last_nonblank_type eq 'k' ) {
11558 $alignment_type = ""
11559 unless $vert_last_nonblank_token =~
11560 /^(if|unless|elsif)$/;
11561 }
11562
11563 # be sure the alignment tokens are unique
11564 # This didn't work well: reason not determined
11565 # if ($token ne $type) {$alignment_type .= $type}
11566 }
11567
11568 # NOTE: This is deactivated because it causes the previous
11569 # if/elsif alignment to fail
11570 #elsif ( $type eq '}' && $token eq '}' && $block_type_to_go[$i])
11571 #{ $alignment_type = $type; }
11572
11573 if ($alignment_type) {
11574 $last_vertical_alignment_before_index = $i;
11575 }
11576
11577 #--------------------------------------------------------
11578 # Next see if we want to align AFTER the previous nonblank
11579 #--------------------------------------------------------
11580
11581 # We want to line up ',' and interior ';' tokens, with the added
11582 # space AFTER these tokens. (Note: interior ';' is included
11583 # because it may occur in short blocks).
11584 if (
11585
11586 # we haven't already set it
11587 !$alignment_type
11588
11589 # and its not the first token of the line
11590 && ( $i > $ibeg )
11591
11592 # and it follows a blank
11593 && $types_to_go[ $i - 1 ] eq 'b'
11594
11595 # and previous token IS one of these:
11596 && ( $vert_last_nonblank_type =~ /^[\,\;]$/ )
11597
11598 # and it's NOT one of these
11599 && ( $type !~ /^[b\#\)\]\}]$/ )
11600
11601 # then go ahead and align
11602 )
11603
11604 {
11605 $alignment_type = $vert_last_nonblank_type;
11606 }
11607
11608 #--------------------------------------------------------
11609 # then store the value
11610 #--------------------------------------------------------
11611 $matching_token_to_go[$i] = $alignment_type;
11612 $count++ if ($alignment_type);
11613 if ( $type ne 'b' ) {
11614 $vert_last_nonblank_type = $type;
11615 $vert_last_nonblank_token = $token;
11616 $vert_last_nonblank_block_type = $block_type;
11617 }
11618 }
11619 }
11620 return;
11621 }
11622}

116241100nssub terminal_type {
11625
11626 # returns type of last token on this line (terminal token), as follows:
11627 # returns # for a full-line comment
11628 # returns ' ' for a blank line
11629 # otherwise returns final token type
11630
11631 my ( $rtype, $rblock_type, $ibeg, $iend ) = @_;
11632
11633 # check for full-line comment..
11634 if ( $rtype->[$ibeg] eq '#' ) {
11635 return wantarray ? ( $rtype->[$ibeg], $ibeg ) : $rtype->[$ibeg];
11636 }
11637 else {
11638
11639 # start at end and walk backwards..
11640 for ( my $i = $iend ; $i >= $ibeg ; $i-- ) {
11641
11642 # skip past any side comment and blanks
11643 next if ( $rtype->[$i] eq 'b' );
11644 next if ( $rtype->[$i] eq '#' );
11645
11646 # found it..make sure it is a BLOCK termination,
11647 # but hide a terminal } after sort/grep/map because it is not
11648 # necessarily the end of the line. (terminal.t)
11649 my $terminal_type = $rtype->[$i];
11650 if (
11651 $terminal_type eq '}'
11652 && ( !$rblock_type->[$i]
11653 || ( $is_sort_map_grep_eval_do{ $rblock_type->[$i] } ) )
11654 )
11655 {
11656 $terminal_type = 'b';
11657 }
11658 return wantarray ? ( $terminal_type, $i ) : $terminal_type;
11659 }
11660
11661 # empty line
11662 return wantarray ? ( ' ', $ibeg ) : ' ';
11663 }
11664}

11666{ # set_bond_strengths

11669 my %is_lt_gt_le_ge;

11672 my %nobreak_lhs;
11673 my %nobreak_rhs;
11674
11675 my @bias_tokens;
116761300ns my $delta_bias;

11678 sub bias_table_key {
11679 my ( $type, $token ) = @_;
11680 my $bias_table_key = $type;
11681 if ( $type eq 'k' ) {
11682 $bias_table_key = $token;
11683 if ( $token eq 'err' ) { $bias_table_key = 'or' }
11684 }
11685 return $bias_table_key;
11686 }

11688 sub initialize_bond_strength_hashes {
11689
11690 my @q;
11691 @q = qw(if unless while until for foreach);
11692 @is_good_keyword_breakpoint{@q} = (1) x scalar(@q);
11693
11694 @q = qw(lt gt le ge);
11695 @is_lt_gt_le_ge{@q} = (1) x scalar(@q);
11696 #
11697 # The decision about where to break a line depends upon a "bond
11698 # strength" between tokens. The LOWER the bond strength, the MORE
11699 # likely a break. A bond strength may be any value but to simplify
11700 # things there are several pre-defined strength levels:
11701
11702 # NO_BREAK => 10000;
11703 # VERY_STRONG => 100;
11704 # STRONG => 2.1;
11705 # NOMINAL => 1.1;
11706 # WEAK => 0.8;
11707 # VERY_WEAK => 0.55;
11708
11709 # The strength values are based on trial-and-error, and need to be
11710 # tweaked occasionally to get desired results. Some comments:
11711 #
11712 # 1. Only relative strengths are important. small differences
11713 # in strengths can make big formatting differences.
11714 # 2. Each indentation level adds one unit of bond strength.
11715 # 3. A value of NO_BREAK makes an unbreakable bond
11716 # 4. A value of VERY_WEAK is the strength of a ','
11717 # 5. Values below NOMINAL are considered ok break points.
11718 # 6. Values above NOMINAL are considered poor break points.
11719 #
11720 # The bond strengths should roughly follow precedence order where
11721 # possible. If you make changes, please check the results very
11722 # carefully on a variety of scripts. Testing with the -extrude
11723 # options is particularly helpful in exercising all of the rules.
11724
11725 # Wherever possible, bond strengths are defined in the following
11726 # tables. There are two main stages to setting bond strengths and
11727 # two types of tables:
11728 #
11729 # The first stage involves looking at each token individually and
11730 # defining left and right bond strengths, according to if we want
11731 # to break to the left or right side, and how good a break point it
11732 # is. For example tokens like =, ||, && make good break points and
11733 # will have low strengths, but one might want to break on either
11734 # side to put them at the end of one line or beginning of the next.
11735 #
11736 # The second stage involves looking at certain pairs of tokens and
11737 # defining a bond strength for that particular pair. This second
11738 # stage has priority.
11739
11740 #---------------------------------------------------------------
11741 # Bond Strength BEGIN Section 1.
11742 # Set left and right bond strengths of individual tokens.
11743 #---------------------------------------------------------------
11744
11745 # NOTE: NO_BREAK's set in this section first are HINTS which will
11746 # probably not be honored. Essential NO_BREAKS's should be set in
11747 # BEGIN Section 2 or hardwired in the NO_BREAK coding near the end
11748 # of this subroutine.
11749
11750 # Note that we are setting defaults in this section. The user
11751 # cannot change bond strengths but can cause the left and right
11752 # bond strengths of any token type to be swapped through the use of
11753 # the -wba and -wbb flags. In this way the user can determine if a
11754 # breakpoint token should appear at the end of one line or the
11755 # beginning of the next line.
11756
11757 # The hash keys in this section are token types, plus the text of
11758 # certain keywords like 'or', 'and'.
11759
11760 # no break around possible filehandle
11761 $left_bond_strength{'Z'} = NO_BREAK;
11762 $right_bond_strength{'Z'} = NO_BREAK;
11763
11764 # never put a bare word on a new line:
11765 # example print (STDERR, "bla"); will fail with break after (
11766 $left_bond_strength{'w'} = NO_BREAK;
11767
11768 # blanks always have infinite strength to force breaks after
11769 # real tokens
11770 $right_bond_strength{'b'} = NO_BREAK;
11771
11772 # try not to break on exponentation
11773 @q = qw# ** .. ... <=> #;
11774 @left_bond_strength{@q} = (STRONG) x scalar(@q);
11775 @right_bond_strength{@q} = (STRONG) x scalar(@q);
11776
11777 # The comma-arrow has very low precedence but not a good break point
11778 $left_bond_strength{'=>'} = NO_BREAK;
11779 $right_bond_strength{'=>'} = NOMINAL;
11780
11781 # ok to break after label
11782 $left_bond_strength{'J'} = NO_BREAK;
11783 $right_bond_strength{'J'} = NOMINAL;
11784 $left_bond_strength{'j'} = STRONG;
11785 $right_bond_strength{'j'} = STRONG;
11786 $left_bond_strength{'A'} = STRONG;
11787 $right_bond_strength{'A'} = STRONG;
11788
11789 $left_bond_strength{'->'} = STRONG;
11790 $right_bond_strength{'->'} = VERY_STRONG;
11791
11792 $left_bond_strength{'CORE::'} = NOMINAL;
11793 $right_bond_strength{'CORE::'} = NO_BREAK;
11794
11795 # breaking AFTER modulus operator is ok:
11796 @q = qw< % >;
11797 @left_bond_strength{@q} = (STRONG) x scalar(@q);
11798 @right_bond_strength{@q} =
11799 ( 0.1 * NOMINAL + 0.9 * STRONG ) x scalar(@q);
11800
11801 # Break AFTER math operators * and /
11802 @q = qw< * / x >;
11803 @left_bond_strength{@q} = (STRONG) x scalar(@q);
11804 @right_bond_strength{@q} = (NOMINAL) x scalar(@q);
11805
11806 # Break AFTER weakest math operators + and -
11807 # Make them weaker than * but a bit stronger than '.'
11808 @q = qw< + - >;
11809 @left_bond_strength{@q} = (STRONG) x scalar(@q);
11810 @right_bond_strength{@q} =
11811 ( 0.91 * NOMINAL + 0.09 * WEAK ) x scalar(@q);
11812
11813 # breaking BEFORE these is just ok:
11814 @q = qw# >> << #;
11815 @right_bond_strength{@q} = (STRONG) x scalar(@q);
11816 @left_bond_strength{@q} = (NOMINAL) x scalar(@q);
11817
11818 # breaking before the string concatenation operator seems best
11819 # because it can be hard to see at the end of a line
11820 $right_bond_strength{'.'} = STRONG;
11821 $left_bond_strength{'.'} = 0.9 * NOMINAL + 0.1 * WEAK;
11822
11823 @q = qw< } ] ) R >;
11824 @left_bond_strength{@q} = (STRONG) x scalar(@q);
11825 @right_bond_strength{@q} = (NOMINAL) x scalar(@q);
11826
11827 # make these a little weaker than nominal so that they get
11828 # favored for end-of-line characters
11829 @q = qw< != == =~ !~ ~~ !~~ >;
11830 @left_bond_strength{@q} = (STRONG) x scalar(@q);
11831 @right_bond_strength{@q} =
11832 ( 0.9 * NOMINAL + 0.1 * WEAK ) x scalar(@q);
11833
11834 # break AFTER these
11835 @q = qw# < > | & >= <= #;
11836 @left_bond_strength{@q} = (VERY_STRONG) x scalar(@q);
11837 @right_bond_strength{@q} =
11838 ( 0.8 * NOMINAL + 0.2 * WEAK ) x scalar(@q);
11839
11840 # breaking either before or after a quote is ok
11841 # but bias for breaking before a quote
11842 $left_bond_strength{'Q'} = NOMINAL;
11843 $right_bond_strength{'Q'} = NOMINAL + 0.02;
11844 $left_bond_strength{'q'} = NOMINAL;
11845 $right_bond_strength{'q'} = NOMINAL;
11846
11847 # starting a line with a keyword is usually ok
11848 $left_bond_strength{'k'} = NOMINAL;
11849
11850 # we usually want to bond a keyword strongly to what immediately
11851 # follows, rather than leaving it stranded at the end of a line
11852 $right_bond_strength{'k'} = STRONG;
11853
11854 $left_bond_strength{'G'} = NOMINAL;
11855 $right_bond_strength{'G'} = STRONG;
11856
11857 # assignment operators
11858 @q = qw(
11859 = **= += *= &= <<= &&=
11860 -= /= |= >>= ||= //=
11861 .= %= ^=
11862 x=
11863 );
11864
11865 # Default is to break AFTER various assignment operators
11866 @left_bond_strength{@q} = (STRONG) x scalar(@q);
11867 @right_bond_strength{@q} =
11868 ( 0.4 * WEAK + 0.6 * VERY_WEAK ) x scalar(@q);
11869
11870 # Default is to break BEFORE '&&' and '||' and '//'
11871 # set strength of '||' to same as '=' so that chains like
11872 # $a = $b || $c || $d will break before the first '||'
11873 $right_bond_strength{'||'} = NOMINAL;
11874 $left_bond_strength{'||'} = $right_bond_strength{'='};
11875
11876 # same thing for '//'
11877 $right_bond_strength{'//'} = NOMINAL;
11878 $left_bond_strength{'//'} = $right_bond_strength{'='};
11879
11880 # set strength of && a little higher than ||
11881 $right_bond_strength{'&&'} = NOMINAL;
11882 $left_bond_strength{'&&'} = $left_bond_strength{'||'} + 0.1;
11883
11884 $left_bond_strength{';'} = VERY_STRONG;
11885 $right_bond_strength{';'} = VERY_WEAK;
11886 $left_bond_strength{'f'} = VERY_STRONG;
11887
11888 # make right strength of for ';' a little less than '='
11889 # to make for contents break after the ';' to avoid this:
11890 # for ( $j = $number_of_fields - 1 ; $j < $item_count ; $j +=
11891 # $number_of_fields )
11892 # and make it weaker than ',' and 'and' too
11893 $right_bond_strength{'f'} = VERY_WEAK - 0.03;
11894
11895 # The strengths of ?/: should be somewhere between
11896 # an '=' and a quote (NOMINAL),
11897 # make strength of ':' slightly less than '?' to help
11898 # break long chains of ? : after the colons
11899 $left_bond_strength{':'} = 0.4 * WEAK + 0.6 * NOMINAL;
11900 $right_bond_strength{':'} = NO_BREAK;
11901 $left_bond_strength{'?'} = $left_bond_strength{':'} + 0.01;
11902 $right_bond_strength{'?'} = NO_BREAK;
11903
11904 $left_bond_strength{','} = VERY_STRONG;
11905 $right_bond_strength{','} = VERY_WEAK;
11906
11907 # remaining digraphs and trigraphs not defined above
11908 @q = qw( :: <> ++ --);
11909 @left_bond_strength{@q} = (WEAK) x scalar(@q);
11910 @right_bond_strength{@q} = (STRONG) x scalar(@q);
11911
11912 # Set bond strengths of certain keywords
11913 # make 'or', 'err', 'and' slightly weaker than a ','
11914 $left_bond_strength{'and'} = VERY_WEAK - 0.01;
11915 $left_bond_strength{'or'} = VERY_WEAK - 0.02;
11916 $left_bond_strength{'err'} = VERY_WEAK - 0.02;
11917 $left_bond_strength{'xor'} = NOMINAL;
11918 $right_bond_strength{'and'} = NOMINAL;
11919 $right_bond_strength{'or'} = NOMINAL;
11920 $right_bond_strength{'err'} = NOMINAL;
11921 $right_bond_strength{'xor'} = STRONG;
11922
11923 #---------------------------------------------------------------
11924 # Bond Strength BEGIN Section 2.
11925 # Set binary rules for bond strengths between certain token types.
11926 #---------------------------------------------------------------
11927
11928 # We have a little problem making tables which apply to the
11929 # container tokens. Here is a list of container tokens and
11930 # their types:
11931 #
11932 # type tokens // meaning
11933 # { {, [, ( // indent
11934 # } }, ], ) // outdent
11935 # [ [ // left non-structural [ (enclosing an array index)
11936 # ] ] // right non-structural square bracket
11937 # ( ( // left non-structural paren
11938 # ) ) // right non-structural paren
11939 # L { // left non-structural curly brace (enclosing a key)
11940 # R } // right non-structural curly brace
11941 #
11942 # Some rules apply to token types and some to just the token
11943 # itself. We solve the problem by combining type and token into a
11944 # new hash key for the container types.
11945 #
11946 # If a rule applies to a token 'type' then we need to make rules
11947 # for each of these 'type.token' combinations:
11948 # Type Type.Token
11949 # { {{, {[, {(
11950 # [ [[
11951 # ( ((
11952 # L L{
11953 # } }}, }], })
11954 # ] ]]
11955 # ) ))
11956 # R R}
11957 #
11958 # If a rule applies to a token then we need to make rules for
11959 # these 'type.token' combinations:
11960 # Token Type.Token
11961 # { {{, L{
11962 # [ {[, [[
11963 # ( {(, ((
11964 # } }}, R}
11965 # ] }], ]]
11966 # ) }), ))
11967
11968 # allow long lines before final { in an if statement, as in:
11969 # if (..........
11970 # ..........)
11971 # {
11972 #
11973 # Otherwise, the line before the { tends to be too short.
11974
11975 $binary_bond_strength{'))'}{'{{'} = VERY_WEAK + 0.03;
11976 $binary_bond_strength{'(('}{'{{'} = NOMINAL;
11977
11978 # break on something like '} (', but keep this stronger than a ','
11979 # example is in 'howe.pl'
11980 $binary_bond_strength{'R}'}{'(('} = 0.8 * VERY_WEAK + 0.2 * WEAK;
11981 $binary_bond_strength{'}}'}{'(('} = 0.8 * VERY_WEAK + 0.2 * WEAK;
11982
11983 # keep matrix and hash indices together
11984 # but make them a little below STRONG to allow breaking open
11985 # something like {'some-word'}{'some-very-long-word'} at the }{
11986 # (bracebrk.t)
11987 $binary_bond_strength{']]'}{'[['} = 0.9 * STRONG + 0.1 * NOMINAL;
11988 $binary_bond_strength{']]'}{'L{'} = 0.9 * STRONG + 0.1 * NOMINAL;
11989 $binary_bond_strength{'R}'}{'[['} = 0.9 * STRONG + 0.1 * NOMINAL;
11990 $binary_bond_strength{'R}'}{'L{'} = 0.9 * STRONG + 0.1 * NOMINAL;
11991
11992 # increase strength to the point where a break in the following
11993 # will be after the opening paren rather than at the arrow:
11994 # $a->$b($c);
11995 $binary_bond_strength{'i'}{'->'} = 1.45 * STRONG;
11996
11997 $binary_bond_strength{'))'}{'->'} = 0.1 * STRONG + 0.9 * NOMINAL;
11998 $binary_bond_strength{']]'}{'->'} = 0.1 * STRONG + 0.9 * NOMINAL;
11999 $binary_bond_strength{'})'}{'->'} = 0.1 * STRONG + 0.9 * NOMINAL;
12000 $binary_bond_strength{'}]'}{'->'} = 0.1 * STRONG + 0.9 * NOMINAL;
12001 $binary_bond_strength{'}}'}{'->'} = 0.1 * STRONG + 0.9 * NOMINAL;
12002 $binary_bond_strength{'R}'}{'->'} = 0.1 * STRONG + 0.9 * NOMINAL;
12003
12004 $binary_bond_strength{'))'}{'[['} = 0.2 * STRONG + 0.8 * NOMINAL;
12005 $binary_bond_strength{'})'}{'[['} = 0.2 * STRONG + 0.8 * NOMINAL;
12006 $binary_bond_strength{'))'}{'{['} = 0.2 * STRONG + 0.8 * NOMINAL;
12007 $binary_bond_strength{'})'}{'{['} = 0.2 * STRONG + 0.8 * NOMINAL;
12008
12009 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12010 # Binary NO_BREAK rules
12011 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12012
12013 # use strict requires that bare word and => not be separated
12014 $binary_bond_strength{'C'}{'=>'} = NO_BREAK;
12015 $binary_bond_strength{'U'}{'=>'} = NO_BREAK;
12016
12017 # Never break between a bareword and a following paren because
12018 # perl may give an error. For example, if a break is placed
12019 # between 'to_filehandle' and its '(' the following line will
12020 # give a syntax error [Carp.pm]: my( $no) =fileno(
12021 # to_filehandle( $in)) ;
12022 $binary_bond_strength{'C'}{'(('} = NO_BREAK;
12023 $binary_bond_strength{'C'}{'{('} = NO_BREAK;
12024 $binary_bond_strength{'U'}{'(('} = NO_BREAK;
12025 $binary_bond_strength{'U'}{'{('} = NO_BREAK;
12026
12027 # use strict requires that bare word within braces not start new
12028 # line
12029 $binary_bond_strength{'L{'}{'w'} = NO_BREAK;
12030
12031 $binary_bond_strength{'w'}{'R}'} = NO_BREAK;
12032
12033 # use strict requires that bare word and => not be separated
12034 $binary_bond_strength{'w'}{'=>'} = NO_BREAK;
12035
12036 # use strict does not allow separating type info from trailing { }
12037 # testfile is readmail.pl
12038 $binary_bond_strength{'t'}{'L{'} = NO_BREAK;
12039 $binary_bond_strength{'i'}{'L{'} = NO_BREAK;
12040
12041 # As a defensive measure, do not break between a '(' and a
12042 # filehandle. In some cases, this can cause an error. For
12043 # example, the following program works:
12044 # my $msg="hi!\n";
12045 # print
12046 # ( STDOUT
12047 # $msg
12048 # );
12049 #
12050 # But this program fails:
12051 # my $msg="hi!\n";
12052 # print
12053 # (
12054 # STDOUT
12055 # $msg
12056 # );
12057 #
12058 # This is normally only a problem with the 'extrude' option
12059 $binary_bond_strength{'(('}{'Y'} = NO_BREAK;
12060 $binary_bond_strength{'{('}{'Y'} = NO_BREAK;
12061
12062 # never break between sub name and opening paren
12063 $binary_bond_strength{'w'}{'(('} = NO_BREAK;
12064 $binary_bond_strength{'w'}{'{('} = NO_BREAK;
12065
12066 # keep '}' together with ';'
12067 $binary_bond_strength{'}}'}{';'} = NO_BREAK;
12068
12069 # Breaking before a ++ can cause perl to guess wrong. For
12070 # example the following line will cause a syntax error
12071 # with -extrude if we break between '$i' and '++' [fixstyle2]
12072 # print( ( $i++ & 1 ) ? $_ : ( $change{$_} || $_ ) );
12073 $nobreak_lhs{'++'} = NO_BREAK;
12074
12075 # Do not break before a possible file handle
12076 $nobreak_lhs{'Z'} = NO_BREAK;
12077
12078 # use strict hates bare words on any new line. For
12079 # example, a break before the underscore here provokes the
12080 # wrath of use strict:
12081 # if ( -r $fn && ( -s _ || $AllowZeroFilesize)) {
12082 $nobreak_rhs{'F'} = NO_BREAK;
12083 $nobreak_rhs{'CORE::'} = NO_BREAK;
12084
12085 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12086 # Bond Strength BEGIN Section 3.
12087 # Define tables and values for applying a small bias to the above
12088 # values.
12089 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12090 # Adding a small 'bias' to strengths is a simple way to make a line
12091 # break at the first of a sequence of identical terms. For
12092 # example, to force long string of conditional operators to break
12093 # with each line ending in a ':', we can add a small number to the
12094 # bond strength of each ':' (colon.t)
12095 @bias_tokens = qw( : && || f and or . ); # tokens which get bias
12096 $delta_bias = 0.0001; # a very small strength level
12097 return;
12098
12099 } ## end sub initialize_bond_strength_hashes
12100
12101 sub set_bond_strengths {
12102
12103 # patch-its always ok to break at end of line
12104 $nobreak_to_go[$max_index_to_go] = 0;
12105
12106 # we start a new set of bias values for each line
12107 my %bias;
12108 @bias{@bias_tokens} = (0) x scalar(@bias_tokens);
12109 my $code_bias = -.01; # bias for closing block braces
12110
12111 my $type = 'b';
12112 my $token = ' ';
12113 my $last_type;
12114 my $last_nonblank_type = $type;
12115 my $last_nonblank_token = $token;
12116 my $list_str = $left_bond_strength{'?'};
12117
12118 my ( $block_type, $i_next, $i_next_nonblank, $next_nonblank_token,
12119 $next_nonblank_type, $next_token, $next_type, $total_nesting_depth,
12120 );
12121
12122 # main loop to compute bond strengths between each pair of tokens
12123 foreach my $i ( 0 .. $max_index_to_go ) {
12124 $last_type = $type;
12125 if ( $type ne 'b' ) {
12126 $last_nonblank_type = $type;
12127 $last_nonblank_token = $token;
12128 }
12129 $type = $types_to_go[$i];
12130
12131 # strength on both sides of a blank is the same
12132 if ( $type eq 'b' && $last_type ne 'b' ) {
12133 $bond_strength_to_go[$i] = $bond_strength_to_go[ $i - 1 ];
12134 next;
12135 }
12136
12137 $token = $tokens_to_go[$i];
12138 $block_type = $block_type_to_go[$i];
12139 $i_next = $i + 1;
12140 $next_type = $types_to_go[$i_next];
12141 $next_token = $tokens_to_go[$i_next];
12142 $total_nesting_depth = $nesting_depth_to_go[$i_next];
12143 $i_next_nonblank = ( ( $next_type eq 'b' ) ? $i + 2 : $i + 1 );
12144 $next_nonblank_type = $types_to_go[$i_next_nonblank];
12145 $next_nonblank_token = $tokens_to_go[$i_next_nonblank];
12146
12147 # We are computing the strength of the bond between the current
12148 # token and the NEXT token.
12149
12150 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12151 # Bond Strength Section 1:
12152 # First Approximation.
12153 # Use minimum of individual left and right tabulated bond
12154 # strengths.
12155 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12156 my $bsr = $right_bond_strength{$type};
12157 my $bsl = $left_bond_strength{$next_nonblank_type};
12158
12159 # define right bond strengths of certain keywords
12160 if ( $type eq 'k' && defined( $right_bond_strength{$token} ) ) {
12161 $bsr = $right_bond_strength{$token};
12162 }
12163 elsif ( $token eq 'ne' or $token eq 'eq' ) {
12164 $bsr = NOMINAL;
12165 }
12166
12167 # set terminal bond strength to the nominal value
12168 # this will cause good preceding breaks to be retained
12169 if ( $i_next_nonblank > $max_index_to_go ) {
12170 $bsl = NOMINAL;
12171 }
12172
12173 # define right bond strengths of certain keywords
12174 if ( $next_nonblank_type eq 'k'
12175 && defined( $left_bond_strength{$next_nonblank_token} ) )
12176 {
12177 $bsl = $left_bond_strength{$next_nonblank_token};
12178 }
12179 elsif ($next_nonblank_token eq 'ne'
12180 or $next_nonblank_token eq 'eq' )
12181 {
12182 $bsl = NOMINAL;
12183 }
12184 elsif ( $is_lt_gt_le_ge{$next_nonblank_token} ) {
12185 $bsl = 0.9 * NOMINAL + 0.1 * STRONG;
12186 }
12187
12188 # Use the minimum of the left and right strengths. Note: it might
12189 # seem that we would want to keep a NO_BREAK if either token has
12190 # this value. This didn't work, for example because in an arrow
12191 # list, it prevents the comma from separating from the following
12192 # bare word (which is probably quoted by its arrow). So necessary
12193 # NO_BREAK's have to be handled as special cases in the final
12194 # section.
12195 if ( !defined($bsr) ) { $bsr = VERY_STRONG }
12196 if ( !defined($bsl) ) { $bsl = VERY_STRONG }
12197 my $bond_str = ( $bsr < $bsl ) ? $bsr : $bsl;
12198 my $bond_str_1 = $bond_str;
12199
12200 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12201 # Bond Strength Section 2:
12202 # Apply hardwired rules..
12203 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12204
12205 # Patch to put terminal or clauses on a new line: Weaken the bond
12206 # at an || followed by die or similar keyword to make the terminal
12207 # or clause fall on a new line, like this:
12208 #
12209 # my $class = shift
12210 # || die "Cannot add broadcast: No class identifier found";
12211 #
12212 # Otherwise the break will be at the previous '=' since the || and
12213 # = have the same starting strength and the or is biased, like
12214 # this:
12215 #
12216 # my $class =
12217 # shift || die "Cannot add broadcast: No class identifier found";
12218 #
12219 # In any case if the user places a break at either the = or the ||
12220 # it should remain there.
12221 if ( $type eq '||' || $type eq 'k' && $token eq 'or' ) {
12222 if ( $next_nonblank_token =~ /^(die|confess|croak|warn)$/ ) {
12223 if ( $want_break_before{$token} && $i > 0 ) {
12224 $bond_strength_to_go[ $i - 1 ] -= $delta_bias;
12225 }
12226 else {
12227 $bond_str -= $delta_bias;
12228 }
12229 }
12230 }
12231
12232 # good to break after end of code blocks
12233 if ( $type eq '}' && $block_type && $next_nonblank_type ne ';' ) {
12234
12235 $bond_str = 0.5 * WEAK + 0.5 * VERY_WEAK + $code_bias;
12236 $code_bias += $delta_bias;
12237 }
12238
12239 if ( $type eq 'k' ) {
12240
12241 # allow certain control keywords to stand out
12242 if ( $next_nonblank_type eq 'k'
12243 && $is_last_next_redo_return{$token} )
12244 {
12245 $bond_str = 0.45 * WEAK + 0.55 * VERY_WEAK;
12246 }
12247
12248 # Don't break after keyword my. This is a quick fix for a
12249 # rare problem with perl. An example is this line from file
12250 # Container.pm:
12251
12252 # foreach my $question( Debian::DebConf::ConfigDb::gettree(
12253 # $this->{'question'} ) )
12254
12255 if ( $token eq 'my' ) {
12256 $bond_str = NO_BREAK;
12257 }
12258
12259 }
12260
12261 # good to break before 'if', 'unless', etc
12262 if ( $is_if_brace_follower{$next_nonblank_token} ) {
12263 $bond_str = VERY_WEAK;
12264 }
12265
12266 if ( $next_nonblank_type eq 'k' && $type ne 'CORE::' ) {
12267
12268 # FIXME: needs more testing
12269 if ( $is_keyword_returning_list{$next_nonblank_token} ) {
12270 $bond_str = $list_str if ( $bond_str > $list_str );
12271 }
12272
12273 # keywords like 'unless', 'if', etc, within statements
12274 # make good breaks
12275 if ( $is_good_keyword_breakpoint{$next_nonblank_token} ) {
12276 $bond_str = VERY_WEAK / 1.05;
12277 }
12278 }
12279
12280 # try not to break before a comma-arrow
12281 elsif ( $next_nonblank_type eq '=>' ) {
12282 if ( $bond_str < STRONG ) { $bond_str = STRONG }
12283 }
12284
12285 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12286 # Additional hardwired NOBREAK rules
12287 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12288
12289 # map1.t -- correct for a quirk in perl
12290 if ( $token eq '('
12291 && $next_nonblank_type eq 'i'
12292 && $last_nonblank_type eq 'k'
12293 && $is_sort_map_grep{$last_nonblank_token} )
12294
12295 # /^(sort|map|grep)$/ )
12296 {
12297 $bond_str = NO_BREAK;
12298 }
12299
12300 # extrude.t: do not break before paren at:
12301 # -l pid_filename(
12302 if ( $last_nonblank_type eq 'F' && $next_nonblank_token eq '(' ) {
12303 $bond_str = NO_BREAK;
12304 }
12305
12306 # in older version of perl, use strict can cause problems with
12307 # breaks before bare words following opening parens. For example,
12308 # this will fail under older versions if a break is made between
12309 # '(' and 'MAIL': use strict; open( MAIL, "a long filename or
12310 # command"); close MAIL;
12311 if ( $type eq '{' ) {
12312
12313 if ( $token eq '(' && $next_nonblank_type eq 'w' ) {
12314
12315 # but it's fine to break if the word is followed by a '=>'
12316 # or if it is obviously a sub call
12317 my $i_next_next_nonblank = $i_next_nonblank + 1;
12318 my $next_next_type = $types_to_go[$i_next_next_nonblank];
12319 if ( $next_next_type eq 'b'
12320 && $i_next_nonblank < $max_index_to_go )
12321 {
12322 $i_next_next_nonblank++;
12323 $next_next_type = $types_to_go[$i_next_next_nonblank];
12324 }
12325
12326 # We'll check for an old breakpoint and keep a leading
12327 # bareword if it was that way in the input file.
12328 # Presumably it was ok that way. For example, the
12329 # following would remain unchanged:
12330 #
12331 # @months = (
12332 # January, February, March, April,
12333 # May, June, July, August,
12334 # September, October, November, December,
12335 # );
12336 #
12337 # This should be sufficient:
12338 if (
12339 !$old_breakpoint_to_go[$i]
12340 && ( $next_next_type eq ','
12341 || $next_next_type eq '}' )
12342 )
12343 {
12344 $bond_str = NO_BREAK;
12345 }
12346 }
12347 }
12348
12349 # Do not break between a possible filehandle and a ? or / and do
12350 # not introduce a break after it if there is no blank
12351 # (extrude.t)
12352 elsif ( $type eq 'Z' ) {
12353
12354 # don't break..
12355 if (
12356
12357 # if there is no blank and we do not want one. Examples:
12358 # print $x++ # do not break after $x
12359 # print HTML"HELLO" # break ok after HTML
12360 (
12361 $next_type ne 'b'
12362 && defined( $want_left_space{$next_type} )
12363 && $want_left_space{$next_type} == WS_NO
12364 )
12365
12366 # or we might be followed by the start of a quote
12367 || $next_nonblank_type =~ /^[\/\?]$/
12368 )
12369 {
12370 $bond_str = NO_BREAK;
12371 }
12372 }
12373
12374 # Breaking before a ? before a quote can cause trouble if
12375 # they are not separated by a blank.
12376 # Example: a syntax error occurs if you break before the ? here
12377 # my$logic=join$all?' && ':' || ',@regexps;
12378 # From: Professional_Perl_Programming_Code/multifind.pl
12379 if ( $next_nonblank_type eq '?' ) {
12380 $bond_str = NO_BREAK
12381 if ( $types_to_go[ $i_next_nonblank + 1 ] eq 'Q' );
12382 }
12383
12384 # Breaking before a . followed by a number
12385 # can cause trouble if there is no intervening space
12386 # Example: a syntax error occurs if you break before the .2 here
12387 # $str .= pack($endian.2, ensurrogate($ord));
12388 # From: perl58/Unicode.pm
12389 elsif ( $next_nonblank_type eq '.' ) {
12390 $bond_str = NO_BREAK
12391 if ( $types_to_go[ $i_next_nonblank + 1 ] eq 'n' );
12392 }
12393
12394 my $bond_str_2 = $bond_str;
12395
12396 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12397 # End of hardwired rules
12398 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12399
12400 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12401 # Bond Strength Section 3:
12402 # Apply table rules. These have priority over the above
12403 # hardwired rules.
12404 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12405
12406 my $tabulated_bond_str;
12407 my $ltype = $type;
12408 my $rtype = $next_nonblank_type;
12409 if ( $token =~ /^[\(\[\{\)\]\}]/ ) { $ltype = $type . $token }
12410 if ( $next_nonblank_token =~ /^[\(\[\{\)\]\}]/ ) {
12411 $rtype = $next_nonblank_type . $next_nonblank_token;
12412 }
12413
12414 if ( $binary_bond_strength{$ltype}{$rtype} ) {
12415 $bond_str = $binary_bond_strength{$ltype}{$rtype};
12416 $tabulated_bond_str = $bond_str;
12417 }
12418
12419 if ( $nobreak_rhs{$ltype} || $nobreak_lhs{$rtype} ) {
12420 $bond_str = NO_BREAK;
12421 $tabulated_bond_str = $bond_str;
12422 }
12423 my $bond_str_3 = $bond_str;
12424
12425 # If the hardwired rules conflict with the tabulated bond
12426 # strength then there is an inconsistency that should be fixed
12427 FORMATTER_DEBUG_FLAG_BOND_TABLES
12428 && $tabulated_bond_str
12429 && $bond_str_1
12430 && $bond_str_1 != $bond_str_2
12431 && $bond_str_2 != $tabulated_bond_str
12432 && do {
12433 print STDERR
12434"BOND_TABLES: ltype=$ltype rtype=$rtype $bond_str_1->$bond_str_2->$bond_str_3\n";
12435 };
12436
12437 #-----------------------------------------------------------------
12438 # Bond Strength Section 4:
12439 # Modify strengths of certain tokens which often occur in sequence
12440 # by adding a small bias to each one in turn so that the breaks
12441 # occur from left to right.
12442 #
12443 # Note that we only changing strengths by small amounts here,
12444 # and usually increasing, so we should not be altering any NO_BREAKs.
12445 # Other routines which check for NO_BREAKs will use a tolerance
12446 # of one to avoid any problem.
12447 #-----------------------------------------------------------------
12448
12449 # The bias tables use special keys
12450 my $left_key = bias_table_key( $type, $token );
12451 my $right_key =
12452 bias_table_key( $next_nonblank_type, $next_nonblank_token );
12453
12454 # add any bias set by sub scan_list at old comma break points.
12455 if ( $type eq ',' ) { $bond_str += $bond_strength_to_go[$i] }
12456
12457 # bias left token
12458 elsif ( defined( $bias{$left_key} ) ) {
12459 if ( !$want_break_before{$left_key} ) {
12460 $bias{$left_key} += $delta_bias;
12461 $bond_str += $bias{$left_key};
12462 }
12463 }
12464
12465 # bias right token
12466 if ( defined( $bias{$right_key} ) ) {
12467 if ( $want_break_before{$right_key} ) {
12468
12469 # for leading '.' align all but 'short' quotes; the idea
12470 # is to not place something like "\n" on a single line.
12471 if ( $right_key eq '.' ) {
12472 unless (
12473 $last_nonblank_type eq '.'
12474 && (
12475 length($token) <=
12476 $rOpts_short_concatenation_item_length )
12477 && ( !$is_closing_token{$token} )
12478 )
12479 {
12480 $bias{$right_key} += $delta_bias;
12481 }
12482 }
12483 else {
12484 $bias{$right_key} += $delta_bias;
12485 }
12486 $bond_str += $bias{$right_key};
12487 }
12488 }
12489 my $bond_str_4 = $bond_str;
12490
12491 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12492 # Bond Strength Section 5:
12493 # Fifth Approximation.
12494 # Take nesting depth into account by adding the nesting depth
12495 # to the bond strength.
12496 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12497 my $strength;
12498
12499 if ( defined($bond_str) && !$nobreak_to_go[$i] ) {
12500 if ( $total_nesting_depth > 0 ) {
12501 $strength = $bond_str + $total_nesting_depth;
12502 }
12503 else {
12504 $strength = $bond_str;
12505 }
12506 }
12507 else {
12508 $strength = NO_BREAK;
12509 }
12510
12511 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12512 # Bond Strength Section 6:
12513 # Sixth Approximation. Welds.
12514 #---------------------------------------------------------------
12515
12516 # Do not allow a break within welds,
12517 if ( weld_len_right_to_go($i) ) { $strength = NO_BREAK }
12518
12519 # But encourage breaking after opening welded tokens
12520 elsif ( weld_len_left_to_go($i) && $is_opening_token{$token} ) {
12521 $strength -= 1;
12522 }
12523
12524 # always break after side comment
12525 if ( $type eq '#' ) { $strength = 0 }
12526
12527 $bond_strength_to_go[$i] = $strength;
12528
12529 FORMATTER_DEBUG_FLAG_BOND && do {
12530 my $str = substr( $token, 0, 15 );
12531 $str .= ' ' x ( 16 - length($str) );
12532 print STDOUT
12533"BOND: i=$i $str $type $next_nonblank_type depth=$total_nesting_depth strength=$bond_str_1 -> $bond_str_2 -> $bond_str_3 -> $bond_str_4 $bond_str -> $strength \n";
12534 };
12535 } ## end main loop
12536 return;
12537 } ## end sub set_bond_strengths
12538}

12640 # routine to decide which commas to break at within a container;
12641 # returns:
12642 # $bp_count = number of comma breakpoints set
12643 # $do_not_break_apart = a flag indicating if container need not
12644 # be broken open
12645 sub set_comma_breakpoints {
12646
12647 my $dd = shift;
12648 my $bp_count = 0;
12649 my $do_not_break_apart = 0;
12650
12651 # anything to do?
12652 if ( $item_count_stack[$dd] ) {
12653
12654 # handle commas not in containers...
12655 if ( $dont_align[$dd] ) {
12656 do_uncontained_comma_breaks($dd);
12657 }
12658
12659 # handle commas within containers...
12660 else {
12661 my $fbc = $forced_breakpoint_count;
12662
12663 # always open comma lists not preceded by keywords,
12664 # barewords, identifiers (that is, anything that doesn't
12665 # look like a function call)
12666 my $must_break_open = $last_nonblank_type[$dd] !~ /^[kwiU]$/;
12667
12668 set_comma_breakpoints_do(
12669 $dd,
12670 $opening_structure_index_stack[$dd],
12671 $i,
12672 $item_count_stack[$dd],
12673 $identifier_count_stack[$dd],
12674 $comma_index[$dd],
12675 $next_nonblank_type,
12676 $container_type[$dd],
12677 $interrupted_list[$dd],
12678 \$do_not_break_apart,
12679 $must_break_open,
12680 );
12681 $bp_count = $forced_breakpoint_count - $fbc;
12682 $do_not_break_apart = 0 if $must_break_open;
12683 }
12684 }
12685 return ( $bp_count, $do_not_break_apart );
12686 }

12688 sub do_uncontained_comma_breaks {
12689
12690 # Handle commas not in containers...
12691 # This is a catch-all routine for commas that we
12692 # don't know what to do with because the don't fall
12693 # within containers. We will bias the bond strength
12694 # to break at commas which ended lines in the input
12695 # file. This usually works better than just trying
12696 # to put as many items on a line as possible. A
12697 # downside is that if the input file is garbage it
12698 # won't work very well. However, the user can always
12699 # prevent following the old breakpoints with the
12700 # -iob flag.
12701 my $dd = shift;
12702 my $bias = -.01;
12703 my $old_comma_break_count = 0;
12704 foreach my $ii ( @{ $comma_index[$dd] } ) {
12705 if ( $old_breakpoint_to_go[$ii] ) {
12706 $old_comma_break_count++;
12707 $bond_strength_to_go[$ii] = $bias;
12708
12709 # reduce bias magnitude to force breaks in order
12710 $bias *= 0.99;
12711 }
12712 }
12713
12714 # Also put a break before the first comma if
12715 # (1) there was a break there in the input, and
12716 # (2) there was exactly one old break before the first comma break
12717 # (3) OLD: there are multiple old comma breaks
12718 # (3) NEW: there are one or more old comma breaks (see return example)
12719 #
12720 # For example, we will follow the user and break after
12721 # 'print' in this snippet:
12722 # print
12723 # "conformability (Not the same dimension)\n",
12724 # "\t", $have, " is ", text_unit($hu), "\n",
12725 # "\t", $want, " is ", text_unit($wu), "\n",
12726 # ;
12727 #
12728 # Another example, just one comma, where we will break after
12729 # the return:
12730 # return
12731 # $x * cos($a) - $y * sin($a),
12732 # $x * sin($a) + $y * cos($a);
12733
12734 # Breaking a print statement:
12735 # print SAVEOUT
12736 # ( $? & 127 ) ? " (SIG#" . ( $? & 127 ) . ")" : "",
12737 # ( $? & 128 ) ? " -- core dumped" : "", "\n";
12738 #
12739 # But we will not force a break after the opening paren here
12740 # (causes a blinker):
12741 # $heap->{stream}->set_output_filter(
12742 # poe::filter::reference->new('myotherfreezer') ),
12743 # ;
12744 #
12745 my $i_first_comma = $comma_index[$dd]->[0];
12746 if ( $old_breakpoint_to_go[$i_first_comma] ) {
12747 my $level_comma = $levels_to_go[$i_first_comma];
12748 my $ibreak = -1;
12749 my $obp_count = 0;
12750 for ( my $ii = $i_first_comma - 1 ; $ii >= 0 ; $ii -= 1 ) {
12751 if ( $old_breakpoint_to_go[$ii] ) {
12752 $obp_count++;
12753 last if ( $obp_count > 1 );
12754 $ibreak = $ii
12755 if ( $levels_to_go[$ii] == $level_comma );
12756 }
12757 }
12758
12759 # Changed rule from multiple old commas to just one here:
12760 if ( $ibreak >= 0 && $obp_count == 1 && $old_comma_break_count > 0 )
12761 {
12762 # Do not to break before an opening token because
12763 # it can lead to "blinkers".
12764 my $ibreakm = $ibreak;
12765 $ibreakm-- if ( $types_to_go[$ibreakm] eq 'b' );
12766 if ( $ibreakm >= 0 && $types_to_go[$ibreakm] !~ /^[\(\{\[L]$/ )
12767 {
12768 set_forced_breakpoint($ibreak);
12769 }
12770 }
12771 }
12772 return;
12773 }

12790 sub set_logical_breakpoints {

12819 }
