12821 sub is_unbreakable_container {
12822
12823 # never break a container of one of these types
12824 # because bad things can happen (map1.t)
12825 my $dd = shift;
12826 return $is_sort_map_grep{ $container_type[$dd] };
12827 }
12828
12829 sub scan_list {
12830
12831 # This routine is responsible for setting line breaks for all lists,
12832 # so that hierarchical structure can be displayed and so that list
12833 # items can be vertically aligned. The output of this routine is
12834 # stored in the array @forced_breakpoint_to_go, which is used to set
12835 # final breakpoints.
12836
12837 $starting_depth = $nesting_depth_to_go[0];
12838
12839 $block_type = ' ';
12840 $current_depth = $starting_depth;
12841 $i = -1;
12842 $last_colon_sequence_number = -1;
12843 $last_nonblank_token = ';';
12844 $last_nonblank_type = ';';
12845 $last_nonblank_block_type = ' ';
12846 $last_old_breakpoint_count = 0;
12847 $minimum_depth = $current_depth + 1; # forces update in check below
12848 $old_breakpoint_count = 0;
12849 $starting_breakpoint_count = $forced_breakpoint_count;
12850 $token = ';';
12851 $type = ';';
12852 $type_sequence = '';
12853
12854 my $total_depth_variation = 0;
12855 my $i_old_assignment_break;
12856 my $depth_last = $starting_depth;
12857
12858 check_for_new_minimum_depth($current_depth);
12859
12860 my $is_long_line = excess_line_length( 0, $max_index_to_go ) > 0;
12861 my $want_previous_breakpoint = -1;
12862
12863 my $saw_good_breakpoint;
12864 my $i_line_end = -1;
12865 my $i_line_start = -1;
12866
12867 # loop over all tokens in this batch
12868 while ( ++$i <= $max_index_to_go ) {
12869 if ( $type ne 'b' ) {
12870 $i_last_nonblank_token = $i - 1;
12871 $last_nonblank_type = $type;
12872 $last_nonblank_token = $token;
12873 $last_nonblank_block_type = $block_type;
12874 } ## end if ( $type ne 'b' )
12875 $type = $types_to_go[$i];
12876 $block_type = $block_type_to_go[$i];
12877 $token = $tokens_to_go[$i];
12878 $type_sequence = $type_sequence_to_go[$i];
12879 my $next_type = $types_to_go[ $i + 1 ];
12880 my $next_token = $tokens_to_go[ $i + 1 ];
12881 my $i_next_nonblank = ( ( $next_type eq 'b' ) ? $i + 2 : $i + 1 );
12882 $next_nonblank_type = $types_to_go[$i_next_nonblank];
12883 $next_nonblank_token = $tokens_to_go[$i_next_nonblank];
12884 $next_nonblank_block_type = $block_type_to_go[$i_next_nonblank];
12885
12886 # set break if flag was set
12887 if ( $want_previous_breakpoint >= 0 ) {
12888 set_forced_breakpoint($want_previous_breakpoint);
12889 $want_previous_breakpoint = -1;
12890 }
12891
12892 $last_old_breakpoint_count = $old_breakpoint_count;
12893 if ( $old_breakpoint_to_go[$i] ) {
12894 $i_line_end = $i;
12895 $i_line_start = $i_next_nonblank;
12896
12897 $old_breakpoint_count++;
12898
12899 # Break before certain keywords if user broke there and
12900 # this is a 'safe' break point. The idea is to retain
12901 # any preferred breaks for sequential list operations,
12902 # like a schwartzian transform.
12903 if ($rOpts_break_at_old_keyword_breakpoints) {
12904 if (
12905 $next_nonblank_type eq 'k'
12906 && $is_keyword_returning_list{$next_nonblank_token}
12907 && ( $type =~ /^[=\)\]\}Riw]$/
12908 || $type eq 'k'
12909 && $is_keyword_returning_list{$token} )
12910 )
12911 {
12912
12913 # we actually have to set this break next time through
12914 # the loop because if we are at a closing token (such
12915 # as '}') which forms a one-line block, this break might
12916 # get undone.
12917 $want_previous_breakpoint = $i;
12918 } ## end if ( $next_nonblank_type...)
12919 } ## end if ($rOpts_break_at_old_keyword_breakpoints)
12920
12921 # Break before attributes if user broke there
12922 if ($rOpts_break_at_old_attribute_breakpoints) {
12923 if ( $next_nonblank_type eq 'A' ) {
12924 $want_previous_breakpoint = $i;
12925 }
12926 }
12927
12928 # remember an = break as possible good break point
12929 if ( $is_assignment{$type} ) {
12930 $i_old_assignment_break = $i;
12931 }
12932 elsif ( $is_assignment{$next_nonblank_type} ) {
12933 $i_old_assignment_break = $i_next_nonblank;
12934 }
12935 } ## end if ( $old_breakpoint_to_go...)
12936
12937 next if ( $type eq 'b' );
12938 $depth = $nesting_depth_to_go[ $i + 1 ];
12939
12940 $total_depth_variation += abs( $depth - $depth_last );
12941 $depth_last = $depth;
12942
12943 # safety check - be sure we always break after a comment
12944 # Shouldn't happen .. an error here probably means that the
12945 # nobreak flag did not get turned off correctly during
12946 # formatting.
12947 if ( $type eq '#' ) {
12948 if ( $i != $max_index_to_go ) {
12949 warning(
12950"Non-fatal program bug: backup logic needed to break after a comment\n"
12951 );
12952 report_definite_bug();
12953 $nobreak_to_go[$i] = 0;
12954 set_forced_breakpoint($i);
12955 } ## end if ( $i != $max_index_to_go)
12956 } ## end if ( $type eq '#' )
12957
12958 # Force breakpoints at certain tokens in long lines.
12959 # Note that such breakpoints will be undone later if these tokens
12960 # are fully contained within parens on a line.
12961 if (
12962
12963 # break before a keyword within a line
12964 $type eq 'k'
12965 && $i > 0
12966
12967 # if one of these keywords:
12968 && $token =~ /^(if|unless|while|until|for)$/
12969
12970 # but do not break at something like '1 while'
12971 && ( $last_nonblank_type ne 'n' || $i > 2 )
12972
12973 # and let keywords follow a closing 'do' brace
12974 && $last_nonblank_block_type ne 'do'
12975
12976 && (
12977 $is_long_line
12978
12979 # or container is broken (by side-comment, etc)
12980 || ( $next_nonblank_token eq '('
12981 && $mate_index_to_go[$i_next_nonblank] < $i )
12982 )
12983 )
12984 {
12985 set_forced_breakpoint( $i - 1 );
12986 } ## end if ( $type eq 'k' && $i...)
12987
12988 # remember locations of -> if this is a pre-broken method chain
12989 if ( $type eq '->' ) {
12990 if ($rOpts_break_at_old_method_breakpoints) {
12991
12992 # Case 1: look for lines with leading pointers
12993 if ( $i == $i_line_start ) {
12994 set_forced_breakpoint( $i - 1 );
12995 }
12996
12997 # Case 2: look for cuddled pointer calls
12998 else {
12999
13000 # look for old lines with leading ')->' or ') ->'
13001 # and, when found, force a break before the
13002 # opening paren and after the previous closing paren.
13003 if (
13004 $types_to_go[$i_line_start] eq '}'
13005 && ( $i == $i_line_start + 1
13006 || $i == $i_line_start + 2
13007 && $types_to_go[ $i - 1 ] eq 'b' )
13008 )
13009 {
13010 set_forced_breakpoint( $i_line_start - 1 );
13011 set_forced_breakpoint(
13012 $mate_index_to_go[$i_line_start] );
13013 }
13014 }
13015 }
13016 } ## end if ( $type eq '->' )
13017
13018 # remember locations of '||' and '&&' for possible breaks if we
13019 # decide this is a long logical expression.
13020 elsif ( $type eq '||' ) {
13021 push @{ $rand_or_list[$depth][2] }, $i;
13022 ++$has_old_logical_breakpoints[$depth]
13023 if ( ( $i == $i_line_start || $i == $i_line_end )
13024 && $rOpts_break_at_old_logical_breakpoints );
13025 } ## end elsif ( $type eq '||' )
13026 elsif ( $type eq '&&' ) {
13027 push @{ $rand_or_list[$depth][3] }, $i;
13028 ++$has_old_logical_breakpoints[$depth]
13029 if ( ( $i == $i_line_start || $i == $i_line_end )
13030 && $rOpts_break_at_old_logical_breakpoints );
13031 } ## end elsif ( $type eq '&&' )
13032 elsif ( $type eq 'f' ) {
13033 push @{ $rfor_semicolon_list[$depth] }, $i;
13034 }
13035 elsif ( $type eq 'k' ) {
13036 if ( $token eq 'and' ) {
13037 push @{ $rand_or_list[$depth][1] }, $i;
13038 ++$has_old_logical_breakpoints[$depth]
13039 if ( ( $i == $i_line_start || $i == $i_line_end )
13040 && $rOpts_break_at_old_logical_breakpoints );
13041 } ## end if ( $token eq 'and' )
13042
13043 # break immediately at 'or's which are probably not in a logical
13044 # block -- but we will break in logical breaks below so that
13045 # they do not add to the forced_breakpoint_count
13046 elsif ( $token eq 'or' ) {
13047 push @{ $rand_or_list[$depth][0] }, $i;
13048 ++$has_old_logical_breakpoints[$depth]
13049 if ( ( $i == $i_line_start || $i == $i_line_end )
13050 && $rOpts_break_at_old_logical_breakpoints );
13051 if ( $is_logical_container{ $container_type[$depth] } ) {
13052 }
13053 else {
13054 if ($is_long_line) { set_forced_breakpoint($i) }
13055 elsif ( ( $i == $i_line_start || $i == $i_line_end )
13056 && $rOpts_break_at_old_logical_breakpoints )
13057 {
13058 $saw_good_breakpoint = 1;
13059 }
13060 } ## end else [ if ( $is_logical_container...)]
13061 } ## end elsif ( $token eq 'or' )
13062 elsif ( $token eq 'if' || $token eq 'unless' ) {
13063 push @{ $rand_or_list[$depth][4] }, $i;
13064 if ( ( $i == $i_line_start || $i == $i_line_end )
13065 && $rOpts_break_at_old_logical_breakpoints )
13066 {
13067 set_forced_breakpoint($i);
13068 }
13069 } ## end elsif ( $token eq 'if' ||...)
13070 } ## end elsif ( $type eq 'k' )
13071 elsif ( $is_assignment{$type} ) {
13072 $i_equals[$depth] = $i;
13073 }
13074
13075 if ($type_sequence) {
13076
13077 # handle any postponed closing breakpoints
13078 if ( $token =~ /^[\)\]\}\:]$/ ) {
13079 if ( $type eq ':' ) {
13080 $last_colon_sequence_number = $type_sequence;
13081
13082 # retain break at a ':' line break
13083 if ( ( $i == $i_line_start || $i == $i_line_end )
13084 && $rOpts_break_at_old_ternary_breakpoints )
13085 {
13086
13087 set_forced_breakpoint($i);
13088
13089 # break at previous '='
13090 if ( $i_equals[$depth] > 0 ) {
13091 set_forced_breakpoint( $i_equals[$depth] );
13092 $i_equals[$depth] = -1;
13093 }
13094 } ## end if ( ( $i == $i_line_start...))
13095 } ## end if ( $type eq ':' )
13096 if ( defined( $postponed_breakpoint{$type_sequence} ) ) {
13097 my $inc = ( $type eq ':' ) ? 0 : 1;
13098 set_forced_breakpoint( $i - $inc );
13099 delete $postponed_breakpoint{$type_sequence};
13100 }
13101 } ## end if ( $token =~ /^[\)\]\}\:]$/[{[(])
13102
13103 # set breaks at ?/: if they will get separated (and are
13104 # not a ?/: chain), or if the '?' is at the end of the
13105 # line
13106 elsif ( $token eq '?' ) {
13107 my $i_colon = $mate_index_to_go[$i];
13108 if (
13109 $i_colon <= 0 # the ':' is not in this batch
13110 || $i == 0 # this '?' is the first token of the line
13111 || $i ==
13112 $max_index_to_go # or this '?' is the last token
13113 )
13114 {
13115
13116 # don't break at a '?' if preceded by ':' on
13117 # this line of previous ?/: pair on this line.
13118 # This is an attempt to preserve a chain of ?/:
13119 # expressions (elsif2.t). And don't break if
13120 # this has a side comment.
13121 set_forced_breakpoint($i)
13122 unless (
13123 $type_sequence == (
13124 $last_colon_sequence_number +
13125 TYPE_SEQUENCE_INCREMENT
13126 )
13127 || $tokens_to_go[$max_index_to_go] eq '#'
13128 );
13129 set_closing_breakpoint($i);
13130 } ## end if ( $i_colon <= 0 ||...)
13131 } ## end elsif ( $token eq '?' )
13132 } ## end if ($type_sequence)
13133
13134#print "LISTX sees: i=$i type=$type tok=$token block=$block_type depth=$depth\n";
13135
13136 #------------------------------------------------------------
13137 # Handle Increasing Depth..
13138 #
13139 # prepare for a new list when depth increases
13140 # token $i is a '(','{', or '['
13141 #------------------------------------------------------------
13142 if ( $depth > $current_depth ) {
13143
13144 $breakpoint_stack[$depth] = $forced_breakpoint_count;
13145 $breakpoint_undo_stack[$depth] = $forced_breakpoint_undo_count;
13146 $has_broken_sublist[$depth] = 0;
13147 $identifier_count_stack[$depth] = 0;
13148 $index_before_arrow[$depth] = -1;
13149 $interrupted_list[$depth] = 0;
13150 $item_count_stack[$depth] = 0;
13151 $last_comma_index[$depth] = undef;
13152 $last_dot_index[$depth] = undef;
13153 $last_nonblank_type[$depth] = $last_nonblank_type;
13154 $old_breakpoint_count_stack[$depth] = $old_breakpoint_count;
13155 $opening_structure_index_stack[$depth] = $i;
13156 $rand_or_list[$depth] = [];
13157 $rfor_semicolon_list[$depth] = [];
13158 $i_equals[$depth] = -1;
13159 $want_comma_break[$depth] = 0;
13160 $container_type[$depth] =
13161 ( $last_nonblank_type =~ /^(k|=>|&&|\|\||\?|\:|\.)$/ )
13162 ? $last_nonblank_token
13163 : "";
13164 $has_old_logical_breakpoints[$depth] = 0;
13165
13166 # if line ends here then signal closing token to break
13167 if ( $next_nonblank_type eq 'b' || $next_nonblank_type eq '#' )
13168 {
13169 set_closing_breakpoint($i);
13170 }
13171
13172 # Not all lists of values should be vertically aligned..
13173 $dont_align[$depth] =
13174
13175 # code BLOCKS are handled at a higher level
13176 ( $block_type ne "" )
13177
13178 # certain paren lists
13179 || ( $type eq '(' ) && (
13180
13181 # it does not usually look good to align a list of
13182 # identifiers in a parameter list, as in:
13183 # my($var1, $var2, ...)
13184 # (This test should probably be refined, for now I'm just
13185 # testing for any keyword)
13186 ( $last_nonblank_type eq 'k' )
13187
13188 # a trailing '(' usually indicates a non-list
13189 || ( $next_nonblank_type eq '(' )
13190 );
13191
13192 # patch to outdent opening brace of long if/for/..
13193 # statements (like this one). See similar coding in
13194 # set_continuation breaks. We have also catch it here for
13195 # short line fragments which otherwise will not go through
13196 # set_continuation_breaks.
13197 if (
13198 $block_type
13199
13200 # if we have the ')' but not its '(' in this batch..
13201 && ( $last_nonblank_token eq ')' )
13202 && $mate_index_to_go[$i_last_nonblank_token] < 0
13203
13204 # and user wants brace to left
13205 && !$rOpts->{'opening-brace-always-on-right'}
13206
13207 && ( $type eq '{' ) # should be true
13208 && ( $token eq '{' ) # should be true
13209 )
13210 {
13211 set_forced_breakpoint( $i - 1 );
13212 } ## end if ( $block_type && ( ...))
13213 } ## end if ( $depth > $current_depth)
13214
13215 #------------------------------------------------------------
13216 # Handle Decreasing Depth..
13217 #
13218 # finish off any old list when depth decreases
13219 # token $i is a ')','}', or ']'
13220 #------------------------------------------------------------
13221 elsif ( $depth < $current_depth ) {
13222
13223 check_for_new_minimum_depth($depth);
13224
13225 # force all outer logical containers to break after we see on
13226 # old breakpoint
13227 $has_old_logical_breakpoints[$depth] ||=
13228 $has_old_logical_breakpoints[$current_depth];
13229
13230 # Patch to break between ') {' if the paren list is broken.
13231 # There is similar logic in set_continuation_breaks for
13232 # non-broken lists.
13233 if ( $token eq ')'
13234 && $next_nonblank_block_type
13235 && $interrupted_list[$current_depth]
13236 && $next_nonblank_type eq '{'
13237 && !$rOpts->{'opening-brace-always-on-right'} )
13238 {
13239 set_forced_breakpoint($i);
13240 } ## end if ( $token eq ')' && ...
13241
13242#print "LISTY sees: i=$i type=$type tok=$token block=$block_type depth=$depth next=$next_nonblank_type next_block=$next_nonblank_block_type inter=$interrupted_list[$current_depth]\n";
13243
13244 # set breaks at commas if necessary
13245 my ( $bp_count, $do_not_break_apart ) =
13246 set_comma_breakpoints($current_depth);
13247
13248 my $i_opening = $opening_structure_index_stack[$current_depth];
13249 my $saw_opening_structure = ( $i_opening >= 0 );
13250
13251 # this term is long if we had to break at interior commas..
13252 my $is_long_term = $bp_count > 0;
13253
13254 # If this is a short container with one or more comma arrows,
13255 # then we will mark it as a long term to open it if requested.
13256 # $rOpts_comma_arrow_breakpoints =
13257 # 0 - open only if comma precedes closing brace
13258 # 1 - stable: except for one line blocks
13259 # 2 - try to form 1 line blocks
13260 # 3 - ignore =>
13261 # 4 - always open up if vt=0
13262 # 5 - stable: even for one line blocks if vt=0
13263 if ( !$is_long_term
13264 && $tokens_to_go[$i_opening] =~ /^[\(\{\[]$/
13265 && $index_before_arrow[ $depth + 1 ] > 0
13266 && !$opening_vertical_tightness{ $tokens_to_go[$i_opening] }
13267 )
13268 {
13269 $is_long_term = $rOpts_comma_arrow_breakpoints == 4
13270 || ( $rOpts_comma_arrow_breakpoints == 0
13271 && $last_nonblank_token eq ',' )
13272 || ( $rOpts_comma_arrow_breakpoints == 5
13273 && $old_breakpoint_to_go[$i_opening] );
13274 } ## end if ( !$is_long_term &&...)
13275
13276 # mark term as long if the length between opening and closing
13277 # parens exceeds allowed line length
13278 if ( !$is_long_term && $saw_opening_structure ) {
13279 my $i_opening_minus = find_token_starting_list($i_opening);
13280
13281 # Note: we have to allow for one extra space after a
13282 # closing token so that we do not strand a comma or
13283 # semicolon, hence the '>=' here (oneline.t)
13284 # Note: we ignore left weld lengths here for best results
13285 $is_long_term =
13286 excess_line_length( $i_opening_minus, $i, 1 ) >= 0;
13287 } ## end if ( !$is_long_term &&...)
13288
13289 # We've set breaks after all comma-arrows. Now we have to
13290 # undo them if this can be a one-line block
13291 # (the only breakpoints set will be due to comma-arrows)
13292 if (
13293
13294 # user doesn't require breaking after all comma-arrows
13295 ( $rOpts_comma_arrow_breakpoints != 0 )
13296 && ( $rOpts_comma_arrow_breakpoints != 4 )
13297
13298 # and if the opening structure is in this batch
13299 && $saw_opening_structure
13300
13301 # and either on the same old line
13302 && (
13303 $old_breakpoint_count_stack[$current_depth] ==
13304 $last_old_breakpoint_count
13305
13306 # or user wants to form long blocks with arrows
13307 || $rOpts_comma_arrow_breakpoints == 2
13308 )
13309
13310 # and we made some breakpoints between the opening and closing
13311 && ( $breakpoint_undo_stack[$current_depth] <
13312 $forced_breakpoint_undo_count )
13313
13314 # and this block is short enough to fit on one line
13315 # Note: use < because need 1 more space for possible comma
13316 && !$is_long_term
13317
13318 )
13319 {
13320 undo_forced_breakpoint_stack(
13321 $breakpoint_undo_stack[$current_depth] );
13322 } ## end if ( ( $rOpts_comma_arrow_breakpoints...))
13323
13324 # now see if we have any comma breakpoints left
13325 my $has_comma_breakpoints =
13326 ( $breakpoint_stack[$current_depth] !=
13327 $forced_breakpoint_count );
13328
13329 # update broken-sublist flag of the outer container
13330 $has_broken_sublist[$depth] =
13331 $has_broken_sublist[$depth]
13332 || $has_broken_sublist[$current_depth]
13333 || $is_long_term
13334 || $has_comma_breakpoints;
13335
13336# Having come to the closing ')', '}', or ']', now we have to decide if we
13337# should 'open up' the structure by placing breaks at the opening and
13338# closing containers. This is a tricky decision. Here are some of the
13339# basic considerations:
13340#
13341# -If this is a BLOCK container, then any breakpoints will have already
13342# been set (and according to user preferences), so we need do nothing here.
13343#
13344# -If we have a comma-separated list for which we can align the list items,
13345# then we need to do so because otherwise the vertical aligner cannot
13346# currently do the alignment.
13347#
13348# -If this container does itself contain a container which has been broken
13349# open, then it should be broken open to properly show the structure.
13350#
13351# -If there is nothing to align, and no other reason to break apart,
13352# then do not do it.
13353#
13354# We will not break open the parens of a long but 'simple' logical expression.
13355# For example:
13356#
13357# This is an example of a simple logical expression and its formatting:
13358#
13359# if ( $bigwasteofspace1 && $bigwasteofspace2
13360# || $bigwasteofspace3 && $bigwasteofspace4 )
13361#
13362# Most people would prefer this than the 'spacey' version:
13363#
13364# if (
13365# $bigwasteofspace1 && $bigwasteofspace2
13366# || $bigwasteofspace3 && $bigwasteofspace4
13367# )
13368#
13369# To illustrate the rules for breaking logical expressions, consider:
13370#
13371# FULLY DENSE:
13372# if ( $opt_excl
13373# and ( exists $ids_excl_uc{$id_uc}
13374# or grep $id_uc =~ /$_/, @ids_excl_uc ))
13375#
13376# This is on the verge of being difficult to read. The current default is to
13377# open it up like this:
13378#
13379# DEFAULT:
13380# if (
13381# $opt_excl
13382# and ( exists $ids_excl_uc{$id_uc}
13383# or grep $id_uc =~ /$_/, @ids_excl_uc )
13384# )
13385#
13386# This is a compromise which tries to avoid being too dense and to spacey.
13387# A more spaced version would be:
13388#
13389# SPACEY:
13390# if (
13391# $opt_excl
13392# and (
13393# exists $ids_excl_uc{$id_uc}
13394# or grep $id_uc =~ /$_/, @ids_excl_uc
13395# )
13396# )
13397#
13398# Some people might prefer the spacey version -- an option could be added. The
13399# innermost expression contains a long block '( exists $ids_... ')'.
13400#
13401# Here is how the logic goes: We will force a break at the 'or' that the
13402# innermost expression contains, but we will not break apart its opening and
13403# closing containers because (1) it contains no multi-line sub-containers itself,
13404# and (2) there is no alignment to be gained by breaking it open like this
13405#
13406# and (
13407# exists $ids_excl_uc{$id_uc}
13408# or grep $id_uc =~ /$_/, @ids_excl_uc
13409# )
13410#
13411# (although this looks perfectly ok and might be good for long expressions). The
13412# outer 'if' container, though, contains a broken sub-container, so it will be

13796
13797 # When testing to see if a block will fit on one line, some
13798 # previous token(s) may also need to be on the line; particularly
13799 # if this is a sub call. So we will look back at least one
13800 # token. NOTE: This isn't perfect, but not critical, because
13801 # if we mis-identify a block, it will be wrapped and therefore
13802 # fixed the next time it is formatted.
13803 my $i_opening_paren = shift;
13804 my $i_opening_minus = $i_opening_paren;
13805 my $im1 = $i_opening_paren - 1;
13806 my $im2 = $i_opening_paren - 2;
13807 my $im3 = $i_opening_paren - 3;
13808 my $typem1 = $types_to_go[$im1];
13809 my $typem2 = $im2 >= 0 ? $types_to_go[$im2] : 'b';
13810
13811 if ( $typem1 eq ',' || ( $typem1 eq 'b' && $typem2 eq ',' ) ) {
13812 $i_opening_minus = $i_opening_paren;
13813 }
13814 elsif ( $tokens_to_go[$i_opening_paren] eq '(' ) {
13815 $i_opening_minus = $im1 if $im1 >= 0;
13816
13817 # walk back to improve length estimate
13818 for ( my $j = $im1 ; $j >= 0 ; $j-- ) {
13819 last if ( $types_to_go[$j] =~ /^[\(\[\{L\}\]\)Rb,]$/ );
13820 $i_opening_minus = $j;
13821 }
13822 if ( $types_to_go[$i_opening_minus] eq 'b' ) { $i_opening_minus++ }
13823 }
13824 elsif ( $typem1 eq 'k' ) { $i_opening_minus = $im1 }
13825 elsif ( $typem1 eq 'b' && $im2 >= 0 && $types_to_go[$im2] eq 'k' ) {
13826 $i_opening_minus = $im2;
13827 }
13828 return $i_opening_minus;
13829}

13844 sub set_comma_breakpoints_do {
13845
13846 # Given a list with some commas, set breakpoints at some of the
13847 # commas, if necessary, to make it easy to read. This list is
13848 # an example:
13849 my (
13850 $depth, $i_opening_paren, $i_closing_paren,
13851 $item_count, $identifier_count, $rcomma_index,
13852 $next_nonblank_type, $list_type, $interrupted,
13853 $rdo_not_break_apart, $must_break_open,
13854 ) = @_;
13855
13856 # nothing to do if no commas seen
13857 return if ( $item_count < 1 );
13858 my $i_first_comma = $rcomma_index->[0];
13859 my $i_true_last_comma = $rcomma_index->[ $item_count - 1 ];
13860 my $i_last_comma = $i_true_last_comma;
13861 if ( $i_last_comma >= $max_index_to_go ) {
13862 $i_last_comma = $rcomma_index->[ --$item_count - 1 ];
13863 return if ( $item_count < 1 );
13864 }
13865
13866 #---------------------------------------------------------------
13867 # find lengths of all items in the list to calculate page layout
13868 #---------------------------------------------------------------
13869 my $comma_count = $item_count;
13870 my @item_lengths;
13871 my @i_term_begin;
13872 my @i_term_end;
13873 my @i_term_comma;
13874 my $i_prev_plus;
13875 my @max_length = ( 0, 0 );
13876 my $first_term_length;
13877 my $i = $i_opening_paren;
13878 my $is_odd = 1;
13879
13880 foreach my $j ( 0 .. $comma_count - 1 ) {
13881 $is_odd = 1 - $is_odd;
13882 $i_prev_plus = $i + 1;
13883 $i = $rcomma_index->[$j];
13884
13885 my $i_term_end =
13886 ( $types_to_go[ $i - 1 ] eq 'b' ) ? $i - 2 : $i - 1;
13887 my $i_term_begin =
13888 ( $types_to_go[$i_prev_plus] eq 'b' )
13889 ? $i_prev_plus + 1
13890 : $i_prev_plus;
13891 push @i_term_begin, $i_term_begin;
13892 push @i_term_end, $i_term_end;
13893 push @i_term_comma, $i;
13894
13895 # note: currently adding 2 to all lengths (for comma and space)
13896 my $length =
13897 2 + token_sequence_length( $i_term_begin, $i_term_end );
13898 push @item_lengths, $length;
13899
13900 if ( $j == 0 ) {
13901 $first_term_length = $length;
13902 }
13903 else {
13904
13905 if ( $length > $max_length[$is_odd] ) {
13906 $max_length[$is_odd] = $length;
13907 }
13908 }
13909 }
13910

13912 # count, because the item count will be one greater than the comma
13913 # count if the last item is not terminated with a comma
13914 my $i_b =
13915 ( $types_to_go[ $i_last_comma + 1 ] eq 'b' )
13916 ? $i_last_comma + 1
13917 : $i_last_comma;
13918 my $i_e =
13919 ( $types_to_go[ $i_closing_paren - 1 ] eq 'b' )
13920 ? $i_closing_paren - 2
13921 : $i_closing_paren - 1;
13922 my $i_effective_last_comma = $i_last_comma;
13923
13924 my $last_item_length = token_sequence_length( $i_b + 1, $i_e );
13925
13926 if ( $last_item_length > 0 ) {
13927
13928 # add 2 to length because other lengths include a comma and a blank
13929 $last_item_length += 2;
13930 push @item_lengths, $last_item_length;
13931 push @i_term_begin, $i_b + 1;
13932 push @i_term_end, $i_e;
13933 push @i_term_comma, undef;
13934
13935 my $i_odd = $item_count % 2;
13936
13937 if ( $last_item_length > $max_length[$i_odd] ) {
13938 $max_length[$i_odd] = $last_item_length;
13939 }
13940
13941 $item_count++;
13942 $i_effective_last_comma = $i_e + 1;
13943
13944 if ( $types_to_go[ $i_b + 1 ] =~ /^[iR\]]$/ ) {
13945 $identifier_count++;
13946 }
13947 }
13948
13949 #---------------------------------------------------------------
13950 # End of length calculations
13951 #---------------------------------------------------------------
13952
13953 #---------------------------------------------------------------
13954 # Compound List Rule 1:
13955 # Break at (almost) every comma for a list containing a broken
13956 # sublist. This has higher priority than the Interrupted List
13957 # Rule.
13958 #---------------------------------------------------------------
13959 if ( $has_broken_sublist[$depth] ) {
13960
13961 # Break at every comma except for a comma between two
13962 # simple, small terms. This prevents long vertical
13963 # columns of, say, just 0's.
13964 my $small_length = 10; # 2 + actual maximum length wanted
13965
13966 # We'll insert a break in long runs of small terms to
13967 # allow alignment in uniform tables.
13968 my $skipped_count = 0;
13969 my $columns = table_columns_available($i_first_comma);
13970 my $fields = int( $columns / $small_length );
13971 if ( $rOpts_maximum_fields_per_table
13972 && $fields > $rOpts_maximum_fields_per_table )
13973 {
13974 $fields = $rOpts_maximum_fields_per_table;
13975 }
13976 my $max_skipped_count = $fields - 1;
13977
13978 my $is_simple_last_term = 0;
13979 my $is_simple_next_term = 0;
13980 foreach my $j ( 0 .. $item_count ) {
13981 $is_simple_last_term = $is_simple_next_term;
13982 $is_simple_next_term = 0;
13983 if ( $j < $item_count
13984 && $i_term_end[$j] == $i_term_begin[$j]
13985 && $item_lengths[$j] <= $small_length )
13986 {
13987 $is_simple_next_term = 1;
13988 }
13989 next if $j == 0;
13990 if ( $is_simple_last_term
13991 && $is_simple_next_term
13992 && $skipped_count < $max_skipped_count )
13993 {
13994 $skipped_count++;
13995 }
13996 else {
13997 $skipped_count = 0;
13998 my $i = $i_term_comma[ $j - 1 ];
13999 last unless defined $i;
14000 set_forced_breakpoint($i);
14001 }
14002 }
14003
14004 # always break at the last comma if this list is
14005 # interrupted; we wouldn't want to leave a terminal '{', for
14006 # example.
14007 if ($interrupted) { set_forced_breakpoint($i_true_last_comma) }
14008 return;
14009 }

14012#print "LISTX: in set_list $a $c interrupt=$interrupted count=$item_count
14013#i_first = $i_first_comma i_last=$i_last_comma max=$max_index_to_go\n";
14014#print "depth=$depth has_broken=$has_broken_sublist[$depth] is_multi=$is_multiline opening_paren=($i_opening_paren) \n";
14015
14016 #---------------------------------------------------------------
14017 # Interrupted List Rule:
14018 # A list is forced to use old breakpoints if it was interrupted
14019 # by side comments or blank lines, or requested by user.
14020 #---------------------------------------------------------------
14021 if ( $rOpts_break_at_old_comma_breakpoints
14022 || $interrupted
14023 || $i_opening_paren < 0 )
14024 {
14025 copy_old_breakpoints( $i_first_comma, $i_true_last_comma );
14026 return;
14027 }
14028
14029 #---------------------------------------------------------------
14030 # Looks like a list of items. We have to look at it and size it up.
14031 #---------------------------------------------------------------
14032
14033 my $opening_token = $tokens_to_go[$i_opening_paren];
14034 my $opening_environment =
14035 $container_environment_to_go[$i_opening_paren];
14036
14037 #-------------------------------------------------------------------
14038 # Return if this will fit on one line
14039 #-------------------------------------------------------------------
14040
14041 my $i_opening_minus = find_token_starting_list($i_opening_paren);
14042 return
14043 unless excess_line_length( $i_opening_minus, $i_closing_paren ) > 0;
14044
14045 #-------------------------------------------------------------------
14046 # Now we know that this block spans multiple lines; we have to set
14047 # at least one breakpoint -- real or fake -- as a signal to break
14048 # open any outer containers.
14049 #-------------------------------------------------------------------
14050 set_fake_breakpoint();
14051
14052 # be sure we do not extend beyond the current list length
14053 if ( $i_effective_last_comma >= $max_index_to_go ) {
14054 $i_effective_last_comma = $max_index_to_go - 1;
14055 }
14056
14057 # Set a flag indicating if we need to break open to keep -lp
14058 # items aligned. This is necessary if any of the list terms
14059 # exceeds the available space after the '('.
14060 my $need_lp_break_open = $must_break_open;
14061 if ( $rOpts_line_up_parentheses && !$must_break_open ) {
14062 my $columns_if_unbroken =
14063 maximum_line_length($i_opening_minus) -
14064 total_line_length( $i_opening_minus, $i_opening_paren );
14065 $need_lp_break_open =
14066 ( $max_length[0] > $columns_if_unbroken )
14067 || ( $max_length[1] > $columns_if_unbroken )
14068 || ( $first_term_length > $columns_if_unbroken );
14069 }
14070
14071 # Specify if the list must have an even number of fields or not.
14072 # It is generally safest to assume an even number, because the
14073 # list items might be a hash list. But if we can be sure that
14074 # it is not a hash, then we can allow an odd number for more
14075 # flexibility.
14076 my $odd_or_even = 2; # 1 = odd field count ok, 2 = want even count
14077
14078 if ( $identifier_count >= $item_count - 1
14079 || $is_assignment{$next_nonblank_type}
14080 || ( $list_type && $list_type ne '=>' && $list_type !~ /^[\:\?]$/ )
14081 )
14082 {
14083 $odd_or_even = 1;
14084 }
14085
14086 # do we have a long first term which should be
14087 # left on a line by itself?
14088 my $use_separate_first_term = (
14089 $odd_or_even == 1 # only if we can use 1 field/line
14090 && $item_count > 3 # need several items
14091 && $first_term_length >
14092 2 * $max_length[0] - 2 # need long first term
14093 && $first_term_length >
14094 2 * $max_length[1] - 2 # need long first term
14095 );
14096
14097 # or do we know from the type of list that the first term should
14098 # be placed alone?
14099 if ( !$use_separate_first_term ) {
14100 if ( $is_keyword_with_special_leading_term{$list_type} ) {
14101 $use_separate_first_term = 1;
14102
14103 # should the container be broken open?
14104 if ( $item_count < 3 ) {
14105 if ( $i_first_comma - $i_opening_paren < 4 ) {
14106 ${$rdo_not_break_apart} = 1;
14107 }
14108 }
14109 elsif ($first_term_length < 20
14110 && $i_first_comma - $i_opening_paren < 4 )
14111 {
14112 my $columns = table_columns_available($i_first_comma);
14113 if ( $first_term_length < $columns ) {
14114 ${$rdo_not_break_apart} = 1;
14115 }
14116 }
14117 }
14118 }
14119
14120 # if so,
14121 if ($use_separate_first_term) {
14122
14123 # ..set a break and update starting values
14124 $use_separate_first_term = 1;
14125 set_forced_breakpoint($i_first_comma);
14126 $i_opening_paren = $i_first_comma;
14127 $i_first_comma = $rcomma_index->[1];
14128 $item_count--;
14129 return if $comma_count == 1;
14130 shift @item_lengths;
14131 shift @i_term_begin;
14132 shift @i_term_end;
14133 shift @i_term_comma;
14134 }
14135
14136 # if not, update the metrics to include the first term
14137 else {
14138 if ( $first_term_length > $max_length[0] ) {
14139 $max_length[0] = $first_term_length;
14140 }
14141 }
14142
14143 # Field width parameters
14144 my $pair_width = ( $max_length[0] + $max_length[1] );
14145 my $max_width =
14146 ( $max_length[0] > $max_length[1] ) ? $max_length[0] : $max_length[1];
14147
14148 # Number of free columns across the page width for laying out tables
14149 my $columns = table_columns_available($i_first_comma);
14150
14151 # Estimated maximum number of fields which fit this space
14152 # This will be our first guess
14153 my $number_of_fields_max =
14154 maximum_number_of_fields( $columns, $odd_or_even, $max_width,
14155 $pair_width );
14156 my $number_of_fields = $number_of_fields_max;
14157
14158 # Find the best-looking number of fields
14159 # and make this our second guess if possible
14160 my ( $number_of_fields_best, $ri_ragged_break_list,
14161 $new_identifier_count )
14162 = study_list_complexity( \@i_term_begin, \@i_term_end, \@item_lengths,
14163 $max_width );
14164
14165 if ( $number_of_fields_best != 0
14166 && $number_of_fields_best < $number_of_fields_max )
14167 {
14168 $number_of_fields = $number_of_fields_best;
14169 }
14170
14171 # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
14172 # If we are crowded and the -lp option is being used, try to
14173 # undo some indentation
14174 # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
14175 if (
14176 $rOpts_line_up_parentheses
14177 && (
14178 $number_of_fields == 0
14179 || ( $number_of_fields == 1
14180 && $number_of_fields != $number_of_fields_best )
14181 )
14182 )
14183 {
14184 my $available_spaces = get_available_spaces_to_go($i_first_comma);
14185 if ( $available_spaces > 0 ) {
14186
14187 my $spaces_wanted = $max_width - $columns; # for 1 field
14188
14189 if ( $number_of_fields_best == 0 ) {
14190 $number_of_fields_best =
14191 get_maximum_fields_wanted( \@item_lengths );
14192 }
14193
14194 if ( $number_of_fields_best != 1 ) {
14195 my $spaces_wanted_2 =
14196 1 + $pair_width - $columns; # for 2 fields
14197 if ( $available_spaces > $spaces_wanted_2 ) {
14198 $spaces_wanted = $spaces_wanted_2;
14199 }
14200 }
14201
14202 if ( $spaces_wanted > 0 ) {
14203 my $deleted_spaces =
14204 reduce_lp_indentation( $i_first_comma, $spaces_wanted );
14205
14206 # redo the math
14207 if ( $deleted_spaces > 0 ) {
14208 $columns = table_columns_available($i_first_comma);
14209 $number_of_fields_max =
14210 maximum_number_of_fields( $columns, $odd_or_even,
14211 $max_width, $pair_width );
14212 $number_of_fields = $number_of_fields_max;
14213
14214 if ( $number_of_fields_best == 1
14215 && $number_of_fields >= 1 )
14216 {
14217 $number_of_fields = $number_of_fields_best;
14218 }
14219 }
14220 }
14221 }
14222 }
14223
14224 # try for one column if two won't work
14225 if ( $number_of_fields <= 0 ) {
14226 $number_of_fields = int( $columns / $max_width );
14227 }
14228
14229 # The user can place an upper bound on the number of fields,
14230 # which can be useful for doing maintenance on tables
14231 if ( $rOpts_maximum_fields_per_table
14232 && $number_of_fields > $rOpts_maximum_fields_per_table )
14233 {
14234 $number_of_fields = $rOpts_maximum_fields_per_table;
14235 }
14236
14237 # How many columns (characters) and lines would this container take
14238 # if no additional whitespace were added?
14239 my $packed_columns = token_sequence_length( $i_opening_paren + 1,
14240 $i_effective_last_comma + 1 );
14241 if ( $columns <= 0 ) { $columns = 1 } # avoid divide by zero
14242 my $packed_lines = 1 + int( $packed_columns / $columns );
14243
14244 # are we an item contained in an outer list?
14245 my $in_hierarchical_list = $next_nonblank_type =~ /^[\}\,]$/;
14246
14247 if ( $number_of_fields <= 0 ) {
14248
14249# #---------------------------------------------------------------
14250# # We're in trouble. We can't find a single field width that works.
14251# # There is no simple answer here; we may have a single long list
14252# # item, or many.
14253# #---------------------------------------------------------------
14254#
14255# In many cases, it may be best to not force a break if there is just one
14256# comma, because the standard continuation break logic will do a better
14257# job without it.
14258#
14259# In the common case that all but one of the terms can fit
14260# on a single line, it may look better not to break open the
14261# containing parens. Consider, for example
14262#
14263# $color =
14264# join ( '/',
14265# sort { $color_value{$::a} <=> $color_value{$::b}; }
14266# keys %colors );
14267#
14268# which will look like this with the container broken:
14269#
14270# $color = join (
14271# '/',
14272# sort { $color_value{$::a} <=> $color_value{$::b}; } keys %colors
14273# );
14274#
14275# Here is an example of this rule for a long last term:
14276#
14277# log_message( 0, 256, 128,
14278# "Number of routes in adj-RIB-in to be considered: $peercount" );
14279#
14280# And here is an example with a long first term:
14281#
14282# $s = sprintf(
14283# "%2d wallclock secs (%$f usr %$f sys + %$f cusr %$f csys = %$f CPU)",
14284# $r, $pu, $ps, $cu, $cs, $tt
14285# )
14286# if $style eq 'all';
14287
14288 my $i_last_comma = $rcomma_index->[ $comma_count - 1 ];
14289 my $long_last_term = excess_line_length( 0, $i_last_comma ) <= 0;
14290 my $long_first_term =
14291 excess_line_length( $i_first_comma + 1, $max_index_to_go ) <= 0;
14292
14293 # break at every comma ...
14294 if (
14295
14296 # if requested by user or is best looking
14297 $number_of_fields_best == 1
14298
14299 # or if this is a sublist of a larger list
14300 || $in_hierarchical_list
14301
14302 # or if multiple commas and we don't have a long first or last
14303 # term
14304 || ( $comma_count > 1
14305 && !( $long_last_term || $long_first_term ) )
14306 )
14307 {
14308 foreach ( 0 .. $comma_count - 1 ) {
14309 set_forced_breakpoint( $rcomma_index->[$_] );
14310 }
14311 }
14312 elsif ($long_last_term) {
14313
14314 set_forced_breakpoint($i_last_comma);
14315 ${$rdo_not_break_apart} = 1 unless $must_break_open;
14316 }
14317 elsif ($long_first_term) {
14318
14319 set_forced_breakpoint($i_first_comma);
14320 }
14321 else {
14322
14323 # let breaks be defined by default bond strength logic
14324 }
14325 return;
14326 }
14327
14328 # --------------------------------------------------------
14329 # We have a tentative field count that seems to work.
14330 # How many lines will this require?
14331 # --------------------------------------------------------
14332 my $formatted_lines = $item_count / ($number_of_fields);
14333 if ( $formatted_lines != int $formatted_lines ) {
14334 $formatted_lines = 1 + int $formatted_lines;
14335 }
14336
14337 # So far we've been trying to fill out to the right margin. But
14338 # compact tables are easier to read, so let's see if we can use fewer
14339 # fields without increasing the number of lines.
14340 $number_of_fields =
14341 compactify_table( $item_count, $number_of_fields, $formatted_lines,
14342 $odd_or_even );
14343
14344 # How many spaces across the page will we fill?
14345 my $columns_per_line =
14346 ( int $number_of_fields / 2 ) * $pair_width +
14347 ( $number_of_fields % 2 ) * $max_width;
14348
14349 my $formatted_columns;
14350
14351 if ( $number_of_fields > 1 ) {
14352 $formatted_columns =
14353 ( $pair_width * ( int( $item_count / 2 ) ) +
14354 ( $item_count % 2 ) * $max_width );
14355 }
14356 else {
14357 $formatted_columns = $max_width * $item_count;
14358 }
14359 if ( $formatted_columns < $packed_columns ) {
14360 $formatted_columns = $packed_columns;
14361 }
14362
14363 my $unused_columns = $formatted_columns - $packed_columns;
14364
14365 # set some empirical parameters to help decide if we should try to
14366 # align; high sparsity does not look good, especially with few lines
14367 my $sparsity = ($unused_columns) / ($formatted_columns);
14368 my $max_allowed_sparsity =
14369 ( $item_count < 3 ) ? 0.1
14370 : ( $packed_lines == 1 ) ? 0.15
14371 : ( $packed_lines == 2 ) ? 0.4
14372 : 0.7;
14373
14374 # Begin check for shortcut methods, which avoid treating a list
14375 # as a table for relatively small parenthesized lists. These
14376 # are usually easier to read if not formatted as tables.
14377 if (
14378 $packed_lines <= 2 # probably can fit in 2 lines
14379 && $item_count < 9 # doesn't have too many items
14380 && $opening_environment eq 'BLOCK' # not a sub-container
14381 && $opening_token eq '(' # is paren list
14382 )
14383 {
14384
14385 # Shortcut method 1: for -lp and just one comma:
14386 # This is a no-brainer, just break at the comma.
14387 if (
14388 $rOpts_line_up_parentheses # -lp
14389 && $item_count == 2 # two items, one comma
14390 && !$must_break_open
14391 )
14392 {
14393 my $i_break = $rcomma_index->[0];
14394 set_forced_breakpoint($i_break);
14395 ${$rdo_not_break_apart} = 1;
14396 set_non_alignment_flags( $comma_count, $rcomma_index );
14397 return;
14398
14399 }
14400
14401 # method 2 is for most small ragged lists which might look
14402 # best if not displayed as a table.
14403 if (
14404 ( $number_of_fields == 2 && $item_count == 3 )
14405 || (
14406 $new_identifier_count > 0 # isn't all quotes
14407 && $sparsity > 0.15
14408 ) # would be fairly spaced gaps if aligned
14409 )
14410 {
14411
14412 my $break_count = set_ragged_breakpoints( \@i_term_comma,
14413 $ri_ragged_break_list );
14414 ++$break_count if ($use_separate_first_term);
14415
14416 # NOTE: we should really use the true break count here,
14417 # which can be greater if there are large terms and
14418 # little space, but usually this will work well enough.
14419 unless ($must_break_open) {
14420
14421 if ( $break_count <= 1 ) {
14422 ${$rdo_not_break_apart} = 1;
14423 }
14424 elsif ( $rOpts_line_up_parentheses && !$need_lp_break_open )
14425 {
14426 ${$rdo_not_break_apart} = 1;
14427 }
14428 }
14429 set_non_alignment_flags( $comma_count, $rcomma_index );
14430 return;
14431 }
14432
14433 } # end shortcut methods
14434
14435 # debug stuff
14436
14437 FORMATTER_DEBUG_FLAG_SPARSE && do {
14438 print STDOUT
14439"SPARSE:cols=$columns commas=$comma_count items:$item_count ids=$identifier_count pairwidth=$pair_width fields=$number_of_fields lines packed: $packed_lines packed_cols=$packed_columns fmtd:$formatted_lines cols /line:$columns_per_line unused:$unused_columns fmtd:$formatted_columns sparsity=$sparsity allow=$max_allowed_sparsity\n";
14440
14441 };
14442
14443 #---------------------------------------------------------------
14444 # Compound List Rule 2:
14445 # If this list is too long for one line, and it is an item of a
14446 # larger list, then we must format it, regardless of sparsity
14447 # (ian.t). One reason that we have to do this is to trigger
14448 # Compound List Rule 1, above, which causes breaks at all commas of
14449 # all outer lists. In this way, the structure will be properly
14450 # displayed.
14451 #---------------------------------------------------------------
14452
14453 # Decide if this list is too long for one line unless broken
14454 my $total_columns = table_columns_available($i_opening_paren);
14455 my $too_long = $packed_columns > $total_columns;
14456
14457 # For a paren list, include the length of the token just before the
14458 # '(' because this is likely a sub call, and we would have to
14459 # include the sub name on the same line as the list. This is still
14460 # imprecise, but not too bad. (steve.t)
14461 if ( !$too_long && $i_opening_paren > 0 && $opening_token eq '(' ) {
14462
14463 $too_long = excess_line_length( $i_opening_minus,
14464 $i_effective_last_comma + 1 ) > 0;
14465 }
14466
14467 # FIXME: For an item after a '=>', try to include the length of the
14468 # thing before the '=>'. This is crude and should be improved by
14469 # actually looking back token by token.
14470 if ( !$too_long && $i_opening_paren > 0 && $list_type eq '=>' ) {
14471 my $i_opening_minus = $i_opening_paren - 4;
14472 if ( $i_opening_minus >= 0 ) {
14473 $too_long = excess_line_length( $i_opening_minus,
14474 $i_effective_last_comma + 1 ) > 0;
14475 }
14476 }
14477
14478 # Always break lists contained in '[' and '{' if too long for 1 line,
14479 # and always break lists which are too long and part of a more complex
14480 # structure.
14481 my $must_break_open_container = $must_break_open
14482 || ( $too_long
14483 && ( $in_hierarchical_list || $opening_token ne '(' ) );
14484
14485#print "LISTX: next=$next_nonblank_type avail cols=$columns packed=$packed_columns must format = $must_break_open_container too-long=$too_long opening=$opening_token list_type=$list_type formatted_lines=$formatted_lines packed=$packed_lines max_sparsity= $max_allowed_sparsity sparsity=$sparsity \n";
14486
14487 #---------------------------------------------------------------
14488 # The main decision:
14489 # Now decide if we will align the data into aligned columns. Do not
14490 # attempt to align columns if this is a tiny table or it would be
14491 # too spaced. It seems that the more packed lines we have, the
14492 # sparser the list that can be allowed and still look ok.
14493 #---------------------------------------------------------------
14494
14495 if ( ( $formatted_lines < 3 && $packed_lines < $formatted_lines )
14496 || ( $formatted_lines < 2 )
14497 || ( $unused_columns > $max_allowed_sparsity * $formatted_columns )
14498 )
14499 {
14500
14501 #---------------------------------------------------------------
14502 # too sparse: would look ugly if aligned in a table;
14503 #---------------------------------------------------------------
14504
14505 # use old breakpoints if this is a 'big' list
14506 # FIXME: goal is to improve set_ragged_breakpoints so that
14507 # this is not necessary.
14508 if ( $packed_lines > 2 && $item_count > 10 ) {
14509 write_logfile_entry("List sparse: using old breakpoints\n");
14510 copy_old_breakpoints( $i_first_comma, $i_last_comma );
14511 }
14512
14513 # let the continuation logic handle it if 2 lines
14514 else {
14515
14516 my $break_count = set_ragged_breakpoints( \@i_term_comma,
14517 $ri_ragged_break_list );
14518 ++$break_count if ($use_separate_first_term);
14519
14520 unless ($must_break_open_container) {
14521 if ( $break_count <= 1 ) {
14522 ${$rdo_not_break_apart} = 1;
14523 }
14524 elsif ( $rOpts_line_up_parentheses && !$need_lp_break_open )
14525 {
14526 ${$rdo_not_break_apart} = 1;
14527 }
14528 }
14529 set_non_alignment_flags( $comma_count, $rcomma_index );
14530 }
14531 return;
14532 }
14533
14534 #---------------------------------------------------------------
14535 # go ahead and format as a table
14536 #---------------------------------------------------------------
14537 write_logfile_entry(
14538 "List: auto formatting with $number_of_fields fields/row\n");
14539
14540 my $j_first_break =
14541 $use_separate_first_term ? $number_of_fields : $number_of_fields - 1;
14542
14543 for (
14544 my $j = $j_first_break ;
14545 $j < $comma_count ;
14546 $j += $number_of_fields
14547 )
14548 {
14549 my $i = $rcomma_index->[$j];
14550 set_forced_breakpoint($i);
14551 }
14552 return;
14553 }
14554}
14555
145561100nssub set_non_alignment_flags {
14557
14558 # set flag which indicates that these commas should not be
14559 # aligned
14560 my ( $comma_count, $rcomma_index ) = @_;
14561 foreach ( 0 .. $comma_count - 1 ) {
14562 $matching_token_to_go[ $rcomma_index->[$_] ] = 1;
14563 }
14564 return;
14565}
14566
14567sub study_list_complexity {
14568
14569 # Look for complex tables which should be formatted with one term per line.
14570 # Returns the following:
14571 #
14572 # \@i_ragged_break_list = list of good breakpoints to avoid lines
14573 # which are hard to read
14574 # $number_of_fields_best = suggested number of fields based on
14575 # complexity; = 0 if any number may be used.
14576 #
14577 my ( $ri_term_begin, $ri_term_end, $ritem_lengths, $max_width ) = @_;
14578 my $item_count = @{$ri_term_begin};
14579 my $complex_item_count = 0;
14580 my $number_of_fields_best = $rOpts_maximum_fields_per_table;
14581 my $i_max = @{$ritem_lengths} - 1;
14582 ##my @item_complexity;
14583
14584 my $i_last_last_break = -3;
14585 my $i_last_break = -2;
14586 my @i_ragged_break_list;
14587
14588 my $definitely_complex = 30;
14589 my $definitely_simple = 12;
14590 my $quote_count = 0;
14591
14592 for my $i ( 0 .. $i_max ) {
14593 my $ib = $ri_term_begin->[$i];
14594 my $ie = $ri_term_end->[$i];
14595
14596 # define complexity: start with the actual term length
14597 my $weighted_length = ( $ritem_lengths->[$i] - 2 );
14598
14599 ##TBD: join types here and check for variations
14600 ##my $str=join "", @tokens_to_go[$ib..$ie];
14601
14602 my $is_quote = 0;
14603 if ( $types_to_go[$ib] =~ /^[qQ]$/ ) {
14604 $is_quote = 1;
14605 $quote_count++;
14606 }
14607 elsif ( $types_to_go[$ib] =~ /^[w\-]$/ ) {
14608 $quote_count++;
14609 }
14610
14611 if ( $ib eq $ie ) {
14612 if ( $is_quote && $tokens_to_go[$ib] =~ /\s/ ) {
14613 $complex_item_count++;
14614 $weighted_length *= 2;
14615 }
14616 else {
14617 }
14618 }
14619 else {
14620 if ( grep { $_ eq 'b' } @types_to_go[ $ib .. $ie ] ) {
14621 $complex_item_count++;
14622 $weighted_length *= 2;
14623 }
14624 if ( grep { $_ eq '..' } @types_to_go[ $ib .. $ie ] ) {
14625 $weighted_length += 4;
14626 }
14627 }
14628
14629 # add weight for extra tokens.
14630 $weighted_length += 2 * ( $ie - $ib );
14631
14632## my $BUB = join '', @tokens_to_go[$ib..$ie];
14633## print "# COMPLEXITY:$weighted_length $BUB\n";
14634
14635##push @item_complexity, $weighted_length;
14636
14637 # now mark a ragged break after this item it if it is 'long and
14638 # complex':
14639 if ( $weighted_length >= $definitely_complex ) {
14640
14641 # if we broke after the previous term
14642 # then break before it too
14643 if ( $i_last_break == $i - 1
14644 && $i > 1
14645 && $i_last_last_break != $i - 2 )
14646 {
14647
14648 ## FIXME: don't strand a small term
14649 pop @i_ragged_break_list;
14650 push @i_ragged_break_list, $i - 2;
14651 push @i_ragged_break_list, $i - 1;
14652 }
14653
14654 push @i_ragged_break_list, $i;
14655 $i_last_last_break = $i_last_break;
14656 $i_last_break = $i;
14657 }
14658
14659 # don't break before a small last term -- it will
14660 # not look good on a line by itself.
14661 elsif ($i == $i_max
14662 && $i_last_break == $i - 1
14663 && $weighted_length <= $definitely_simple )
14664 {
14665 pop @i_ragged_break_list;
14666 }
14667 }
14668
14669 my $identifier_count = $i_max + 1 - $quote_count;
14670
14671 # Need more tuning here..
14672 if ( $max_width > 12
14673 && $complex_item_count > $item_count / 2
14674 && $number_of_fields_best != 2 )
14675 {
14676 $number_of_fields_best = 1;
14677 }
14678
14679 return ( $number_of_fields_best, \@i_ragged_break_list, $identifier_count );
14680}

14682sub get_maximum_fields_wanted {
14683
14684 # Not all tables look good with more than one field of items.
14685 # This routine looks at a table and decides if it should be
14686 # formatted with just one field or not.
14687 # This coding is still under development.
14688 my ($ritem_lengths) = @_;
14689
14690 my $number_of_fields_best = 0;
14691
14692 # For just a few items, we tentatively assume just 1 field.
14693 my $item_count = @{$ritem_lengths};
14694 if ( $item_count <= 5 ) {
14695 $number_of_fields_best = 1;
14696 }
14697
14698 # For larger tables, look at it both ways and see what looks best
14699 else {
14700
14701 my $is_odd = 1;
14702 my @max_length = ( 0, 0 );
14703 my @last_length_2 = ( undef, undef );
14704 my @first_length_2 = ( undef, undef );
14705 my $last_length = undef;
14706 my $total_variation_1 = 0;
14707 my $total_variation_2 = 0;
14708 my @total_variation_2 = ( 0, 0 );
14709
14710 foreach my $j ( 0 .. $item_count - 1 ) {
14711
14712 $is_odd = 1 - $is_odd;
14713 my $length = $ritem_lengths->[$j];
14714 if ( $length > $max_length[$is_odd] ) {
14715 $max_length[$is_odd] = $length;
14716 }
14717
14718 if ( defined($last_length) ) {
14719 my $dl = abs( $length - $last_length );
14720 $total_variation_1 += $dl;
14721 }
14722 $last_length = $length;
14723
14724 my $ll = $last_length_2[$is_odd];
14725 if ( defined($ll) ) {
14726 my $dl = abs( $length - $ll );
14727 $total_variation_2[$is_odd] += $dl;
14728 }
14729 else {
14730 $first_length_2[$is_odd] = $length;
14731 }
14732 $last_length_2[$is_odd] = $length;
14733 }
14734 $total_variation_2 = $total_variation_2[0] + $total_variation_2[1];
14735
14736 my $factor = ( $item_count > 10 ) ? 1 : ( $item_count > 5 ) ? 0.75 : 0;
14737 unless ( $total_variation_2 < $factor * $total_variation_1 ) {
14738 $number_of_fields_best = 1;
14739 }
14740 }
14741 return ($number_of_fields_best);
14742}

14744sub table_columns_available {

14748 leading_spaces_to_go($i_first_comma);
14749

14751 # exactly equal the available line length because of allowances
14752 # that must be made for side comments. Therefore, the number of
14753 # available columns is reduced by 1 character.
14754 $columns -= 1;

14758sub maximum_number_of_fields {
14759
14760 # how many fields will fit in the available space?
14761 my ( $columns, $odd_or_even, $max_width, $pair_width ) = @_;
14762 my $max_pairs = int( $columns / $pair_width );
14763 my $number_of_fields = $max_pairs * 2;
14764 if ( $odd_or_even == 1
14765 && $max_pairs * $pair_width + $max_width <= $columns )
14766 {
14767 $number_of_fields++;
14768 }
14769 return $number_of_fields;
14770}

14772sub compactify_table {
14773
14774 # given a table with a certain number of fields and a certain number
14775 # of lines, see if reducing the number of fields will make it look
14776 # better.
14777 my ( $item_count, $number_of_fields, $formatted_lines, $odd_or_even ) = @_;
14778 if ( $number_of_fields >= $odd_or_even * 2 && $formatted_lines > 0 ) {
14779 my $min_fields;
14780
14781 for (
14782 $min_fields = $number_of_fields ;
14783 $min_fields >= $odd_or_even
14784 && $min_fields * $formatted_lines >= $item_count ;
14785 $min_fields -= $odd_or_even
14786 )
14787 {
14788 $number_of_fields = $min_fields;
14789 }
14790 }
14791 return $number_of_fields;
14792}

14854sub set_forced_breakpoint {
14855 my $i = shift;
14856
14857 return unless defined $i && $i >= 0;
14858
14859 # no breaks between welded tokens
14860 return if ( weld_len_right_to_go($i) );
14861
14862 # when called with certain tokens, use bond strengths to decide
14863 # if we break before or after it
14864 my $token = $tokens_to_go[$i];
14865
14866 if ( $token =~ /^([\=\.\,\:\?]|and|or|xor|&&|\|\|)$/ ) {
14867 if ( $want_break_before{$token} && $i >= 0 ) { $i-- }
14868 }
14869
14870 # breaks are forced before 'if' and 'unless'
14871 elsif ( $is_if_unless{$token} ) { $i-- }
14872
14873 if ( $i >= 0 && $i <= $max_index_to_go ) {
14874 my $i_nonblank = ( $types_to_go[$i] ne 'b' ) ? $i : $i - 1;
14875
14876 FORMATTER_DEBUG_FLAG_FORCE && do {
14877 my ( $a, $b, $c ) = caller();
14878 print STDOUT
14879"FORCE $forced_breakpoint_count from $a $c with i=$i_nonblank max=$max_index_to_go tok=$tokens_to_go[$i_nonblank] type=$types_to_go[$i_nonblank] nobr=$nobreak_to_go[$i_nonblank]\n";
14880 };
14881
14882 if ( $i_nonblank >= 0 && $nobreak_to_go[$i_nonblank] == 0 ) {
14883 $forced_breakpoint_to_go[$i_nonblank] = 1;
14884
14885 if ( $i_nonblank > $index_max_forced_break ) {
14886 $index_max_forced_break = $i_nonblank;
14887 }
14888 $forced_breakpoint_count++;
14889 $forced_breakpoint_undo_stack[ $forced_breakpoint_undo_count++ ] =
14890 $i_nonblank;
14891
14892 # if we break at an opening container..break at the closing
14893 if ( $tokens_to_go[$i_nonblank] =~ /^[\{\[\(\?]$/ ) {
14894 set_closing_breakpoint($i_nonblank);
14895 }
14896 }
14897 }
14898 return;
14899}

14991 sub delete_one_line_semicolons {
14992
14993 my ( $self, $ri_beg, $ri_end ) = @_;
14994 my $rLL = $self->{rLL};
14995 my $K_opening_container = $self->{K_opening_container};
14996
14997 # Walk down the lines of this batch and delete any semicolons
14998 # terminating one-line blocks;
14999 my $nmax = @{$ri_end} - 1;
15000
15001 foreach my $n ( 0 .. $nmax ) {
15002 my $i_beg = $ri_beg->[$n];
15003 my $i_e = $ri_end->[$n];
15004 my $K_beg = $K_to_go[$i_beg];
15005 my $K_e = $K_to_go[$i_e];
15006 my $K_end = $K_e;
15007 my $type_end = $rLL->[$K_end]->[_TYPE_];
15008 if ( $type_end eq '#' ) {
15009 $K_end = $self->K_previous_nonblank($K_end);
15010 if ( defined($K_end) ) { $type_end = $rLL->[$K_end]->[_TYPE_]; }
15011 }
15012
15013 # we are looking for a line ending in closing brace
15014 next
15015 unless ( $type_end eq '}' && $rLL->[$K_end]->[_TOKEN_] eq '}' );
15016
15017 # ...and preceded by a semicolon on the same line
15018 my $K_semicolon = $self->K_previous_nonblank($K_end);
15019 my $i_semicolon = $i_beg + ( $K_semicolon - $K_beg );
15020 next if ( $i_semicolon <= $i_beg );
15021 next unless ( $rLL->[$K_semicolon]->[_TYPE_] eq ';' );
15022
15023 # safety check - shouldn't happen
15024 if ( $types_to_go[$i_semicolon] ne ';' ) {
15025 Fault("unexpected type looking for semicolon, ignoring");
15026 next;
15027 }
15028
15029 # ... with the corresponding opening brace on the same line
15030 my $type_sequence = $rLL->[$K_end]->[_TYPE_SEQUENCE_];
15031 my $K_opening = $K_opening_container->{$type_sequence};
15032 my $i_opening = $i_beg + ( $K_opening - $K_beg );
15033 next if ( $i_opening < $i_beg );
15034
15035 # ... and only one semicolon between these braces
15036 my $semicolon_count = 0;
15037 foreach my $K ( $K_opening + 1 .. $K_semicolon - 1 ) {
15038 if ( $rLL->[$K]->[_TYPE_] eq ';' ) {
15039 $semicolon_count++;
15040 last;
15041 }
15042 }
15043 next if ($semicolon_count);
15044
15045 # ...ok, then make the semicolon invisible
15046 $tokens_to_go[$i_semicolon] = "";
15047 }
15048 return;
15049 }

15074 sub recombine_breakpoints {
15075
15076 # sub set_continuation_breaks is very liberal in setting line breaks
15077 # for long lines, always setting breaks at good breakpoints, even
15078 # when that creates small lines. Sometimes small line fragments
15079 # are produced which would look better if they were combined.
15080 # That's the task of this routine.
15081 #
15082 # We are given indexes to the current lines:
15083 # $ri_beg = ref to array of BEGinning indexes of each line
15084 # $ri_end = ref to array of ENDing indexes of each line
15085 my ( $ri_beg, $ri_end ) = @_;
15086
15087 # Make a list of all good joining tokens between the lines
15088 # n-1 and n.
15089 my @joint;
15090 my $nmax = @{$ri_end} - 1;
15091 for my $n ( 1 .. $nmax ) {
15092 my $ibeg_1 = $ri_beg->[ $n - 1 ];
15093 my $iend_1 = $ri_end->[ $n - 1 ];
15094 my $iend_2 = $ri_end->[$n];
15095 my $ibeg_2 = $ri_beg->[$n];
15096
15097 my ( $itok, $itokp, $itokm );
15098
15099 foreach my $itest ( $iend_1, $ibeg_2 ) {
15100 my $type = $types_to_go[$itest];
15101 if ( $is_math_op{$type}
15102 || $is_amp_amp{$type}
15103 || $is_assignment{$type}
15104 || $type eq ':' )
15105 {
15106 $itok = $itest;
15107 }
15108 }
15109 $joint[$n] = [$itok];
15110 }
15111
15112 my $more_to_do = 1;
15113
15114 # We keep looping over all of the lines of this batch
15115 # until there are no more possible recombinations
15116 my $nmax_last = @{$ri_end};
15117 my $reverse = 0;
15118 while ($more_to_do) {
15119 my $n_best = 0;
15120 my $bs_best;
15121 my $nmax = @{$ri_end} - 1;
15122
15123 # Safety check for infinite loop
15124 unless ( $nmax < $nmax_last ) {
15125
15126 # Shouldn't happen because splice below decreases nmax on each
15127 # pass.
15128 Fault("Program bug-infinite loop in recombine breakpoints\n");
15129 }
15130 $nmax_last = $nmax;
15131 $more_to_do = 0;
15132 my $skip_Section_3;
15133 my $leading_amp_count = 0;
15134 my $this_line_is_semicolon_terminated;
15135
15136 # loop over all remaining lines in this batch
15137 for my $iter ( 1 .. $nmax ) {
15138
15139 # alternating sweep direction gives symmetric results
15140 # for recombining lines which exceed the line length
15141 # such as eval {{{{.... }}}}
15142 my $n;
15143 if ($reverse) { $n = 1 + $nmax - $iter; }
15144 else { $n = $iter }
15145
15146 #----------------------------------------------------------
15147 # If we join the current pair of lines,
15148 # line $n-1 will become the left part of the joined line
15149 # line $n will become the right part of the joined line
15150 #
15151 # Here are Indexes of the endpoint tokens of the two lines:
15152 #
15153 # -----line $n-1--- | -----line $n-----
15154 # $ibeg_1 $iend_1 | $ibeg_2 $iend_2
15155 # ^
15156 # |
15157 # We want to decide if we should remove the line break
15158 # between the tokens at $iend_1 and $ibeg_2
15159 #
15160 # We will apply a number of ad-hoc tests to see if joining
15161 # here will look ok. The code will just issue a 'next'
15162 # command if the join doesn't look good. If we get through
15163 # the gauntlet of tests, the lines will be recombined.
15164 #----------------------------------------------------------
15165 #
15166 # beginning and ending tokens of the lines we are working on
15167 my $ibeg_1 = $ri_beg->[ $n - 1 ];
15168 my $iend_1 = $ri_end->[ $n - 1 ];
15169 my $iend_2 = $ri_end->[$n];
15170 my $ibeg_2 = $ri_beg->[$n];
15171 my $ibeg_nmax = $ri_beg->[$nmax];
15172
15173 # combined line cannot be too long
15174 my $excess = excess_line_length( $ibeg_1, $iend_2, 1, 1 );
15175 next if ( $excess > 0 );
15176
15177 my $type_iend_1 = $types_to_go[$iend_1];
15178 my $type_iend_2 = $types_to_go[$iend_2];
15179 my $type_ibeg_1 = $types_to_go[$ibeg_1];
15180 my $type_ibeg_2 = $types_to_go[$ibeg_2];
15181
15182 # terminal token of line 2 if any side comment is ignored:
15183 my $iend_2t = $iend_2;
15184 my $type_iend_2t = $type_iend_2;
15185
15186 # some beginning indexes of other lines, which may not exist
15187 my $ibeg_0 = $n > 1 ? $ri_beg->[ $n - 2 ] : -1;
15188 my $ibeg_3 = $n < $nmax ? $ri_beg->[ $n + 1 ] : -1;
15189 my $ibeg_4 = $n + 2 <= $nmax ? $ri_beg->[ $n + 2 ] : -1;
15190
15191 my $bs_tweak = 0;
15192
15193 #my $depth_increase=( $nesting_depth_to_go[$ibeg_2] -
15194 # $nesting_depth_to_go[$ibeg_1] );
15195
15196 FORMATTER_DEBUG_FLAG_RECOMBINE && do {
15197 print STDERR
15198"RECOMBINE: n=$n imid=$iend_1 if=$ibeg_1 type=$type_ibeg_1 =$tokens_to_go[$ibeg_1] next_type=$type_ibeg_2 next_tok=$tokens_to_go[$ibeg_2]\n";
15199 };
15200
15201 # If line $n is the last line, we set some flags and
15202 # do any special checks for it
15203 if ( $n == $nmax ) {
15204
15205 # a terminal '{' should stay where it is
15206 # unless preceded by a fat comma
15207 next if ( $type_ibeg_2 eq '{' && $type_iend_1 ne '=>' );
15208
15209 if ( $type_iend_2 eq '#'
15210 && $iend_2 - $ibeg_2 >= 2
15211 && $types_to_go[ $iend_2 - 1 ] eq 'b' )
15212 {
15213 $iend_2t = $iend_2 - 2;
15214 $type_iend_2t = $types_to_go[$iend_2t];
15215 }
15216
15217 $this_line_is_semicolon_terminated = $type_iend_2t eq ';';
15218 }
15219
15220 #----------------------------------------------------------
15221 # Recombine Section 0:
15222 # Examine the special token joining this line pair, if any.
15223 # Put as many tests in this section to avoid duplicate code and
15224 # to make formatting independent of whether breaks are to the
15225 # left or right of an operator.
15226 #----------------------------------------------------------
15227
15228 my ($itok) = @{ $joint[$n] };
15229 if ($itok) {
15230
15231 # FIXME: Patch - may not be necessary
15232 my $iend_1 =
15233 $type_iend_1 eq 'b'
15234 ? $iend_1 - 1
15235 : $iend_1;
15236
15237 my $iend_2 =
15238 $type_iend_2 eq 'b'
15239 ? $iend_2 - 1
15240 : $iend_2;
15241 ## END PATCH
15242
15243 my $type = $types_to_go[$itok];

15918 #X: RT #81854
15919 $forced_breakpoint_to_go[$iend_1] = 0
15920 unless $old_breakpoint_to_go[$iend_1];
15921 }
15922
15923 # handle leading 'and'
15924 elsif ( $tokens_to_go[$ibeg_2] eq 'and' ) {
15925
15926 # Decide if we will combine a single terminal 'and'
15927 # after an 'if' or 'unless'.
15928
15929 # This looks best with the 'and' on the same
15930 # line as the 'if':
15931 #
15932 # $a = 1
15933 # if $seconds and $nu < 2;
15934 #
15935 # But this looks better as shown:
15936 #
15937 # $a = 1
15938 # if !$this->{Parents}{$_}
15939 # or $this->{Parents}{$_} eq $_;
15940 #
15941 next
15942 unless (
15943 $this_line_is_semicolon_terminated
15944 && (
15945
15946 # following 'if' or 'unless' or 'or'
15947 $type_ibeg_1 eq 'k'
15948 && ( $is_if_unless{ $tokens_to_go[$ibeg_1] }
15949 || $tokens_to_go[$ibeg_1] eq 'or' )
15950 )
15951 );
15952 }
15953
15954 # handle leading "if" and "unless"
15955 elsif ( $is_if_unless{ $tokens_to_go[$ibeg_2] } ) {
15956
15957 # FIXME: This is still experimental..may not be too useful
15958 next
15959 unless (
15960 $this_line_is_semicolon_terminated
15961
15962 # previous line begins with 'and' or 'or'
15963 && $type_ibeg_1 eq 'k'
15964 && $is_and_or{ $tokens_to_go[$ibeg_1] }
15965
15966 );
15967 }
15968
15969 # handle all other leading keywords
15970 else {
15971
15972 # keywords look best at start of lines,
15973 # but combine things like "1 while"
15974 unless ( $is_assignment{$type_iend_1} ) {
15975 next
15976 if ( ( $type_iend_1 ne 'k' )
15977 && ( $tokens_to_go[$ibeg_2] ne 'while' ) );
15978 }
15979 }
15980 }
15981
15982 # similar treatment of && and || as above for 'and' and 'or':
15983 # NOTE: This block of code is currently bypassed because
15984 # of a previous block but is retained for possible future use.
15985 elsif ( $is_amp_amp{$type_ibeg_2} ) {
15986
15987 # maybe looking at something like:
15988 # unless $TEXTONLY || $item =~ m%</?(hr>|p>|a|img)%i;
15989
15990 next
15991 unless (
15992 $this_line_is_semicolon_terminated
15993
15994 # previous line begins with an 'if' or 'unless' keyword
15995 && $type_ibeg_1 eq 'k'
15996 && $is_if_unless{ $tokens_to_go[$ibeg_1] }
15997
15998 );
15999 }
16000
16001 # handle line with leading = or similar
16002 elsif ( $is_assignment{$type_ibeg_2} ) {
16003 next unless ( $n == 1 || $n == $nmax );
16004 next if $old_breakpoint_to_go[$iend_1];
16005 next
16006 unless (
16007
16008 # unless we can reduce this to two lines
16009 $nmax == 2
16010
16011 # or three lines, the last with a leading semicolon
16012 || ( $nmax == 3 && $types_to_go[$ibeg_nmax] eq ';' )
16013
16014 # or the next line ends with a here doc
16015 || $type_iend_2 eq 'h'
16016
16017 # or this is a short line ending in ;
16018 || ( $n == $nmax && $this_line_is_semicolon_terminated )
16019 );
16020 $forced_breakpoint_to_go[$iend_1] = 0;
16021 }
16022
16023 #----------------------------------------------------------
16024 # Recombine Section 4:
16025 # Combine the lines if we arrive here and it is possible
16026 #----------------------------------------------------------
16027
16028 # honor hard breakpoints
16029 next if ( $forced_breakpoint_to_go[$iend_1] > 0 );
16030
16031 my $bs = $bond_strength_to_go[$iend_1] + $bs_tweak;
16032
16033 # Require a few extra spaces before recombining lines if we are
16034 # at an old breakpoint unless this is a simple list or terminal
16035 # line. The goal is to avoid oscillating between two
16036 # quasi-stable end states. For example this snippet caused
16037 # problems:
16038## my $this =
16039## bless {
16040## TText => "[" . ( join ',', map { "\"$_\"" } split "\n", $_ ) . "]"
16041## },
16042## $type;
16043 next
16044 if ( $old_breakpoint_to_go[$iend_1]
16045 && !$this_line_is_semicolon_terminated
16046 && $n < $nmax
16047 && $excess + 4 > 0
16048 && $type_iend_2 ne ',' );
16049
16050 # do not recombine if we would skip in indentation levels
16051 if ( $n < $nmax ) {
16052 my $if_next = $ri_beg->[ $n + 1 ];
16053 next
16054 if (
16055 $levels_to_go[$ibeg_1] < $levels_to_go[$ibeg_2]
16056 && $levels_to_go[$ibeg_2] < $levels_to_go[$if_next]
16057
16058 # but an isolated 'if (' is undesirable
16059 && !(
16060 $n == 1
16061 && $iend_1 - $ibeg_1 <= 2
16062 && $type_ibeg_1 eq 'k'
16063 && $tokens_to_go[$ibeg_1] eq 'if'
16064 && $tokens_to_go[$iend_1] ne '('
16065 )
16066 );
16067 }
16068
16069 # honor no-break's
16070 next if ( $bs >= NO_BREAK - 1 );
16071
16072 # remember the pair with the greatest bond strength
16073 if ( !$n_best ) {
16074 $n_best = $n;
16075 $bs_best = $bs;
16076 }
16077 else {
16078
16079 if ( $bs > $bs_best ) {
16080 $n_best = $n;
16081 $bs_best = $bs;
16082 }
16083 }
16084 }
16085
16086 # recombine the pair with the greatest bond strength
16087 if ($n_best) {
16088 splice @{$ri_beg}, $n_best, 1;
16089 splice @{$ri_end}, $n_best - 1, 1;
16090 splice @joint, $n_best, 1;
16091
16092 # keep going if we are still making progress
16093 $more_to_do++;
16094 }
16095 }
16096 return ( $ri_beg, $ri_end );
16097 }
16098} # end recombine_breakpoints
16099
161001200nssub break_all_chain_tokens {
16101
16102 # scan the current breakpoints looking for breaks at certain "chain
16103 # operators" (. : && || + etc) which often occur repeatedly in a long
16104 # statement. If we see a break at any one, break at all similar tokens
16105 # within the same container.
16106 #
16107 my ( $ri_left, $ri_right ) = @_;
16108
16109 my %saw_chain_type;
16110 my %left_chain_type;
16111 my %right_chain_type;
16112 my %interior_chain_type;
16113 my $nmax = @{$ri_right} - 1;
16114
16115 # scan the left and right end tokens of all lines
16116 my $count = 0;
16117 for my $n ( 0 .. $nmax ) {
16118 my $il = $ri_left->[$n];
16119 my $ir = $ri_right->[$n];
16120 my $typel = $types_to_go[$il];
16121 my $typer = $types_to_go[$ir];
16122 $typel = '+' if ( $typel eq '-' ); # treat + and - the same
16123 $typer = '+' if ( $typer eq '-' );
16124 $typel = '*' if ( $typel eq '/' ); # treat * and / the same
16125 $typer = '*' if ( $typer eq '/' );
16126 my $tokenl = $tokens_to_go[$il];
16127 my $tokenr = $tokens_to_go[$ir];
16128
16129 if ( $is_chain_operator{$tokenl} && $want_break_before{$typel} ) {
16130 next if ( $typel eq '?' );
16131 push @{ $left_chain_type{$typel} }, $il;
16132 $saw_chain_type{$typel} = 1;
16133 $count++;
16134 }
16135 if ( $is_chain_operator{$tokenr} && !$want_break_before{$typer} ) {
16136 next if ( $typer eq '?' );
16137 push @{ $right_chain_type{$typer} }, $ir;
16138 $saw_chain_type{$typer} = 1;
16139 $count++;
16140 }
16141 }
16142 return unless $count;
16143
16144 # now look for any interior tokens of the same types
16145 $count = 0;
16146 for my $n ( 0 .. $nmax ) {
16147 my $il = $ri_left->[$n];
16148 my $ir = $ri_right->[$n];
16149 foreach my $i ( $il + 1 .. $ir - 1 ) {
16150 my $type = $types_to_go[$i];
16151 $type = '+' if ( $type eq '-' );
16152 $type = '*' if ( $type eq '/' );
16153 if ( $saw_chain_type{$type} ) {
16154 push @{ $interior_chain_type{$type} }, $i;
16155 $count++;
16156 }
16157 }
16158 }
16159 return unless $count;
16160
16161 # now make a list of all new break points
16162 my @insert_list;
16163
16164 # loop over all chain types
16165 foreach my $type ( keys %saw_chain_type ) {
16166
16167 # quit if just ONE continuation line with leading . For example--
16168 # print LATEXFILE '\framebox{\parbox[c][' . $h . '][t]{' . $w . '}{'
16169 # . $contents;
16170 last if ( $nmax == 1 && $type =~ /^[\.\+]$/ );
16171
16172 # loop over all interior chain tokens
16173 foreach my $itest ( @{ $interior_chain_type{$type} } ) {
16174
16175 # loop over all left end tokens of same type
16176 if ( $left_chain_type{$type} ) {
16177 next if $nobreak_to_go[ $itest - 1 ];
16178 foreach my $i ( @{ $left_chain_type{$type} } ) {
16179 next unless in_same_container( $i, $itest );
16180 push @insert_list, $itest - 1;
16181
16182 # Break at matching ? if this : is at a different level.
16183 # For example, the ? before $THRf_DEAD in the following
16184 # should get a break if its : gets a break.
16185 #
16186 # my $flags =
16187 # ( $_ & 1 ) ? ( $_ & 4 ) ? $THRf_DEAD : $THRf_ZOMBIE
16188 # : ( $_ & 4 ) ? $THRf_R_DETACHED
16189 # : $THRf_R_JOINABLE;
16190 if ( $type eq ':'
16191 && $levels_to_go[$i] != $levels_to_go[$itest] )
16192 {
16193 my $i_question = $mate_index_to_go[$itest];
16194 if ( $i_question > 0 ) {
16195 push @insert_list, $i_question - 1;
16196 }
16197 }
16198 last;
16199 }
16200 }
16201
16202 # loop over all right end tokens of same type
16203 if ( $right_chain_type{$type} ) {
16204 next if $nobreak_to_go[$itest];
16205 foreach my $i ( @{ $right_chain_type{$type} } ) {
16206 next unless in_same_container( $i, $itest );
16207 push @insert_list, $itest;
16208
16209 # break at matching ? if this : is at a different level
16210 if ( $type eq ':'
16211 && $levels_to_go[$i] != $levels_to_go[$itest] )
16212 {
16213 my $i_question = $mate_index_to_go[$itest];
16214 if ( $i_question >= 0 ) {
16215 push @insert_list, $i_question;
16216 }
16217 }
16218 last;
16219 }
16220 }
16221 }
16222 }
16223
16224 # insert any new break points
16225 if (@insert_list) {
16226 insert_additional_breaks( \@insert_list, $ri_left, $ri_right );
16227 }
16228 return;
16229}
