16231sub break_equals {
16232
16233 # Look for assignment operators that could use a breakpoint.
16234 # For example, in the following snippet
16235 #
16236 # $HOME = $ENV{HOME}
16237 # || $ENV{LOGDIR}
16238 # || $pw[7]
16239 # || die "no home directory for user $<";
16240 #
16241 # we could break at the = to get this, which is a little nicer:
16242 # $HOME =
16243 # $ENV{HOME}
16244 # || $ENV{LOGDIR}
16245 # || $pw[7]
16246 # || die "no home directory for user $<";
16247 #
16248 # The logic here follows the logic in set_logical_padding, which
16249 # will add the padding in the second line to improve alignment.
16250 #
16251 my ( $ri_left, $ri_right ) = @_;
16252 my $nmax = @{$ri_right} - 1;
16253 return unless ( $nmax >= 2 );
16254
16255 # scan the left ends of first two lines
16256 my $tokbeg = "";
16257 my $depth_beg;
16258 for my $n ( 1 .. 2 ) {
16259 my $il = $ri_left->[$n];
16260 my $typel = $types_to_go[$il];
16261 my $tokenl = $tokens_to_go[$il];
16262
16263 my $has_leading_op = ( $tokenl =~ /^\w/ )
16264 ? $is_chain_operator{$tokenl} # + - * / : ? && ||
16265 : $is_chain_operator{$typel}; # and, or
16266 return unless ($has_leading_op);
16267 if ( $n > 1 ) {
16268 return
16269 unless ( $tokenl eq $tokbeg
16270 && $nesting_depth_to_go[$il] eq $depth_beg );
16271 }
16272 $tokbeg = $tokenl;
16273 $depth_beg = $nesting_depth_to_go[$il];
16274 }
16275
16276 # now look for any interior tokens of the same types
16277 my $il = $ri_left->[0];
16278 my $ir = $ri_right->[0];
16279
16280 # now make a list of all new break points
16281 my @insert_list;
16282 for ( my $i = $ir - 1 ; $i > $il ; $i-- ) {
16283 my $type = $types_to_go[$i];
16284 if ( $is_assignment{$type}
16285 && $nesting_depth_to_go[$i] eq $depth_beg )
16286 {
16287 if ( $want_break_before{$type} ) {
16288 push @insert_list, $i - 1;
16289 }
16290 else {
16291 push @insert_list, $i;
16292 }
16293 }
16294 }
16295
16296 # Break after a 'return' followed by a chain of operators
16297 # return ( $^O !~ /win32|dos/i )
16298 # && ( $^O ne 'VMS' )
16299 # && ( $^O ne 'OS2' )
16300 # && ( $^O ne 'MacOS' );
16301 # To give:
16302 # return
16303 # ( $^O !~ /win32|dos/i )
16304 # && ( $^O ne 'VMS' )
16305 # && ( $^O ne 'OS2' )
16306 # && ( $^O ne 'MacOS' );
16307 my $i = 0;
16308 if ( $types_to_go[$i] eq 'k'
16309 && $tokens_to_go[$i] eq 'return'
16310 && $ir > $il
16311 && $nesting_depth_to_go[$i] eq $depth_beg )
16312 {
16313 push @insert_list, $i;
16314 }
16315
16316 return unless (@insert_list);
16317
16318 # One final check...
16319 # scan second and third lines and be sure there are no assignments
16320 # we want to avoid breaking at an = to make something like this:
16321 # unless ( $icon =
16322 # $html_icons{"$type-$state"}
16323 # or $icon = $html_icons{$type}
16324 # or $icon = $html_icons{$state} )
16325 for my $n ( 1 .. 2 ) {
16326 my $il = $ri_left->[$n];
16327 my $ir = $ri_right->[$n];
16328 foreach my $i ( $il + 1 .. $ir ) {
16329 my $type = $types_to_go[$i];
16330 return
16331 if ( $is_assignment{$type}
16332 && $nesting_depth_to_go[$i] eq $depth_beg );
16333 }
16334 }
16335
16336 # ok, insert any new break point
16337 if (@insert_list) {
16338 insert_additional_breaks( \@insert_list, $ri_left, $ri_right );
16339 }
16340 return;
16341}
16342
16343sub insert_final_breaks {
16344
16345 my ( $ri_left, $ri_right ) = @_;
16346
16347 my $nmax = @{$ri_right} - 1;
16348
16349 # scan the left and right end tokens of all lines
16350 my $count = 0;
16351 my $i_first_colon = -1;
16352 for my $n ( 0 .. $nmax ) {
16353 my $il = $ri_left->[$n];
16354 my $ir = $ri_right->[$n];
16355 my $typel = $types_to_go[$il];
16356 my $typer = $types_to_go[$ir];
16357 return if ( $typel eq '?' );
16358 return if ( $typer eq '?' );
16359 if ( $typel eq ':' ) { $i_first_colon = $il; last; }
16360 elsif ( $typer eq ':' ) { $i_first_colon = $ir; last; }
16361 }
16362
16363 # For long ternary chains,
16364 # if the first : we see has its # ? is in the interior
16365 # of a preceding line, then see if there are any good
16366 # breakpoints before the ?.
16367 if ( $i_first_colon > 0 ) {
16368 my $i_question = $mate_index_to_go[$i_first_colon];
16369 if ( $i_question > 0 ) {
16370 my @insert_list;
16371 for ( my $ii = $i_question - 1 ; $ii >= 0 ; $ii -= 1 ) {
16372 my $token = $tokens_to_go[$ii];
16373 my $type = $types_to_go[$ii];
16374
16375 # For now, a good break is either a comma or,
16376 # in a long chain, a 'return'.
16377 # Patch for RT #126633: added the $nmax>1 check to avoid
16378 # breaking after a return for a simple ternary. For longer
16379 # chains the break after return allows vertical alignment, so
16380 # it is still done. So perltidy -wba='?' will not break
16381 # immediately after the return in the following statement:
16382 # sub x {
16383 # return 0 ? 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa' :
16384 # 'bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb';
16385 # }
16386 if (
16387 (
16388 $type eq ','
16389 || $type eq 'k' && ( $nmax > 1 && $token eq 'return' )
16390 )
16391 && in_same_container( $ii, $i_question )
16392 )
16393 {
16394 push @insert_list, $ii;
16395 last;
16396 }
16397
16398## # For now, a good break is either a comma or a 'return'.
16399## if ( ( $type eq ',' || $type eq 'k' && $token eq 'return' )
16400## && in_same_container( $ii, $i_question ) )
16401## {
16402## push @insert_list, $ii;
16403## last;
16404## }
16405 }
16406
16407 # insert any new break points
16408 if (@insert_list) {
16409 insert_additional_breaks( \@insert_list, $ri_left, $ri_right );
16410 }
16411 }
16412 }
16413 return;
16414}
16415
16416sub in_same_container {
16417
16418 # check to see if tokens at i1 and i2 are in the
16419 # same container, and not separated by a comma, ? or :
16420 # FIXME: this can be written more efficiently now
16421 my ( $i1, $i2 ) = @_;
16422 my $type = $types_to_go[$i1];
16423 my $depth = $nesting_depth_to_go[$i1];
16424 return unless ( $nesting_depth_to_go[$i2] == $depth );
16425 if ( $i2 < $i1 ) { ( $i1, $i2 ) = ( $i2, $i1 ) }
16426
16427 ###########################################################
16428 # This is potentially a very slow routine and not critical.
16429 # For safety just give up for large differences.
16430 # See test file 'infinite_loop.txt'
16431 # TODO: replace this loop with a data structure
16432 ###########################################################
16433 return if ( $i2 - $i1 > 200 );
16434
16435 foreach my $i ( $i1 + 1 .. $i2 - 1 ) {
16436 next if ( $nesting_depth_to_go[$i] > $depth );
16437 return if ( $nesting_depth_to_go[$i] < $depth );
16438
16439 my $tok = $tokens_to_go[$i];
16440 $tok = ',' if $tok eq '=>'; # treat => same as ,
16441
16442 # Example: we would not want to break at any of these .'s
16443 # : "<A HREF=\"#item_" . htmlify( 0, $s2 ) . "\">$str</A>"
16444 if ( $type ne ':' ) {
16445 return if ( $tok =~ /^[\,\:\?]$/ ) || $tok eq '||' || $tok eq 'or';
16446 }
16447 else {
16448 return if ( $tok =~ /^[\,]$/ );
16449 }
16450 }
16451 return 1;
16452}
16453
16454sub set_continuation_breaks {
16455
16456 # Define an array of indexes for inserting newline characters to
16457 # keep the line lengths below the maximum desired length. There is
16458 # an implied break after the last token, so it need not be included.
16459
16460 # Method:
16461 # This routine is part of series of routines which adjust line
16462 # lengths. It is only called if a statement is longer than the
16463 # maximum line length, or if a preliminary scanning located
16464 # desirable break points. Sub scan_list has already looked at
16465 # these tokens and set breakpoints (in array
16466 # $forced_breakpoint_to_go[$i]) where it wants breaks (for example
16467 # after commas, after opening parens, and before closing parens).
16468 # This routine will honor these breakpoints and also add additional
16469 # breakpoints as necessary to keep the line length below the maximum
16470 # requested. It bases its decision on where the 'bond strength' is
16471 # lowest.
16472
16473 # Output: returns references to the arrays:
16474 # @i_first
16475 # @i_last
16476 # which contain the indexes $i of the first and last tokens on each
16477 # line.
16478
16479 # In addition, the array:
16480 # $forced_breakpoint_to_go[$i]
16481 # may be updated to be =1 for any index $i after which there must be
16482 # a break. This signals later routines not to undo the breakpoint.
16483
16484 my $saw_good_break = shift;
16485 my @i_first = (); # the first index to output
16486 my @i_last = (); # the last index to output
16487 my @i_colon_breaks = (); # needed to decide if we have to break at ?'s
16488 if ( $types_to_go[0] eq ':' ) { push @i_colon_breaks, 0 }
16489
16490 set_bond_strengths();
16491
16492 my $imin = 0;
16493 my $imax = $max_index_to_go;
16494 if ( $types_to_go[$imin] eq 'b' ) { $imin++ }
16495 if ( $types_to_go[$imax] eq 'b' ) { $imax-- }
16496 my $i_begin = $imin; # index for starting next iteration
16497
16498 my $leading_spaces = leading_spaces_to_go($imin);
16499 my $line_count = 0;
16500 my $last_break_strength = NO_BREAK;
16501 my $i_last_break = -1;
16502 my $max_bias = 0.001;
16503 my $tiny_bias = 0.0001;
16504 my $leading_alignment_token = "";
16505 my $leading_alignment_type = "";
16506
16507 # see if any ?/:'s are in order
16508 my $colons_in_order = 1;
16509 my $last_tok = "";
16510 my @colon_list = grep { /^[\?\:]$/ } @types_to_go[ 0 .. $max_index_to_go ];
16511 my $colon_count = @colon_list;
16512 foreach (@colon_list) {
16513 if ( $_ eq $last_tok ) { $colons_in_order = 0; last }
16514 $last_tok = $_;
16515 }
16516
16517 # This is a sufficient but not necessary condition for colon chain
16518 my $is_colon_chain = ( $colons_in_order && @colon_list > 2 );
16519
16520 #-------------------------------------------------------
16521 # BEGINNING of main loop to set continuation breakpoints
16522 # Keep iterating until we reach the end
16523 #-------------------------------------------------------
16524 while ( $i_begin <= $imax ) {
16525 my $lowest_strength = NO_BREAK;
16526 my $starting_sum = $summed_lengths_to_go[$i_begin];
16527 my $i_lowest = -1;
16528 my $i_test = -1;
16529 my $lowest_next_token = '';
16530 my $lowest_next_type = 'b';
16531 my $i_lowest_next_nonblank = -1;
16532
16533 #-------------------------------------------------------
16534 # BEGINNING of inner loop to find the best next breakpoint
16535 #-------------------------------------------------------
16536 for ( $i_test = $i_begin ; $i_test <= $imax ; $i_test++ ) {
16537 my $type = $types_to_go[$i_test];
16538 my $token = $tokens_to_go[$i_test];
16539 my $next_type = $types_to_go[ $i_test + 1 ];
16540 my $next_token = $tokens_to_go[ $i_test + 1 ];
16541 my $i_next_nonblank = $inext_to_go[$i_test];
16542 my $next_nonblank_type = $types_to_go[$i_next_nonblank];
16543 my $next_nonblank_token = $tokens_to_go[$i_next_nonblank];
16544 my $next_nonblank_block_type = $block_type_to_go[$i_next_nonblank];
16545 my $strength = $bond_strength_to_go[$i_test];
16546 my $maximum_line_length = maximum_line_length($i_begin);
16547

17007 #-------------------------------------------------------

17010 #-------------------------------------------------------

17014 # corresponding '?' unless this is a chain of ?: expressions
17015 #-------------------------------------------------------

17017
17018 # using a simple method for deciding if we are in a ?/: chain --
17019 # this is a chain if it has multiple ?/: pairs all in order;
17020 # otherwise not.
17021 # Note that if line starts in a ':' we count that above as a break
17022 my $is_chain = ( $colons_in_order && @i_colon_breaks > 1 );

17024 unless ($is_chain) {
17025 my @insert_list = ();

17027 my $i_question = $mate_index_to_go[$_];
17028 if ( $i_question >= 0 ) {

17030 $i_question = $iprev_to_go[$i_question];

17032

17037 insert_additional_breaks( \@insert_list, \@i_first, \@i_last );
17038 }
17039 }
17040 }

17042}

17044sub insert_additional_breaks {
17045
17046 # this routine will add line breaks at requested locations after
17047 # sub set_continuation_breaks has made preliminary breaks.
17048
17049 my ( $ri_break_list, $ri_first, $ri_last ) = @_;
17050 my $i_f;
17051 my $i_l;
17052 my $line_number = 0;
17053 foreach my $i_break_left ( sort { $a <=> $b } @{$ri_break_list} ) {
17054
17055 $i_f = $ri_first->[$line_number];
17056 $i_l = $ri_last->[$line_number];
17057 while ( $i_break_left >= $i_l ) {
17058 $line_number++;
17059
17060 # shouldn't happen unless caller passes bad indexes
17061 if ( $line_number >= @{$ri_last} ) {
17062 warning(
17063"Non-fatal program bug: couldn't set break at $i_break_left\n"
17064 );
17065 report_definite_bug();
17066 return;
17067 }
17068 $i_f = $ri_first->[$line_number];
17069 $i_l = $ri_last->[$line_number];
17070 }
17071
17072 # Do not leave a blank at the end of a line; back up if necessary
17073 if ( $types_to_go[$i_break_left] eq 'b' ) { $i_break_left-- }
17074
17075 my $i_break_right = $inext_to_go[$i_break_left];
17076 if ( $i_break_left >= $i_f
17077 && $i_break_left < $i_l
17078 && $i_break_right > $i_f
17079 && $i_break_right <= $i_l )
17080 {
17081 splice( @{$ri_first}, $line_number, 1, ( $i_f, $i_break_right ) );
17082 splice( @{$ri_last}, $line_number, 1, ( $i_break_left, $i_l ) );
17083 }
17084 }
17085 return;
17086}

17088sub set_closing_breakpoint {
17089
17090 # set a breakpoint at a matching closing token
17091 # at present, this is only used to break at a ':' which matches a '?'
17092 my $i_break = shift;
17093
17094 if ( $mate_index_to_go[$i_break] >= 0 ) {
17095
17096 # CAUTION: infinite recursion possible here:
17097 # set_closing_breakpoint calls set_forced_breakpoint, and
17098 # set_forced_breakpoint call set_closing_breakpoint
17099 # ( test files attrib.t, BasicLyx.pm.html).
17100 # Don't reduce the '2' in the statement below
17101 if ( $mate_index_to_go[$i_break] > $i_break + 2 ) {
17102
17103 # break before } ] and ), but sub set_forced_breakpoint will decide
17104 # to break before or after a ? and :
17105 my $inc = ( $tokens_to_go[$i_break] eq '?' ) ? 0 : 1;
17106 set_forced_breakpoint( $mate_index_to_go[$i_break] - $inc );
17107 }
17108 }
17109 else {
17110 my $type_sequence = $type_sequence_to_go[$i_break];
17111 if ($type_sequence) {
17112 my $closing_token = $matching_token{ $tokens_to_go[$i_break] };
17113 $postponed_breakpoint{$type_sequence} = 1;
17114 }
17115 }
17116 return;
17117}

17122 # this can be very useful for debugging a script which has an extra
17123 # or missing brace

17125 if ( $guessed_indentation_level ne $structural_indentation_level ) {
17126 $last_tabbing_disagreement = $input_line_number;
17127
17128 if ($in_tabbing_disagreement) {
17129 }
17130 else {
17131 $tabbing_disagreement_count++;
17132
17133 if ( $tabbing_disagreement_count <= MAX_NAG_MESSAGES ) {
17134 write_logfile_entry(
17135"Start indentation disagreement: input=$guessed_indentation_level; output=$structural_indentation_level\n"
17136 );
17137 }
17138 $in_tabbing_disagreement = $input_line_number;
17139 $first_tabbing_disagreement = $in_tabbing_disagreement
17140 unless ($first_tabbing_disagreement);
17141 }
17142 }
17143 else {
17144
17145 if ($in_tabbing_disagreement) {
17146
17147 if ( $tabbing_disagreement_count <= MAX_NAG_MESSAGES ) {

17150 );
